title: Hummus: A Dataset of Humorous Multimodal Metaphor Use

benchmarks.name: HUMMUS
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on their ability to understand and explain humorous multimodal metaphors, a key aspect of creative and figurative language understanding.

tasks.name: Classification
tasks.description: Models must determine if the humor in an image-caption pair involves metaphor use, answering 'Yes' or 'No'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Multiclass F1 score

tasks.name: Naming
tasks.description: Given a metaphorical image-caption pair, models must identify the underlying conceptual metaphor in the format 'TARGET DOMAIN IS SOURCE DOMAIN'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Sentence similarity (via LaBSE)

tasks.name: ImageBbox
tasks.description: Models must identify the metaphor-related object in the image by providing its label and normalized bounding box coordinates.
tasks.scoring_detail: IoU, precision, recall

tasks.name: ImageLabel
tasks.description: Models must identify the metaphor-related object in the image by answering with a single word label.
tasks.scoring_detail: Sentence similarity (via LaBSE)

tasks.name: CaptionHL
tasks.description: Models must identify the metaphor-related part of the caption by surrounding it with HTML tags.
tasks.scoring_detail: Jaccard index, precision, recall

tasks.name: Explanation
tasks.description: Models must generate a short explanation (max 30 words) of how the metaphor contributes to the humor of the image-caption pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2

title: CM-Gen: A Neural Framework for Chinese Metaphor Generation with Explicit Context Modelling

benchmarks.name: Chinese NM Corpus (CMC)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset and task for Chinese nominal metaphor generation, a form of creative language generation. The evaluation framework includes human ratings for creativity and consistency.

tasks.name: Chinese Nominal Metaphor (NM) Generation
tasks.description: Given a tenor (a subject concept), the model must generate a complete nominal metaphor, including a vehicle (the object of comparison), a comparator (e.g., 'like', 'is'), and a context that explains the comparison.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include SeqGAN, GPT2, BART, and the proposed CM-Gen.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: Perplexity (PPL), Dist-1, Dist-2, Metaphoricity (Meta score from a classifier), Novelty (unseen tenor-vehicle pairs). Human: Fluency, Consistency, Creativity ratings (1-5 scale).

tasks.name: Nominal Metaphor (NM) Identification
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine if a given sentence is a nominal metaphor. This classifier is trained on the CMC dataset and used to create the 'Meta' automatic metric for the generation task.
tasks.origin_paper: Liu et al., 2018; Zeng et al., 2020
tasks.task_type_notes: This task is used to build an automatic evaluation metric for the main generation task.
tasks.model_type_notes: A RoBERTa-based classifier was trained and evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy on a test split of the CMC dataset.

title: Understanding Figurative Meaning through Explainable Visual Entailment

benchmarks.name: V-FLUTE
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new multimodal dataset and task for evaluating Vision-Language Models on understanding figurative language (metaphors, similes, idioms, sarcasm, humor) through an explainable visual entailment framework.

tasks.name: Explainable Figurative Visual Entailment
tasks.description: Given an image (premise) and a caption (hypothesis) containing figurative phenomena, a model must predict whether the image entails or contradicts the caption and generate a textual explanation for the decision.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves both classification (predicting an 'Entailment' or 'Contradiction' label) and generation (producing a textual explanation).
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested models include LLaVA, Claude-3, GPT-4, GeminiPro, Instruct-BLIP, and GPT-4o.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics (F1 score, F1@ExplanationScore using BERTScore and BLEURT) and human evaluation (adequacy ratings, preference rates, error analysis for hallucination, unsound/incomplete reasoning).

benchmarks.name: e-SNLI-VE (eViL)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This benchmark focuses on literal visual entailment, not figurative language or creativity. It was used as a training set for a baseline model to show that models trained on literal tasks do not generalize well to the paper's new figurative task.

tasks.name: Explainable Visual Entailment
tasks.description: A model was fine-tuned on this dataset of literal image-text pairs to predict entailment labels and generate explanations. The resulting model was then evaluated on the V-FLUTE dataset as a baseline.
tasks.task_type_notes: The dataset was used for fine-tuning a model, not for direct evaluation on its own test set. The evaluation of the trained model happened on a different benchmark (V-FLUTE).
tasks.model_type_notes: LLaVA-1.5-7B was fine-tuned on this dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: The model trained on e-SNLI-VE was evaluated on the V-FLUTE test set using F1 score and F1@ExplanationScore.

title: Mothman at SemEval-2024 Task 9: An Iterative System for Chain-of-Thought Prompt Optimization

benchmarks.name: BRAINTEASER
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A shared task designed to evaluate lateral thinking and creative, 'outside the box' problem-solving in LLMs using sentence puzzles.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Jiang et al., 2023; Jiang et al., 2024

tasks.name: Sentence Puzzle Subtask
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question-answering task where an LLM must solve lateral thinking puzzles (riddles). The paper evaluates GPT-4 on the Base, Semantic Reconstruction (SR), and Context Reconstruction (CR) versions of the puzzles. A human performance baseline is also established by having participants solve the same puzzles to inform prompt engineering.
tasks.origin_paper: Jiang et al., 2023; Jiang et al., 2024
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is to generate the correct answer choice for a multiple-choice question.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates GPT-4. It also uses human participants to establish a performance baseline.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy. Scores are reported for the LLM and for human participants on various subsets of the data (Base, SR, CR, Base&SR, Adversarial, Overall).

title: Evaluating Text Creativity across Diverse Domains: A Dataset and Large Language Model Evaluator

benchmarks.name: CreataSet
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale dataset with over 100K human-level and 1M synthetic pairs for evaluating textual creativity across 87 domains. It is the central contribution of the paper and used for the main experiments.

tasks.name: Pairwise Creativity Evaluation
tasks.description: Given an instruction and two text responses, models are evaluated on their ability to judge which response is more creative, or if they are comparable. The evaluation is performed on a human-annotated test set of over 3,000 samples.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates a wide range of LLMs as judges, including GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, LLaMA3.1, Gemma, Qwen2.5, as well as evaluation-centric models like Prometheus and WritingBench-Critic.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score, Kappa score, and Agreement rate against human judgments.

benchmarks.name: Creative Writing Out-of-Distribution (O.O.D.) Test
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Uses an existing creative writing dataset to test the out-of-distribution generalization capability of creativity evaluators on long-form text.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Chakrabarty et al. (2024), "Art or artifice? large language models and the false promise of creativity"

tasks.name: Human vs. Model Creative Writing Comparison
tasks.description: Evaluators judge creativity in 36 pairs of long-form creative writing responses, where one response is human-written and the other is model-generated. The task assesses if evaluators can correctly identify the human response as more creative.
tasks.origin_paper: Chakrabarty et al. (2024), "Art or artifice? large language models and the false promise of creativity"
tasks.scoring_detail: Agreement and F1 scores against the ground truth that human responses are more creative.

benchmarks.name: Model Creativity Enhancement Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new evaluation setup to demonstrate the practical utility of the CrEval evaluator in enhancing the creativity of other LLMs through preference optimization (DPO).

tasks.name: Win Rate Comparison against Baseline
tasks.description: Models fine-tuned for creativity using DPO generate responses, which are then compared against responses from a baseline model (GPT-4o-mini). The evaluation measures the win rate of the fine-tuned models.
tasks.task_type_notes: Models first generate creative text, which is then evaluated by various judges.
tasks.model_type_notes: The models being evaluated are fine-tuned versions of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
tasks.scoring_detail: Win rate against GPT-4o-mini responses, as judged by CrEval, GPT-4o, and human annotators.

title: Open-ended Scientific Discovery via Bayesian Surprise

benchmarks.name: Open-ended Data-Driven Discovery Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Presents and evaluates a new framework (AUTODS) for open-ended scientific hypothesis generation, a form of creativity. The framework is tested on real-world datasets with LLMs, and results are reported using both automated and human evaluation.

tasks.name: Hypothesis Discovery via Bayesian Surprise
tasks.description: An LLM agent uses a search strategy (MCTS, greedy, beam search, etc.) guided by a Bayesian surprise reward to iteratively generate and verify novel scientific hypotheses from a given dataset. The goal is to maximize the number of surprising discoveries within a fixed budget.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o and o4-mini were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Primary metric is the count of 'surprisals' (an LLM-based score derived from KL divergence of beliefs). Also measures number of unique hypotheses and correlates LLM surprisal with human ratings of surprise, interestingness, and utility.

tasks.name: Hypothesis Discovery via Alternative Rewards
tasks.description: An ablation study where the MCTS-based agent is guided by alternative LLM-based rewards (interestingness, utility, direct surprisal) instead of Bayesian surprise, to compare their effectiveness.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings of surprisal, interestingness, and utility for the generated hypotheses.

tasks.name: Discovery Agent Process Validation
tasks.description: Internal human evaluation of the validity and faithfulness of the agent's generated components: experiment plans, code implementations, and hypothesis deduplication.
tasks.task_type_notes: Humans evaluate the outputs of the LLM agent's internal steps.
tasks.model_type_notes: The agent being evaluated is LLM-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Validity ratings (%) and inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1).

title: HypoBench: Towards Systematic and Principled Benchmarking for Hypothesis Generation

benchmarks.name: HypoBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale benchmark for evaluating hypothesis generation in LLMs, a key aspect of scientific and creative reasoning. It includes 12 diverse real-world and synthetic tasks with controlled difficulty levels and multiple evaluation metrics.

tasks.name: Deception Detection
tasks.description: Distinguish genuine and fake hotel reviews to understand subtle linguistic cues that indicate deceptive writing.
tasks.origin_paper: Zhou et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference), Novelty rating (1-5), Plausibility rating (1-5), Clarity rating (1-5) via GPT-4o judge

tasks.name: AI-generated Content Detection
tasks.description: Identify whether a story is written by a human or AI given a writing prompt, to discover distinctive features between human and AI-generated content.
tasks.origin_paper: Zhou et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference), Novelty rating (1-5), Plausibility rating (1-5), Clarity rating (1-5) via GPT-4o judge

tasks.name: Persuasive Argument Prediction
tasks.description: Predict which text is more persuasive between pairs of arguments to explore linguistic features that contribute to effective persuasion.
tasks.origin_paper: Zhou et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference), Novelty rating (1-5), Plausibility rating (1-5), Clarity rating (1-5) via GPT-4o judge

tasks.name: Mental Stress Detection
tasks.description: Detect mental stress signals from Reddit posts across different communities to investigate linguistic features indicative of mental stress.
tasks.origin_paper: Zhou et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference), Novelty rating (1-5), Plausibility rating (1-5), Clarity rating (1-5) via GPT-4o judge

tasks.name: News Headline Engagements
tasks.description: Given a pair of headlines for the same news article, predict which one will get more clicks from readers.
tasks.origin_paper: Zhou et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference), Novelty rating (1-5), Plausibility rating (1-5), Clarity rating (1-5) via GPT-4o judge

tasks.name: Retweets
tasks.description: Given a pair of tweets, predict which one will be retweeted more.
tasks.origin_paper: Zhou et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference), Novelty rating (1-5), Plausibility rating (1-5), Clarity rating (1-5) via GPT-4o judge

tasks.name: Paper Citations
tasks.description: Classify whether an academic paper will get high or low citations based on its abstract.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference), Novelty rating (1-5), Plausibility rating (1-5), Clarity rating (1-5) via GPT-4o judge

tasks.name: Presidential Election (Synthetic)
tasks.description: Given a person’s tweet post, predict which party they will vote for in the 2024 election.
tasks.scoring_detail: Hypothesis Discovery Rate (HDR) via GPT-4o judge, Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference)

tasks.name: Personality Prediction (Synthetic)
tasks.description: Given a person’s tweet, determine the personal preferences of the user based on the content, sentiment, and language patterns.
tasks.scoring_detail: Hypothesis Discovery Rate (HDR) via GPT-4o judge, Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference)

tasks.name: College Admission (Synthetic)
tasks.description: Predicting whether a student will be admitted or not based on their background information.
tasks.scoring_detail: Hypothesis Discovery Rate (HDR) via GPT-4o judge, Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference)

tasks.name: Shoe Sales (Synthetic)
tasks.description: Given a customer’s appearance, predict the shoe they will buy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Hypothesis Discovery Rate (HDR) via GPT-4o judge, Accuracy, F1 score (via LLM-based inference)

tasks.name: Marine Ecosystem (Synthetic)
tasks.description: Given information about a marine ecosystem, predict the daily sunlight hours received per day at the location.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean Squared Error (MSE), Hypothesis Discovery Rate (HDR) via GPT-4o judge

title: Let Androids Dream of Electric Sheep: A Human-like Image Implication Understanding and Reasoning Framework

benchmarks.name: Image Implication Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark of 100 images (50 English, 50 Chinese) with MCQ and open-ended questions designed to evaluate AI's ability to understand abstract, metaphorical, and cultural implications in images.

tasks.name: Multiple-Choice Question (MCQ)
tasks.description: Models answer a multiple-choice question about the implication of an image from a set of six options. The evaluation is performed on a newly constructed set of 50 English and 50 Chinese images.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is to select the correct option from a list.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Open-Style Question (OSQ)
tasks.description: Models generate a free-text explanation of an image's implication in response to the fixed question: 'What is the implication in this image?'. This is a new evaluation method introduced by the paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4o judge scoring 1-5 based on 5 criteria (Surface-level Information, Emotional Expression, Domain and Context, Rhetorical Skills, Deep Implications); validated against human scores.

title: Pun2Pun: Benchmarking LLMs on Textual-Visual Chinese-English Pun Translation via Pragmatics Model and Linguistic Reasoning

benchmarks.name: Pun2Pun
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark for evaluating AI systems on the creative and complex reasoning task of cross-lingual pun translation (Chinese-English), covering both textual and visual modalities.

tasks.name: Textual Pun Classification
tasks.description: Classifying a given textual pun as either homophonic (based on sound) or homographic (based on writing/meaning).
tasks.task_type_notes: Classification task (Task I for textual puns)
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (Acc)

tasks.name: Textual Pun Locating
tasks.description: Identifying and locating the specific punning word or phrase within a sentence.
tasks.task_type_notes: Task II for textual puns
tasks.scoring_detail: Agent-Accuracy (AAcc) using a judge model (gpt-4o-mini) to score consistency with human annotations on a 0-10 scale.

tasks.name: Textual Pun Decomposition
tasks.description: Extracting and explaining the two elements or meanings that constitute the pun's mechanism.
tasks.task_type_notes: Task III for textual puns
tasks.scoring_detail: Agent-Accuracy (AAcc) using a judge model (gpt-4o-mini) to score consistency with human annotations on a 0-10 scale.

tasks.name: Textual Pun Translation
tasks.description: Translating a pun from Chinese to English (or vice versa) while preserving the original pun effect or creating a new, equivalent pun in the target language.
tasks.task_type_notes: Task IV for textual puns
tasks.scoring_detail: Hit (binary success judged by gpt-4o-mini), Overlap (Ovl) (weighted quality score from 0-100 judged by gpt-4o-mini), Cosine Similarity (Cos).

tasks.name: Visual Pun Classification
tasks.description: Classifying a given visual pun (image with caption) as either homophonic or homographic.
tasks.task_type_notes: Classification task (Task I for visual puns)
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (Acc)

tasks.name: Visual Pun Decomposition
tasks.description: Extracting and explaining the two elements or meanings that constitute the visual pun's mechanism, based on the image and its caption.
tasks.task_type_notes: Task II for visual puns
tasks.scoring_detail: Agent-Accuracy (AAcc) using a judge model (gpt-4o-mini) to score consistency with human annotations on a 0-10 scale.

tasks.name: Visual Pun Appreciation
tasks.description: Explaining the interplay between the caption and the image, including cultural background and usage scenarios.
tasks.task_type_notes: Task III for visual puns
tasks.scoring_detail: Agent-Accuracy (AAcc) using a judge model (gpt-4o-mini) to score consistency with human annotations on a 0-10 scale.

tasks.name: Visual Pun Translation
tasks.description: Translating the caption of a visual pun from Chinese to English (or vice versa) while preserving the pun effect in relation to the static image.
tasks.task_type_notes: Task IV for visual puns
tasks.scoring_detail: Hit (binary success judged by gpt-4o-mini), Overlap (Ovl) (weighted quality score from 0-100 judged by gpt-4o-mini), Cosine Similarity (Cos).

tasks.name: Iterative Refinement for Pun Translation
tasks.description: A study where a model (deepseek-r1) iteratively refines its own pun translation over five consecutive steps to assess if simple repetition improves quality.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is referred to as the 'Optimization Study' in the paper.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper specifies using deepseek-r1 for this task.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation by two authors on a 5-point scale across three dimensions: innovativeness, content retention, and target language fluency.

title: Meta4XNLI: A Crosslingual Parallel Corpus for Metaphor Detection and Interpretation

benchmarks.name: Meta4XNLI
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new parallel corpus for evaluating AI's ability to detect and interpret metaphors, a key aspect of creative and figurative language understanding.

tasks.name: Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: A sequence labeling task where models identify metaphorical tokens (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) in Spanish and English sentences.
tasks.task_type_notes: Sequence labeling / token classification
tasks.model_type_notes: mDeBERTa, XLM-RoBERTa
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score, Precision, Recall, In-vocabulary (Inv) F1, Out-of-vocabulary (Oov) F1

tasks.name: Metaphor Interpretation via NLI
tasks.description: A Natural Language Inference (NLI) task where models determine the relationship between premise-hypothesis pairs where understanding a metaphor is crucial for correct inference.
tasks.task_type_notes: NLI classification
tasks.model_type_notes: mDeBERTa, XLM-RoBERTa
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: VUAM
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard benchmark for metaphor detection, a form of creative language, used here for cross-domain training and evaluation.

tasks.name: Cross-domain Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: The VUAM dataset was used to train models (DeBERTa, XLM-RoBERTa) which were then evaluated on the new Meta4XNLI corpus to test cross-domain performance on metaphor detection.
tasks.task_type_notes: Sequence labeling / token classification
tasks.model_type_notes: DeBERTa, XLM-RoBERTa
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score, In-vocabulary (Inv) F1, Out-of-vocabulary (Oov) F1

tasks.name: Generalization Evaluation
tasks.description: The VUAM test set was used to evaluate models that were trained on the new Meta4XNLIEN corpus to test generalization from the new data to an established benchmark.
tasks.task_type_notes: Sequence labeling / token classification
tasks.model_type_notes: mDeBERTa, XLM-RoBERTa
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score, In-vocabulary (Inv) F1, Out-of-vocabulary (Oov) F1

benchmarks.name: CoMeta
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for metaphor detection in Spanish, a form of creative language, used here for cross-domain training and evaluation.

tasks.name: Cross-domain Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: The CoMeta dataset was used to train models (mDeBERTa) which were then evaluated on the new Meta4XNLIES corpus to test cross-domain performance on metaphor detection.
tasks.task_type_notes: Sequence labeling / token classification
tasks.model_type_notes: mDeBERTa
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score, In-vocabulary (Inv) F1, Out-of-vocabulary (Oov) F1

tasks.name: Generalization Evaluation
tasks.description: The CoMeta test set was used to evaluate models that were trained on the new Meta4XNLIES corpus to test generalization from the new data to an established benchmark.
tasks.task_type_notes: Sequence labeling / token classification
tasks.model_type_notes: mDeBERTa, XLM-RoBERTa
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score, In-vocabulary (Inv) F1, Out-of-vocabulary (Oov) F1

benchmarks.name: MultiNLI
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard NLU benchmark for textual inference, not specifically designed for creativity evaluation. It is used here to fine-tune models for the general NLI task before testing on metaphor-specific data.

tasks.name: NLI Model Fine-tuning
tasks.description: The MultiNLI dataset was used to fine-tune LLMs for the general Natural Language Inference task. These fine-tuned models were then evaluated on the metaphor interpretation task using the Meta4XNLI dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: Model fine-tuning for NLI classification
tasks.model_type_notes: mDeBERTa, XLM-RoBERTa
tasks.scoring_detail: N/A (used for model training, evaluation performed on Meta4XNLI)

title: ProCreate, Don't Reproduce! Propulsive Energy Diffusion for Creative Generation

benchmarks.name: FSCG-8 (Few-Shot Creative Generation 8)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset specifically curated to test sample diversity, memorization, and creative generation in few-shot settings for image generation models. The tasks are open-ended and focus on generating novel images inspired by a small reference set.

tasks.name: Few-Shot Creative Generation
tasks.description: Given a small set of 10 training images from one of eight categories (e.g., Amedeo Modigliani's paintings, Burberry's apparel design), the model generates new images from text prompts. The goal is to achieve high diversity and conceptual similarity to the reference set without direct reproduction.
tasks.model_type_notes: Stable Diffusion v1-5, fine-tuned with standard methods and DreamBooth.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, KID, Precision, Recall, Mean Similarity Score (MSS), Vendi score, Prompt Fidelity (CLIP cosine similarity), SSCD score (for qualitative comparison).

benchmarks.name: Training Data Replication Prevention
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This benchmark evaluates a model's ability to avoid reproducing its training data, which is a crucial aspect of creative generation (i.e., producing novel, non-memorized content). The task is open-ended image generation.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Somepalli et al. (2023), "Diffusion art or digital forgery? investigating data replication in diffusion models"

tasks.name: Replication Prevention on LAION12M
tasks.description: A pre-trained diffusion model generates images using prompts from the LAION12M dataset. The goal is to generate images that are novel and do not replicate existing images from the LAION12M training set, measured by similarity scores.
tasks.origin_paper: Somepalli et al. (2023), "Diffusion art or digital forgery? investigating data replication in diffusion models"
tasks.model_type_notes: Stable Diffusion v1-5
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage of generations exceeding Top-1 SSCD score thresholds (0.4, 0.5, 0.6), FID, KID.

title: EvolvR: Self-Evolving Pairwise Reasoning for Story Evaluation to Enhance Generation

benchmarks.name: StoryER
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A public benchmark with human annotations for multi-dimensional story quality evaluation, focusing on aspects like coherence, style, and empathy. It is used to test the paper's story evaluation model.

tasks.name: Story Evaluation
tasks.description: The paper's evaluator model (EvolvR) and various baselines predict multi-dimensional quality scores for stories from the StoryER dataset. These predictions are then compared against the ground-truth human judgments to measure correlation and accuracy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation, Mean Squared Error (MSE), F1-Score

benchmarks.name: HANNA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A public benchmark with human annotations for multi-dimensional story quality evaluation, focusing on aspects like relevance, coherence, surprise, and engagement. It is used both for evaluating the story evaluator and for a story generation task.

tasks.name: Story Evaluation
tasks.description: The paper's evaluator model (EvolvR) and various baselines predict multi-dimensional quality scores for stories from the HANNA dataset. These predictions are compared against ground-truth human judgments to measure correlation and accuracy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation, Mean Squared Error (MSE), F1-Score

tasks.name: Story Generation
tasks.description: A generator model is fine-tuned using the EvolvR evaluator as a reward model. The task is to generate high-quality stories from prompts taken from the HANNA dataset. The quality of the generated stories is assessed by human experts.
tasks.model_type_notes: The generator model is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average Score (1-5 scale across Relevance, Coherence, Empathy, Surprise, Engagement, Complexity), Win Rate (head-to-head comparison against baseline and original dataset stories)

benchmarks.name: OpenMEVA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A public benchmark for evaluating the holistic 'Overall Quality' of open-ended story generation. It is used in this paper to test the zero-shot generalization capability of the proposed evaluator.

tasks.name: Story Evaluation (Zero-shot)
tasks.description: The paper's evaluator model (EvolvR) predicts a single holistic quality score for stories from the OpenMEVA benchmark without any fine-tuning on it. The model's multi-dimensional scores are averaged to produce the holistic score, which is then compared against human ground-truth ratings.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation

title: DeepMath-Creative: A Benchmark for Evaluating Mathematical Creativity of Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: DeepMath-Creative
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark is explicitly designed to evaluate the mathematical creativity of LLMs using open-ended constructive problems (proofs and counterexamples).

tasks.name: Problem requiring a formal proof
tasks.description: Given a mathematical proposition, the model is required to construct a mathematical object or a formal proof to validate it. This task constitutes approximately 40% of the dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Manual scoring by mathematical experts: 0 for incorrect direction, 0.5 for flawed proof, 1 for complete and correct proof.

tasks.name: Problem requiring a counterexample
tasks.description: Given a mathematical proposition, the model is required to construct a counterexample to invalidate it. This task constitutes approximately 60% of the dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Manual scoring by mathematical experts: 0 for incorrect direction, 0.5 for flawed counterexample, 1 for valid counterexample.

benchmarks.name: Foundational problems evaluation set
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This set consists of standard, foundational math problems to evaluate fundamental reasoning, not creativity. It is used as a baseline to show that models perform well on standard tasks, highlighting the need for a creativity-focused benchmark.

tasks.name: Foundational mathematical problem solving
tasks.description: An evaluation set of 170 foundational problems from undergraduate-level mathematics (analysis, algebra, probability, etc.) to assess baseline reasoning abilities.
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall accuracy (reported as ~85%)

benchmarks.name: Open problems set
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This set evaluates the ability of LLMs to contribute to cutting-edge mathematical research by tackling unsolved problems, which is a direct test of high-level mathematical creativity and novel synthesis.

tasks.name: Open mathematical problem exploration
tasks.description: A compiled set of open mathematical problems used to evaluate if LLMs can provide information of substantial referential value for advanced mathematical research.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative assessment of whether the output has 'substantial referential value'.

title: Collaborative Neural Painting

benchmarks.name: Collaborative Neural Painting (CNP) Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new task, dataset, and evaluation protocol for collaborative, stroke-based image generation, a creative task. It uses open-ended generation tasks and evaluates models with both automatic metrics and human studies.

tasks.name: Block Completion
tasks.description: The model completes a painting where a contiguous block of strokes in the sequence is missing, simulating the undoing of the last N strokes suggested by the model.
tasks.model_type_notes: The model is a Masked Diffusion Transformer operating on sequences of parameterized brushstrokes.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, Image L2 distance, Stroke L1 distance (with Hungarian Matching), User preference ranking

tasks.name: Level Completion
tasks.description: The model generates fine details (strokes from higher granularity levels) for a coarse sketch of an object (strokes from lower granularity levels).
tasks.model_type_notes: The model is a Masked Diffusion Transformer operating on sequences of parameterized brushstrokes.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, Image L2 distance, Stroke L1 distance (with Hungarian Matching), User preference ranking

tasks.name: Random Completion
tasks.description: The model completes a painting by generating strokes in various spatial locations where a random percentage of strokes have been removed, simulating retouching operations.
tasks.model_type_notes: The model is a Masked Diffusion Transformer operating on sequences of parameterized brushstrokes.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, Image L2 distance, Stroke L1 distance (with Hungarian Matching), User preference ranking

tasks.name: Square Completion
tasks.description: The model generates a local area of a painting by completing strokes missing within a square region of the rendered image.
tasks.model_type_notes: The model is a Masked Diffusion Transformer operating on sequences of parameterized brushstrokes.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, Image L2 distance, Stroke L1 distance (with Hungarian Matching), User preference ranking

tasks.name: No Context Generation
tasks.description: The model generates an entire painting from scratch, conditioned only on a desired object class label, with no initial strokes provided.
tasks.model_type_notes: The model is a Masked Diffusion Transformer operating on sequences of parameterized brushstrokes.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, User preference ranking

title: MIRROR: A Novel Approach for the Automated Evaluation of Open-Ended Question Generation

benchmarks.name: MIRROR (Multi-LLM Iterative Review and Response for Optimized Rating)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces and tests a new method for evaluating open-ended question generation, a task related to creativity. The evaluation criteria explicitly include 'novelty' and 'complexity', which are core components of creativity assessment.

tasks.name: Open-Ended Question Generation
tasks.description: An LLM (GPT-3.5 Turbo) generates open-ended questions from context paragraphs sourced from the EduProbe and SciQ datasets. These generated questions serve as the input for the subsequent evaluation task.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5 Turbo was used to generate the questions.
tasks.scoring_detail: This task only generated the questions for evaluation; the outputs were scored in the evaluation task.

tasks.name: Question Quality Evaluation
tasks.description: LLMs (GPT-4, Gemini, Llama2-70b) and human experts evaluate the quality of generated questions on five criteria: grammaticality, appropriateness, relevance, novelty, and complexity. The paper compares a direct prompting evaluation method with its new iterative feedback method, MIRROR.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4, Gemini, and Llama2-70b were used as evaluators.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings on a 1-5 scale, LLM ratings on a 1-5 scale, Pearson's correlation between LLM and human scores, Fleiss's Kappa for inter-annotator agreement.

title: HW-TSC at SemEval-2024 Task 9: Exploring Prompt Engineering Strategies for Brain Teaser Puzzles Through LLMs

benchmarks.name: BRAINTEASER
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A multiple-choice QA benchmark designed to evaluate the lateral thinking and creative problem-solving capabilities of LLMs, which are key aspects of creativity.
benchmarks.origin_name: BRAINTEASER: A Novel Task Defying Common Sense (SemEval-2024 Task 9)

tasks.name: Word Puzzle
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question answering subtask where the answer to a word-based brain teaser relies on creative interpretation of letter composition or phonetics, rather than the word's literal meaning.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is to select the correct option from a list, which is a form of constrained generation or prediction.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Sentence Puzzle
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question answering subtask with sentence-type brain teasers based on nonsensical or illogical text, requiring lateral thinking to identify the correct solution.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is to select the correct option from a list, which is a form of constrained generation or prediction.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: Pron vs Prompt: Can Large Language Models already Challenge a World-Class Fiction Author at Creative Text Writing?

benchmarks.name: Pron vs Prompt Creative Writing Contest
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This paper introduces a new, comprehensive contest-style benchmark to directly compare the creative writing skills of a top-tier LLM (GPT-4) against a world-class human novelist (Patricio Pron). The evaluation uses open-ended generation tasks and expert human judgment based on a custom rubric derived from creativity theory.

tasks.name: Title Generation
tasks.description: A human author (Patricio Pron) and an LLM (GPT-4) each proposed 30 creative movie titles. These titles were then evaluated by literary experts and used as prompts for the synopsis generation task.
tasks.scoring_detail: Expert ratings (0-3 Likert scale) for title attractiveness, originality, and creativity.

tasks.name: Synopsis Generation
tasks.description: A human author (Patricio Pron) and an LLM (GPT-4) wrote ~600-word synopses for 60 movie titles (30 from each contender). GPT-4 generated synopses in both English and Spanish, which were then evaluated by literary experts.
tasks.scoring_detail: Expert ratings (0-3 Likert scale) for Attractiveness (style, theme), Originality (style, theme), Creativity, Anthology Potential, and Own Voice. Also includes author identification (human/AI).

title: When 'YES' Meets 'BUT': Can Large Models Comprehend Contradictory Humor Through Comparative Reasoning?

benchmarks.name: YESBUT (V2)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark is designed to evaluate AI's ability to understand humor in comics arising from juxtaposition and contradiction, which requires deep narrative reasoning, interpretation of symbolism, and understanding of cultural context—all facets of creative intelligence.

tasks.name: Literal Description Writing
tasks.description: Given a two-panel comic, the model generates a textual description capturing the overarching narrative depicted across the panels.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper states that only Vision-Language Models (VLMs) were evaluated on this task.
tasks.scoring_detail: BERT Score, ROUGE-2, GPT-based Score, Human ratings (Correctness, Completeness, Fidelity)

tasks.name: Explicit Contradiction Generation
tasks.description: Given a two-panel comic, the model generates a textual explanation identifying the core contradiction embedded within the narrative.
tasks.model_type_notes: Both VLMs and LLMs (using VLM-generated captions) were evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: BERT Score, ROUGE-2, GPT-based Score, Human ratings (Correctness, Fidelity)

tasks.name: Underlying Symbolism Selection
tasks.description: Given a comic and four possible symbolic interpretations, the model must select the correct one.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a multiple-choice question task to evaluate deep narrative comprehension.
tasks.model_type_notes: Both VLMs and LLMs (using VLM-generated captions) were evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Title Matching
tasks.description: Given a comic and four possible titles, the model must select the title that best encapsulates the comic's thematic essence.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a multiple-choice question task to evaluate holistic understanding and thematic summarization.
tasks.model_type_notes: Both VLMs and LLMs (using VLM-generated captions) were evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: FHS-adapter: fine-grained hierarchical semantic adapter for Chinese landscape paintings generation

benchmarks.name: T2ICLP
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and evaluation framework for a creative generation task: generating traditional Chinese landscape paintings from fine-grained text prompts. This is an open-ended artistic task.

tasks.name: Chinese Landscape Painting Generation
tasks.description: Generating Chinese landscape paintings from fine-grained textual prompts that include four perspectives: Meta (historical info), Description (content), Sentiment (mood), and Poem.
tasks.model_type_notes: Text-to-image generation models, primarily Diffusion-based (e.g., Stable Diffusion, SDXL, GLIDE, P+) but also includes a GAN-based model (ControlGAN).
tasks.scoring_detail: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), CLIP-T Score

benchmarks.name: User Study for Chinese Painting Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A human evaluation study where experts rate generated images on artistic and creative dimensions like composition, brushwork, and emotional expression. This directly measures creative quality.

tasks.name: Chinese Landscape Painting Generation Evaluation
tasks.description: Human experts evaluate the quality of generated Chinese landscape paintings based on five artistic dimensions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The study compared the paper's FHS-adapter with the Textual Inversion model, both of which are diffusion-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Ratings from 21 scholars on 5 dimensions: composition and layout, technique and brushwork, colors, antiquing effect, and expression of emotion.

tasks.name: Chinese Flower-and-Bird Painting Generation Evaluation
tasks.description: Human experts evaluate the quality of generated Chinese flower-and-bird paintings to test the model's generalization to a related domain.
tasks.model_type_notes: The study compared the paper's FHS-adapter with the Textual Inversion model, both of which are diffusion-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Ratings from 21 scholars on 5 dimensions: composition and layout, technique and brushwork, colors, antiquing effect, and expression of emotion.

title: DeepRapper: Neural Rap Generation with Rhyme and Rhythm Modeling

benchmarks.name: Rap Generation Evaluation on D-RAP
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset (D-RAP) and a comprehensive evaluation protocol for the creative task of rap generation, assessing rhyme, rhythm, fluency, and thematic coherence using both automatic metrics and human judgment.

tasks.name: Rap Generation with Rhyme and Rhythm
tasks.description: The model generates rap lyrics, including rhyme patterns and rhythmic beat tokens, conditioned on a given starting sentence. The evaluation assesses the quality of the generated language, rhyme, and rhythm.
tasks.scoring_detail: Objective metrics: Perplexity (PPL), Rhyme Accuracy (RA), Rhyme Density (RD), Combo-N (N-gram rhyme), Beat Accuracy (BA), First/Second Order Distribution (FOD/SOD) of beats via Wasserstein Distance. Subjective metrics (human rating 1-5): Theme, Fluency, Rhyme Quality, Rhyme Diversity.

title: ParallelPARC: A Scalable Pipeline for Generating Natural-Language Analogies

benchmarks.name: ProPara-Logy
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a new benchmark for evaluating analogical reasoning in LLMs, which is a core component of creative cognition. The tasks involve judging the structural similarity between complex, paragraph-level descriptions.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition (Binary Classification)
tasks.description: Given a pair of paragraphs describing scientific processes (a base and a target), the task is to decide whether the processes are analogous. The target can be a true analogy, a random paragraph (simple negative), or a distractor paragraph with altered causal/temporal relations (challenging negative).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (Overall and per target type: Analogy, Random, Distractor). Model performance is compared against a human-validated gold set, and human performance is also measured directly.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition (Multiple-Choice)
tasks.description: Given a base paragraph and four candidate paragraphs, the task is to identify the candidate that is most analogous to the base. The paper proposes two setups: a 'Basic' version with one analogy and three random paragraphs, and an 'Advanced' version that includes a challenging distractor among the candidates.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (for Basic and Advanced setups). Model performance is compared against a human-validated gold set, and human performance is also measured directly.

title: MineAnyBuild: Benchmarking Spatial Planning for Open-world AI Agents

benchmarks.name: MineAnyBuild
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new comprehensive benchmark for evaluating AI agents on spatial planning, a key component of creative construction. It includes a specific task for creativity and other open-ended generation tasks within the Minecraft environment, with empirical results for multiple MLLMs.

tasks.name: Executable Spatial Plan Generation
tasks.description: The agent generates executable spatial plans, in the form of a 3D blueprint matrix, to construct an architecture in Minecraft based on abstract instructions and a reference image.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) like GPT-4o, Claude-3, and Gemini.
tasks.scoring_detail: Weighted 'Evaluation Score' from a GPT-4.1 critic model based on Completeness, Complexity, and Overall Aesthetic/Fidelity.

tasks.name: Spatial Understanding
tasks.description: The agent translates step-by-step instructions, which contain the specific positions of each building block, into a complete 3D blueprint matrix.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) like GPT-4o, Claude-3, and Gemini.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4.1 critic model score based on Completeness (Instruction Following) compared to a reference.

tasks.name: Creativity
tasks.description: Given a textual instruction, the agent must brainstorm block combinations and a structural layout to generate a creative and aesthetically unique architecture, outputting the result as a blueprint matrix.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) like GPT-4o, Claude-3, and Gemini.
tasks.scoring_detail: Weighted 'Evaluation Score' from a GPT-4.1 critic model based on Creativity, Completeness, Complexity, Architecture Structure, and Overall Aesthetic/Fidelity.

tasks.name: Spatial Reasoning
tasks.description: A Visual Question Answering (VQA) task inspired by mental rotation experiments, where the agent must analyze the geometric structure of a 3D object made of blocks and compare it to other objects with different orientations.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) like GPT-4o, Claude-3, and Gemini.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

tasks.name: Spatial Commonsense
tasks.description: A Visual Question Answering (VQA) task where the agent answers questions about real-world spatial commonsense (e.g., rationality of object placement, navigation) based on an image of a scene within Minecraft.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) like GPT-4o, Claude-3, and Gemini.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4.1 critic model score based on the matching degree between the model's response and a standard answer.

title: InstaStyle: Inversion Noise of a Stylized Image is Secretly a Style Adviser

benchmarks.name: Stylized Image Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates a core creative AI task (stylized image generation) using both automated metrics and human judgment on open-ended generation tasks.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Gal et al., 2022 (Textual Inversion); Sohn et al., 2023 (StyleDrop)

tasks.name: Quantitative Evaluation of Stylized Generation
tasks.description: Generated images are evaluated for style consistency (CLIP score vs. reference image) and content fidelity (CLIP score vs. text prompt). Content prompts are based on 100 object classes from CIFAR100.
tasks.origin_name: CLIP score for style consistency and content fidelity
tasks.origin_paper: Gal et al., 2022 (Textual Inversion); Sohn et al., 2023 (StyleDrop)
tasks.scoring_detail: Style consistency (CLIP score between generated and reference image), Content fidelity (CLIP score between generated image and prompt)

tasks.name: User Study on Stylized Generation
tasks.description: Human participants perform pairwise comparisons of images generated by the proposed method and baselines, evaluating them on 'stylization effects and content structures'.
tasks.origin_paper: Deng et al., 2022 (Stytr2); Sohn et al., 2023 (StyleDrop)
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise preference votes on stylization effects and content structures

benchmarks.name: Combination of Two Styles
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Demonstrates a creative capability of combining two distinct artistic styles in a single image generation task, which is an open-ended creative process.

tasks.name: Two-Style Combination Generation
tasks.description: The model generates a single image that combines two different reference styles, with controllable mixing ratios for the style noise and text prompts.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative visual assessment of the combined style effect (no formal scores reported).

title: PersonaVlog: Personalized Multimodal Vlog Generation with Multi-Agent Collaboration and Iterative Self-Correction

benchmarks.name: ThemeVlogEval
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, comprehensive benchmark introduced by the paper for evaluating personalized, theme-driven Vlog generation, a creative task. It includes a dataset and multi-faceted evaluation metrics for storyboards, images, and videos.

tasks.name: Storyboard Evaluation
tasks.description: Generating a text-based storyboard from a theme and evaluating its quality based on story interest, temporal continuity, behavioral diversity, and thematic consistency.
tasks.model_type_notes: The overall framework is multimodal, involving MLLMs and various generative models. Baselines are also multimodal systems.
tasks.scoring_detail: MLLM scores (1-5) for Story Interest (SI), Temporal Continuity (TC), Behavioral Diversity (BD), and Thematic Consistency (ThC).

tasks.name: Keyframe Image Evaluation
tasks.description: Generating keyframe images from storyboards and a reference image, and evaluating them for semantic consistency and character consistency.
tasks.model_type_notes: The overall framework is multimodal, involving MLLMs and various generative models. Baselines are also multimodal systems.
tasks.scoring_detail: Text-Image Alignment (TIA) via average CLIP score; Character Consistency (CC) via weighted average of CLIP feature cosine similarity and Euclidean distance of character skeleton keypoints.

tasks.name: Video Evaluation
tasks.description: Generating video clips from keyframe images and video descriptions, and evaluating them on multiple quality dimensions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The overall framework is multimodal, involving MLLMs and various generative models. Baselines are also multimodal systems.
tasks.scoring_detail: Metrics include Subject Consistency (SC), Background Consistency (BC), Motion Smoothness (MS), Dynamic Degree (DyD), Aesthetic Quality (AQ), and Imaging Quality (IQ).

title: Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation

benchmarks.name: NEOCODER
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new benchmark for evaluating LLM creativity in a problem-solving context (code generation). It uses open-ended tasks with verifiable correctness and measures both convergent (correctness, constraint-following) and divergent (novelty vs. human solutions) thinking.

tasks.name: Constrained Code Generation on Codeforces Problems
tasks.description: Generate a Python code solution for a competitive programming problem from Codeforces. The task is performed at different 'states', where each state adds an additional constraint prohibiting the use of a specific programming technique (e.g., 'for loop', 'hashmap') identified in a previous solution.
tasks.origin_paper: Codeforces is a competitive programming website, not from a specific paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: NEOGAUGE score, which combines: 1) Convergent creativity (functional correctness via unit tests and constraint adherence checked by an LLM) and 2) Divergent creativity (ratio of novel programming techniques compared to a set of human solutions, with techniques identified by an LLM). Also reports pass@1 and constraint following ratio.

title: One Joke to Rule them All? On the (Im)possibility of Generalizing Humor

benchmarks.name: Humor Transfer Learning Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Proposes and implements a new framework for systematically evaluating humor detection in LLMs, focusing on transfer learning across different humor styles. Humor detection is a creativity judgment task.

tasks.name: Amazon Questions Humor Detection
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine if a user-submitted question about a product on Amazon is humorous.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: One Liners Humor Detection
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine if a one-liner sentence is humorous.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Sarcasm Headlines Detection
tasks.description: A binary classification task to distinguish sarcastic headlines (from The Onion) from real news headlines.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Reddit Dad Jokes Humor Detection
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine if a joke from the r/dadjokes subreddit is humorous. The dataset was extended by the paper's authors who generated non-humorous examples using GPT-4 to enable binary classification.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: CFunModel: A "Funny" Language Model Capable of Chinese Humor Generation and Processing

benchmarks.name: CFunSet
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale, multi-task dataset specifically for Chinese humor generation and processing, used for both training and evaluation in the paper.

tasks.name: Humor Recognition
tasks.description: The model is tasked with determining whether a given text is humorous. The evaluation is performed on a test split of the HumorWB dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Crosstalk Response Selection
tasks.description: The model must select the most appropriate response (for either Dougen or Penggen roles) from multiple choices for a given Crosstalk script segment. The evaluation is performed on test data from the CrossDial dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Joke Generation and Continuation
tasks.description: The model generates jokes based on topics or continues a joke from a starting sentence. This is evaluated qualitatively through a case study.
tasks.origin_paper: Data is from Tieba-JokeBar and CCL2019-Chinese-Humor-Computation, but the evaluation setup (case study) is specific to this paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative evaluation via case study

tasks.name: Crosstalk Generation and Continuation
tasks.description: The model generates or continues a crosstalk script based on a theme or a given segment. This is evaluated qualitatively through a case study.
tasks.origin_paper: Data is from Chinese-Humor-Sentiment and Crosstalk-Generation datasets, but the evaluation setup (case study) is specific to this paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative evaluation via case study

title: FutureGen: A RAG-based Approach to Generate the Future Work of Scientific Article

benchmarks.name: FutureGen
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset and framework for generating future research directions from scientific papers, a task involving creative ideation, divergent thinking, and novelty evaluation.

tasks.name: Future Work Generation
tasks.description: Generating a 'Future Work' section for a scientific article based on its content, with and without a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include BART, T5, LLaMA 3.1, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4o mini.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: ROUGE, BERTScore, Jaccard Similarity, Cosine Similarity, BLEU. LLM Judge: Coherence, Relevance, Readability, Grammar, Overall Impression, Novelty, Hallucination, Feasibility. Human: Alignment with ground truth, quality improvement from feedback.

tasks.name: LLM-as-Judge Evaluation Suite
tasks.description: A suite of evaluation tasks where an LLM assesses the quality of generated 'Future Work' sections on multiple criteria, including novelty, hallucination, and feasibility.
tasks.origin_paper: Cites prior work on LLM judgments, such as Chiang & Lee (2023) and Nguyen et al. (2024).
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o mini used as primary judge; LLaMA 3 70B and LLaMA 3 8B also tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Outputs ratings for Coherence (1-5), Relevance (1-5), Readability (1-5), Grammar (1-5), Overall Impression (1-5), Novelty (0-10), Hallucination (NLI-based classification), and Feasibility (binary 'feasible'/'not feasible').

tasks.name: Future Work Extraction
tasks.description: An auxiliary task to create the ground truth dataset by extracting 'Future Work' sentences from scientific papers, using an LLM to refine the output from a rule-based tool.
tasks.task_type_notes: Data extraction and refinement task used for dataset creation.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o mini was used as the extractor.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore, Jaccard/Cosine Similarity) comparing LLM-extracted vs. tool-extracted text. Human evaluation of faithfulness (checking for hallucination/new content).

title: Deep Associations, High Creativity: A Simple yet Effective Metric for Evaluating Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: PACE (Parallel Association Chain Evaluation)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces this new benchmark specifically to evaluate the associative creativity of LLMs using an open-ended word association generation task. It reports empirical results for 30+ models.

tasks.name: Parallel Word Association Chain Generation
tasks.description: For each of 110 seed words from the Intercontinental Dictionary Series, LLMs generate three independent 20-word association chains. The creativity score is derived from the semantic distance within these chains.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean association distance, calculated using cosine distance from FastText word embeddings.

tasks.name: Human-Model Associative Creativity Comparison
tasks.description: LLMs generate association chains for 6 specific seed words (bear, table, candle, snow, paper, toaster) to enable direct comparison with human performance data from a prior study.
tasks.scoring_detail: Association Distance, Concreteness scores, LLM-classified association types (syntagmatic, paradigmatic, etc.), Type-Token Ratio (TTR).

benchmarks.name: Chatbot Arena
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used only for correlation analysis. The paper does not run the benchmark tasks, but uses its published rankings (both overall and for creative writing) to validate the PACE metric. It is a general LLM benchmark based on human preference.

tasks.name: Arena All / Arena Creative Writing (CW) Ranking Comparison
tasks.description: The paper uses the overall (Arena All) and creative writing (Arena CW) rankings from the Chatbot Arena leaderboard to calculate Spearman correlation with its own PACE rankings.
tasks.task_type_notes: The paper uses pre-existing rankings from this benchmark for a correlation analysis; it does not run the evaluation tasks itself.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human preference voting (Elo rating).

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used only for correlation analysis. It is a closed-ended, multi-task language understanding benchmark, not focused on creativity. The paper uses its rankings to validate PACE.

tasks.name: MMLU-Pro Ranking Comparison
tasks.description: The paper uses the rankings from the MMLU-Pro benchmark to calculate Spearman correlation with PACE rankings.
tasks.task_type_notes: The paper uses pre-existing rankings from this benchmark for a correlation analysis; it does not run the evaluation tasks itself.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy on multiple-choice questions.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used only for correlation analysis. It is a general capabilities benchmark, not specifically focused on creativity. The paper uses its rankings to validate PACE.

tasks.name: LiveBench Ranking Comparison
tasks.description: The paper uses the rankings from the LiveBench benchmark to calculate Spearman correlation with PACE rankings.
tasks.task_type_notes: The paper uses pre-existing rankings from this benchmark for a correlation analysis; it does not run the evaluation tasks itself.
tasks.scoring_detail: The paper does not specify the scoring method for LiveBench.

benchmarks.name: EQ-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used only for correlation analysis. The paper uses the creative writing leaderboard from this benchmark to validate PACE, but does not run the tasks itself.

tasks.name: EQ-Bench Creative Writing Ranking Comparison
tasks.description: The paper uses the rankings from the EQ-Bench creative writing leaderboard to calculate Spearman correlation with PACE rankings.
tasks.task_type_notes: The paper uses pre-existing rankings from this benchmark for a correlation analysis; it does not run the evaluation tasks itself.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-as-judge scoring.

title: Idea-2-3D: Collaborative LMM Agents Enable 3D Model Generation from Interleaved Multimodal Inputs

benchmarks.name: Eval3DAIGC-198
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset for generating 3D models from creative, abstract, multimodal user prompts (IDEAs), which is an open-ended creative task. The paper uses this dataset to evaluate its proposed AI system.

tasks.name: Quantitative 3D Model Generation
tasks.description: Generate a 3D model from a multimodal IDEA (text, image, 3D model) and evaluate its alignment with a ground truth text description using automated metrics.
tasks.model_type_notes: The system uses a combination of LMMs (e.g., GPT-4o, InternVL2.5), Text-to-Image models (e.g., FLUX, SDXL), and Image-to-3D models (e.g., InstantMesh, Hunyuan3D).
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIP similarity, ULIP-2 similarity

tasks.name: Human Preference and Compliance Study
tasks.description: Generate 3D models from multimodal IDEAs. Human participants then evaluate which model output is better and whether the generated model satisfies the input IDEA.
tasks.model_type_notes: The system uses a combination of LMMs (e.g., GPT-4V, LLaVA), Text-to-Image models (e.g., DALL-E, SD-XL, DeepFloyd IF), and Image-to-3D models (e.g., Zero123, Wonder3D, TripoSR).
tasks.scoring_detail: User preference score (Which is better %), IDEA satisfaction rating (Satisfying IDEA %)

title: Large Language Models as Biomedical Hypothesis Generators: A Comprehensive Evaluation

benchmarks.name: LLM4BioHypoGen
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and evaluation framework for a core scientific creativity task: generating novel biomedical hypotheses with LLMs, using temporal splits to ensure novelty.

tasks.name: Hypothesis Generation
tasks.description: Large language models generate biomedical hypotheses based on provided background knowledge from scientific literature. The task is evaluated in zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned settings on both 'seen' and 'unseen' test sets based on publication date.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU, ROUGE, SelfBLEU, GPT-4 ratings (Novelty, Relevance, Significance, Verifiability on a 0-3 scale), Human ratings (Novelty, Relevance, Significance, Verifiability on a 0-3 scale)

tasks.name: Multi-agent Hypothesis Generation
tasks.description: A multi-agent framework with distinct roles (Analyst, Engineer, Scientist, Critic) and optional tool use (PubMed search) collaborates to generate biomedical hypotheses from background knowledge.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU, ROUGE, GPT-4 ratings (Novelty, Relevance, Significance, Verifiability)

title: IRFL: Image Recognition of Figurative Language

benchmarks.name: Image Recognition of Figurative Language (IRFL)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for evaluating AI's ability to understand figurative language (metaphors, idioms, similes) in a multimodal context, which is a key aspect of abstract and creative reasoning.

tasks.name: Multimodal Figurative Language Detection Task
tasks.description: Given a figurative phrase (idiom, metaphor, or simile) and four candidate images, the model must select the image that best visualizes the figurative meaning of the phrase.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (percentage of instances annotated correctly)

tasks.name: Multimodal Figurative Language Retrieval Task
tasks.description: Given a figurative phrase and a set of images (some figurative, some partially literal), the model must rank the figurative images higher than the partially literal ones.
tasks.scoring_detail: mean precision at k (where k is the number of figurative images)

tasks.name: Figurative Image Generation
tasks.description: Generative models are prompted with idioms and their definitions to assess their ability to generate figurative, rather than literal, images.
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage of generated images classified by humans into categories (Figurative, Literal, etc.)

title: PoetryDiffusion: Towards Joint Semantic and Metrical Manipulation in Poetry Generation

benchmarks.name: Sonnet Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The task involves generating sonnets, a form of creative poetry. The evaluation uses a combination of standard NLP metrics, specific poetic structural metrics (format, rhyme), and human judgments of poetic quality, making it a clear benchmark for creative text generation.

tasks.name: Sonnet Generation
tasks.description: Generating 14-line English sonnets that adhere to specific format (line count) and rhyme schemes.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include SeqGAN, MRCG, SongNet, GPT3, ChatGPT, Llama2-70B-chat, and the proposed PoetryDiffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: BLEU, ROUGE, Distinct, Perplexity (PPL), Format accuracy (line count = 14), Rhyme accuracy (matching classic schemes). Human: Fluency, Coherence, Meaningfulness, Poeticness (1-5 scale).

benchmarks.name: SongCi Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The task involves generating Chinese SongCi poetry, which requires adherence to strict metrical rules (format, rhyme, tone). This is a challenging creative generation task evaluated with both automatic and human methods.

tasks.name: SongCi Generation
tasks.description: Generating Chinese SongCi poetry that adheres to metrical structures designated by its CiPai (title), including format, rhyme, and tone rules.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include SeqGAN, MRCG, SongNet, GPT3, ChatGPT, Llama2-70B-chat, and the proposed PoetryDiffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: BLEU, ROUGE, Distinct, Perplexity (PPL), Format accuracy (symbol type), Rhyme accuracy, Tone accuracy. Human: Fluency, Coherence, Meaningfulness, Poeticness (1-5 scale).

title: FigCLIP: A Generative Multimodal Model with Bidirectional Cross-attention for Understanding Figurative Language via Visual Entailment

benchmarks.name: FigLang-2024 Multimodal Figurative Language Shared Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark evaluates a model's ability to understand figurative language (metaphors, irony, humor) in a multimodal context (image+text), requiring both classification and open-ended generation of explanations.
benchmarks.origin_name: FigLang-2024 Multimodal Figurative Language Shared Task

tasks.name: Understanding of Figurative Language Through Visual Entailment
tasks.description: Given an image-text pair, the model must 1) classify whether the image entails or contradicts the text (a 'claim'), and 2) generate a natural language explanation for the decision. The evaluation is performed on the V-FLUTE dataset.
tasks.origin_name: Understanding of Figurative Language Through Visual Entailment
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves both binary classification (entailment/contradiction) and text generation (explanation).
tasks.scoring_detail: F1, F1@50, F1@60. F1@50 and F1@60 are F1 scores where correct predictions also require the generated explanation to have a BERTscore above 50 or 60, respectively, compared to a reference explanation.

title: CHIMERA: A Knowledge Base of Scientific Idea Recombinations for Research Analysis and Ideation

benchmarks.name: Recombination Extraction
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new information extraction benchmark for identifying idea recombinations (blends and inspirations) in scientific text, a form of creative ideation. It involves open-ended span extraction and reports empirical results for LLMs.

tasks.name: Abstract Classification
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine if a scientific abstract discusses a recombination of ideas (either a blend or an inspiration).
tasks.scoring_detail: Precision, Recall, F1

tasks.name: Entity Extraction
tasks.description: Extract the text spans representing the scientific concepts involved in a recombination (e.g., combination-elements, inspiration-source, inspiration-target).
tasks.scoring_detail: Soft matching of entities judged by GPT-4o-mini for semantic similarity, followed by Precision, Recall, F1 calculation.

tasks.name: Relation Extraction
tasks.description: Extract the full recombination, including the type (blend or inspiration) and the constituent entities, forming a complete relation tuple.
tasks.scoring_detail: Partial matching of relations based on correctly matched entities (judged by GPT-4o-mini), followed by Precision, Recall, F1 calculation.

benchmarks.name: Recombination Prediction
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new generative task for scientific ideation where models predict novel concept combinations or inspirations for a given research problem. It is an open-ended creative task evaluated with both automatic metrics and human judgment.

tasks.name: Recombination Prediction (Retrieval Evaluation)
tasks.description: Given a research context and a scientific concept, retrieve a ranked list of candidate concepts to form a plausible recombination. Performance is measured against a ground-truth concept from the CHIMERA knowledge base.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests encoder-based retrievers and an LLM-based reranker (RankGPT with GPT-4o).
tasks.scoring_detail: H@3, H@5, H@10, H@50, H@100, MRR, MedR (Median Rank)

tasks.name: Recombination Prediction (Human Evaluation)
tasks.description: Human researchers rank AI-generated recombination suggestions based on their helpfulness in inspiring interesting ideas for a given research query.
tasks.scoring_detail: Median and mean rank of helpfulness assigned by researchers.

title: GraphEval: A Lightweight Graph-Based LLM Framework for Idea Evaluation

benchmarks.name: ICLR Papers
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset for evaluating AI systems on the task of assessing research paper quality, which is a form of expert-level creative judgment.

tasks.name: Research Idea Evaluation
tasks.description: Classifying paper abstracts into one of four review decisions: Reject, Accept (Poster), Accept (Oral), or Accept (Spotlight).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various LLM prompting strategies, a fine-tuned BERT model, and their proposed GNN-based methods (GraphEval-LP and GraphEval-GNN).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro F1 score, normed token cost

tasks.name: Novelty Assessment
tasks.description: Evaluating the model's ability to detect and down-score artificially constructed plagiarized or derivative ideas based on the ICLR Papers dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: This task specifically evaluates the GraphEval-GNN model with and without its novelty assessment feature.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 Score

benchmarks.name: AI Researcher Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A reused dataset for evaluating AI systems on the task of assessing research paper quality, a form of expert-level creative judgment.

tasks.name: Research Idea Evaluation
tasks.description: Classifying paper abstracts into three review decisions. The original 'Accept (Oral)' and 'Accept (Spotlight)' labels are combined into a single class.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various LLM prompting strategies, a fine-tuned BERT model, and their proposed GNN-based methods (GraphEval-LP and GraphEval-GNN).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro F1 score, normed token cost

benchmarks.name: FActScore
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a fact verification benchmark, not a creativity benchmark. It evaluates if generated text is supported by source material, which is a closed-ended task focused on correctness.

tasks.name: Long Form Text Evaluation (Fact Verification)
tasks.description: Predicting whether 'atomic facts' generated by LLMs about celebrities are supported by provided source materials.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests Prompted LLMs, Finetuned-Bert, and their GraphEval methods.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Macro Precision, Macro Recall, Macro F1 Score

benchmarks.name: ASAP-Review
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A large-scale dataset of peer reviews used to evaluate AI systems on the task of assessing research paper quality, a form of expert-level creative judgment.

tasks.name: Large-Scale Research Idea Evaluation
tasks.description: Classifying paper abstracts from a large dataset (ICLR and NeurIPS papers) into review decisions. For NeurIPS papers without specific labels, a default 'Accept (Poster)' label was assigned.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests Prompted LLMs, Finetuned-Bert, and their GraphEval-GNN method.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Macro Precision, Macro Recall, Macro F1 Score

benchmarks.name: Viewpoint Accuracy Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is an internal validation task to measure the factual consistency of an intermediate component ('viewpoints') against the source text, not a benchmark for end-to-end creativity.

tasks.name: LLM-based Consistency Evaluation
tasks.description: A large LLM (LLaMa-3.1 405b) is used as a judge to assess whether viewpoints extracted by the system are consistent with the original paper abstract.
tasks.model_type_notes: LLaMa-3.1 (405b) is used as the evaluator.
tasks.scoring_detail: Consistency rate

tasks.name: Entity-level Factual Consistency
tasks.description: Measuring the entity-level factual consistency between the aggregated viewpoints and the original idea using metrics from prior work.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task evaluates the output of the viewpoint extraction component of the GraphEval framework.
tasks.model_type_notes: This is a metric applied to the output of the viewpoint extraction process, not a direct evaluation of a generative or evaluative model.
tasks.scoring_detail: Entity-level Precision, Recall, and F1 Score

title: TIGeR: Unifying Text-to-Image Generation and Retrieval with Large Multimodal Models

benchmarks.name: TIGeR-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark with a 'Creative Domain' subset focused on generating novel, counterfactual, and imaginative images, which directly evaluates AI creativity through generation and retrieval tasks.

tasks.name: Unified Text-to-Image Generation and Retrieval
tasks.description: Given a text prompt from creative or knowledge-intensive domains, the model must autonomously decide whether to generate a new image or retrieve an existing one from a database, and output the best-matched result.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves generation, retrieval, and an autonomous decision-making step to select the final output.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares LMMs (SEED-LLaMA, LaVIT, GILL) and agent-based methods using diffusion models (SDXL) and retrieval models (CLIP).
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIP-T score, CLIP-I score

tasks.name: Text-to-Image Generation
tasks.description: Models are evaluated solely on their ability to generate images from text prompts from the TIGeR-Bench dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares diffusion models (SDXL) and LMMs (GILL, Emu, DreamLLM, SEED-LLaMA, LaVIT).
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIP-T score, CLIP-I score

tasks.name: Text-to-Image Retrieval
tasks.description: Models are evaluated solely on their ability to retrieve the correct image from the TIGeR-Bench database given a text prompt.
tasks.task_type_notes: Text-to-image retrieval
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares retrieval models (CLIP), diffusion models (SDXL), and LMMs (Emu, DreamLLM, SEED-LLaMA, LaVIT, GILL).
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIP-T score, CLIP-I score, R@1, R@5, R@10

benchmarks.name: Flickr30K
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Standard text-to-image retrieval benchmark. The task is to find a pre-existing image from a fixed set, not to create novel content. It does not directly measure creativity.

tasks.name: Text-to-Image Retrieval
tasks.description: Given a text caption, retrieve the corresponding image from the Flickr30K dataset to evaluate the model's generative retrieval performance.
tasks.task_type_notes: Text-to-image retrieval
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares the proposed LMM-based method (on LaVIT, SEED-LLaMA) with a dense retrieval model (CLIP) and other generative retrieval models (GRACE, IRGen).

benchmarks.name: MS-COCO
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Standard text-to-image retrieval benchmark. The task is to find a pre-existing image from a fixed set, not to create novel content. It does not directly measure creativity.

tasks.name: Text-to-Image Retrieval
tasks.description: Given a text caption, retrieve the corresponding image from the MS-COCO dataset to evaluate the model's generative retrieval performance.
tasks.task_type_notes: Text-to-image retrieval
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares the proposed LMM-based method (on LaVIT, SEED-LLaMA) with a dense retrieval model (CLIP) and other generative retrieval models (GRACE, IRGen).

tasks.name: Text-to-Image Ranking
tasks.description: Evaluate the performance of three different likelihood-based similarity proxies by ranking images in the MS-COCO dataset against a text prompt.
tasks.task_type_notes: The LMM is used to score and rank text-image pairs.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluates SEED-LLaMA and LaVIT.

benchmarks.name: VisDial
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates image generation/acquisition in a conversational context. While generation can be creative, the benchmark's primary focus is on multi-turn dialog understanding and instruction following, not explicitly creativity.

tasks.name: Chat-to-Image Acquisition
tasks.description: In a multi-turn chat scenario, the model must acquire an appropriate image, either by generating a new one or retrieving an existing one, based on the dialog history.
tasks.task_type_notes: The method autonomously selects between generation and retrieval.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares the proposed method (on LaVIT, SEED-LLaMA) against diffusion models (GLIDE, SD-v1.5) and other LMMs (GILL).
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIP-I score

title: GuessBench: Sensemaking Multimodal Creativity in the Wild

benchmarks.name: GuessBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed to evaluate the 'sensemaking creativity' of Vision Language Models by having them guess concepts from user-generated Minecraft builds. The task is open-ended and focuses on interpreting creative expression.

tasks.name: Static Task
tasks.description: A VLM is given a single image of a completed Minecraft build and a natural language hint (e.g., word length, some letters) and must guess the concept the build represents.
