tasks.task_type_notes: The VLM's task is to understand and identify a creative concept, which is a form of evaluation or 'sensemaking'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, where the final answer is extracted from the VLM's response using GPT-4o.

tasks.name: Dynamic Task
tasks.description: A VLM is presented with a sequence of three images showing a Minecraft build becoming progressively more complete, along with corresponding hints for each of the three attempts to guess the concept.
tasks.task_type_notes: The VLM's task is to understand and identify a creative concept over several steps, which is a form of evaluation or 'sensemaking'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, where the final answer is extracted from the VLM's response using GPT-4o. A guess is marked correct for all subsequent attempts if it's correct at any stage.

tasks.name: Generative Task (Flipping the Paradigm)
tasks.description: A VLM (Gemini-2.0-Flash) is prompted to generate an image of a Minecraft build based on a given concept word, reversing the primary task of GuessBench to compare generative vs. discriminative difficulty.
tasks.model_type_notes: Specifically Gemini-2.0-Flash was used for this experiment.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human-judged accuracy based on two criteria: containing specified entities and appearing plausibly constructed in Minecraft.

benchmarks.name: MathVista
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, which is a closed-ended problem-solving task, not a creativity evaluation task. It was used for comparison and transfer learning evaluation.

tasks.name: AutoBencher Comparison Task
tasks.description: VLMs were evaluated on the MathVista benchmark to generate performance scores, which were then used as input for the AutoBencher framework to calculate the difficulty, separability, and novelty of GuessBench in comparison.
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall Accuracy

tasks.name: Transfer Learning Evaluation Task
tasks.description: The MathVista benchmark was used as a downstream test set to evaluate the performance of a VLM (Qwen2-VL-7B) after it was fine-tuned on data from GuessBench.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: HallusionBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on diagnosing visual illusion and language hallucination in VLMs, not on evaluating creativity. It was used for comparison purposes.

tasks.name: AutoBencher Comparison Task
tasks.description: VLMs were evaluated on HallusionBench to generate performance scores, which were then used as input for the AutoBencher framework to compare its metrics (difficulty, separability, novelty) against GuessBench.
tasks.scoring_detail: aAcc (overall accuracy across atomic questions)

benchmarks.name: MMBench V1.1 Test (EN)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A general-purpose multi-modal benchmark for perception and reasoning, not specifically focused on creativity. It was used for comparison purposes.

tasks.name: AutoBencher Novelty Calculation
tasks.description: VLM performance scores on MMBench were used as a prior dataset within the AutoBencher framework to calculate the 'Novelty' score of GuessBench.
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall Accuracy

benchmarks.name: AI2D (AI2 Diagrams)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A diagram understanding and question answering dataset, which is a reasoning task, not a creativity task. It was used for comparison purposes.

tasks.name: AutoBencher Novelty Calculation
tasks.description: VLM performance scores on AI2D were used as a prior dataset within the AutoBencher framework to calculate the 'Novelty' score of GuessBench.
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall Accuracy

benchmarks.name: MultiChartQA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on question answering over multiple charts, a complex reasoning task, not a creativity evaluation. It was used for transfer learning evaluation.

tasks.name: Transfer Learning Evaluation Task
tasks.description: The MultiChartQA benchmark was used as a downstream test set to evaluate the performance of a VLM (Qwen2-VL-7B) after it was fine-tuned on data from GuessBench.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: BLINK
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on fine-grained visual perception and localization, not creativity. It was used for transfer learning evaluation.

tasks.name: Transfer Learning Evaluation Task
tasks.description: The BLINK benchmark was used as a downstream test set to evaluate the performance of a VLM (Qwen2-VL-7B) after it was fine-tuned on data from GuessBench.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: ConlangCrafter: Constructing Languages with a Multi-Hop LLM Pipeline

benchmarks.name: ConlangCrafter Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new framework for evaluating the creativity of LLMs in the open-ended task of constructing novel languages, focusing on typological diversity and internal logical consistency.

tasks.name: Typological Diversity Analysis
tasks.description: Measures the typological variation across a set of generated languages. A judge LLM classifies each language against 16 features from the World Atlas of Language Structures (WALS), and diversity is calculated as the mean pairwise Hamming distance between the resulting feature vectors.
tasks.task_type_notes: An LLM judge evaluates features of languages generated by other LLMs.
tasks.model_type_notes: Generator models (DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 2.5) are evaluated by a judge LLM (OpenAI o3).
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean pairwise Hamming distance of one-hot vectors representing 16 WALS typological features, classified by a judge LLM.

tasks.name: Internal Consistency Evaluation
tasks.description: Assesses whether translations into a generated language adhere to the language's own generated rules (phonology, morphology, syntax). This is done for a fixed set of 10 test sentences.
tasks.task_type_notes: An LLM judge and a human expert evaluate the consistency of translations produced by a generator LLM.
tasks.model_type_notes: Generator models (DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 2.5) are evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM Judge: Ratio of correctly formed translations (Consistency Rate). Human Expert: Ordinal rating (0-2) for consistency; agreement with LLM judge measured by Spearman ρ and weighted κ.

title: IdeaBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Research Idea Generation

benchmarks.name: IdeaBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark system, including a dataset and evaluation framework, for assessing the creativity of LLMs in generating novel and feasible scientific research ideas.

tasks.name: Research Idea Generation
tasks.description: An LLM, profiled as a domain-specific researcher, generates novel research hypotheses based on the abstracts of provided reference papers. The quality of the generated ideas is then evaluated against the research idea from a 'target paper' using several metrics.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested models include Llama 3.1 series, Gemini series, and GPT series.
tasks.scoring_detail: Insight Score (for novelty and feasibility) calculated from GPT-4o rankings; Semantic Similarity (BERTScore F1); Idea Overlap (GPT-4o rating on a 1-10 scale).

title: Creative Painting with Latent Diffusion Models

benchmarks.name: Comparative Artistic Generation from LDM Prompts
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Qualitative evaluation of a diffusion model's ability to generate creative and artistic images, using prompts from a prior paper for direct visual comparison.
benchmarks.origin_name: Prompts from High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models paper

tasks.name: Artistic Image Generation
tasks.description: Generating images from prompts used in the original Latent Diffusion Models paper (e.g., 'a chair that looks like an octopus') to qualitatively compare the artistry of the author's retrained model against the original. The comparison is presented visually in Figure 4.
tasks.model_type_notes: A Latent Diffusion Model (Stable Diffusion v1-4) retrained on the Wikiart dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative author assessment of creativity, artistry, and inclusion of environmental and humane information based on visual inspection of generated images.

benchmarks.name: Thematic Image Generation with Prompt Extension
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Showcases a method for generating creative images from abstract, high-level themes by first extending the prompts. The evaluation is a qualitative demonstration of the model's expressiveness.

tasks.name: Image Generation from Abstract and Extended Prompts
tasks.description: Generating artistic images from a high-level abstract prompt ('urbanization of China') and several more concrete, extended versions of that prompt (e.g., 'a train runs on the snow-capped mountains...') to demonstrate the model's ability to create expressive images.
tasks.model_type_notes: A Latent Diffusion Model (Stable Diffusion v1-4) retrained on the Wikiart dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative author assessment of the expressiveness of generated images and their reflection of specific artists' styles.

title: Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Conceptual Design Generation Problems
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Uses 12 open-ended engineering design problems to prompt an LLM to generate creative solutions. The solutions are evaluated for novelty, feasibility, and usefulness by human experts and computational metrics.
benchmarks.origin_name: Design problems for generating inspirational stimuli
benchmarks.origin_paper: Goucher-Lambert, K., and Cagan, J., 2019. “Crowdsourcing inspiration: Using crowd generated inspirational stimuli to support designer ideation”

tasks.name: Conceptual Design Generation
tasks.description: An LLM (GPT-3) generates 100 textual design solutions for each of 12 design problems, using base, zero-shot, and few-shot prompting techniques. The output is compared to a baseline of crowdsourced solutions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses GPT-3 (davinci-003).
tasks.scoring_detail: The generated concepts are evaluated via human expert ratings (feasibility, novelty, usefulness) and automatic metrics (similarity via nearest generated sample, diversity via convex hull volume).

tasks.name: Expert Evaluation of Design Concepts (using CAT)
tasks.description: Two human experts rated a subset of LLM-generated and crowdsourced design solutions on a 3-point anchored scale (0-2) for feasibility, novelty, and usefulness.
tasks.origin_paper: Amabile, T. M., 1982. “Social psychology of creativity: A consensual assessment technique.”
tasks.scoring_detail: Feasibility rating (0-2), Novelty rating (0-2), Usefulness rating (0-2)

tasks.name: Similarity to Human Baseline (Nearest Generated Sample)
tasks.description: Measures the similarity between the LLM-generated solution set and a crowdsourced baseline by calculating the mean cosine similarity of the nearest neighbors in a SentenceBERT embedding space.
tasks.origin_name: mean of the nearest generated samples
tasks.origin_paper: Regenwetter, L., et al., 2023. “Beyond statistical similarity: Rethinking metrics for deep generative models in engineering design”
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean cosine similarity of nearest samples using SentenceBERT embeddings

tasks.name: Novelty/Diversity Evaluation (Convex Hull Volume)
tasks.description: Measures the novelty and diversity of a set of generated design solutions by calculating the convex hull hypervolume of their SentenceBERT embeddings.
tasks.origin_name: convex hull hypervolume of the solution sets
tasks.origin_paper: Regenwetter, L., et al., 2023. “Beyond statistical similarity: Rethinking metrics for deep generative models in engineering design”
tasks.scoring_detail: Convex hull hypervolume of SentenceBERT embeddings

title: TinyStories: How Small Can Language Models Be and Still Speak Coherent English?

benchmarks.name: TinyStories
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new synthetic dataset of short stories designed to train small language models for coherent, creative text generation. The paper's experiments are based on models trained on this dataset.

tasks.name: Model Training on TinyStories
tasks.description: The paper uses the TinyStories dataset to train small language models (1M-35M parameters) to generate coherent short stories with simple vocabulary.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a dataset used for model training, which is a prerequisite for the generation and evaluation tasks.
tasks.scoring_detail: The models are evaluated using other benchmarks after being trained on this dataset. The paper reports standard training metrics like training and evaluation loss.

benchmarks.name: TinyStories-Instruct
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new synthetic dataset of short stories paired with instructions, designed to train and evaluate instruction-following capabilities in small language models, which is a form of controllable creative generation.

tasks.name: Instruction-Following Model Training
tasks.description: A variant of the TinyStories dataset where each story is preceded by instructions (words to include, summary, features, etc.). It is used to train models for instruction-following generation.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a dataset used for model training, which is a prerequisite for the instruction-following evaluation task.
tasks.scoring_detail: The models are evaluated using the GPT-Eval framework after being trained on this dataset.

benchmarks.name: GPT-Eval
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new evaluation framework introduced in the paper that uses GPT-4 as a judge to grade generated stories on multiple dimensions, including creativity, consistency, and grammar.

tasks.name: Story Completion Evaluation
tasks.description: Models complete a story from a given prompt taken from a manually-prepared set of 50 prompts. The full story is then evaluated by GPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4 scores for grammar (1-10), creativity (1-10), and consistency (1-10), plus a guessed age group of the writer.

tasks.name: Instruction-Following Story Generation Evaluation
tasks.description: Models generate a story based on a set of instructions from an evaluation set of 50 instruction sets. The generated story is evaluated by GPT-4 against the instructions.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4 scores for grammar (1-10), creativity (1-10), consistency with instructions (1-10), and plot coherence (1-10).

benchmarks.name: Factual, Reasoning, and Consistency Prompts
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A set of manually created prompts to test models' common-sense knowledge, reasoning, and context-tracking abilities, which are crucial for coherent and creative story generation.

tasks.name: Factual Prompts
tasks.description: Models complete sentences that test their knowledge of common sense facts (e.g., 'If I throw a ball up in the air, eventually it will...').
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative assessment by authors, color-coded in tables as success (green), partial success (yellow), or failure (red).

tasks.name: Reasoning Prompts
tasks.description: Models complete sentences that require basic reasoning, such as cause and effect or elimination (e.g., 'Lily likes cats and dogs. She asked her mom for a dog and her mom said no, so instead she...').
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative assessment by authors, color-coded in tables as success (green), partial success (yellow), or failure (red).

tasks.name: Consistency (Context-Tracking) Prompts
tasks.description: Models complete sentences that test their ability to maintain coherence and continuity with the given context, such as character names and actions.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative assessment by authors, color-coded in tables as success (green), partial success (yellow), or failure (red).

benchmarks.name: Diversity and Memorization Analysis
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A quantitative method to evaluate the diversity and novelty of generated stories by measuring n-gram overlap (using Rouge scores) against the training data and other generations.

tasks.name: Quantitative Diversity Measurement
tasks.description: Models complete 100 truncated stories from the training set. The generated completions are then quantitatively analyzed for diversity and overlap with the training corpus and with each other.
tasks.scoring_detail: Rouge-2 precision score vs original story; max Rouge-2 f-measure vs other generations; k-gram frequency in training data; max Rouge-2 precision vs entire training dataset.

title: Evaluating the Creativity of LLMs in Persian Literary Text Generation

benchmarks.name: Persian Literary Creativity Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A comprehensive new framework, including a new dataset (CPers) and culturally-adapted evaluation criteria based on TTCT, for assessing LLM creativity in Persian literary text generation.

tasks.name: Persian Literary Text Generation and Evaluation
tasks.description: Six LLMs generate single-sentence literary texts in Persian for five themes (love, longing, friendship, hope, despair). The creativity of the output is evaluated using an LLM judge based on four dimensions: originality, fluency, flexibility, and elaboration.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5, GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen2.5, Gemma
tasks.scoring_detail: Claude 3.7 Sonnet ratings on a 1-5 scale for Originality, Fluency, Flexibility, and Elaboration.

tasks.name: LLM-as-Judge Validation
tasks.description: Two LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet) are evaluated on their ability to score the creativity of Persian literary texts in alignment with human judgments.
tasks.origin_paper: General concept, but paper cites Zhao et al., 2024 for a similar application with TTCT.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet
tasks.scoring_detail: Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) between LLM scores and average human scores.

tasks.name: Figure of Speech Analysis of Generated Text

tasks.name: Layout Optimization
tasks.description: An LLM optimizes a given suboptimal layout (e.g., with incorrect or missing bounding boxes) to create a more harmonious and aesthetically pleasing one.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (correctness of bounding box format) and Quality (IR score of an image generated from the planned layout).

title: Unveiling the Invisible: Captioning Videos with Metaphors

tasks.scoring_detail: Grammaticality (errors/word via LanguageTool), vocabulary diversity (distinct-2), ideation (new named entity reuse via Stanza), collaboration metrics (equality, mutuality from event logs), human survey ratings (ownership, satisfaction).

tasks.name: Title Matching

tasks.model_type_notes: Both VLMs and LLMs were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson χ² divergence from uniform distribution, distribution histograms.

tasks.scoring_detail: χ² divergence from uniform distribution, count of repeated integers, Mean Squared Error (MSE) of repetition counts vs. expected counts.

benchmarks.relevance_reason: Tests the ability to deploy unpredictable mixed strategies, a form of strategic creativity, by having models play games against a deterministic adversary.

tasks.name: Rock Paper Scissors

tasks.scoring_detail: Win/Tie/Loss rates, Net score (Wins - Losses), determinism (probability of the most probable move).

tasks.name: Hide & Seek
tasks.description: A one-vs-one version of Hide & Seek where the model chooses a hiding spot and a greedy adversary tries to find it.
tasks.scoring_detail: Win/Loss rates, Net score (rate_win - rate_loss).

tasks.scoring_detail: Contest wins based on pairwise comparisons for originality, pleasantness, and preference. Spearman rank correlation (ρ) between axes. Cohen's Kappa for inter-annotator agreement.

title: ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives

tasks.name: Analogical Narrative Selection
tasks.description: A binary question-answering task where a model is given a query narrative and two candidate narratives. The model must select the candidate that is truly analogous (shares a 'system mapping' or high-level message) versus a distractor narrative. The benchmark is partitioned into four categories based on the semantic distance (near/far) of the analogy and the distractor.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: MATDESIGN
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A novel benchmark for evaluating the ability of LLMs to generate creative and scientifically plausible hypotheses for materials discovery, which is an open-ended, divergent thinking task. It explicitly measures novelty and innovation.

tasks.name: Hypothesis Generation for Materials Discovery and Design
tasks.description: Given a goal statement and a set of constraints from a recent materials science research paper, the task is for an LLM agent to generate multiple novel hypotheses detailing materials and methods to achieve the specified goal.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM (OpenAI-o1-preview) and human expert ratings on two primary metrics: Closeness (Concept Overlap, Property Overlap, Keyword Matching) and Quality (Alignment, Scientific Plausibility, Innovation & Novelty, Testability, Feasibility & Scalability, Impact Potential), each on a 1-5 scale.

title: Mind the Blind Spots: A Focus-Level Evaluation Framework for LLM Reviews

benchmarks.name: Focus-Level Evaluation Framework for LLM Reviews
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new framework and dataset for evaluating LLM-generated scientific peer reviews, with a specific focus on assessing critical facets like 'novelty' and 'impact', which are key components of originality and creative assessment.

tasks.name: Peer Review Generation and Focus Analysis
tasks.description: LLMs generate peer reviews for scientific papers. The generated reviews are analyzed by extracting strengths/weaknesses, annotating them with 'target' (e.g., Method, Experiment) and 'aspect' (e.g., Novelty, Validity) facets, and comparing the distribution of these facets ('focus') against human expert reviews.
tasks.scoring_detail: Focus Similarity (Kullback-Leibler Divergence, F1 score on facet pairs) using an LLM annotator, and Text Similarity (ROUGE-L, BERTScore, BLEU-4).

title: PopBlends: Strategies for Conceptual Blending with Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: PopBlends Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new evaluation framework for an LLM-based system designed to support conceptual blending, a form of combinatorial creativity. The evaluation involves both automated generation of creative connections and human judgment of their quality and utility.

tasks.name: Connecting Concept Relevance Annotation
tasks.description: The system generates 'connecting concepts' to link a pop culture domain and a product using three different strategies (No-GPT, Half-GPT, Full-GPT). Human annotators then evaluate whether the generated concepts are relevant to both the pop culture and product domains.
tasks.task_type_notes: The system generates concepts, which are then evaluated by humans.
tasks.model_type_notes: The evaluation compares three strategies, two of which use GPT-3.
tasks.scoring_detail: Binary relevance rating (True/False) for connection to pop culture and product domains; success rate.

tasks.name: Entity Attribute Relevance Annotation
tasks.description: To evaluate a component of the 'Half-GPT' strategy, GPT-3 generates entity attributes (activities, adjectives, catchphrases) for pop culture entities. Human annotators rate how many of the generated attributes are relevant to the given entity.
tasks.task_type_notes: The system generates attributes, which are then evaluated by humans.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3 is used for generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Relevance rating on a 0-5 scale (count of relevant items out of 5).

tasks.name: Scene Relevance Annotation
tasks.description: The system retrieves (from Wikipedia) or generates (with GPT-3) scenes related to a connecting concept for both the pop culture and product domains. Human annotators evaluate if the scenes are relevant to the connecting concept.
tasks.task_type_notes: The system generates/retrieves scenes, which are then evaluated by humans.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3 is used for generating product-related scenes.
tasks.scoring_detail: Binary relevance rating (True/False) for scene's relation to the connecting concept.

tasks.name: User Study on Pop Culture Blend Ideation
tasks.description: A within-subjects user study where participants use the PopBlends system versus a baseline (internet search) to ideate pop culture blends. The number of ideas generated and the perceived mental workload (NASA-TLX) are measured.
tasks.task_type_notes: The system's task is to generate creative stimuli to aid human users in their generation task.
tasks.model_type_notes: The PopBlends system is powered by GPT-3.
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of ideas generated, NASA-TLX scores (mental demand, effort, performance, etc.), qualitative interview feedback.

title: Do LLMs Plan Like Human Writers? Comparing Journalist Coverage of Press Releases with LLMs

benchmarks.name: PressRelease Creative Planning Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new large-scale dataset and evaluation framework for creative planning in journalism, comparing LLM-generated story angles and sources against those used by human journalists and evaluating creativity with human experts.

tasks.name: Contrastive Summarization Detection
tasks.description: A classification task to identify news articles that both substantially cover (contextualize) and challenge (contradict) a source press release. This is used to filter for examples of 'effective coverage' for the main evaluation.
tasks.task_type_notes: Binary classification task to determine if a news article is a 'contrastive summary' of a press release.
tasks.model_type_notes: Logistic Regression, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and a binned-MLP, using features from sentence-level NLI models.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1-score on a human-annotated test set.

tasks.name: Angle Suggestion
tasks.description: Given a press release, an LLM generates potential 'angles' (specific perspectives or story directions) a journalist could take to cover it critically. The suggestions are compared to the angles taken by human journalists.
tasks.scoring_detail: Alignment with human journalist's angle (Precision, Recall, F1) measured via GPT-4 judge; Creativity rating (1-5 scale) from human journalists.

tasks.name: Source Suggestion
tasks.description: Given a press release, an LLM generates suggestions for types of informational sources (e.g., 'an industry expert', 'a former employee') a journalist could consult. The suggestions are compared to sources used by human journalists.
tasks.scoring_detail: Alignment with human journalist's sources (Precision, Recall, F1) measured via GPT-4 judge; Creativity rating (1-5 scale) from human journalists.

title: Death of the Novel(ty): Beyond n-Gram Novelty as a Metric for Textual Creativity

benchmarks.name: Close Reading Annotation Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and annotation scheme created specifically to evaluate textual creativity (novelty, sensicality, pragmaticality) of AI-generated text using expert human annotators. It forms the basis for the paper's primary experiments.

tasks.name: Novel Expression Identification
tasks.description: Given a passage, an LLM must extract expressions that are novel (unusual, surprising, or original). The LLM's output is compared against a ground truth of expressions identified by expert human writers.
tasks.task_type_notes: The LLM acts as a judge to identify creative expressions.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested zero-shot, few-shot (GPT-5, Claude 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro) and finetuned models (GPT-4.1 FT, Llama-3.1 8B FT, Qwen-3 8B FT, OLMo-2 7B FT).
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score based on approximate string matching (Levenstein ratio ≥90% or subset/superset) against human annotations.

tasks.name: Non-pragmatic Expression Identification
tasks.description: Given a passage, an LLM must extract expressions that do not make sense contextually or flow naturally. The LLM's output is compared against a ground truth of expressions identified by expert human writers.
tasks.task_type_notes: The LLM acts as a judge to identify writing flaws.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested zero-shot, few-shot (GPT-5, Claude 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro) and finetuned models (GPT-4.1 FT, Llama-3.1 8B FT, Qwen-3 8B FT, OLMo-2 7B FT).
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score based on approximate string matching (Levenstein ratio ≥90% or subset/superset) against human annotations.

benchmarks.name: Style Mimic
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An existing dataset of expert writer preferences comparing human vs. LLM creative writing (imitations of famous authors). It is used here to validate the paper's LLM-as-a-judge approach.

tasks.name: Expert Preference Alignment
tasks.description: An LLM-as-a-judge (few-shot GPT-5) scores passages from the Style Mimic dataset for novelty and non-pragmaticality. These scores are then tested for their ability to predict the original expert preference labels in the dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates how well an LLM judge's creativity scores align with human expert preferences.
tasks.model_type_notes: Few-shot GPT-5 was used as the judge.
tasks.scoring_detail: Hierarchical logistic regression predicting human preference from LLM-judged novelty/pragmaticality scores (β, SE, OR, p-value).

benchmarks.name: LMArena dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An existing dataset of crowd-sourced preferences on writing quality. It is used here to validate the paper's LLM-as-a-judge approach against crowd preferences.

tasks.name: Crowd Preference Alignment
tasks.description: An LLM-as-a-judge (few-shot GPT-5) scores passages from the LMArena dataset for novelty and non-pragmaticality. These scores are then tested for their ability to predict the original crowd preference labels in the dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates how well an LLM judge's creativity scores align with crowd preferences.
tasks.model_type_notes: Few-shot GPT-5 was used as the judge.
tasks.scoring_detail: Logistic regression predicting crowd preference from LLM-judged novelty/pragmaticality scores (β, SE, OR, p-value).

benchmarks.name: CREATIVITY INDEX
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An existing metric for linguistic creativity, based heavily on n-gram novelty. It is used as a baseline to compare against the paper's proposed LLM-as-a-judge method.

tasks.name: Expert Preference Alignment (Comparison)
tasks.description: The CREATIVITY INDEX metric is calculated for passages from the Style Mimic dataset. The resulting scores are tested for their ability to predict the original expert preference labels, serving as a baseline comparison against the paper's LLM-judge novelty scores.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task uses an existing automatic metric to evaluate text and compares its predictive power to the paper's method.
tasks.model_type_notes: The texts being evaluated are from the Style Mimic dataset, which contains LLM generations.
tasks.scoring_detail: Logistic regression predicting human preference from CREATIVITY INDEX scores (β, SE, OR, p-value), and AIC for model comparison.

title: Creation-MMBench: Assessing Context-Aware Creative Intelligence in MLLM

benchmarks.name: Creation-MMBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed to evaluate the creative capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in real-world, image-based, open-ended tasks.

tasks.name: Context-Aware Creative Generation
tasks.description: MLLMs perform 765 test cases across 51 fine-grained creative tasks (categorized into Literary Writing, Common Functional Writing, Professional Functional Writing, and Creative Multimodal Understanding) based on one or more images and detailed textual prompts specifying a role, background, and instructions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper refers to them as MLLMs (Multimodal Large Language Models).
tasks.scoring_detail: Visual Factuality Score (VFS) from GPT-4o judge (1-10 scale); Reward score from pairwise comparison against a baseline by GPT-4o judge (-100 to +100); Human preference validation on a subset.

benchmarks.name: Creation-MMBench-TO
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A text-only variant of a creativity benchmark used to evaluate LLMs and analyze the impact of visual instruction tuning on MLLMs' creative abilities.

tasks.name: Text-Only Creative Generation
tasks.description: A text-only version of Creation-MMBench where models generate creative responses based on textual prompts and GPT-4o-generated image descriptions instead of actual images. This is used to evaluate both LLMs and MLLMs.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests both LLMs and MLLMs (VLMs) on this text-only benchmark to compare their performance.
tasks.scoring_detail: Visual Factuality Score (VFS) and Reward score from GPT-4o judge.

title: “A good pun is its own reword”: Can Large Language Models Understand Puns?

benchmarks.name: Pun Understanding Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Systematically evaluates LLMs on the creative and humorous task of understanding puns through recognition, explanation, and generation, using both automatic metrics and human judgment.

tasks.name: Pun Recognition
tasks.description: LLMs must determine if a given text is a pun or a non-pun. The evaluation uses dual-biased prompts (leaning towards 'pun' or 'non-pun') to test model confidence and consistency.
tasks.origin_paper: Zou and Lu, 2019; Zhou et al., 2020
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is a binary classification of text.
tasks.scoring_detail: True Positive Rate (TPR), True Negative Rate (TNR), Cohen’s Kappa (κ), variations in TPR/TNR under biased prompts

tasks.name: Pun Explanation
tasks.description: LLMs must generate a natural language explanation for a given pun, clarifying the pun pair (pun word, alternative word, and their senses) and the source of humor.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation (Average Mention Ratio of pun pair elements via punchline check) and LLM-as-judge (GPT-4 pairwise comparison for Win/Tie/Loss Rate).

tasks.name: Pun Generation
tasks.description: LLMs must generate a pun sentence based on a given pun pair (words and senses), either freely (free generation) or using a provided set of contextual words (constrained generation).
tasks.origin_paper: Mittal et al., 2022; Tian et al., 2022
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics (Ambiguity, Distinctiveness, Surprise, Incorporation Rates, Overlap for originality) and human evaluation (Success Rate, Funniness Rating 1-5).

title: MacGyver: Are Large Language Models Creative Problem Solvers?

benchmarks.name: MACGYVER
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset and benchmark for evaluating creative problem-solving in LLMs, focusing on unconventional object use, out-of-the-box thinking, and physical reasoning.

tasks.name: GPT-4 Zero-shot Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating the zero-shot performance of GPT-4 on the entire MACGYVER dataset (1,683 problems) to assess its baseline creative problem-solving capabilities.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4 was tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: For solvable problems: classification into 'feasible and efficient', 'feasible yet inefficient', 'infeasible', or 'wrongly says unsolvable'. For unsolvable problems: classification into 'correctly identifies unsolvable (right reason)', 'correctly identifies unsolvable (wrong reason)', or 'wrongly says solvable'.

tasks.name: Comparative Benchmarking of LLMs and Humans
tasks.description: Comparing the performance of several LLMs (PaLM2, Claude2, Llama2, GPT-3.5, GPT-4) against human participants on a representative subset of 323 problems from the MACGYVER dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested PaLM2, Claude2, Llama2-7b, Llama2-13b, Llama2-70b, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation into six fine-grained categories: A (efficient solution), B (less efficient solution), C (correctly identifies unsolvable), D (partially incorrect), E (mostly wrong), F (fail to identify solvability status).

tasks.name: Prompting Strategy Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating the effectiveness of two novel prompting strategies (Iterative Step-Wise Reflection, Divergent-Convergent Thinking) against a vanilla prompt to enhance LLM problem-solving on a subset of 180 solvable problems.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested GPT-4, Claude2, and Llama2-13b.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation of solutions into four categories: 'Efficient', 'Inefficient', 'Infeasible', 'Says Impossible'.

title: Out of Many, One: Designing and Scaffolding Proteins at the Scale of the Structural Universe with Genie 2

benchmarks.name: Unconditional Protein Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark evaluates the generation of novel and diverse protein structures, which is a creative task in structural biology. Metrics like 'Diversity' and 'Novelty' directly measure creative output.

tasks.name: Unconditional protein structure generation
tasks.description: Generating protein structures of varying lengths (50 to 500 residues) without any specific constraints, and evaluating them on designability, diversity, and novelty against known protein databases.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein diffusion models (Genie 2, Chroma, RFDiffusion, FrameFlow)
tasks.scoring_detail: Designability (scRMSD ≤ 2Å, mean pLDDT ≥ 70), Diversity (fraction of distinct clusters via TM-score), F1 score (harmonic mean of designability and diversity), PDB Novelty (TM-score vs PDB), AFDB Novelty (TM-score vs AFDB)

benchmarks.name: Single-Motif Scaffolding Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a constrained creative generation task. The goal is to design a novel protein structure (the scaffold) that correctly incorporates a predefined functional part (the motif).

tasks.name: Single-motif scaffolding
tasks.description: A set of 24 tasks where a model must generate a protein structure that incorporates a single, specific functional motif.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein diffusion models (Genie 2, RFDiffusion)
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of unique successes, where success requires designability (scRMSD ≤ 2Å, pLDDT ≥ 70, pAE ≤ 5) and motif satisfaction (backbone RMSD ≤ 1Å). Uniqueness is determined by TM-score clustering.

benchmarks.name: Multi-Motif Scaffolding Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a complex, constrained creative generation task requiring the model to design a novel protein that incorporates multiple functional motifs, often with unspecified relative positions, which is a significant creative challenge.

tasks.name: Multi-motif scaffolding (curated set)
tasks.description: A set of 6 challenging scaffolding tasks curated from the literature, each requiring the incorporation of multiple distinct functional motifs into a single protein chain.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein diffusion model (Genie 2)
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of unique successes, where success requires designability (scRMSD ≤ 2Å, pLDDT ≥ 70, pAE ≤ 5) and satisfaction of all motifs (backbone RMSD ≤ 1Å). Uniqueness is determined by TM-score clustering.

tasks.name: Multi-epitope immunogen scaffolding
tasks.description: A single task to scaffold an immunogen containing three unique epitopes from the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion protein.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein diffusion model (Genie 2)
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of successful designs based on generating a designable structure that satisfies motif constraints.

title: When to use Graphs in RAG: A Comprehensive Analysis for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

benchmarks.name: GraphRAG-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark is designed to evaluate LLM-based RAG systems and includes a specific task category for 'Creative Generation' which requires inference beyond retrieved content and generating novel scenarios.

tasks.name: Fact Retrieval
tasks.description: Requires retrieving isolated knowledge points with minimal reasoning, mainly testing precise keyword matching.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates various RAG and GraphRAG frameworks, which are LLM-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Answer Accuracy (ACC), ROUGE-L

tasks.name: Complex Reasoning
tasks.description: Requires chaining multiple knowledge points across documents via logical connections.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates various RAG and GraphRAG frameworks, which are LLM-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Answer Accuracy (ACC), ROUGE-L

tasks.name: Contextual Summarize
tasks.description: Involves synthesizing fragmented information into a coherent, structured answer, emphasizing logical coherence and context.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates various RAG and GraphRAG frameworks, which are LLM-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Answer Accuracy (ACC), Evidence Coverage (Cov)

tasks.name: Creative Generation
tasks.description: Requires inference beyond retrieved content, often involving hypothetical or novel scenarios, such as retelling a scene as a newspaper article.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates various RAG and GraphRAG frameworks, which are LLM-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Answer Accuracy (ACC), Faithfulness (FS), Evidence Coverage (Cov)

title: HumorDB: Can AI understand graphical humor?

benchmarks.name: HumorDB
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, curated dataset and evaluation framework specifically designed to test AI's ability to understand visual humor, a form of creativity. It includes controlled, minimally contrastive image pairs and reports empirical results for multiple AI systems.

tasks.name: Binary Humor Classification
tasks.description: Models perform a two-alternative forced choice classification, labeling images as either 'Funny' or 'Not Funny'.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both vision-only models (DINOv2, ViT, Swin2, ConvNeXt, ResNet152) and vision-language models (LLaVA, BLIP, GPT-4o, Gemini-Flash).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, compared against the average human-based label (threshold of 0.5).

tasks.name: Funniness Rating Prediction (Range Task)
tasks.description: Models rate the funniness of an image on a scale from 1 (Not at all funny) to 10 (Extremely funny).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both vision-only models (DINOv2, ViT, Swin2, ConvNeXt, ResNet152) and vision-language models (LLaVA, BLIP, GPT-4o, Gemini-Flash).
tasks.scoring_detail: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) between the predicted rating and the mean human rating.

tasks.name: Pairwise Humor Comparison (Comparison Task)
tasks.description: Given two side-by-side images, models must select which of the two is funnier.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both vision-only models (DINOv2, ViT, Swin2, ConvNeXt, ResNet152) and vision-language models (LLaVA, BLIP, GPT-4o, Gemini-Flash).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, computed as the fraction of pairs correctly identified compared to the majority human vote.

tasks.name: VLM Explanation Evaluation
tasks.description: Vision-Language Models generate textual explanations for why an image is funny, which are then evaluated by both humans and automated metrics.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on GPT-4o, Gemini-Flash, and LLaVA.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating (1-5 scale for identifying humor source and factual accuracy); Automated synonym matching score (All Words Score, Common Words Score).

tasks.name: Attention Map Analysis
tasks.description: An interpretability analysis to evaluate whether vision transformers focus their attention on the specific regions of an image that make it humorous.
tasks.task_type_notes: Interpretability analysis to evaluate model focus on humorous regions.
tasks.model_type_notes: Vision Transformers (ViT variants, DINOv2).
tasks.scoring_detail: Recall, Strict Box Containment (SBC), Outside Box Ratio (OBR).

tasks.name: Mechanistic Interpretability (Logit Attribution)
tasks.description: An interpretability analysis that adapts logit attribution to evaluate how each transformer layer contributes to the final humor classification.
tasks.task_type_notes: Interpretability analysis to evaluate layer-wise contribution to humor classification.
tasks.model_type_notes: Vision Transformers (ViT variants, DINOv2).
tasks.scoring_detail: Layer-wise classification accuracy.

title: Seeing the Unseen: Visual Metaphor Captioning for Videos

benchmarks.name: Video Metaphor Captioning (VMC)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new task, dataset (VMCD), and evaluation metrics (ACD, human protocol) for generating and evaluating creative visual metaphors in videos, which is an open-ended creative generation task.

tasks.name: Video Metaphor Caption Generation
tasks.description: Given a video from the newly created Video Metaphor Captioning Dataset (VMCD), the task is to generate a single-line caption describing the visual metaphor, typically following the format: ‘Primary concept’ is as ‘property’ as ‘secondary concept’.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests GIT, Valley, Video-ChatGPT, Video-LLaVa, and their own GIT-LLaVA models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Evaluated using a mix of methods: 1) Standard automatic metrics: BLEU-4, Rouge-L, CIDEr, BERT-F1. 2) A new automatic creativity metric: Average Concept Distance (ACD). 3) Human evaluation on four criteria: Fluency, Creativity, Primary Concept Consistency, and Consistency.

benchmarks.name: Metaphoric Image Captioning Pretraining
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A pretraining setup used to teach models about metaphors before the main video task. It involves generating metaphorical captions for images, which is a creative language task.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Chakrabarty et al., 2023; Lin et al., 2014

tasks.name: Image-to-Metaphor Captioning
tasks.description: During pretraining, the model learns to generate captions for images. For images from the HAIVMet dataset, it generates metaphorical captions. For images from the MSCOCO dataset, it generates standard literal captions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper's proposed GIT-LLaVA model is pretrained using this setup.
tasks.scoring_detail: This is a pretraining stage; the paper does not report evaluation metrics on this task itself, only on the downstream VMC task. Training uses cross-entropy loss.

benchmarks.name: Synthetic Metaphor Caption Generation (Ablation)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An ablation study involving a synthetically generated dataset where GPT-3.5-turbo converts literal image captions into metaphorical ones. This is used for pretraining and directly relates to creative text generation.

tasks.name: Synthetic Metaphor Pretraining
tasks.description: Pretraining a model on a synthetic dataset where literal MSCOCO captions are converted to metaphorical captions by GPT-3.5-turbo. The model learns to generate these metaphoric captions from the original images.
tasks.model_type_notes: Used in an ablation study to pretrain variants of the GIT-LLaVA model.
tasks.scoring_detail: This is a pretraining stage for an ablation study; final evaluation is performed on the VMC task. Training uses cross-entropy loss.

title: Reason-SVG: Hybrid Reward RL for Aha-Moments in Vector Graphics Generation

benchmarks.name: SVGX-DwT-10k Evaluation Set (DEval)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark for evaluating text-to-SVG generation, an open-ended creative task involving visual design, composition, and semantic interpretation. The paper provides empirical results for multiple AI systems.

tasks.name: Text-to-SVG Generation
tasks.description: Generating Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) code from a natural language text prompt. Evaluation assesses the output's structural validity, semantic alignment, visual quality, and realism, as well as the quality of an optional intermediate reasoning process (Drawing-with-Thought).
tasks.model_type_notes: Tests include proprietary LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude), open-source LLMs (DeepSeek, Qwen2.5), and optimization-based methods (VectorFusion, SVGDreamer).
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics: FID, CLIPScore, HPSv2, SVG Validity (Val%), DwT Adherence (DwT-Cover%). Human evaluation (1-5 Likert): Semantic Accuracy, Visual Appeal, DwT Quality.

title: Multimodal Knowledge Alignment with Reinforcement Learning

benchmarks.name: ESP dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate a model's ability to generate diverse, styled text (blog, social media, instruction, story, news) from a single image, directly testing creative and stylistic generation capabilities.

tasks.name: Diverse Styled Caption Generation
tasks.description: Generate captions for an image in five different styles: blog, social media, instruction, story, and news, based on a textual style prompt.
tasks.model_type_notes: The ESPER model adapts a frozen LLM (GPT-2) to accept visual inputs.
tasks.scoring_detail: CIDEr score; Human evaluation on a 5-point Likert scale for visual relevance, informativeness, and fluency.

benchmarks.name: COCO Captions
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Standard image captioning benchmark used for zero-shot and finetuning generation tasks. The zero-shot 'unpaired' setting requires creative alignment between modalities without direct supervision.
benchmarks.origin_name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context

tasks.name: Unpaired Image Captioning
tasks.description: Generate a descriptive caption for an image from the COCO test split without being trained on paired image-caption data.
tasks.origin_paper: Feng et al., 2019; Laina et al., 2019
tasks.model_type_notes: The ESPER model adapts a frozen LLM (GPT-2) to accept visual inputs.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, METEOR, CIDEr

tasks.name: Supervised Image Captioning (Finetuning)
tasks.description: Finetune the model on paired COCO image-caption data to evaluate the quality of the RL-trained encoder as a pretrained weight initialization.
tasks.model_type_notes: The ESPER model adapts a frozen LLM (GPT-2) to accept visual inputs.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, METEOR, CIDEr

benchmarks.name: AudioCaps
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Audio captioning benchmark used in an unpaired setting to evaluate the model's ability to generate descriptive text from audio inputs, a cross-modal creative generation task.
benchmarks.origin_name: AudioCaps: Generating captions for audios in the wild

tasks.name: Unpaired Audio Captioning
tasks.description: Generate a descriptive caption for an audio clip from the AudioCaps test split without being trained on paired audio-caption data.
tasks.model_type_notes: Audio-adapted LLM (GPT-2 backbone with Wav2CLIP for audio features).
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, METEOR, CIDEr

benchmarks.name: VisualNews
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The task requires generating news-style captions that explain an image's relevance to a news story, which goes beyond literal description to contextual and narrative generation.
benchmarks.origin_name: Visual News: Benchmark and challenges in news image captioning

tasks.name: Visual News Captioning
tasks.description: Generate a news-style caption for an image that describes its relevance to a news article, not just its literal content.
tasks.model_type_notes: The ESPER model adapts a frozen LLM (GPT-2) to accept visual inputs.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, METEOR, CIDEr

benchmarks.name: VisDial
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates a model's ability to understand an image-grounded dialogue by ranking candidate answers. This tests contextual and conversational reasoning, which is a component of creative interaction.

tasks.name: Visual Dialogue Answer Ranking
tasks.description: Given an image and a dialogue history (question), rank 100 candidate answers by their likelihood.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model's task is to rank provided answer candidates, not generate new ones.
tasks.model_type_notes: The ESPER model adapts a frozen LLM (GPT-2) to accept visual inputs.
tasks.scoring_detail: NDCG, MRR, R@1

title: One Does Not Simply Meme Alone: Evaluating Co-Creativity Between LLMs and Humans in the Generation of Humor

benchmarks.name: Co-Creative Meme Generation and Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new user study to evaluate the co-creativity of LLMs and humans in the open-ended, humor-based task of meme generation, using human ratings for creativity, humor, and shareability.

tasks.name: Meme Caption Generation
tasks.description: In a between-subject study, three groups—human-only, human-AI collaboration (with GPT-4o), and AI-only (GPT-4o)—generated captions for popular meme templates based on given topics (work, food, sports).
tasks.model_type_notes: The study used GPT-4o.
tasks.scoring_detail: The generated memes were evaluated by human raters in a subsequent task. Process metrics like number of ideas generated and subjective workload (NASA-TLX) were also collected during this task.

tasks.name: Meme Quality Evaluation
tasks.description: A second group of human participants rated a sample of the generated memes from the three conditions (human-only, human-AI, AI-only) on three dimensions.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a human evaluation task where humans act as judges to rate the creative output from different generation conditions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The artifacts being evaluated were generated by an LLM (GPT-4o), either alone or in collaboration with a human.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings on scales for humor, creativity, and shareability.

title: LitBench: A Benchmark and Dataset for Reliable Evaluation of Creative Writing

benchmarks.name: LitBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark and dataset specifically designed for evaluating AI systems on their ability to judge the quality of creative writing, a core aspect of creativity.

tasks.name: Zero-shot LLM Judge Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating off-the-shelf LLMs as zero-shot judges on their ability to select the human-preferred story from a pair of creative writing samples from the LitBench test set.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy / Agreement with human preferences derived from Reddit upvotes.

tasks.name: Reward Model Evaluation
tasks.description: Training and evaluating Bradley-Terry (BT) and Generative Reward Models (GenRM) on the LitBench dataset to assess their ability to predict human preferences for creative writing.
tasks.task_type_notes: Models are trained on the LitBench training set and then evaluated on the test set for their judging capability.
tasks.model_type_notes: Reward models use Llama, Qwen, and Gemma backbones.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy / Agreement with human preferences derived from Reddit upvotes.

tasks.name: Human Validation of Reward Model Rankings
tasks.description: An online human study where crowd-workers evaluate pairs of LLM-generated stories that were ranked as 'best' and 'worst' by a trained reward model, to test the model's generalization to new content.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task evaluates the performance of a reward model trained on LitBench.
tasks.model_type_notes: The reward model being evaluated is a fine-tuned Llama-8B. The stories were generated by GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human preference agreement rate with the reward model's ranking.

title: SEED-Story: Multimodal Long Story Generation with Large Language Model

benchmarks.name: StoryStream
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new large-scale, high-resolution dataset of animated stories with narrative-rich text, designed specifically for training and benchmarking multimodal story generation models.

tasks.name: Multimodal Story Generation
tasks.description: Generating a sequence of consecutive storylines and corresponding images in an interleaved, auto-regressive manner, continuing from a user-provided start.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests MLLMs, specifically their SEED-Story model against MM-interleaved.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID score, GPT-4V preference ratings (Style Consistency, Story Engagement, Image-Text Coherence), and a human user study (Image Quality, Style Consistency, Diversity, Engagement, Coherence).

tasks.name: Long Story Generation with Attention Mechanisms
tasks.description: An ablation study comparing different attention mechanisms (Dense, Window, Attention Sink, Multimodal Attention Sink) for generating long multimodal stories efficiently.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests variants of its SEED-Story MLLM.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, CLIP Score, Inference Time, Memory usage.

tasks.name: Story Visualization
tasks.description: Generating the next image in a story sequence based on the current text prompt and the previous image.
tasks.origin_paper: The paper compares against models from papers like LDM (Rombach et al., 2022) and StoryGen (Liu et al., 2023a).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper adapts its SEED-Story model and compares it against diffusion models (LDM, StoryGen).
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, CLIP Score.

title: DiffDesign: Controllable diffusion with meta prior for efficient interior design generation

benchmarks.name: DesignHelper
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of interior design solutions (text descriptions, floor plans, renderings) created specifically for training and evaluating generative AI models in a creative domain.

tasks.name: Zero-shot image-text retrieval
tasks.description: Evaluating the alignment between images and text descriptions in the DesignHelper dataset using the paper's fine-tuned CLIP model.
tasks.model_type_notes: CLIP text encoder
tasks.scoring_detail: R@1, R@5, R@10 accuracy

tasks.name: Computational efficiency evaluation
tasks.description: Generating interior design images using the DesignHelper dataset to evaluate the computational efficiency (training time) of different diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Training time

benchmarks.name: Flickr
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Standard image-text dataset used to evaluate the performance of the CLIP component, not directly for creative generation evaluation.

tasks.name: Zero-shot image-text retrieval
tasks.description: Evaluating the alignment between images and text descriptions in the Flickr dataset using the paper's fine-tuned CLIP model.
tasks.model_type_notes: CLIP text encoder
tasks.scoring_detail: R@1, R@5, R@10 accuracy

benchmarks.name: MSCOCO
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Standard image-text dataset used to evaluate the performance of the CLIP component, not directly for creative generation evaluation.

tasks.name: Zero-shot image-text retrieval
tasks.description: Evaluating the alignment between images and text descriptions in the MSCOCO dataset using the paper's fine-tuned CLIP model.
tasks.model_type_notes: CLIP text encoder
tasks.scoring_detail: R@1, R@5, R@10 accuracy

benchmarks.name: English Dataset for Interior Design
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An existing dataset for interior design generation, used here for quantitative comparison of generative models on a creative task.

tasks.name: Text-to-image generation for quantitative evaluation
tasks.description: Generating interior design images from text prompts to evaluate generation quality and text-image alignment using automated metrics.
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIP Similarity (CLIP Sim), Inception Score (IS), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID)

benchmarks.name: Human Preference Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A human study designed to assess the perceptual quality and relevance of AI-generated interior designs, which is a core aspect of creativity evaluation.

tasks.name: Human rating of generated interior designs
tasks.description: 20 interior design professionals rated images generated from 20 prompts by six different models on a five-point quality scale based on design appeal, task relevance, and usability.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average preference score (5-point scale) on Design Appeal, Task Relevance, Usability; Win rate

benchmarks.name: Qualitative Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A qualitative assessment where the authors generate and visually inspect interior design images from specific text prompts to demonstrate model capabilities in a creative task.

tasks.name: Interior design generation from fixed prompts
tasks.description: Generating interior design images for five specific spaces (hotel lobby, café, study, living room, clothing store) from fixed text descriptions to visually assess generation quality and adherence to prompts.
tasks.scoring_detail: Visual inspection and comparison by authors

benchmarks.name: Ablation Study Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An evaluation using human scoring to assess the impact of different model components on the quality of generated creative content.

tasks.name: Human scoring of ablated model outputs
tasks.description: Volunteers scored generated samples from models with different components disabled (generated appearance control, design specification control, specific CLIP) to evaluate their impact on the final image.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human scores (unspecified scale)

title: Hypothesis Search: Inductive Reasoning with Language Models

benchmarks.name: Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for abstract and inductive reasoning, requiring models to infer general principles from a few visual examples. This aligns with creative problem-solving and divergent thinking.

tasks.name: Inductive Reasoning on 2D Grids
tasks.description: Given a set of input-output 2D grid pairs demonstrating a transformation rule, the model must infer the rule (by generating natural language hypotheses and then Python programs) and apply it to a novel test input grid. A random subset of 100 problems was used.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 were used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Top-1 accuracy

benchmarks.name: 1D-ARC
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A one-dimensional version of the ARC benchmark, focusing on inductive reasoning over sequences. It requires inferring abstract patterns from examples, which is a key component of creative problem-solving.

tasks.name: Inductive Reasoning on 1D Sequences
tasks.description: Given a set of input-output 1D sequence pairs, the model must infer the shared transformation rule (by generating hypotheses and programs) and apply it to a novel test input. A random subset of 108 problems was used.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 were used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: SyGuS
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A program synthesis benchmark requiring the generation of a program to explain string transformations from examples. This is a form of inductive reasoning and creative rule discovery.

tasks.name: String Transformation Program Synthesis
tasks.description: Given pairs of input-output strings, the model synthesizes a Python program that performs the demonstrated transformation. All 89 tasks from the dataset were evaluated.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 were used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (passing all examples)

benchmarks.name: List Functions
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A cognitive-science-inspired benchmark for inductive reasoning, involving the mapping of one list of numbers to another. It requires discovering underlying rules, a form of creative problem-solving.

tasks.name: List Transformation Program Synthesis
tasks.description: Given pairs of input-output lists of numbers, the model must generate a Python program that implements the underlying transformation rule. A random sample of 100 tasks was used.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 were used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: Enumerate-Conjecture-Prove: Formally Solving Answer-Construction Problems in Math Competitions

benchmarks.name: ConstructiveBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark of competition-level math problems specifically designed to test the creative task of constructing mathematical objects, which the paper frames as a creative reasoning challenge for LLMs, distinct from standard theorem-proving.

tasks.name: Formal Answer-Construction and Proving
tasks.description: Given a formal answer-construction problem in Lean, the model must first conjecture a closed-form answer and then generate a formal proof in Lean that verifies the correctness of the conjectured answer.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves both generating a candidate answer (conjecture) and then generating a proof to verify it (evaluation). The paper reports metrics for both stages: 'Answer-Construction Accuracy' and 'End-to-End Problem Solving'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Answer-construction accuracy (provable equivalence to ground truth via Lean automation tactics) and End-to-end accuracy (successful Lean verification of the generated proof, reported as Pass@32).

benchmarks.name: PutnamBench (Answer-Construction Subset)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Uses problems from the highly challenging Putnam competition, focusing on a subset that requires creative construction of mathematical solutions, a task the paper identifies as requiring creativity beyond standard logical deduction.

tasks.name: Formal Answer-Construction and Proving
tasks.description: Given a formal answer-construction problem from the PutnamBench dataset, the model must first conjecture a closed-form answer and then generate a formal proof in Lean that verifies its correctness.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves both generating a candidate answer (conjecture) and then generating a proof to verify it (evaluation). The paper reports metrics for both stages.
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of correct answer constructions (provable equivalence to ground truth via Lean automation tactics) and number of end-to-end solved problems (successful Lean verification of the generated proof, reported as Pass@32).

title: CS4: Measuring the Creativity of Large Language Models Automatically by Controlling the Number of Story-Writing Constraints

benchmarks.name: CS4 (Comparing the Skill of Creating Stories by Controlling the Synthesized Constraint Specificity)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed to evaluate the creativity of LLMs in story writing. It uses prompts with a varying number of constraints (up to 39) to hinder memorization and force novel generation, and measures performance through a suite of automated and LLM-based metrics.

tasks.name: Constrained Story Generation
tasks.description: LLMs are prompted to revise a given 'base story' to satisfy a varying number of constraints (7, 15, 23, 31, or 39) for a user instruction. The constraints are generated using two different approaches: 'instruction-based' and 'story-based'.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on LLaMA-2-7B Chat, Gemma-7B Instruct, Mistral-7B Instruct, OLMo-7B Base, OLMo-7B SFT, and OLMo-7B Instruct.
tasks.scoring_detail: The generated stories are evaluated using constraint satisfaction ratio, story quality scores (coherence, grammar, likability), output diversity metrics, and composite creativity scores.

tasks.name: Constraint Satisfaction Evaluation
tasks.description: An LLM judge evaluates whether the generated stories satisfy each individual constraint in the prompt. The final metric is the ratio of satisfied constraints.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5-Turbo is used as the evaluator.
tasks.scoring_detail: Ratio of satisfied constraints, judged by GPT-3.5-Turbo.

tasks.name: Story Quality Evaluation
tasks.description: An LLM judge evaluates the quality of generated stories via pairwise comparison against a baseline story for each user instruction. The paper focuses on coherence but also reports grammar and likeability.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 are used as evaluators.
tasks.scoring_detail: Normalized coherence, grammar, and likeability scores on a 1-5 scale.

tasks.name: Output Diversity Evaluation
tasks.description: Automated metrics are used to measure the diversity of the stories generated by the tested LLMs.
tasks.model_type_notes: Metrics are calculated on the output of the tested LLMs (LLaMA, Gemma, Mistral, OLMo).
tasks.scoring_detail: self perplexity, dist-n diversity (product of dist-2, dist-3, and dist-4).

tasks.name: Creativity Measurement
tasks.description: Two novel metrics are calculated to quantify an LLM's creativity by measuring its performance under a high number of constraints and its performance decay as constraints increase.
tasks.model_type_notes: Metrics are calculated for the tested LLMs based on their scores from other evaluation tasks.
tasks.scoring_detail: Quality Under n Constraints (QUCn), which is the product of coherence and constraint satisfaction scores; and Relative Creativity Score (RCSm,n), which is the quality difference between outputs generated with m and n constraints.

title: Getting Serious about Humor: Crafting Humor Datasets with Unfunny Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Unfun Corpus
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for evaluating the ability of systems to edit humorous text (satirical headlines) to make them non-humorous, and vice-versa. It is an open-ended generation task focused on a key aspect of creativity (humor) and reports empirical results with LLMs.

tasks.name: Unfun Generation
tasks.description: LLMs are prompted to edit existing satirical headlines from The Onion to transform them into corresponding serious, non-humorous headlines.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested: GPT-4, GPT-3.5-TURBO, MISTRAL-7B-INSTRUCT, MISTRAL-7B, and a ROBERTA-SWAP baseline.
tasks.scoring_detail: Holdout accuracy of fine-tuned humor classifiers (MISTRAL, ROBERTA), Human ratings (realness, funniness, grammaticality, coherence), Edit Distance, Type-Token Ratio (TTR).

tasks.name: Humor Generation
tasks.description: LLMs are prompted to edit serious/unfunny headlines to make them humorous or satirical. This is the reverse of the primary 'unfun' task.
tasks.origin_name: This is the reverse of the Unfun task, used for comparison.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested: GPT-4, GPT-3.5, MISTRAL-INSTRUCT, MISTRAL.
tasks.scoring_detail: Holdout accuracy of fine-tuned humor classifiers (MISTRAL, ROBERTA), Human ratings (realness, funniness), Edit Distance, Type-Token Ratio (TTR).

benchmarks.name: English-Hindi Code-Mixed Humor Dataset Unfunning
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper extends an existing humor detection dataset by applying a creative generation task (unfunning) to it. This creates a new set of paired data for a low-resource, code-mixed language setting and evaluates an LLM's performance on this creative editing task.
benchmarks.origin_name: Humor detection in english-hindi code-mixed social media content

tasks.name: English-Hindi Unfun Generation
tasks.description: GPT-4 is prompted to edit humorous code-mixed English-Hindi tweets to make them non-humorous, generalizing the 'unfun' task to a new language and domain.
tasks.model_type_notes: Model tested: GPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings (humor, coherence), Edit distance, Holdout accuracy of a fine-tuned humor classifier (XLM-ROBERTA).

tasks.name: Unfun Filtering
tasks.description: As part of the data generation pipeline, GPT-4 is used as a classifier to filter its own generated 'unfunned' tweets, removing any outputs that it still considers humorous.
tasks.model_type_notes: Model used: GPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4 classification (humorous vs. non-humorous).

title: RPGBENCH: Evaluating Large Language Models as Role-Playing Game Engines

benchmarks.name: RPGBENCH
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for evaluating LLMs as text-based role-playing game engines, focusing on the creative tasks of game world generation and interactive simulation, which are open-ended and require coherence, consistency, and creativity.

tasks.name: Game Creation (GC)
tasks.description: An LLM is prompted to create a valid and playable text-based RPG world, including characters, state variables, events, and termination conditions, based on a given fictional character's Wikipedia page. The output must conform to a specific JSON schema.
tasks.scoring_detail: Format-check pass rate (FCR), Valid-check pass rate (VCR) using a BFS Validity Checker, w. Success ratio, w. Lose ratio, Reachability ratio, CountRatio, LengthRatio.

tasks.name: Game Simulation (GS)
tasks.description: Given a valid game from the GC task, an LLM acts as a game engine to simulate interactive gameplay over multiple rounds. In each round, it generates an event plan, game narration with candidate actions for the player, and updates the game state variables.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: Narration length, Mechanic score (MEC), Event condition error rate (ECE), Variable update error rate (VUE). LLM Judge: Action Quality (ACT), Interestingness (INT), Role-Playing Factual Consistency (FAC), Role-Playing Personality Consistency (PER) via TIPI. Human: Ratings for FAC, PER, ACT, and INT on a subset of games.

title: The GPT-WritingPrompts Dataset: A Comparative Analysis of Character Portrayal in Short Stories

benchmarks.name: GPT-WritingPrompts Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset pairing human-written and LLM-generated short stories from the same creative prompts, used for comparative analysis of narrative characteristics, biases, and other creative writing attributes.

tasks.name: Comparative Analysis of Character Portrayal
tasks.description: GPT-3.5 generates short stories from Reddit WritingPrompts. These stories, alongside existing human-written ones, are then automatically analyzed to compare character portrayal along six dimensions: valence, arousal, dominance, power, appearance, and intellect.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves generating stories with an LLM and then evaluating the generated text against human-written text using a computational analysis pipeline.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo) was used for generation. Other models (SpanBERT, COMeT, word2vec) were used for the analysis pipeline.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean z-scored values for valence, arousal, dominance, power, appearance, and intellect. Scores are derived from protagonist attributes using lexicon-based methods (NRC-VAD, Fast et al.) and embedding-based methods (word2vec axis projection and cosine similarity).

title: Poetry in Pixels: Prompt Tuning for Poem Image Generation via Diffusion Models

benchmarks.name: PoemSum
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used to evaluate poem summarization and poem-to-image generation, focusing on interpreting and visualizing creative text.

tasks.name: Poem Summarization
tasks.description: Evaluating the ability of LLMs to generate concise summaries of poems from the PoemSum dataset, capturing their theme, mood, and literary devices.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested: GPT-4o mini, Pegasus, BART, T5, Falcon.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human expert ratings (+1/-1), ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, BLEU-1, BLEU-2, BLEU-3, BLEU-4, METEOR

tasks.name: Poem-to-Image Generation
tasks.description: Generating images that visually represent the interpretation, themes, and emotions of poems from the PoemSum dataset using the proposed PoemToPixel framework.
tasks.model_type_notes: The PoemToPixel pipeline uses an LLM (GPT-4o mini) and a Diffusion model (SDXL Turbo, SDXL Base 1.0).
tasks.scoring_detail: Human expert ratings (1-5 scale for alignment), Image-Text Matching Loss (ITM), Image-Text Contrastive Loss (ITC)

benchmarks.name: MiniPo
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of children's poems and corresponding images, created and used to evaluate a creative poem-to-image generation system.

tasks.name: Poem-to-Image Generation
tasks.description: Generating images that visually represent the plot and themes of children's poems from the newly introduced MiniPo dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: The PoemToPixel pipeline uses an LLM (GPT-4o mini) and a Diffusion model (SDXL Base 1.0).
tasks.scoring_detail: Image-Text Matching Loss (ITM), Image-Text Contrastive Loss (ITC)

title: CCEdit: Creative and Controllable Video Editing via Diffusion Models

benchmarks.name: BalanceCC
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark dataset introduced by the paper for evaluating generative video editing models. It focuses on both controllability and creativity, featuring 100 videos with varied prompts for style, object, and background changes, and includes a 'Fantasy Level' to rate the creative degree of the prompts.

tasks.name: Text-guided Video Editing Evaluation
tasks.description: Given an input video and a target text prompt, models generate an edited video. The experiments were conducted on a 50-video subset called mini-BalanceCC. The generated videos were evaluated by both human judges and automatic metrics.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests its CCEdit model and compares it against eight other state-of-the-art video editing methods, all based on diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human: Mean Opinion Score (MOS) on a 1-5 scale for editing accuracy, aesthetics, temporal consistency, and overall impression; side-by-side win/tie/lose percentage. Automatic: Temporal Consistency (Tem-Con), Text Alignment (Tex-Ali), and PickScore.

title: MusicLDM: Enhancing Novelty in text-to-music Generation Using Beat-Synchronous mixup Strategies

benchmarks.name: Generation Quality Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Uses standard automatic metrics for audio generation (FD, IS, KL) to measure quality and diversity, which are prerequisites for creativity but not direct measures of it.

tasks.name: Frechet Distance (FD)
tasks.description: Measures the similarity between the embedding space of generated music and groundtruth music using audio embedding models (VGGish and PANN).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: FDpann, FDvgg

tasks.name: Inception Score (IS)
tasks.description: Measures the diversity and quality of the full set of generated audio outputs.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Inception Score

tasks.name: Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence
tasks.description: Measures the divergence between individual pairs of generated and groundtruth audio samples, then averaged.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: KL Divergence

benchmarks.name: CLAP-based Novelty and Relevance Metrics
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Proposes new automatic metrics to directly measure novelty, plagiarism risk, and text-relevance of generated music, which are core aspects of creativity.

tasks.name: Text-Audio Similarity
tasks.description: Measures the relevance between a text prompt and generated audio using the cosine similarity of their CLAP embeddings.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine similarity between text and audio CLAP embeddings

tasks.name: Nearest-Neighbor Audio Similarity Ratio (SIMAA)
tasks.description: Measures novelty/plagiarism risk by calculating the fraction of generated audio samples that are highly similar (above a threshold) to their nearest neighbor in the training dataset, based on CLAP audio embeddings.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: SIMAA@90, SIMAA@95 (fraction of samples with cosine similarity > 0.90 or 0.95 to nearest training sample)

benchmarks.name: Subjective Listening Test
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Uses human evaluation to assess perceptual quality, relevance to a text prompt, and musicality of generated audio, which are key subjective dimensions of creativity.

tasks.name: Quality Rating
tasks.description: Human subjects rate the overall quality of the generated music, considering clarity, absence of noise, and general audio quality.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating (scale not specified, higher score is better)

tasks.name: Relevance Rating
