tasks.description: Human subjects rate how well the generated music matches a given textual description.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating (scale not specified, higher score is better)

tasks.name: Musicality Rating
tasks.description: Human subjects evaluate the musical attributes of the song, including rhythm, melodies, and textures.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-music latent diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating (scale not specified, higher score is better)

benchmarks.name: Zero-shot Audio Classification
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Standard audio classification tasks used to evaluate a component (CLAP model), not the creative generation task itself. Focus is on classification accuracy, not creativity.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Piczak, 2015; Salamon et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2020; Tzanetakis & Cook, 2002

tasks.name: Zero-shot classification on audio datasets
tasks.description: Zero-shot classification on benchmark datasets (ESC-50, UrbanSound 8K, VGGSound, GTZAN) to evaluate the performance of the CLAP model.
tasks.origin_paper: Piczak, 2015; Salamon et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2020; Tzanetakis & Cook, 2002
tasks.model_type_notes: Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining (CLAP) model
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy

title: MuSe '24: The 5th Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Challenge and Workshop: Social Perception & Humor

benchmarks.name: Social Perception Sub-Challenge (MuSe-Perception)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on predicting perceived social attributes (e.g., assertiveness, likability), which is related to social intelligence and affective computing but is not a direct measure of creativity like divergent thinking or novelty.

tasks.name: Social Perception Prediction
tasks.description: Predict 16 different social attributes of individuals (e.g., assertiveness, dominance, likability, sincerity) from audio-visual data on a 1-7 Likert scale.
tasks.model_type_notes: Gated Recurrent Unit - Recurrent Neural Network (GRU-RNN)
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean Pearson's Correlation Coefficient (ρ) across 16 target attributes.

benchmarks.name: Cross-Cultural Humor Detection Sub-Challenge (MuSe-Humor)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on the detection of spontaneous humor, a key area in computational creativity and affective computing.

tasks.name: Cross-Cultural Humor Detection
tasks.description: Perform binary prediction for the presence or absence of spontaneous humor in a cross-lingual and cross-cultural setting, training on German videos and testing on English videos.
tasks.model_type_notes: Gated Recurrent Unit - Recurrent Neural Network (GRU-RNN)
tasks.scoring_detail: Area Under the Curve (AUC)

title: MERMAID: Metaphor Generation with Symbolism and Discriminative Decoding

benchmarks.name: Metaphor Generation from Literal Sentences
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates an LLM's ability to generate creative metaphors from literal sentences, using both automatic metrics and human judgments of creativity, fluency, meaning, and metaphoricity.

tasks.name: Metaphor Generation
tasks.description: Given a literal sentence, the model must generate a metaphorical version by replacing a verb, while preserving the sentence's core meaning. The evaluation is performed on a custom test set of 150 literal utterances.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings (1-5 Likert scale) for Fluency, Meaning, Creativity, Metaphoricity. Automatic metrics: SBERT semantic similarity, BLEU-2, BERTScore.

benchmarks.name: Poem Enhancement via Metaphorical Rewriting
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A task-based evaluation where an AI model is used to creatively enhance human-written poetry, with quality judged by human preference.

tasks.name: Poem Rewriting
tasks.description: A single literal sentence within a human-written four-line poem (quatrain) is rewritten by the model to be metaphorical. The goal is to assess if the change improves the poem.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human preference test comparing the original poem quatrain with the model-rewritten version.

title: AnalogGenie: A Generative Engine for Automatic Discovery of Analog Circuit Topologies

benchmarks.name: Analog Circuit Topology Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new dataset and a set of generation tasks for analog circuit topologies, a process explicitly described as the 'most challenging and creative' part of analog IC design. The evaluation focuses on generating novel, valid, and high-performance circuits.

tasks.name: Op-Amp Topology Generation
tasks.description: Generate novel and high-performance operational-amplifier (Op-Amp) circuit topologies.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates its own GPT-based model (AnalogGenie) against a VAE-based model (CktGNN) and other foundation models (LaMAGIC, AnalogCoder).
tasks.scoring_detail: Correctness (simulatable), Scalability (number of devices), Novelty (% different from dataset), Performance (Figure-of-Merit/FoM after sizing with a genetic algorithm).

tasks.name: Power Converter Topology Generation
tasks.description: Generate novel and high-performance power converter circuit topologies.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates its own GPT-based model (AnalogGenie) against a VAE-based model (CktGNN) and other foundation models (LaMAGIC, AnalogCoder).
tasks.scoring_detail: Correctness (simulatable), Scalability (number of devices), Novelty (% different from dataset), Performance (Figure-of-Merit/FoM after sizing with a genetic algorithm).

tasks.name: Bandgap Reference Topology Generation
tasks.description: Generate novel and high-performance bandgap reference circuit topologies.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates its own GPT-based model (AnalogGenie) against other models, though AnalogGenie was the only one capable of this specific task.
tasks.scoring_detail: Correctness (simulatable), Scalability (number of devices), Novelty (% different from dataset), Performance (Figure-of-Merit/FoM after sizing with a genetic algorithm).

tasks.name: Zero-shot Circuit Generation
tasks.description: Generate a circuit topology for a type not seen during training (a transconductance amplifier) to test zero-shot generalization.
tasks.model_type_notes: This was demonstrated specifically for the AnalogGenie model.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative assessment of the generated circuit schematic, which was manually drawn and visualized in an industry-standard tool.

title: Dynamic Knowledge Exchange and Dual-diversity Review: Concisely Unleashing the Potential of a Multi-Agent Research Team

benchmarks.name: Computer Sciences Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset of scientific papers used for the open-ended task of generating novel and impactful scientific abstracts, a form of scientific creativity. The evaluation uses metrics designed to quantify novelty and impact.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Derived from AMiner (Tang et al. 2008), and its use for this task follows VIRSCI (Su et al. 2025).

tasks.name: Scientific Abstract Generation
tasks.description: A multi-agent system of LLMs collaborates to generate a novel and impactful scientific abstract based on a corpus of existing computer science literature.
tasks.scoring_detail: Historical Dissimilarity (HD), Contemporary Dissimilarity (CD), Contemporary Impact (CI), Overall Novelty (ON)

benchmarks.name: Health Sciences Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of scientific papers introduced to evaluate the open-ended task of generating novel and impactful scientific abstracts in a different domain, testing for scientific creativity.

tasks.name: Scientific Abstract Generation
tasks.description: A multi-agent system of LLMs collaborates to generate a novel and impactful scientific abstract based on a corpus of existing health sciences literature, collected from PubMed.
tasks.scoring_detail: Historical Dissimilarity (HD), Contemporary Dissimilarity (CD), Contemporary Impact (CI), Overall Novelty (ON)

title: AssoCiAm: A Benchmark for Evaluating Association Thinking while Circumventing Ambiguity

benchmarks.name: AssoCiAm
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed to evaluate associative thinking, a core component of creativity, in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) through visual association tasks.

tasks.name: Visual Association Task (4T1, 7T1, 10T1)
tasks.description: MLLMs are given an image containing a natural object (e.g., cloud, beach) shaped like a common object. They must answer a multiple-choice question to identify which object the shape most resembles. The task is presented in three variants with 4, 7, or 10 options (4T1, 7T1, 10T1). Human experts were also evaluated on a subset of the benchmark to provide a performance baseline.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper refers to them as Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Top-1 accuracy, weighted average accuracy

benchmarks.name: Ambiguity Impact Analysis Sets
benchmarks.relevance_reason: These datasets were created specifically for this paper to empirically test how different types of ambiguity (internal and external) affect the performance of MLLMs on creative association tasks.

tasks.name: Ori (Original Validation Set)
tasks.description: A baseline validation set sampled from AssoCiAm, designed to be free of ambiguity, to measure model performance under ideal conditions.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy score

tasks.name: Int (Internal Ambiguity Set)
tasks.description: A derivative of the Ori set where correct answers are replaced with unreasonable ones to explicitly introduce and evaluate the impact of internal ambiguity.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy score

tasks.name: Ext (External Ambiguity Set)
tasks.description: A derivative of the Ori set where distractors are replaced with other plausible, ambiguous options to explicitly introduce and evaluate the impact of external ambiguity.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy score

benchmarks.name: MMMU
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A general cognitive benchmark used only for a correlation analysis to relate cognitive ability to associative thinking. It was not used to directly evaluate creativity.
benchmarks.origin_name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI

tasks.name: Correlation Analysis with Cognitive Scores
tasks.description: The paper uses existing MMMU benchmark scores as a proxy for MLLMs' cognitive ability and calculates the Pearson Correlation Coefficient between these scores and the models' performance on the AssoCiAm benchmark.
tasks.task_type_notes: Correlation analysis between AssoCiAm scores and existing MMMU scores.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson Correlation Coefficient

title: Learning to Evaluate Humor in Memes Based on the Incongruity Theory

benchmarks.name: Meme Humor Dataset (Ours)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Presents a new dataset of memes with human-annotated humor scores (using Best-Worst Scaling) and uses it to evaluate models on a humor classification task.

tasks.name: Meme Humor Classification
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine whether a given meme (image + caption) is humorous. Models are trained and evaluated on a refined dataset of 1,411 memes where items with ambiguous human humor ratings were removed.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested are based on ViLT and CLIP.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy (average over 10-fold cross-validation with 8 runs)

title: EXPOTION: Facial Expression and Motion Control for Multimodal Music Generation

benchmarks.name: EXPOTION Multimodal Music Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark involves an open-ended creative task (music generation) controlled by expressive human inputs (facial expressions, motion) and explicitly evaluates creativity as a metric in its human study.

tasks.name: Music Generation from Facial Expression, Motion, and Text
tasks.description: Generate a music clip that is expressively and temporally aligned with a given input video showing facial expressions and upper-body motion, and semantically aligned with a text prompt. The evaluation uses a new dataset of 7 hours of synchronized video-music pairs.
tasks.model_type_notes: Multimodal music generation model (fine-tuned Transformer-based text-to-music model).
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings (Musicality, Text-audio Similarity, Video-audio Consistency, Creativity); Automatic metrics: Frechet Audio Distance (FAD-VGG), Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, Inter-Sample Score (IS Score), Tempo Error (bpm), Beat F1-score, CLAP score (text-audio similarity), LanguageBind score (video-audio similarity).

title: AnaloBench: Benchmarking the Identification of Abstract and Long-context Analogies

benchmarks.name: ANALOBENCH
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark is designed to evaluate the analogical reasoning of LMs, a key component of creative and abstract thinking. It uses open-ended story identification tasks that require understanding deep relational structures rather than surface-level similarity.

tasks.name: Identify analogies from mini story bank (T1)
tasks.description: Given a target story, the model must select the most analogous story from 4 options (one correct, three distractors). The task is evaluated on stories of three different lengths: 1, 10, and 30 sentences.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (model performance vs gold standard, and human baseline performance)

tasks.name: Identify analogies from large story bank (T2)
tasks.description: Given a target story, the model must retrieve the top 10 most analogous stories from a bank of 200 stories. This retrieval task is evaluated on stories of three different lengths: 1, 10, and 30 sentences.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean Average Precision (MAP), Precision@K, Recall@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR)

title: Exploring Scientific Hypothesis Generation with Mamba

benchmarks.name: SciMON
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on generating novel, literature-informed scientific ideas, which is a creative ideation task. Evaluation includes metrics for novelty.
benchmarks.origin_name: SciMON (Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty)

tasks.name: Scientific Hypothesis Generation
tasks.description: Given a seed term and background context from an NLP paper, the model generates a target sentence proposing a new scientific idea or research direction.
tasks.model_type_notes: T5, Mamba, GPT-4
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic (ROUGE-L, BERTScore), LLM-as-judge (Claude-3.5 rating of 'effective'/'ineffective' based on relevance, novelty, soundness, clarity), and Human expert rating ('effective'/'ineffective' on the same criteria).

benchmarks.name: Long-Text Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: These are standard NLP tasks (NLI, QA) used to evaluate the long-context capabilities of the models, not their creativity.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Koreeda and Manning, 2021; Pang et al., 2021; Kociský et al., 2017

tasks.name: ContractNLI
tasks.description: A document-level natural language inference task for contracts.
tasks.task_type_notes: Natural Language Inference
tasks.model_type_notes: T5, Mamba
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

tasks.name: QuALITY
tasks.description: A question answering task with long input texts.
tasks.task_type_notes: Question Answering
tasks.model_type_notes: T5, Mamba
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

tasks.name: NarrativeQA
tasks.description: A reading comprehension challenge on long narratives (stories and movie scripts).
tasks.task_type_notes: Question Answering / Reading Comprehension
tasks.model_type_notes: T5, Mamba
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score

benchmarks.name: General In-Context Learning Tasks
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Standard closed-ended question answering and reasoning benchmarks (MMLU, MATHQA, etc.) used to test general model capabilities, not creativity.

tasks.name: MATHQA
tasks.description: Mathematical reasoning question answering.
tasks.task_type_notes: Question Answering
tasks.model_type_notes: Mamba, T5
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

tasks.name: MMLU
tasks.description: Massive Multitask Language Understanding benchmark.
tasks.task_type_notes: Question Answering
tasks.model_type_notes: Mamba, T5
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

tasks.name: MMLUSR
tasks.description: A variant of the MMLU benchmark.
tasks.task_type_notes: Question Answering
tasks.model_type_notes: Mamba, T5
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

tasks.name: GPQA
tasks.description: Graduate-level Google-Proof Question Answering.
tasks.task_type_notes: Question Answering
tasks.model_type_notes: Mamba, T5
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

title: GLDesigner: Leveraging Multi-Modal LLMs as Designer for Enhanced Aesthetic Text Glyph Layouts

benchmarks.name: TextLogo3K
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset for the creative task of aesthetic text logo layout generation, which is an open-ended design problem. Used to evaluate an AI system's generative capabilities.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Wang et al., Aesthetic Text Logo Synthesis via Content-aware Layout Inferring, 2022

tasks.name: Unconstrained Text Logo Layout Generation
tasks.description: The model generates a text logo layout based on input glyphs without any specific user constraints, aiming for general aesthetic quality and diversity.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper's VLM-based model is compared against a previous GAN-based method.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Overlap IoU, Visual Balance (V.B), Glyph Ratio Consistency

benchmarks.name: SynTextLogo
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale dataset for the creative task of aesthetic text logo layout generation. It consists of synthesized logos from designer-crafted templates and is used to train and evaluate a generative AI model.

tasks.name: Ablation Study Evaluation
tasks.description: The dataset is used in an ablation study to evaluate its contribution to the model's performance on layout generation when included in the training data.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Overlap IoU, Visual Balance (V.B), Glyph Ratio Consistency

benchmarks.name: GenTextLogo
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale dataset of real-world text logos for the creative task of aesthetic layout generation. It is used to evaluate an AI system's ability to handle complex, diverse designs and user constraints.

tasks.name: Unconstrained Text Logo Layout Generation
tasks.description: The model generates a text logo layout based on input glyphs from the GenTextLogo dataset without any specific user constraints.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Overlap IoU, Visual Balance (V.B), Glyph Ratio Consistency

tasks.name: User-Constrained Text Logo Layout Generation
tasks.description: The model generates a text logo layout following specific natural language constraints (e.g., 'Horizontal Constraint', 'Vertical Constraint'), with performance assessed by human evaluators.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human preference rate, Quality rating (1-5), Constraint Violation Ratio (ViO)

title: ZeroSumEval: Scaling LLM Evaluation with Inter-Model Competition

benchmarks.name: ZeroSumEval
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A novel, extensible framework for evaluating LLMs through competitive, multi-player zero-sum games. It assesses a range of capabilities including strategic reasoning, planning, knowledge application, and creativity in dynamic environments.

tasks.name: Chess
tasks.description: Two LLMs play a classic game of chess against each other, providing moves in FEN notation. The game evaluates strategic reasoning and long-term planning.
tasks.origin_paper: Classic game; paper cites prior work like carlini/chess-llm as examples.
tasks.scoring_detail: Bradley-Terry (BT) rating based on game wins/losses. Win conditions include checkmate or opponent failing to make a valid move within a set number of attempts.

tasks.name: Poker
tasks.description: A two-player variant of Texas Hold 'Em where models play multiple rounds starting with a fixed number of chips. It evaluates decision-making under uncertainty.
tasks.scoring_detail: Bradley-Terry (BT) rating based on game wins/losses; Normalized chip differences.

tasks.name: Liar's Dice
tasks.description: A two-player bluffing game where models take turns bidding on the outcome of dice rolls or calling the opponent's bluff.
tasks.scoring_detail: Bradley-Terry (BT) rating based on game wins/losses.

tasks.name: MathQuiz
tasks.description: A two-player game where a 'teacher' LLM must generate a valid and solvable math problem for a given answer, and a 'student' LLM must solve it. This tests knowledge application and the ability to create novel, challenging questions.
tasks.scoring_detail: Bradley-Terry (BT) rating based on game wins/losses. Win is determined by the student's answer correctness or the teacher's failure to generate a valid question.

tasks.name: Debate
tasks.description: Two LLMs debate for or against a randomly selected stance. A jury of other LLMs scores the debate based on a rubric to determine the winner, assessing persuasive and conversational capabilities.
tasks.scoring_detail: Numerical score from a jury of LLMs (gpt-4o and claude-3.5-sonnet) based on a rubric; Bradley-Terry (BT) rating based on game wins.

tasks.name: Gandalf
tasks.description: A conversational game where a 'sentinel' LLM must guard a secret password while an 'infiltrator' LLM attempts to trick it into revealing the password. This tests instruction following and creative persuasion/jailbreaking.
tasks.scoring_detail: Bradley-Terry (BT) rating based on game wins/losses. Win is determined by password revelation or reaching a maximum turn limit.

tasks.name: PyJail
tasks.description: A cybersecurity game where a 'defender' LLM creates a Python sandbox ('pyjail') that a 'attacker' LLM must break to access a flag. This tests the ability to create and solve creative, multi-step puzzles in a restricted environment.
tasks.scoring_detail: Bradley-Terry (BT) rating based on game wins/losses. Win is determined by the attacker solving the sandbox or the defender failing to create a valid one.

title: CodeScientist: End-to-End Semi-Automated Scientific Discovery with Code-based Experimentation

benchmarks.name: CodeScientist Scientific Discovery Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new framework for evaluating an AI system's ability to generate novel, sound, and interesting scientific discoveries (code, experiments, papers), which is a high-level creative task.

tasks.name: Scientific Discovery Generation and Evaluation
tasks.description: An end-to-end system (CodeScientist) generates research ideas, plans, experimental code, and reports in the domain of AI agents. The resulting 19 scientific 'discoveries' are then evaluated by human experts.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses CLAUDE-SONNET-3.5-1022 as the base model for CodeScientist and GPT-4O-MINI for the generated experiments.
tasks.scoring_detail: External conference-style review on soundness and novelty; internal code review and replication attempts by a domain expert.

benchmarks.name: TextWorldExpress
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A platform for text-based game environments (e.g., CookingWorld) that require open-ended problem solving and reasoning from AI agents, used as the testbed for multiple experiments generated by CodeScientist.

tasks.name: Agent Performance in Generated Experiments
tasks.description: The CodeScientist system generated novel experiments where LLM agents performed tasks within TextWorldExpress environments (specifically CookingWorld). Tasks included state prediction confidence, action prediction, and agent performance with custom planning or memory.
tasks.task_type_notes: The CodeScientist system generates the entire experiment, including the agent code that is then run in the environment.
tasks.scoring_detail: Varies by generated experiment: Correlation coefficient (r), prediction accuracy, task scores, LLM-as-a-judge.

benchmarks.name: ScienceWorld
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A text-based environment simulating a science lab, used as a testbed for a generated experiment requiring complex, goal-oriented reasoning.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Implicitly used as it is reimplemented in TextWorldExpress, which is cited.

tasks.name: Affordance Agent Performance
tasks.description: The CodeScientist system generated an experiment where an LLM agent that predicts object affordances was evaluated against a random baseline in the ScienceWorld environment.
tasks.scoring_detail: Comparison of agent performance against a random baseline.

benchmarks.name: DISCOVERYWORLD
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A virtual environment explicitly designed for developing and evaluating automated scientific discovery agents, directly aligning with the paper's goals.

tasks.name: Graph Agent Performance
tasks.description: The CodeScientist system generated an experiment comparing a ReAct agent augmented with a graph-based memory against a baseline ReAct agent on a task in the DISCOVERYWORLD environment.
tasks.scoring_detail: DiscoveryWorld Task Completion and Task Process scores.

title: QUDsim: Quantifying Discourse Similarities in LLM-Generated Text

benchmarks.name: QUDsim
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new metric and framework to quantify discourse similarity in LLM-generated text, directly addressing the creativity-related problem of structural repetitiveness and formulaic writing.

tasks.name: Segment Alignment Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating the ability of similarity metrics (QUDsim and baselines) to align structurally similar segments between two documents, using human annotations as a gold standard.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the performance of different similarity metrics, not the generative models directly.
tasks.model_type_notes: The objects being evaluated are similarity metrics (QUDsim, n-gram Jaccard, ROUGE-L, cosine similarity, LLM-judges). These metrics are applied to texts generated by LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Flash) and humans.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score against a human-annotated alignment set.

tasks.name: Discourse Homogeneity Analysis
tasks.description: Using the QUDsim metric to measure and compare the structural similarity of texts generated by different LLMs and humans, particularly for prompts that are identical or minimally different.
tasks.scoring_detail: QUDsim similarity score (harmonic mean of aligned segment fractions).

tasks.name: Discourse Template Tracking
tasks.description: Identifying and counting consecutive sequences of aligned segments (discourse templates) between pairs of documents to quantify structural reuse.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average count of discourse templates of length 2, 3, and 4.

title: GODBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models in Video Comment Art

benchmarks.name: GODBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale benchmark for evaluating the creativity of Multimodal Large Language Models in generating and understanding artistic video comments. It includes both generative and discriminative tasks across multiple creative dimensions.

tasks.name: Selection
tasks.description: MLLMs must choose the most creative comment (the GOD-level comment) from a set of multiple-choice options which include high-quality and ordinary comments as distractors.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various Video MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (acc), top-2 accuracy

tasks.name: Ranking
tasks.description: MLLMs must order multiple comments according to their quality, based on human preferences reflected by upvote counts.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various Video MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG), Exact Match Accuracy (EMA)

tasks.name: Classification
tasks.description: MLLMs are required to classify multiple comments into three quality categories: GOD-level, High-Quality, and Ordinary.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various Video MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (acc), Exact Match Accuracy (EMA)

tasks.name: Explanation
tasks.description: MLLMs must predict the 'Comment Art dimensions' (e.g., Humor, Metaphor, Role Immersion) for a given GOD-level comment and provide a textual explanation for their prediction.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves both classifying tags and generating a textual explanation.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various Video MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Tag discrimination accuracy, GPT-4o score based on Precision, Reasonableness, Completeness, Relevance, and Clarity

tasks.name: Creation
tasks.description: MLLMs must generate a creative, contextually appropriate, and emotionally resonant comment based on the video content.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various Video MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics (BLEU, DIST, ROUGE, F1BERT), LLM-based judgment (GPT-4o score for Creativity, Quality, Style, Impact), and human preference study (voting %)

tasks.name: Divergent Association Task
tasks.description: A specific analysis of the Creation task focusing on entity innovation. The creativity of generated comments is assessed by comparing the overlap of novel entities with those in human-written GOD-level comments.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is an evaluation of the output from the Creation task.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests various Video MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Weighted Entity Overlap (WEO) score, which uses GPT-4o for entity extraction and then an automatic calculation.

title: Measuring LLM Novelty As The Frontier Of Original And High-Quality Output

benchmarks.name: Measuring LLM Novelty as the Frontier of Original and High-Quality Output
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new evaluation framework for LLM novelty, combining originality (unseen n-grams) and task-specific quality (LLM-judge) on several creative generation tasks.

tasks.name: Story Completion
tasks.description: Models are given the first line of a story from the TinyStories dataset and must generate a coherent and creative completion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Harmonic mean of n-gram originality (fraction of unseen n-grams for n=4,5,6) and a quality score (0-5) from an LLM-as-judge (o3-mini).

tasks.name: Poetry Writing
tasks.description: Models generate a single line of poetry based on instructions from the CoPoet dataset regarding content and literary devices.
tasks.scoring_detail: Harmonic mean of n-gram originality (fraction of unseen n-grams for n=4,5,6) and a quality score (0-5) from an LLM-as-judge (o3-mini).

tasks.name: Creative Tool Use
tasks.description: Models generate a solution for a physical problem requiring creative use of common objects, based on scenarios from the MacGyver dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Harmonic mean of n-gram originality (fraction of unseen n-grams for n=4,5,6) and a quality score (0-5) from an LLM-as-judge (o3-mini).

title: D ELTA S CORE : Story Evaluation with Perturbations

benchmarks.name: Story Generation Evaluation on ROCStories and WritingPrompts
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Uses a dataset of AI-generated stories with human ratings on creative writing aspects like interestingness, coherence, and logicality to evaluate automated story quality metrics.
benchmarks.origin_name: Generated stories and human ratings from ROCStories and WritingPrompts

tasks.name: Fine-Grained Story Quality Evaluation
tasks.description: Automatically scoring AI-generated stories on five fine-grained aspects (fluency, coherence, relatedness, logicality, and interestingness). The performance of the scoring metric is measured by its correlation with human judgments.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates various metrics. Its proposed DELTASCORE uses PLMs (BART, FLAN-T5, BLOOM, LLaMA, OPT, GPT-3.5) as a backbone. It is compared against other metrics, some of which are also LLM-based.
tasks.scoring_detail: Kendall correlation of metric scores against human ratings (1-5 ordinal scale) for fluency, coherence, relatedness, logicality, and interestingness.

title: MixAssist: An Audio-Language Dataset for Co-Creative AI Assistance in Music Mixing

benchmarks.name: MIXASSIST
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new audio-language dataset and task for evaluating AI in a co-creative, instructional context (music mixing), focusing on generating open-ended, helpful dialogue.

tasks.name: music-mixing response generation
tasks.description: Given a conversation history, an amateur producer's query, and an audio segment, an AI assistant generates a contextually relevant, technically correct, and pedagogically helpful response to assist in music mixing.
tasks.model_type_notes: Audio Language Models (ALMs) were tested: Qwen-Audio-Instruct-7B, LTU, and MU-LLaMA.
tasks.scoring_detail: Evaluation was multi-faceted: 1. LLM-as-a-judge ranking (technical accuracy, helpfulness, fluency). 2. Human preference study (AI vs. human expert responses). 3. Real-time interaction user study (survey on naturalness, creativity, novelty). 4. Automated metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, BERTScore). 5. Manual analysis of guidance correctness.

title: Arabic Automatic Story Generation with Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Arabic Story Generation Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new framework for evaluating the creative task of Arabic story generation using both LLM and human judges on criteria like fluency, coherence, and instruction following.

tasks.name: GPT-4 as a Judge
tasks.description: GPT-4 is prompted to act as an Arabic language expert and evaluate generated stories on a five-point scale across five criteria: Fluency, Coherence, Instruction Following, Consistency, and Variety. The evaluation is performed on 20 new prompts.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4 scores on a 1-5 scale for Fluency, Coherence, Instruction Following, Consistency, and Variety.

tasks.name: Human Story Evaluation
tasks.description: Four Arabic native speakers rank stories generated by different models based on Instruction Following, Fluency, and Variety Adherence, performing pairwise comparisons.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise preference ranking by human judges on Instruction Following, Fluency, and Variety Adherence.

title: Can Multimodal Large Language Model Think Analogically?

benchmarks.name: MARS
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates multimodal analogical reasoning, a cognitive ability the paper links to creativity, by requiring models to predict a missing entity in a proportional analogy.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Zhang et al., Multimodal analogical reasoning over knowledge graphs (2023)

tasks.name: Multimodal Analogical Reasoning
tasks.description: Given an analogy example (eh, et) and a question entity (eq), the task is to predict the missing entity (ea) that completes the analogy. The task is evaluated on three sub-tasks with different input modalities: (Image, Image) : (Text, ?), (Text, Text) : (Image, ?), and (Image, Text) : (Image, ?).
tasks.origin_paper: Zhang et al., Multimodal analogical reasoning over knowledge graphs (2023)
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both Multimodal Pre-trained Transformer (MPT) models and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Hits@k (k=1, 3, 5, 10), MRR, Accuracy (Hits@1)

tasks.name: Implicit Relation Inference
tasks.description: In the context of a multimodal analogy (eh, et) : (eq, ea), the task is to predict the implicit semantic relation between the entities eh and et.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both MPT models and MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Hits@k (k=1, 3, 5), Accuracy (Hits@1)

tasks.name: Analogical Validity Judgment
tasks.description: The analogical reasoning task is framed in a True/False format to determine whether a given analogical reasoning example is valid.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated using the paper's 'Predictor' framework based on MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (inferred from graph)

benchmarks.name: MBARD
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset constructed by the paper to evaluate zero-shot analogical reasoning with verb-noun pairs, which is framed as being closer to real-world creative problem-solving in unfamiliar contexts.

tasks.name: Zero-shot Verb-Noun Analogical Reasoning
tasks.description: Evaluate the model's ability to solve verb-noun analogies of the form (Text-verb, Image-noun) : (Text-verb, ?) in a zero-shot setting, where the entities and task format have not been seen during training.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluates MLLMs (e.g., LLaVA, ChatGPT-4) and MPTs (e.g., MKGformer).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Human evaluation (for comparison)

benchmarks.name: MarKG
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a background multimodal knowledge graph used for pre-training and fine-tuning models, not for direct evaluation of a creative task.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Zhang et al., Multimodal analogical reasoning over knowledge graphs (2023)

tasks.name: Knowledge Graph Triplet Prediction
tasks.description: For a given triplet (head, relation, tail) from the knowledge graph, predict one missing component (head entity, relation, or tail entity) given the other two. This is used for the step-1 fine-tuning of the 'Predictor' model.
tasks.origin_paper: Generic task, applied to MarKG dataset
tasks.model_type_notes: Used to fine-tune MLLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: N/A (used for model fine-tuning, not evaluation)

title: MLLM-Bench: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs with Per-sample Criteria

benchmarks.name: MLLM-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark for evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on open-ended tasks across six cognitive levels, including a 'Creation' level. It uses a novel per-sample criteria evaluation method specifically designed for tasks without a single ground-truth answer.

tasks.name: MLLM Capability Evaluation
tasks.description: 26 MLLMs generate answers to 420 image-instruction pairs spanning 42 capabilities across 6 cognitive levels (Perception, Understanding, Applying, Analyzing, Evaluation, Creation). The answers are evaluated in a pairwise comparison against an anchor model.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Model) and benchmarks 26 different models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise comparison (win/tie/lose) against an anchor model (LLaVA-v1.5-13B) judged by a powerful MLLM (GPT-4-Turbo or Claude-3-Opus) using per-sample criteria. Elo ratings are also calculated.

tasks.name: Human Alignment Validation
tasks.description: Various AI judges (both text-only LLMs with visual proxies and MLLMs) and human evaluators perform pairwise comparisons on a subset of 252 model-generated answers from the MLLM-Bench dataset. The AI judgments are then compared to human judgments to measure alignment.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task evaluates the paper's evaluation paradigm itself by comparing AI judges to human judges.
tasks.model_type_notes: The experiment tests both text-only LLMs (GPT-4) and VLMs/MLLMs (GPT-4-Turbo) as judges.
tasks.scoring_detail: Agreement rate (percentage) between various AI judges and human judges. Human judgment is the ground truth.

title: Evaluating Creativity and Deception in Large Language Models: A Simulation Framework for Multi-Agent Balderdash

benchmarks.name: LLM-MA Balderdash
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new multi-agent simulation framework based on the game Balderdash specifically to evaluate the creativity (generating plausible fictitious definitions) and logical reasoning of LLMs in an interactive setting. It involves open-ended generation and reports empirical results.

tasks.name: Definition Generation
tasks.description: LLM agents generate plausible-sounding definitions for obscure or common English words. The goal is either to provide the true definition or a fictitious one that can deceive other players.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include Llama-3-8B, Phi-3-small, Gemma-1.1-7b, Mistral-7B, and gpt-3.5-turbo.
tasks.scoring_detail: True Definition Ratio (TDR), LLM Knows Ratio (LKR), Deception Ratio (DR), and Average Score (AS). Scoring relies on an LLM judge for semantic equivalence and votes from other LLM players.

tasks.name: Definition Voting
tasks.description: LLM agents vote for the definition they believe is the correct one from a list containing other players' generated definitions and the true dictionary definition.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include Llama-3-8B, Phi-3-small, Gemma-1.1-7b, Mistral-7B, and gpt-3.5-turbo.
tasks.scoring_detail: Correct Guess Ratio (CGR) and Average Score (AS). Scoring is based on whether the agent correctly identifies the reference definition.

benchmarks.name: Judge LLM Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a preliminary evaluation created to select the best LLM for the judge role in the main Balderdash framework. The task itself is a closed-ended semantic equivalence judgment, not a direct measure of creativity, but it is a necessary component for the creativity benchmark.

tasks.name: Semantic Equivalence Judgment
tasks.description: An LLM is prompted to determine if a generated definition is semantically equivalent to a reference dictionary definition, responding with 'True' or 'False'. This was used to select the best LLM to act as the judge in the Balderdash game.
tasks.model_type_notes: Llama, Phi, Gemma, Mistral, and GPT-3.5 were evaluated for this role.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1, Recall, Precision, and Accuracy were calculated by comparing LLM judgments against a human-annotated ground truth dataset created for this purpose ('Judge Evaluation Data').

title: BannerAgency: Advertising Banner Design with Multimodal LLM Agents

benchmarks.name: BannerRequest400
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark for evaluating AI-driven creative graphic design generation, specifically for advertising banners, using multimodal inputs (logo + text). The task is open-ended and focuses on a creative domain.

tasks.name: Banner Ad Generation
tasks.description: Generating advertising banners from a multimodal request (brand logo and text description) across various standard dimensions. The generated banners are evaluated for advertising effectiveness and general design quality.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-to-image models (DALL-E3, FLUX.1-schnell), a prompt-based graphic design model (OpenCOLE), and the proposed MLLM agent system (BannerAgency).
tasks.scoring_detail: Evaluated using a mix of methods: (1) LLM (GPT-4o) and human ratings on 6 custom advertising metrics (TAA, LPS, CTAE, CPYQ, BIS, AQS). (2) Human preference study via pairwise comparisons. (3) Human evaluation of iterative refinement effectiveness. (4) LLM (GPT-4o) ratings on 8 general design metrics (DL, CR, TC, GI, INV, ALM, OLP, WS). (5) Automatic metric: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID).

title: PodEval: A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for Podcast Audio Generation

benchmarks.name: RAG Test Coverage Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This framework evaluates the semantic coverage and thoroughness of test sets for RAG systems. It is a measure of test quality and completeness, not AI creativity.

tasks.name: Incomplete Test Coverage Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluates an existing test set (31 questions) against a real-world product's documentation (415 chunks) to identify and quantify semantic coverage gaps. The framework is then used to guide the generation of new questions to improve coverage.
tasks.task_type_notes: The primary task is to evaluate a test set's semantic coverage against a knowledge base, not to generate creative output from a model.
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses LLMs for embeddings (OpenAI, Voyage AI) and for generating suggested questions during the gap analysis phase.
tasks.scoring_detail: Basic coverage, weighted coverage, multi-cluster coverage (all based on cosine distance between embeddings).

tasks.name: Irrelevant Knowledge Detection
tasks.description: Evaluates a mixed corpus containing a relevant financial document and an irrelevant document about birds, using a small set of relevant questions. The goal is to demonstrate that the framework can identify the irrelevant document cluster by assigning it a significantly lower coverage score.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is to evaluate document relevance within a knowledge base by measuring test set coverage.
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses LLMs for embeddings (OpenAI, Voyage AI).
tasks.scoring_detail: Basic coverage score per cluster.

title: SS-Bench: A Benchmark for Social Story Generation and Evaluation

benchmarks.name: SS-GEN
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new task, dataset, and evaluation framework for generating 'Social Stories,' a constrained creative writing task for a specific audience (children with autism). It reports empirical results for several LLMs using human, LLM-based, and automatic metrics.

tasks.name: Social Story Generation
tasks.description: Given a title, the task is to generate a Social Story that adheres to specific constraints (Structural Clarity, Descriptive Orientation, Situational Safety) designed for children with autism.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating (Structural Clarity, Descriptive Orientation, Situational Safety), GPT-4 rating (Coherence, Descriptiveness, Empathy, Grammaticality, Relevance), and automatic metrics (BLEU-4, ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, BertScore).

title: Speak-to-Structure: Evaluating LLMs in Open-domain Natural Language-Driven Molecule Generation

benchmarks.name: Speak-to-Structure (S2-Bench)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a benchmark for open-domain molecule generation, framing it as a creative design task with one-to-many mappings to test genuine understanding and generation capabilities beyond memorization.

tasks.name: AddComponent
tasks.description: A molecule editing task where LLMs must add a specific functional group to a given molecule.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (correct functional group modification), Tanimoto Similarity, Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Similarity * Success Rate)

tasks.name: DelComponent
tasks.description: A molecule editing task where LLMs must remove a specific functional group from a given molecule.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (correct functional group modification), Tanimoto Similarity, Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Similarity * Success Rate)

tasks.name: SubComponent
tasks.description: A molecule editing task where LLMs must substitute a specific functional group in a given molecule with another.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (correct functional group modification), Tanimoto Similarity, Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Similarity * Success Rate)

tasks.name: LogP
tasks.description: A molecule optimization task where LLMs must modify a given molecule to increase or decrease its LogP (lipophilicity) value.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (property changed in desired direction), Tanimoto Similarity, Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Similarity * Success Rate)

tasks.name: MR
tasks.description: A molecule optimization task where LLMs must modify a given molecule to increase or decrease its Molecular Refractivity (MR) value.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (property changed in desired direction), Tanimoto Similarity, Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Similarity * Success Rate)

tasks.name: QED
tasks.description: A molecule optimization task where LLMs must modify a given molecule to increase or decrease its Quantitative Estimation of Drug-Likeness (QED) value.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (property changed in desired direction), Tanimoto Similarity, Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Similarity * Success Rate)

tasks.name: AtomNum
tasks.description: A customized molecule generation task where LLMs must generate a novel molecule from scratch with a specified number of certain atoms.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (adherence to structural constraints), Novelty (comparison against Zinc-250K), Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Novelty * Success Rate)

tasks.name: BondNum
tasks.description: A customized molecule generation task where LLMs must generate a novel molecule from scratch with a specified number and type of chemical bonds.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (adherence to structural constraints), Novelty (comparison against Zinc-250K), Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Novelty * Success Rate)

tasks.name: FunctionalGroup
tasks.description: A customized molecule generation task where LLMs must generate a novel molecule from scratch containing a specified number of particular functional groups.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success Rate (adherence to structural constraints), Novelty (comparison against Zinc-250K), Validity, Weighted Success Rate (Novelty * Success Rate)

title: Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Divergent Association Task (DAT)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A validated psychometric test of divergent thinking, a core component of creativity, by measuring semantic distance between generated words.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Olson, J. A., Nahas, J., Chmoulevitch, D., Cropper, S. J., & Webb, M. E. (2021). Naming unrelated words predicts creativity. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

tasks.name: Standard DAT
tasks.description: Generate 10 nouns that are as semantically different from each other as possible, following specific rules (no proper nouns, no technical terms). Performance is compared against a large human dataset (N=100,000).
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean pairwise semantic distance calculated using cosine similarity between GLoVe word embeddings.

tasks.name: DAT Control Condition
tasks.description: Generate a list of 10 words without any instructions for semantic difference, used as a baseline to test prompt adherence.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean pairwise semantic distance calculated using cosine similarity between GLoVe word embeddings.

tasks.name: DAT with Linguistic Strategies
tasks.description: Generate 10 semantically distant words while being prompted to use a specific linguistic strategy, such as meaning opposition, thesaurus, or varying etymology.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean pairwise semantic distance calculated using cosine similarity between GLoVe word embeddings.

benchmarks.name: Creative Writing Tasks
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates creativity in longer-form text generation (poetry, narrative) using computational metrics for semantic divergence and complexity.
benchmarks.origin_name: Haiku, Movie Synopsis, and Flash Fiction generation
benchmarks.origin_paper: Human data for comparison was sourced from The Movie DataBase (TMDB) and Temps Libre online platform.

tasks.name: Haiku Generation
tasks.description: Generate a haiku (a three-line poem with a 5-7-5 syllable structure). LLM outputs were compared against a corpus of human-written haikus.
tasks.origin_paper: Human data from Temps Libre online platform.
tasks.scoring_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) using BERT embeddings; Lempel-Ziv (LZ) complexity.

tasks.name: Movie Synopsis Generation
tasks.description: Generate a movie synopsis with a 50-word limit. LLM outputs were compared against a corpus of human-written synopses.
tasks.origin_paper: Human data from The Movie DataBase (TMDB).
tasks.scoring_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) using BERT embeddings; Lempel-Ziv (LZ) complexity.

tasks.name: Flash Fiction Generation
tasks.description: Generate a flash fiction story with a 200-word limit. LLM outputs were compared against each other using automated metrics, human ratings, and LLM-as-a-judge ratings.
tasks.scoring_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) using BERT embeddings; Lempel-Ziv (LZ) complexity; Human creativity ratings (1-5 scale); GPT-4 creativity ratings (1-5 scale).

title: Improving Linguistic Diversity of Large Language Models with Possibility Exploration Fine-Tuning

benchmarks.name: Open-domain Dialogue Generation for Diversity
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The tasks focus on generating multiple, semantically distinct responses to a single prompt, which is a direct measure of divergent thinking and linguistic diversity, key aspects of creativity.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Smith et al., 2020; Logacheva et al., 2018; Gopalakrishnan et al., 2023; Rashkin et al., 2018; Dinan et al., 2018

tasks.name: Multiple responses generation
tasks.description: Given a dialogue context, the task is to generate multiple possible and semantically distinct responses for the next turn.
tasks.model_type_notes: Mistral 7B, LLAMA 2 7B
tasks.scoring_detail: Distinct-1, Distinct-2, 1 - SBERT similarity (semantic diversity), Percentage of incoherent responses (rated by GPT-4o and LLAMA 3)

tasks.name: Persona generation test
tasks.description: A chatbot is asked to play the role of a random individual in a conversation, revealing demographic attributes. The diversity of the generated personas across 300 conversations is then measured.
tasks.model_type_notes: Mistral 7B and its fine-tuned versions
tasks.scoring_detail: Shannon entropy on persona attributes (age group, gender, location, education, occupation sector). Attribute extraction is performed by GPT-4o.

benchmarks.name: Story Generation for Diversity
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The task requires generating multiple, diverse endings for a story, which is a classic creative writing task that evaluates divergent thinking.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Mostafazadeh et al., 2016; Mostafazadeh et al., 2017

tasks.name: Multiple diverse endings generation
tasks.description: Given a 4-sentence story as input, the task is to generate multiple diverse endings for the given story.
tasks.model_type_notes: Mistral 7B
tasks.scoring_detail: 1 - SBERT similarity (semantic diversity), Percentage of incoherent responses (rated by GPT-4o and LLAMA 3)

title: Large Language Models are Zero Shot Hypothesis Proposers

benchmarks.name: Background and Hypothesis Pairs (BHP) dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark is newly created to evaluate the scientific discovery and hypothesis generation capabilities of LLMs, which is a core aspect of creative reasoning. The task is open-ended and involves empirical evaluation of AI models.

tasks.name: Hypothesis Generation
tasks.description: Given background knowledge extracted from a biomedical paper, the model generates a plausible scientific hypothesis. This is tested in zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned settings.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU, ROUGE, ChatGPT-based evaluation (novelty, relevance, significance, verifiability scores 0-3), Human evaluation (novelty, relevance, significance, verifiability scores 0-3)

tasks.name: Hypothesis Generation with Multi-Agent Framework
tasks.description: A multi-agent system with distinct roles (Analyst, Engineer, Scientist, Critic) collaborates to generate a scientific hypothesis from background knowledge, with an option to use external search tools.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses API-based models like GPT-4 for this framework.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU, ROUGE, GPT-4 based evaluation (novelty, relevance, significance, verifiability scores)

title: Jointly Reinforcing Diversity and Quality in Language Model Generations

benchmarks.name: AlpacaEval 2.0
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard benchmark for general instruction-following, not specifically designed to measure creativity.

tasks.name: Instruction Following
tasks.description: Generate responses to general instruction prompts, which are then compared against reference responses from GPT-4-turbo.
tasks.scoring_detail: Length-controlled win rate (LCWR) judged by GPT-4o.

benchmarks.name: ArenaHard v2.0
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper specifically evaluates on the creative writing subset of this benchmark.

tasks.name: Creative Writing
tasks.description: Generate responses for prompts from the creative writing subset of the benchmark.
tasks.scoring_detail: Win rate (WR) with style control, judged by GPT-4o.

benchmarks.name: EQ-Bench (Creative Writing)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Explicitly designed to evaluate creative writing abilities of LLMs.

tasks.name: Creative Writing
tasks.description: Generate responses to creative writing prompts, which are evaluated on multiple rubrics and through pairwise comparisons.
tasks.scoring_detail: Normalized ELO score and rubric-based win rates (e.g., "Interesting and Original"), judged by Claude 3.7 Sonnet.

benchmarks.name: NoveltyBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Explicitly designed to measure novelty and semantic diversity of generated text, which are key aspects of creativity.

tasks.name: Diverse Response Generation
tasks.description: Generate multiple responses to prompts that require diverse outputs, which are then evaluated for semantic and lexical diversity.
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of semantically distinct generations (Distinct), average number of distinct 4-grams (Distinct-4), and a quality score from a reward model.

benchmarks.name: AIME25
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A math competition benchmark used to evaluate correctness. The paper frames solution variety (pass@k) as a form of diversity, linking it to creativity, but the task itself is convergent.

tasks.name: Math Problem Solving
tasks.description: Generate solutions to competition-level math problems from the AIME 2025 competition.
tasks.scoring_detail: pass@k, with correctness verified by the Math-Verify library.

benchmarks.name: OlympiadBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A math competition benchmark used to evaluate correctness. The paper frames solution variety (pass@k) as a form of diversity, linking it to creativity, but the task itself is convergent.

tasks.name: Math Problem Solving
tasks.description: Generate solutions to olympiad-level scientific problems.
tasks.scoring_detail: pass@k, with correctness verified by the Math-Verify library.

benchmarks.name: HMMT 2025
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A math competition benchmark used to evaluate correctness. The paper frames solution variety (pass@k) as a form of diversity, linking it to creativity, but the task itself is convergent.

tasks.name: Math Problem Solving
tasks.description: Generate solutions to problems from the Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament 2025.
tasks.scoring_detail: pass@k, with correctness verified by the Math-Verify library.

benchmarks.name: Brumo 2025
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A math competition benchmark used to evaluate correctness. The paper frames solution variety (pass@k) as a form of diversity, linking it to creativity, but the task itself is convergent.

tasks.name: Math Problem Solving
tasks.description: Generate solutions to problems from the British Mathematical Olympiad 2025.
tasks.scoring_detail: pass@k, with correctness verified by the Math-Verify library.

title: Towards Multimodal Metaphor Understanding: A Chinese Dataset and Model for Metaphor Mapping Identification

benchmarks.name: CM3D (Chinese Multimodal Metaphor Mapping Dataset)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Provides a new multimodal dataset and benchmark for evaluating AI's ability to understand metaphors, a key component of figurative and creative language, by identifying their source and target domains.

tasks.name: Target Domain Identification
tasks.description: Given a metaphorical image-text pair from a Chinese advertisement, the model must generate the target domain of the metaphor (the concept being described).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-only LLMs (BART, GPT-3.5, ERNIE-Bot) and Vision-Language Models (GPT-4, LLaVA, Qwen-VL, BART+ViT, BART+DETR).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (exact match), BertScore (F1), Human Evaluation (H-E) score, Cohen's Kappa for inter-annotator agreement on H-E.

tasks.name: Source Domain Identification
tasks.description: Given a metaphorical image-text pair from a Chinese advertisement, the model must generate the source domain of the metaphor (the concept used to describe the target).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-only LLMs (BART, GPT-3.5, ERNIE-Bot) and Vision-Language Models (GPT-4, LLaVA, Qwen-VL, BART+ViT, BART+DETR).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (exact match), BertScore (F1), Human Evaluation (H-E) score, Cohen's Kappa for inter-annotator agreement on H-E.

title: LiveIdeaBench: Evaluating LLMs' Divergent Thinking for Scientific Idea Generation with Minimal Context

benchmarks.name: LiveIdeaBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed specifically to evaluate the divergent thinking and scientific idea generation capabilities of LLMs, which are core aspects of creativity.

tasks.name: Scientific Idea Generation
tasks.description: Over 40 LLMs were prompted with single scientific keywords (from a set of 1,180) to generate novel scientific ideas, testing their divergent thinking capabilities.
tasks.scoring_detail: A panel of judge LLMs rated ideas on five dimensions: Originality (1-10), Feasibility (1-10), Clarity (1-10), Fluency (distinctiveness of ideas, mapped to 1-10 scale), and Flexibility (30th percentile of other scores).

tasks.name: Human Expert Validation of LLM-as-Judge
tasks.description: To validate the benchmark's scoring method, 6 human experts in Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) rated 22 AI-generated ideas on the same criteria as the LLM judges, and the ratings were compared.
tasks.task_type_notes: Human experts evaluated AI-generated content to validate the LLM-as-a-judge scoring method. The AI's role was generating the content being evaluated.
tasks.model_type_notes: The output from 11 LLMs was evaluated by humans.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human expert ratings (Originality, Feasibility, Clarity on a 1-10 scale) were correlated with the average LLM judge ratings using Pearson correlation.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used for comparison of general intelligence scores against creativity scores, not for creativity evaluation itself. The paper uses its results but does not run its tasks.

tasks.name: General Intelligence Score Comparison
tasks.description: The paper used pre-existing general intelligence scores from LiveBench for over 40 LLMs and compared them against the scientific ideation scores from LiveIdeaBench to analyze the correlation between the two capabilities.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is not a task run by the paper's authors, but a comparative analysis using external benchmark results.
tasks.scoring_detail: The paper uses the final average scores from LiveBench for correlation analysis (Pearson's r).

title: IGA: An Intent-Guided Authoring Assistant

benchmarks.name: IGA Intent-Guided Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates an AI system on a set of open-ended, creative text generation tasks based on specific rhetorical directives. Includes both automatic and human evaluation.

tasks.name: Rhetorical Intent Infilling
tasks.description: Given a context with a specific rhetorical tag (e.g., CAUSE, EFFECT, DESCP, CNTRA, IDIOM, BIO), the model generates text to fill in the tag, fulfilling the specified intent. This covers multiple sub-tasks evaluated both automatically and by humans.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates its IGA model against an ILM baseline, both based on GPT-2.
tasks.scoring_detail: ROUGE-2, self-BLEU-2; Human ratings for fluency, coherence, and adequacy on a 5-point scale (collapsed to 3-point).

tasks.name: Embellishing Paraphrase Generation
tasks.description: Paraphrase a given sentence with the goal of improving writing quality or embellishment, rather than simplification.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates its IGA model against the STRAP model.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEURT, BLEU, self-BLEU, iBLEU

benchmarks.name: Creative Writing User Study
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates the utility of an AI writing assistant in an interactive, open-ended creative story writing task with human authors, measuring both interaction patterns and subjective preferences.

tasks.name: AI-Assisted Story Writing
tasks.description: Participants write short stories in response to prompts using one of three modes: from scratch, with an uncontrolled infilling model (ILM), or with the intent-guided assistant (IGA).
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a human-in-the-loop generation task where the AI assists a human author.
tasks.model_type_notes: The study compares writing with IGA, ILM, and no AI assistance.
tasks.scoring_detail: User interaction logs (# clicks, tokens kept/deleted/inserted), post-session survey (user preference, Likert scale ratings for quality, fluency, satisfaction), unigram precision/recall/F1 of generated text vs final text.

title: How do Humans and Language Models Reason About Creativity? A Comparative Analysis

benchmarks.name: Design Problems Task (DPT)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An open-ended task for generating solutions to real-world STEM challenges, used in this paper to evaluate the creative reasoning and judgment of LLMs compared to human experts.

tasks.name: Fine-grained Creativity Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating existing solutions to STEM design problems on 5-point Likert scales for four facets: originality, cleverness, remoteness, and uncommonness.
tasks.origin_paper: Patterson et al. (2025) used originality ratings; this paper extends it with cleverness, remoteness, and uncommonness facets based on theory from Silvia et al. (2008).
tasks.model_type_notes: CLAUDE-3.5-HAIKU and GPT-4O-MINI were tested and compared against human expert ratings.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson correlation (r) and Cohen's Kappa between LLM ratings and ground truth scores, and between different rating facets.

tasks.name: Explanation Generation for Originality Ratings
tasks.description: Generating a 1-2 sentence explanation to justify the originality score given to a solution.
tasks.model_type_notes: CLAUDE-3.5-HAIKU and GPT-4O-MINI were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Explanations were not scored for quality but were analyzed for linguistic features in a subsequent task.

tasks.name: Linguistic Analysis of Explanations
tasks.description: Using LLMs to classify generated explanations for the presence or absence of five linguistic markers: past/future expressions, perceptual details, causal/analytical, comparative, and cleverness language.
tasks.origin_name: Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) analysis
tasks.origin_paper: Inspired by Orwig et al. (2024), but extended by using LLMs as classifiers instead of LIWC, justified by Rathje et al. (2024).
tasks.model_type_notes: CLAUDE-3.5-SONNET and GPT-4O were used as the classifiers.
tasks.scoring_detail: Binary classification (present/absent) for linguistic markers, with distributions compared using Mann-Whitney U test and Cramer's V.

title: MiQA: A Benchmark for Inference on Metaphorical Questions

benchmarks.name: MiQA (Metaphorical Inference Questions and Answers)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Proposes a new benchmark to assess reasoning with conventional metaphors, a form of non-literal and figurative language understanding related to creative language use. It uses open-ended and multiple-choice tasks that require distinguishing between literal and metaphorical interpretations.

tasks.name: implies-questions
tasks.description: A binary-choice task where a model is given a metaphorical premise and must select the correct implication from two choices: one based on a correct metaphorical interpretation and one based on an incorrect literal interpretation.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a multiple-choice question answering task where the model evaluates the likelihood of two given options.
tasks.scoring_detail: Model accuracy based on log likelihood of choices; Human accuracy baseline.

tasks.name: implied-by-questions
tasks.description: A binary-choice task where a model is given a literal conclusion and must select the correct premise that implies it from two choices: one literal and one metaphorical.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a multiple-choice question answering task where the model evaluates the likelihood of two given options.
tasks.scoring_detail: Model accuracy based on log likelihood of choices; Human accuracy baseline.

tasks.name: Generative Task
tasks.description: An open-ended task where the model is prompted with a metaphorical premise and a potential (but incorrect) literal implication (e.g., 'My future looks bright. Could that imply that I could use sunglasses?'), and must generate a textual response.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating of generated answers as 'correct', 'wrong', or 'ambiguous'. Accuracy calculated with correct=1, ambiguous=0.5. Inter-rater reliability measured with ICC.

title: VBench-2.0: Advancing Video Generation Benchmark Suite for Intrinsic Faithfulness

benchmarks.name: VBench-2.0
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, comprehensive benchmark suite for evaluating advanced capabilities ('intrinsic faithfulness') of video generation models. It includes a specific dimension for creativity and uses open-ended video generation tasks.

tasks.name: Human Anatomy
tasks.description: Detects anomalies in the appearance and structure of the human body, hands, and faces in generated videos using specialist anomaly detection models.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage of frames without detected anomalies from three specialist ViT-based detectors (body, hands, face).

tasks.name: Human Temporal Consistency - Clothes
tasks.description: Assesses whether a person's clothing remains consistent throughout the video.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using LLaVA-Video-7B.

tasks.name: Human Temporal Consistency - Identity
tasks.description: Evaluates if a person's facial identity remains consistent across frames by measuring facial feature similarity.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Facial feature similarity score using ArcFace.

tasks.name: Diversity
tasks.description: Measures the inter-sample variation (style and content) across multiple videos generated from the same text prompt.
tasks.origin_paper: Gatys et al., A neural algorithm of artistic style, 2015
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Inter-sample variation calculated from VGG-19 feature representations.

tasks.name: Composition
tasks.description: Measures the model's ability to generate novel and uncommon compositions, such as species combinations or unusual actions.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using a VLM.

tasks.name: Dynamic Attribute
tasks.description: Tests if models can modify an object's attribute (e.g., color, size) mid-video as specified in the prompt.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using a VLM.

tasks.name: Dynamic Spatial Relationship
tasks.description: Assesses if models accurately reposition objects in response to spatial instructions in the prompt.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using a VLM.

tasks.name: Motion Order Understanding
tasks.description: Evaluates if models generate a sequence of actions or motions in the specified order.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judges the alignment of a VLM-generated action sequence caption with the prompt.

tasks.name: Human Interaction
tasks.description: Assesses if models can generate plausible interactions between two humans as described in the prompt.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judges the alignment of a VLM-generated interaction description with the prompt.

tasks.name: Complex Plot
tasks.description: Tests a model's ability to construct multi-scene narratives from long prompts describing multi-stage events.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judges the alignment of VLM-generated plot summaries with ground-truth plot points.

tasks.name: Complex Landscape
tasks.description: Evaluates if models faithfully follow long-form landscape descriptions that include multiple scene transitions.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judges the alignment of VLM-generated landscape descriptions with ground-truth plot points.

tasks.name: Camera Motion
tasks.description: Evaluates if models can generate specified camera movements (e.g., pan, zoom, orbit).
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification of camera motion based on point tracking with CoTracker-v2 and heuristics.

tasks.name: Mechanics
tasks.description: Evaluates if generated videos follow basic mechanical principles such as gravity, buoyancy, and stress.
tasks.origin_paper: Meng et al., Towards world simulator..., 2024
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using a VLM on expected physical behavior.

tasks.name: Thermotics
tasks.description: Evaluates how well models simulate thermal state transitions like vaporization, liquefaction, and sublimation.
tasks.origin_paper: Meng et al., Towards world simulator..., 2024
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using a VLM on thermal state changes.

tasks.name: Material
tasks.description: Evaluates if models correctly depict material properties such as color mixing, hardness, combustion, and solubility.
tasks.origin_paper: Meng et al., Towards world simulator..., 2024
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using a VLM on material properties.

tasks.name: Multi-View Consistency
tasks.description: Assesses the 3D geometric consistency of objects and scenes when viewed from different angles or with camera movement.
tasks.origin_paper: Li et al., Sora generates videos with stunning geometrical consistency, 2024
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Feature matching stability (SIFT, FLANN, RANSAC) adjusted by camera motion speed (RAFT).

tasks.name: Motion Rationality
tasks.description: Evaluates whether generated motions lead to correct and plausible real-world consequences (e.g., food is reduced after being eaten).
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from video-based multi-question answering using a VLM on the consequences of motions.

tasks.name: Instance Preservation
tasks.description: Detects unnatural entity states such as sudden merging, splitting, appearance, or disappearance of objects.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on text-to-video diffusion models like Sora, Kling, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX-1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score from a fine-tuned VLM-based (Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct) clip-level anomaly detector.

title: VideoCanvas: Unified Video Completion from Arbitrary Spatiotemporal Patches via In-Context Conditioning

benchmarks.name: VideoCanvasBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for arbitrary spatio-temporal video completion, a creative and open-ended generation task, and uses it to systematically evaluate video diffusion models.

tasks.name: AnyP2V (Any-Timestamp Patch-to-Video)
tasks.description: Generate a complete video from one or more user-specified patches placed at arbitrary spatial locations and timestamps. The benchmark includes single-frame, two-frame, and three-frame conditions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent video diffusion model with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: PSNR, FVD, Aesthetic Quality, Imaging Quality, Temporal Coherence, Dynamic Degree, User study (Visual Quality, Semantic Quality, Overall Preference win rates).

tasks.name: AnyI2V (Any-Timestamp Image-to-Video)
tasks.description: Generate a complete video from one or more user-specified full frames placed at arbitrary timestamps. The benchmark includes single-frame, two-frame, and three-frame conditions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent video diffusion model with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: PSNR, FVD, Aesthetic Quality, Imaging Quality, Temporal Coherence, Dynamic Degree, User study (Visual Quality, Semantic Quality, Overall Preference win rates).

tasks.name: AnyV2V (Video Transition)
tasks.description: Generate a seamless and logical transition between two entirely different, non-homologous video clips, where one clip provides the start and the other provides the end.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent video diffusion model with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: PSNR, FVD, Aesthetic Quality, Imaging Quality, Temporal Coherence, Dynamic Degree, User study (Visual Quality, Semantic Quality, Overall Preference win rates).

tasks.name: AnyV2V (Video Inpainting)
tasks.description: Fill in masked (missing) rectangular regions within a video with plausible and temporally consistent content.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent video diffusion model with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: PSNR, FVD, Aesthetic Quality, Imaging Quality, Temporal Coherence, Dynamic Degree, User study (Visual Quality, Semantic Quality, Overall Preference win rates).

tasks.name: AnyV2V (Video Outpainting)
tasks.description: Extend the video frame by generating plausible content beyond the original boundaries, extrapolating the scene.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent video diffusion model with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: PSNR, FVD, Aesthetic Quality, Imaging Quality, Temporal Coherence, Dynamic Degree, User study (Visual Quality, Semantic Quality, Overall Preference win rates).

tasks.name: Single-frame I2V Alignment Ablation
tasks.description: An ablation study task to evaluate different pixel-frame alignment strategies by generating a video from a single image condition at specific target frame indices (e.g., 2, 3, 4).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent video diffusion model with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: Per-frame PSNR, Dynamic Degree, Imaging Quality.

title: VLMgineer: Vision Language Models as Robotic Toolsmiths

benchmarks.name: ROBOTOOLBENCH
