benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, comprehensive simulation benchmark designed specifically to evaluate the creativity and physical reasoning of AI models in designing and using tools for robotic manipulation tasks.

tasks.name: BringCube
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to bring a red cube, initially out of reach, closer to a target zone on a desk.
tasks.origin_paper: James et al., "RLBench: The robot learning benchmark & learning environment", 2020
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on cube's proximity to target, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: CleanTable
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to push multiple small cubes (representing dust) into a circular target zone.
tasks.origin_paper: James et al., "RLBench: The robot learning benchmark & learning environment", 2020
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on average distance cubes are pushed toward goal, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: DislodgeCube
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to dislodge a cube confined within a transparent pipe through one of two openings.
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on cube's progress toward either pipe exit, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: ElevatePlate
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to securely lift a white plate from a desk.
tasks.origin_paper: Liu et al., "Learning to design and use tools for robotic manipulation", 2023
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on how far the plate has been lifted, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: GatherSpheres
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to gather and elevate as many small spheres as possible from a container.
tasks.origin_paper: James et al., "RLBench: The robot learning benchmark & learning environment", 2020
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on the average height spheres are lifted, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: HighObject
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to move a green cube from a high shelf into a box on a lower level.
tasks.origin_paper: Liu et al., "Learning to design and use tools for robotic manipulation", 2023
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on whether the cube is in the box and its distance, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: LiftBox
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to lift a brown box on a desk above a specific height threshold.
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on how high the box is lifted, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: MoveBall
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to move a red ball from its left side to its right side on a desk.
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on ball's proximity to target and speed, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: OneBook
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to pull out the middle book from a row of five books without disturbing the others.
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on pulling the target book while keeping others still, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: ScoreGoal
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to hit a hockey puck into a goal that is far away.
tasks.origin_paper: James et al., "RLBench: The robot learning benchmark & learning environment", 2020
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on whether the puck is in the goal, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: SnatchCookie
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to take at least one cookie from a transparent jar.
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on whether a cookie is lifted out of the jar, Total distance traversed by end-effector

tasks.name: TurkeyLegs
tasks.description: A robot must design a tool to transfer all turkey legs from a pot into a box without moving the pot.
tasks.scoring_detail: Task-specific normalized reward (0-1) based on getting legs into the box while keeping the pot still, Total distance traversed by end-effector

title: TF1-EN-3M: Three Million Synthetic Moral Fables for Training Small, Open Language Models

benchmarks.name: Fable Generation Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new multi-faceted framework for evaluating the creative task of fable generation, using an explicit 'Creativity' metric and a mix of LLM-as-judge and automatic scoring methods on an open-ended generation task.

tasks.name: LLM-based Quality Scoring
tasks.description: An LLM critic, prompted with a rubric, assigns scores from 1 to 10 to generated fables along four dimensions: Grammar & Style, Creativity, Moral Clarity, and Prompt Adherence.
tasks.scoring_detail: 1-10 scores for Grammar & Style, Creativity, Moral Clarity, Prompt Adherence

tasks.name: Age Group Classification
tasks.description: An LLM classifies each generated fable into one of five age brackets (A: 0–3 yrs, B: 4–7 yrs, C: 8–11 yrs, D: 12–15 yrs, E: 16+ yrs) based on vocabulary, theme, and complexity.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification into one of five age brackets (A-E)

tasks.name: Reference-Free Corpus Evaluation
tasks.description: Corpus-level, unreferenced statistics are computed to assess diversity (Self-BLEU), lexical richness (Distinct-1), and readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of the generated fables.
tasks.origin_paper: Zhu et al., 2018; Li et al., 2016; Kincaid et al., 1975
tasks.scoring_detail: Self-BLEU, Distinct-1, Flesch Reading Ease scores

title: Do Androids Laugh at Electric Sheep? Humor “Understanding” Benchmarks from The New Yorker Caption Contest

benchmarks.name: New Yorker Cartoon Caption Contest Humor 'Understanding' Benchmarks
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a suite of three tasks based on the New Yorker Cartoon Caption Contest to evaluate AI's ability to understand humor, a key aspect of creativity. It includes tasks for matching captions to cartoons, ranking caption quality, and generating explanations of jokes, with evaluations on various multimodal and language models.

tasks.name: Matching
tasks.description: Given a cartoon, the model must select the correct caption from five choices. The single correct caption is a finalist for the cartoon, while the four distractors are finalist captions from other, different cartoons.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a 5-way multiple choice classification task.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests both vision-language models (CLIP, OFA) on raw pixels and large language models (T5, GPT series) on human-authored image descriptions.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Quality Ranking
tasks.description: Given a cartoon and two captions written for it (one finalist and one non-finalist), the model must identify which caption was rated as higher quality.
tasks.origin_paper: Shahaf et al. (2015); Radev et al. (2016)
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a binary classification task.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests both vision-language models (CLIP, OFA) on raw pixels and large language models (T5, GPT series) on human-authored image descriptions.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (NYAcc and CrowdAcc)

tasks.name: Explanation Generation
tasks.description: Given a cartoon and its winning caption, the model must generate a free-form text explanation of why the combination is funny.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests both vision-language models (OFA composed with an LLM) on raw pixels and large language models (T5, GPT series) on human-authored image descriptions.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise human preference, BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, Perplexity

title: Word2Minecraft: Generating 3D Game Levels through Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Word2Minecraft
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new system and a comprehensive, multi-faceted evaluation framework for a creative, open-ended task: generating 3D game levels from text stories using LLMs. It reports empirical results for several AI systems.

tasks.name: Minecraft Level Generation
tasks.description: The core task of the Word2Minecraft system, which generates a playable 3D Minecraft level from a structured story. This includes story generation, map layout, tile scaling, and sub-map creation for specific objectives.
tasks.scoring_detail: Evaluated via a suite of metrics including story coherence, diversity, enjoyment, aesthetics, and functionality.

tasks.name: Story Coherence Evaluation (Metric-based)
tasks.description: Automatically assesses how well generated levels match their original stories using direct LLM assessment and cosine similarity between original and LLM-reconstructed stories.
tasks.scoring_detail: Direct coherence score (from LLM), Cosine similarity (using text-embedding-3-large)

tasks.name: Story Coherence Evaluation (Human-based)
tasks.description: A user study where participants match stories to top-down views of main maps, objectives to sub-maps, and identify levels generated from the same story.
tasks.scoring_detail: Participant choice accuracy

tasks.name: Diversity Evaluation
tasks.description: Measures the environmental richness and variety of generated game levels by analyzing the distribution of tile types.
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of distinct tile types, Shannon Entropy

tasks.name: Enjoyment Evaluation
tasks.description: Measures the playability and challenge of generated levels using pathfinding and map layout metrics. Compares LLM performance against an Evolutionary Algorithm baseline.
tasks.model_type_notes: LLMs (GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o-Mini) and an Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) baseline.
tasks.scoring_detail: Playability (path existence), Valid Unwalkable Tiles Ratio (VUTR), Average Shortest Path to All Objectives (ASPAO)

tasks.name: Aesthetic and Functionality Evaluation
tasks.description: A user study where participants watch gameplay videos of generated levels and rank them based on visual appeal and functionality.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human preference counts/rankings

tasks.name: Ablation Study Evaluation
tasks.description: A user study where participants rank four variations of a level (generated with/without scaling algorithm, by two different LLMs) to assess component impact.
tasks.scoring_detail: Composite score based on human rankings

title: Salsa as a Nonverbal Embodied Language - The CoMPAS3D Dataset and Benchmarks

benchmarks.name: CoMPAS3D
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new dataset for improvised, expressive salsa dancing, a form of creative and embodied communication. The associated tasks involve generating novel, stylistic, and interactive dance motion, which is an open-ended creative task.

tasks.name: Solo Dance Generation
tasks.description: Generate a 3D motion sequence for a single dancer (leader or follower) based on an accompanying music track and a specified proficiency level (beginner, intermediate, or professional).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses SalsaAgent, a model built upon the MotionLLM text-to-motion backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fréchet Inception Distance (kinematic FIDk, graphical FIDg), diversity (Divk, Divg), Beat-Align Score (BAS)

tasks.name: Duet Dance Generation
tasks.description: Generate a follower's 3D motion sequence conditioned on the leader's motion, the shared music, and a specified proficiency level.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses SalsaAgent, a model built upon the MotionLLM text-to-motion backbone.
tasks.scoring_detail: FIDk, FIDg, Divk, Divg, FID with cross-distance (FIDcd), Div with cross-distance (Divcd), Beat Echo Degree (BED), Beat-Align Score (BAS)

tasks.name: Move Classification
tasks.description: Classify 3D motion segments into one of 30 predefined salsa move categories using the dataset's annotations.
tasks.task_type_notes: Classification
tasks.model_type_notes: K Nearest Neighbours, XG-Boost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron on VQ-VAE embeddings.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, weighted F1-score

title: LLM-SRBench: A New Benchmark for Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: LLM-SRBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark for scientific equation discovery, a form of creative hypothesis generation, using LLMs. It involves open-ended tasks and reports empirical results with multiple AI systems.

tasks.name: LSR-Transform
tasks.description: Discovering equations that are symbolic transformations of 100 common physics equations from the Feynman benchmark. The goal is to test reasoning beyond memorization of common forms by presenting less common mathematical representations of the same physical problem.
tasks.scoring_detail: Symbolic Accuracy (SA) via GPT-4o judge, Accuracy to tolerance (Acc0.1), Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE)

tasks.name: LSR-Synth
tasks.description: Discovering novel synthetic equations across four scientific domains (chemistry, biology, physics, material science). The equations combine known scientific terms with novel synthetic terms to require data-driven reasoning.
tasks.scoring_detail: Symbolic Accuracy (SA) via GPT-4o judge, Accuracy to tolerance (Acc0.1), Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE) on in-domain and out-of-domain data

benchmarks.name: Feynman benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for scientific equation discovery, a form of creative hypothesis generation. Used for comparison to demonstrate the increased difficulty of the new LLM-SRBench.

tasks.name: Equation Discovery on Feynman Problems
tasks.description: Discovering the original 100 physics equations from the Feynman benchmark from data. This task was used as a baseline to compare against the performance on the new LSR-Transform dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Symbolic accuracy (via GPT-4o judge), Numeric precision (Acc0.1)

title: Vietnamese Poem Generation & The Prospect Of Cross-Language Poem-To-Poem Translation

benchmarks.name: Vietnamese Poem Quality Scoring System
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Presents a custom, automated scoring system for evaluating the quality of generated Vietnamese poems based on structural rules like length, rhyme, and tone. This is an open-ended generation task focused on a creative domain.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Tuan Nguyen et al., 2021 (SP-gpt2: Semantics improvement in vietnamese poetry generation)

tasks.name: Text-to-Poem Generation
tasks.description: Generating Vietnamese poems of various genres from natural language prompts that specify a theme, style, and/or keywords.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on GPT-3 (Davinci, Babbage), BLOOM, and ChatGPT (zero-shot).
tasks.scoring_detail: A custom weighted score based on line length, tonal patterns, and rhyme scheme rules for different Vietnamese poetry genres.

tasks.name: Poem-to-Poem Generation
tasks.description: Generating a Vietnamese 'luc bat' poem from a paraphrased, non-poetic text version of another poem, with the goal of capturing the full context and content.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on GPT-3 Babbage.
tasks.scoring_detail: A custom weighted score based on line length, tonal patterns, and rhyme scheme rules for the 'luc bat' genre.

tasks.name: Blind Test Poem Generation
tasks.description: Generating a Vietnamese poem from a prompt where the genre is not specified. The generated poem's genre is first identified by a classifier, and then the poem is scored according to that genre's rules.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on BLOOM, Babbage, and ChatGPT.
tasks.scoring_detail: A custom weighted score based on line length, tonal patterns, and rhyme scheme rules, applied after a BERT classifier identifies the generated genre.

benchmarks.name: Vietnamese Poem Genre Classification
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a standard, closed-ended classification task (identifying a poem's genre from line lengths) rather than a creativity evaluation. It was used as an auxiliary tool for the 'Blind Test' but is not a creativity benchmark itself.

tasks.name: Genre Classification from Line Word Counts
tasks.description: A BERT-based classifier was trained to identify the genre of a poem based on a string containing the word count of each line.
tasks.task_type_notes: classification
tasks.model_type_notes: BERT-based classifier
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: ByGPT5: End-to-End Style-conditioned Poetry Generation with Token-free Language Models

benchmarks.name: Style-conditioned Quatrain Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Presents a new evaluation framework for a creative task (style-conditioned poetry generation). It uses both automatic metrics and human judgments to assess AI-generated poems based on creative constraints like rhyme, meter, and alliteration.

tasks.name: Automatic Style Adherence Evaluation
tasks.description: Models generate quatrains conditioned on a combination of rhyme scheme, meter, and alliteration level. The generated poems are then automatically scored for adherence to these styles using classifiers, as well as for coherence.
tasks.model_type_notes: ByGPT5, GPT-2, ByT5, mT5
tasks.scoring_detail: Rhyme Score (classifier-based recall), Alliteration Score (classifier-based accuracy), Meter Score (classifier-based accuracy), Coherence (BERT next sentence prediction)

tasks.name: Human Evaluation of Poetry (Best-Worst Scaling)
tasks.description: Human annotators evaluate generated quatrains using Best-Worst Scaling (BWS) on the properties of rhyme, meter, and human likeness.
tasks.model_type_notes: ByGPT5 (base), GPT-2 (base), ByT5 (small), mT5 (small), and human-written poems
tasks.scoring_detail: Best-Worst Scaling scores for rhyme, meter, and human likeness

tasks.name: Emotion-conditioned Poetry Generation
tasks.description: Models are conditioned on emotions to generate quatrains. The output is evaluated by a classifier to measure the recall of the intended emotions.
tasks.model_type_notes: ByGPT5, GPT-2, ByT5, mT5
tasks.scoring_detail: Recall of correctly classified emotions

tasks.name: Extractive Memorization Test
tasks.description: Measures the rate at which generated poems are verbatim or near-verbatim copies of poems from the training data (QuaTrain) to assess originality.
tasks.model_type_notes: ByGPT5, GPT-2, ByT5, mT5
tasks.scoring_detail: Ratcliff-Obershelp similarity score > 0.7

tasks.name: Comparison with ChatGPT on Rhyme Adherence
tasks.description: ChatGPT and ByGPT5 are prompted to generate quatrains with specific rhyme schemes. The outputs are compared using an automatic rhyme scorer to determine which model adheres better to the constraints.
tasks.model_type_notes: ByGPT5, ChatGPT
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic rhyme scorer (classifier-based)

title: ProteinBench: A Holistic Evaluation of Protein Foundation Models

benchmarks.name: ProteinBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on highly domain-specific scientific generation (protein design and conformation) rather than general or artistic creativity. Tasks are generative but success is measured by biophysical plausibility and functional metrics, not creative attributes like originality or humor.

tasks.name: Inverse Folding
tasks.description: Predict an optimal amino acid sequence for a given target protein structure, considering factors such as stability, refoldability, and potential functionality.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., ProteinMPNN, ESM-IF1, LM-DESIGN, ESM3)
tasks.scoring_detail: Sequence Recovery (AAR), Refoldability (scTM, scRMSD via AlphaFold2), Stability (pLDDT via AlphaFold2)

tasks.name: Protein Backbone Design
tasks.description: Creating new protein folds to achieve de novo design objectives, expanding the repertoire of protein structures beyond those found in nature.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., Rfdiffusion, Frameflow, Chroma)
tasks.scoring_detail: Quality (scTM, scRMSD), Novelty (Max TM score to PDB database), Diversity (Pairwise TM, Max Cluster)

tasks.name: Protein Sequence Design
tasks.description: Generate amino acid sequences of desired properties, such as quality, diversity and novelty, evaluated on both sequence and structural characteristics.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., ProGen2, EvoDiff, DPLM, ESM3)
tasks.scoring_detail: Sequence Naturalness (perplexity), Structural Quality (pLDDT), Structural Diversity (pairwise TM, Max Cluster), Structural Novelty (Max TM score to PDB database)

tasks.name: Structure and Sequence Co-design
tasks.description: Simultaneously optimizing both the backbone structure and amino acid sequence of a protein to achieve desired properties or functions.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., ProteinGenerator, ProtPardelle, Multiflow, ESM3)
tasks.scoring_detail: Sequence-Structure Compatibility (scTM, scRMSD), Diversity (Max Cluster), Novelty (Max TM score to PDB database)

tasks.name: Motif Scaffolding
tasks.description: Designing a protein structure (scaffold) that incorporates a specific functional motif or binding site in the correct geometry for its function.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., RFdiffusion, TDS, FrameFlow, EvoDiff, DPLM, ESM3)
tasks.scoring_detail: Number of designable scaffolds, Motif RMSD, Scaffold RMSD

tasks.name: Antibody Design
tasks.description: Generate antibodies that can specifically bind to a given antigen, simplified to the design of the third Complementarity-Determining Region in the heavy chain (CDR-H3).
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., HERN, MEAN, DiffAb, AbDPO)
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (AAR, RMSD, TM-score), Functionality (Binding Energy), Specificity (Sequence Similarity, PHR), Rationality (CN-Score, Clashes, Sequence Naturalness, Total Energy, scRMSD)

tasks.name: Protein Folding (Single-state Prediction)
tasks.description: Predicting the single folded 3D structure of a protein from its amino acid sequence.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., AlphaFold2, OpenFold, ESMFold)
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (TM score, RMSD, GDT, lDDT), Quality (CA clash rate, Peptide bond break rate)

tasks.name: Multiple-state Prediction
tasks.description: Predicting two or more distinct conformational states of a protein that have been observed under different conditions.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., EigenFold, Str2Str, AlphaFlow, ConfDiff)
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (Ensemble TM score, Ensemble RMSD), Diversity (pairwise TM/RMSD), Quality (CA clash rate, Peptide bond break rate)

tasks.name: Distribution Prediction
tasks.description: Generating a sample distribution of protein conformations that resembles a target distribution, such as from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations.
tasks.model_type_notes: Protein Foundation Models (e.g., AlphaFlow, ConfDiff, MSA-subsampling)
tasks.scoring_detail: Flexibility (Pearson r), Distributional Accuracy (Wasserstein distance, PCA similarity), Ensemble Observables (Jaccard similarity, Mutual Information), Diversity (Pairwise RMSD, RMSF), Quality (CA clash rate, Peptide bond break rate)

title: Calligrapher: Freestyle Text Image Customization

benchmarks.name: style-centric text customization benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new benchmark with a training and test set for evaluating AI models on artistic typography generation, a creative, open-ended task. It includes empirical results for several diffusion models.

tasks.name: Text Image Customization and Generation
tasks.description: A set of tasks to evaluate a model's ability to generate stylized text images. This includes: 1) Self-reference customization (modifying text while preserving the original style), 2) Cross-reference customization (transferring style from a different text image), 3) Non-text reference customization (transferring style from a non-text image), and 4) Reference-based generation (creating a new image from scratch).
tasks.model_type_notes: The base models used are FLUX and FLUX-Fill.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics (FID, CLIP similarity, DINO similarity, OCR Accuracy) and a human user study rating Style Sync, Text Matching, and Aesthetics (1-4 scale) plus Overall preference %.

title: I Dream My Painting: Connecting MLLMs and Diffusion Models via Prompt Generation for Text-Guided Multi-Mask Inpainting

benchmarks.name: WikiArt (ArtGraph)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used to evaluate a new creative generation task (multi-mask inpainting and prompt generation) on artistic images, which requires creative interpretation and generation.

tasks.name: Multi-Mask Prompt Generation
tasks.description: An MLLM (LLaVA) generates multiple text prompts for corresponding colored masks overlaid on an artistic image, predicting the content of the masked regions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses LLaVA, a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (noun chunk matching), BLEU, ROUGE-L, CLIPSim, Distinct-N, Self-BLEU

tasks.name: Multi-Mask Inpainting
tasks.description: A diffusion model (Stable Diffusion) simultaneously inpaints multiple masked regions in an artistic image, with each region guided by a distinct text prompt.
tasks.scoring_detail: FID, LPIPS, PSNR, CLIP-IQA, CLIPSim-T2I, CLIPSim-I2I

benchmarks.name: Densely Captioned Images (DCI)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used to evaluate the new creative generation task (multi-mask inpainting and prompt generation) on photographic images, demonstrating the method's generalizability.

tasks.name: Multi-Mask Prompt Generation
tasks.description: An MLLM (LLaVA) generates multiple text prompts for corresponding colored masks overlaid on a photographic image, predicting the content of the masked regions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses LLaVA, a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, BLEU@1, CLIPSim

tasks.name: Multi-Mask Inpainting
tasks.description: A diffusion model (Stable Diffusion) simultaneously inpaints multiple masked regions in a photographic image, with each region guided by a distinct text prompt.
tasks.scoring_detail: LPIPS, PSNR, CLIPSim-T2I

title: Assessing the Creativity of LLMs in Proposing Novel Solutions to Mathematical Problems

benchmarks.name: CREATIVEMATH
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed to evaluate the creativity of LLMs in a mathematical context by tasking them with generating novel solutions to problems with known solutions. It is an open-ended generation task with empirical results.

tasks.name: Novel Mathematical Solution Generation
tasks.description: Given a mathematical problem and k known solutions, an LLM is tasked with generating a new, correct solution that is distinct from the provided ones.
tasks.scoring_detail: A panel of 3 LLMs (GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro) evaluates correctness (unanimous vote) and novelty (majority vote). Metrics include Correctness Ratio, Novelty Ratio, and Novel-Unknown Ratio.

tasks.name: Pairwise Solution Similarity Analysis
tasks.description: Compares novel solutions generated by pairs of different LLMs for the same problem to measure their similarity and map their solution spaces.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper implies the same LLM evaluator setup as the main task is used.
tasks.scoring_detail: An LLM evaluator judges if two generated solutions are distinct. A similarity score is computed as the ratio of similar solutions.

title: Creative4U: MLLMs-based Advertising Creative Image Selector with Comparative Reasoning

benchmarks.name: CreativePair
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on the task of selecting the better advertising creative image from a pair, including generating comparative reasoning. This is a core creativity task focused on effectiveness and explainability.

tasks.name: Explainable Creative Image Selection
tasks.description: Given a pair of creative images, product title, and user queries, the model must select the image more likely to be clicked and generate a detailed comparative reasoning for its choice, structured according to the paper's 'Creative Evaluation Protocol'.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task requires both generating a textual reasoning (generate) and making a final selection (evaluate).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Model), which is synonymous with VLM in this context. The primary model is Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, and baselines are also VLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Selection accuracy, Qwen-Score (LLM-based evaluation of reasoning quality)

benchmarks.name: Online A/B test for Creative Selection
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A real-world evaluation of an AI system's ability to select effective advertising creatives. The task is to predict which images will perform best with actual users, a direct measure of creative effectiveness.

tasks.name: Top-10 Creative Selection
tasks.description: For a given ad set with N candidate creatives, the model selects the top-10 most effective images. These selections are then deployed in a live e-commerce environment to measure their performance against baseline selection methods.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model's primary evaluated output is the ranked list of selected creatives.
tasks.model_type_notes: The Creative4U model, a VLM, is evaluated in this test.
tasks.scoring_detail: Click-Through Rate (CTR), Conversion Rate (CVR), Revenue Per Mille (RPM)

title: A Causality-Aware Paradigm for Evaluating Creativity of Multimodal Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Oogiri-GO Standard Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset (Oogiri-GO) and a set of standard evaluation tasks (choice, ranking) to measure the creative humor generation capabilities of MLLMs.

tasks.name: Choice Questions (mTn)
tasks.description: MLLMs select n creative/humorous responses from m options (specific formats include 2T1, 3T1, 4T1, and 5T2) for a given multimodal prompt from the Oogiri-GO dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both multimodal models (MLLMs/VLMs) and text-only LLMs on the respective subsets of the data.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Ranking Questions
tasks.description: MLLMs rank five candidate responses for a given multimodal prompt from the Oogiri-GO dataset based on creativity and humor, compared against human preference data.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both multimodal models (MLLMs/VLMs) and text-only LLMs on the respective subsets of the data.
tasks.scoring_detail: Top-1 accuracy, Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG)

benchmarks.name: LoTbench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A novel interactive benchmark designed to measure MLLM creativity by quantifying the effort (number of rounds) required to generate a high-quality creative response, addressing issues like information leakage and interpretability in standard evaluations.

tasks.name: Interactive Creative Response Generation
tasks.description: In a multi-round interactive process, an MLLM fills in a masked key text of a creative response. The goal is to generate a response that achieves a 'different approach but equally satisfactory outcome' (DAESO) compared to a human-level creative response (HHCR) in as few rounds as possible.
tasks.scoring_detail: Creativity score (Sc) calculated from the number of rounds required to generate a response judged as DAESO by a causal LLM evaluator (E1).

benchmarks.name: Human Evaluation for Creativity
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A user study was conducted to directly assess the creativity of model-generated responses, providing a human-centric baseline for creativity.

tasks.name: User Preference Study
tasks.description: Human participants were asked to choose the most creative and humorous responses generated by different MLLMs for questions from the Oogiri-GO dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task evaluates the output of generative models via human judgment.
tasks.scoring_detail: User preference voting percentage

benchmarks.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation for Creativity
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An experiment was conducted to assess the ability of LLMs to judge creativity in alignment with human preferences, which is a meta-evaluation of a common scoring method.

tasks.name: Creative Response Ranking
tasks.description: LLMs were tasked with ranking five generated creative responses. Their rankings were then compared against a ground truth ranking derived from human preferences.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tested Qwen-VL and its fine-tuned variants as judges.
tasks.scoring_detail: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (SP) against human preference ranking; ranking error distribution

benchmarks.name: MMMU
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a general multimodal cognition and reasoning benchmark, not a creativity benchmark. It was used only for a correlation analysis to validate the new creativity benchmarks, not for direct creativity evaluation.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Yue et al., MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI, 2024

tasks.name: Correlation Analysis
tasks.description: The paper calculates the Pearson correlation coefficient between MLLM performance on MMMU and their performance on the new creativity benchmarks (Standard Evaluation and LoTbench).
tasks.task_type_notes: Correlation analysis between benchmark results. No models were run on this benchmark in this paper; existing results were used for comparison.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson correlation coefficient

title: The Geometry of Creative Variability: How Credal Sets Expose Calibration Gaps in Language Models

benchmarks.name: Credal Set Analysis for Creative Variability
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new geometric framework using credal sets to quantify and evaluate the creative variability of LLMs against a human baseline on an open-ended text generation task.

tasks.name: Creative Story Continuation on WRITINGPROMPTS
tasks.description: Language models generate multiple story continuations for prompts from a curated subset of the WRITINGPROMPTS dataset. The evaluation measures how well the geometric distribution of the model's creative variability (in terms of semantic, lexical, and syntactic diversity) aligns with the distribution of human-written continuations.
tasks.scoring_detail: Calibration score (credal set overlap coefficient), credal set volume, centroid distance, Wasserstein distance, semantic diversity (cosine distance on S-BERT embeddings), lexical diversity (Jaccard distance on unigrams), syntactic diversity (Jaccard distance on POS bigrams).

title: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation

benchmarks.name: Scientist-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for evaluating the end-to-end scientific discovery capabilities of AI agents, including hypothesis generation, implementation, and paper writing, which are core aspects of creative and innovative problem-solving.

tasks.name: Guided Innovation (Level-1)
tasks.description: An AI agent receives explicit research instructions and reference papers, and is tasked with implementing the proposed methodology, running experiments, and generating a technical research paper.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates the AI-Researcher framework, which is a multi-agent system built on LLMs like GPT-4o and Claude-3.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Code implementation Completeness (binary) and Correctness (1-5 scale) rated by LLM agents. Scientific quality of the generated paper is rated by LLM agents on a -3 to +3 scale compared to a human-authored ground truth paper.

tasks.name: Autonomous Exploration (Level-2)
tasks.description: An AI agent receives only reference papers and must independently formulate a novel research direction, implement it, run experiments, and generate a technical research paper.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates the AI-Researcher framework, which is a multi-agent system built on LLMs like GPT-4o and Claude-3.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Code implementation Completeness (binary) and Correctness (1-5 scale) rated by LLM agents. Scientific quality of the generated paper is rated by LLM agents on a -3 to +3 scale compared to a human-authored ground truth paper.

benchmarks.name: Paper Review Agent Validation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a meta-evaluation task that assesses an AI agent's ability to judge scientific quality and novelty, which is a key component of creativity evaluation. It directly tests if an LLM's judgment aligns with human expert peer-review decisions.

tasks.name: ICLR Peer Review Alignment
tasks.description: An LLM-based review agent performs a pairwise comparison of an accepted and a rejected paper from ICLR proceedings to determine if its judgment aligns with the human reviewers' final decision.
tasks.origin_paper: The paper uses accepted/rejected papers from ICLR proceedings from 2021-2023 to construct the validation dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates multiple LLMs as review agents, including Gemini-2.0-flash, GPT-4o, o3-mini, Claude-3.5, and Claude-3.7.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean discriminative rating (-3 to +3), comparable quality detection rate (%), and acceptance prediction accuracy (%) against the ground truth ICLR decisions.

title: Digital Avatars: Framework Development and Their Evaluation

benchmarks.name: Crowd Vote
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An evaluation framework using LLM judges to assess anthropomorphic and creative-adjacent qualities like humor, authenticity, and favorability in LLM-generated text for role-playing tasks. It is an open-ended task with empirical results.

tasks.name: Humor Evaluation
tasks.description: LLM candidates generate responses to prompts in character (e.g., as Joe Biden). A panel of LLM judges with different humor preferences (affiliative, self-enhancing, etc.) vote for the single most humorous response.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates their own prompted LLM, a baseline zero-shot LLM, and Character.ai.
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage of votes from LLM judges for the 'most humorous' response.

tasks.name: Authenticity Evaluation
tasks.description: LLM candidates (and real-world persona transcripts) provide answers to 17 questions from a 2020 US presidential debate. A panel of LLM judges with different personas (e.g., 'a psychologist', 'a political commentator', 'a close family member') vote for the most authentic response.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates their own prompted LLM, a baseline zero-shot LLM, Character.ai, and transcripts of the real-world personas.
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage of votes from LLM judges for the 'most authentic' response.

tasks.name: Favorability Evaluation
tasks.description: LLM candidates (and real-world persona transcripts) provide answers to 17 questions from a 2020 US presidential debate. A panel of LLM judges with personas spanning the US political spectrum ('far-right', 'conservative', 'centrist', 'liberal', 'far-left') vote for the most favorable response.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates their own prompted LLM, a baseline zero-shot LLM, Character.ai, and transcripts of the real-world personas.
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage of votes from LLM judges for the 'most favorable' response.

title: LiveIdeaBench: Evaluating LLMs' Scientific Creativity and Idea Generation with Minimal Context

benchmarks.name: LiveIdeaBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed specifically to evaluate LLMs' divergent thinking and scientific idea generation capabilities from minimal context, which are core aspects of creativity.

tasks.name: Scientific Idea Generation and Evaluation
tasks.description: LLMs generate scientific ideas from a single keyword prompt. A dynamic panel of other state-of-the-art LLMs then evaluates these ideas across five dimensions of creativity: originality, feasibility, clarity, fluency, and flexibility.
tasks.task_type_notes: Models generate ideas, and a panel of LLM judges evaluates them.
tasks.model_type_notes: Over 40 models were tested as idea generators, and the top 10 from LiveBench were used as judges.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judges rate Originality, Feasibility, and Clarity (1-10 scale). Fluency is rated by an LLM judge on a 4-point scale (A-D, mapped to 1-10) based on idea distinctiveness. Flexibility is calculated as the 30th percentile of other scores. A human expert validation study was also conducted on a subset of ideas.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a general intelligence benchmark (measuring reasoning, coding, math), not a creativity benchmark. It was used in the paper for comparative analysis to show that scientific idea generation capability is distinct from general intelligence.

tasks.name: General Intelligence Comparison
tasks.description: The paper uses the overall scores from the LiveBench leaderboard to represent the 'general intelligence' of the tested LLMs. These scores are then correlated with the creativity scores from LiveIdeaBench.
tasks.task_type_notes: Scores from the external benchmark were used for comparison; the tasks were not re-run in this paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall general intelligence scores from the LiveBench leaderboard were used for correlation analysis.

title: LLM Discussion: Enhancing the Creativity of Large Language Models via Discussion Framework and Role-Play

benchmarks.name: Alternative Uses Test (AUT)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A classic divergent thinking task from psychology, used here to evaluate an LLM's ability to generate novel and practical uses for common objects. The paper extends the existing task set with new items.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Wallach, M. A., and Kogan, N., 1965

tasks.name: Alternative Uses Task
tasks.description: Assesses the ability to develop practical and innovative use cases for common objects like a fork or a shoe.
tasks.origin_paper: Wallach, M. A., and Kogan, N., 1965
tasks.model_type_notes: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM (ChatGPT) and human evaluation of Originality (5-point Likert), Elaboration (5-point Likert), Fluency (count), and Flexibility (count).

benchmarks.name: Instances Test
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A divergent thinking task from psychology that measures an LLM's ability to generate varied examples fitting a specific criterion. The paper extends the existing task set with new criteria.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Wallach, M. A., and Kogan, N., 1965

tasks.name: Instances Task
tasks.description: Requires participants to list as many things as possible that follow a specific criterion (e.g., things that move on wheels).
tasks.origin_paper: Wallach, M. A., and Kogan, N., 1965
tasks.model_type_notes: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM (ChatGPT) and human evaluation of Originality (5-point Likert), Elaboration (5-point Likert), Fluency (count), and Flexibility (count).

benchmarks.name: Similarities Test
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A task from psychology that evaluates an LLM's creativity in making connections and identifying commonalities between disparate concepts. The paper extends the existing task set with new pairs.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Wallach, M. A., and Kogan, N., 1965

tasks.name: Similarities Task
tasks.description: Evaluates creativity in making connections by asking participants to brainstorm and link ideas through commonalities between two objects (e.g., how a book and a magazine are alike).
tasks.origin_paper: Wallach, M. A., and Kogan, N., 1965
tasks.model_type_notes: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM (ChatGPT) and human evaluation of Originality (5-point Likert), Elaboration (5-point Likert), Fluency (count), and Flexibility (count).

benchmarks.name: Scientific Creativity Test
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for evaluating an LLM's ability to generate practical and creative solutions to scientific problems, focusing on a specific domain of creativity. The paper extends the existing task set with new problems.

tasks.name: Scientific Creativity Task
tasks.description: Evaluates creativity in scientific contexts and the ability to devise practical and creative solutions to scientific problems, such as improving a regular bicycle.
tasks.model_type_notes: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM (ChatGPT) and human evaluation of Originality (5-point Likert), Elaboration (5-point Likert), Fluency (count), and Flexibility (count).

title: Large Language Models for Classical Chinese Poetry Translation: Benchmarking, Evaluating, and Improving

benchmarks.name: PoetMT
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for classical Chinese poetry translation, a task requiring creative preservation of poetic qualities like rhyme, meter, and elegance, beyond literal accuracy. It uses open-ended generation and judges creative attributes.

tasks.name: Discourse-Level Poetry Translation
tasks.description: Translating 608 full classical Chinese poems into English, with an emphasis on evaluating adequacy, fluency, and poetic elegance (beauty of sound, form, and meaning).
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU, COMET, BLEURT, LLM-based scores (1-5) for Beauty of Sound/Form/Meaning, human evaluation for correlation and error analysis

tasks.name: Sentence-Level Adequacy Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating translation adequacy on a set of 758 sentences, each with a correct and incorrect reference translation, to test the model's handling of historical and commonsense knowledge.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human-judged accuracy (ACC), LLM-based Beauty of Meaning score (LLM-BM), Human-rated Beauty of Meaning score (Human-BM)

title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas

benchmarks.name: Research Idea Execution Study
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a large-scale, controlled study to evaluate the quality of AI-generated research ideas by having human experts execute them and write papers, which are then peer-reviewed. This directly measures a high-level creative capability (scientific ideation) and its practical value.
benchmarks.origin_name: Large-scale human study of LLM research ideas

tasks.name: Ideation Evaluation (Pre-Execution)
tasks.description: Expert human reviewers evaluate the quality of AI-generated (and human-generated) NLP research ideas based on the idea description alone, before any implementation. The scores from this stage are used as a baseline for comparison.
tasks.model_type_notes: An LLM agent based on Claude-3.5-Sonnet was used to generate the ideas.
tasks.scoring_detail: Expert ratings on Novelty, Excitement, Expected Effectiveness, Overall score (1-10 scale).

tasks.name: Execution Evaluation (Post-Execution)
tasks.description: Human experts execute AI-generated (and human-generated) NLP research ideas, write 4-page papers, and submit code. Other expert reviewers then blindly evaluate these executed projects to measure the real-world outcome of the ideas.
tasks.model_type_notes: An LLM agent based on Claude-3.5-Sonnet was used to generate the ideas that were then executed by humans.
tasks.scoring_detail: Expert ratings on Novelty (1-10), Excitement (1-10), Soundness (1-10), Effectiveness (1-10), Overall (1-10), Faithfulness (1-10), Codebase Quality (1-5).

title: Spark: A System for Scientifically Creative Idea Generation

benchmarks.name: JUDGE Model Evaluation on OpenReview
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new evaluation framework and dataset for assessing an LLM's ability to perform a creative/critical task: writing peer reviews for scientific ideas. This directly measures a model's capacity for critical evaluation, a key aspect of scientific creativity.

tasks.name: Review Generation Quality Assessment
tasks.description: A model generates a textual peer review for a scientific abstract from a held-out temporal split of the OpenReview dataset. The quality of the generated review is then evaluated.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests two versions of its JUDGE model: wintermute-tiny (based on Qwen-7B) and wintermute-medium (based on Qwen-72B), comparing them to their base models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative assessment of review quality and RMSE of the final review scores in aggregate.

tasks.name: Explicit Review Score Prediction
tasks.description: A model predicts the explicit numerical review score for a scientific abstract from a held-out set where scores are available.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests two versions of its JUDGE model: wintermute-tiny (based on Qwen-7B) and wintermute-medium (based on Qwen-72B), comparing them to their base models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy of predicting explicit review scores.

title: Prose for a Painting

benchmarks.name: Human Evaluation of Generated Prose for Paintings
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A human evaluation framework designed to assess the creativity, content relevance, and stylistic accuracy of AI-generated artistic prose for paintings.

tasks.name: Shakespearean Prose Generation for Paintings
tasks.description: An AI model generates Shakespearean-style prose based on an input painting. The output is then evaluated by 32 students.
tasks.model_type_notes: A pipeline model combining CNNs for feature extraction and an RNN (actor-critic) for poem generation, followed by a Seq2Seq model for style transfer.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average ratings for content, creativity, and style on a 1-5 Likert scale.

benchmarks.name: Shakespearean Style Transfer Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates a sub-task (style transfer) of a creative pipeline using a standard machine translation metric (BLEU), not a direct creativity metric.

tasks.name: Modern English to Shakespearean Prose Translation
tasks.description: A sequence-to-sequence model translates modern English sentences into Shakespearean style. The quality is measured against a parallel corpus.
tasks.model_type_notes: Seq2Seq models with LSTM encoder/decoder and attention mechanisms.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU score

title: Automatic Extraction of Metaphoric Analogies from Literary Texts: Task Formulation, Dataset Construction, and Evaluation

benchmarks.name: Metaphoric Analogies from Literary Texts Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset and task for evaluating LLMs on their ability to understand and structure non-literal, creative language (metaphoric analogies), which requires high-level reasoning. The tasks are open-ended (extracting phrases, generating implicit concepts) and the paper reports empirical results for several LLMs.

tasks.name: Metaphoric Analogy Extraction
tasks.description: Given a short literary text containing a metaphor and one of the four concepts (T1, T2, S1, or S2), the task is to extract the other three concepts from the text that form the proportional analogy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy based on exact match, overlap, lemmatized expression, and lemmatized head noun matching against gold annotations.

tasks.name: Implicit Term Generation
tasks.description: For analogies where one of the four concepts is implicit (not stated in the text), the task is to generate a relevant concept to complete the analogical frame.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating of relevance on a 0-2 scale (0: incorrect, 1: imperfect, 2: very good).

title: In BLOOM: Creativity and Affinity in Artificial Lyrics and Art

benchmarks.name: Chinese Lyric Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on a creative, open-ended task (song lyric generation) and evaluates the output using both human judgments of creativity and automated metrics.

tasks.name: Human Evaluation of Lyrics
tasks.description: Human reviewers on Amazon Mechanical Turk rated AI-generated (BLOOM-176B) and real Chinese song lyrics for coherence, creativity, affinity (liking), and recognition on a normalized 0-10 scale.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean normalized scores (0-10) for coherence, creativity, affinity, and recognition.

tasks.name: Computational Evaluation of Lyrics
tasks.description: Automated and model-based metrics were used to assess the quality, diversity, and distributional similarity of generated Chinese song lyrics compared to a human corpus (MojimLyrics dataset).
tasks.origin_paper: Pillutla et al. 2021; Welleck et al. 2020; Li et al. 2016; Su et al. 2022
tasks.scoring_detail: MAUVE, rep-n, distinct-n, diversity

benchmarks.name: Lyric-Guided Album Art Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A multimodal creative task where generated text (lyrics) is used to guide the generation of creative images (album art), which are then evaluated for quality.

tasks.name: FID Evaluation of Generated Album Art
tasks.description: A diffusion model (Taiyi Stable Diffusion) generates album art from AI-generated lyrics. The quality of the generated images is measured by calculating the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) against a dataset of real album covers.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID)

title: CreativEval: Evaluating Creativity of LLM-Based Hardware Code Generation

benchmarks.name: CreativEval
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new framework introduced in this paper to evaluate the creativity of LLMs in hardware (Verilog) code generation. It is based on the four cognitive dimensions of divergent thinking: fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration.

tasks.name: Fluency
tasks.description: Measures the average number of unique, functional Verilog solutions an LLM can generate for a given hardware design prompt from the HDLBits dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average number of unique functional solutions per prompt, where uniqueness is determined by comparing GNN4IP circuit similarity scores.

tasks.name: Flexibility
tasks.description: Measures the LLM's ability to generate a functional and unique alternative implementation of a Verilog module when provided with an existing solution.
tasks.scoring_detail: Proportion of prompts for which the LLM generates a functional solution with a GNN4IP similarity score below a threshold (s < 0) compared to the provided example.

tasks.name: Originality
tasks.description: Measures the uniqueness of an LLM-generated Verilog module compared to a typical, 'golden' implementation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average re-normalized GNN4IP similarity score between the generated solution and a golden response. Higher scores indicate less similarity and thus more originality.

tasks.name: Elaboration
tasks.description: Measures the LLM's ability to use provided smaller Verilog modules to implement a larger, more complex module.
tasks.scoring_detail: Proportion of prompts for which the LLM generates a functional solution that correctly utilizes the provided smaller modules.

benchmarks.name: Hardware Code Functionality
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Measures functional correctness (pass@k), a standard code generation metric, not creativity. It is used as a baseline and a prerequisite filter for the creativity tasks.
benchmarks.origin_paper: e.g., Chen et al., 2021, 'Evaluating large language models trained on code'

tasks.name: Verilog Functionality Test (pass@10)
tasks.description: Measures the functional correctness of LLM-generated Verilog code by checking if it passes a testbench. The pass@10 metric is calculated over a dataset of 120 prompts from HDLBits.
tasks.origin_paper: e.g., Chen et al., 2021, 'Evaluating large language models trained on code'
tasks.scoring_detail: pass@10 (functional correctness against a testbench using Icarus Verilog simulator)

title: Time-R1: Towards Comprehensive Temporal Reasoning in LLMs

benchmarks.name: Time-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale benchmark for evaluating comprehensive temporal reasoning in LLMs, including foundational logic, future prediction, and creative scenario generation. It uses open-ended generation tasks and reports empirical results.

tasks.name: Timestamp Inference
tasks.description: Infer the specific date (YYYY-MM) of a news event based on its headline and abstract from historical data.
tasks.scoring_detail: Rule-based total score R(x, y) including accuracy based on exponential decay of temporal distance from ground truth, format bonuses, and penalties.

tasks.name: Time-Difference Estimation
tasks.description: Estimate the temporal gap in months between two news events, after inferring the date of each.
tasks.scoring_detail: Rule-based total score R(x, y) combining accuracy for inferred dates and the time difference, with penalties for logical inconsistency.

tasks.name: Event Ordering
tasks.description: Determine the correct chronological sequence of three news events, after inferring the date of each.
tasks.scoring_detail: Rule-based total score R(x, y) combining accuracy for inferred dates and order, with penalties for logical inconsistency and trivial solutions.

tasks.name: Masked Time Entity Completion
tasks.description: Fill in a masked temporal expression (<Year> or <Month>) within a news event description, after inferring the event's primary date.
tasks.scoring_detail: Rule-based total score R(x, y) combining accuracy for the inferred event date and the completed masked entity.

tasks.name: Future Event Time Prediction
tasks.description: Predict the specific future date (YYYY-MM) of a news event occurring after the model's knowledge cutoff.
tasks.scoring_detail: Rule-based total score R(x, y) based on exponential decay of temporal distance from ground truth, with a strict decay coefficient.

tasks.name: Creative Future Scenario Generation
tasks.description: Generate plausible and diverse news headlines and abstracts for a specified future date and theme.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average Maximum Similarity (AvgMaxSim) score, calculated using cosine similarity between semantic embeddings of generated scenarios and real news from the target month.

title: Another Turn, Better Output? A Turn-Wise Analysis of Iterative LLM Prompting

benchmarks.name: LiveIdeaBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark is explicitly designed to evaluate divergent thinking for scientific idea generation, a core aspect of creativity.

tasks.name: Scientific Idea Generation
tasks.description: Models generate a novel and feasible scientific idea based on a given keyword, which is then iteratively refined over 12 turns based on vague or specific feedback.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-Sonnet-4.0, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, GPT-OSS-20B.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-as-judge (Gemini 2.5-pro) ratings for Feasibility, Novelty, Originality, and Clarity (1-10 scale); automatic metrics including Drift from Origin (cosine similarity), Turn-to-Turn Volatility (cosine similarity), Lexical Novelty (new n-grams), and Growth Factor (word count).

benchmarks.name: DS-1000
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a standard code generation benchmark focused on functional correctness via unit tests, not explicitly on creative or divergent problem-solving.

tasks.name: Code Generation
tasks.description: Models generate a Python code solution for a data science problem, which is then iteratively refined over 12 turns based on vague or specific feedback.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-Sonnet-4.0, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, GPT-OSS-20B.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic correctness score from unit tests; LLM-as-judge (Gemini 2.5-pro) ratings for Pragmatism and Readability (1-10 scale); automatic metrics including Drift from Origin, Turn-to-Turn Volatility, Lexical Novelty, and Growth Factor (lines of code).

benchmarks.name: Omni-MATH
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a mathematical reasoning benchmark focused on finding a single correct answer to a closed-ended problem, not on open-ended or creative tasks.

tasks.name: Mathematical Reasoning
tasks.description: Models solve high-difficulty mathematical problems requiring multi-step reasoning, with the solution being iteratively refined over 12 turns based on vague or specific feedback.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-Sonnet-4.0, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, GPT-OSS-20B.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-as-judge (Gemini) ratings for binary answer_correctness and reasoning_soundness (1-10 scale), as well as Logical Soundness and Clarity of Explanation; automatic metrics including Drift from Origin, Turn-to-Turn Volatility, Lexical Novelty, and Growth Factor (word count).

title: Enhancing multimodal analogical reasoning with Logic Augmented Generation

benchmarks.name: MOH-X
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on metaphor detection, a form of figurative language understanding which is a component of creative reasoning. The task is to classify sentences as metaphorical or literal.

tasks.name: Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: Given a sentence, the model generates an extended knowledge graph (XKG) based on a blending ontology to classify the sentence as metaphorical or literal.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model generates a structured knowledge graph to perform a final classification task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Llama 3.1 70B-Instruct were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score

benchmarks.name: TroFi
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard benchmark for metaphor detection, which evaluates a system's ability to understand non-literal, creative language use.

tasks.name: Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: Given a sentence from the Wall Street Journal corpus, the model generates an extended knowledge graph (XKG) to classify the sentence as metaphorical or literal.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model generates a structured knowledge graph to perform a final classification task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Llama 3.1 70B-Instruct were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score

benchmarks.name: WG dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on conceptual metaphor understanding, a deeper creative reasoning task that requires identifying the abstract source and target domains of a metaphor.
benchmarks.origin_name: dataset refined by Wachowiak and Gromann

tasks.name: Conceptual Metaphor Understanding
tasks.description: For a given metaphorical sentence, the task is to identify the correct source and target domains that constitute the conceptual metaphor.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Llama 3.1 70B-Instruct were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Manual evaluation of source/target correctness by 3 annotators (majority vote, Fleiss' Kappa), BLEURT score, point-biserial correlation, Spearman correlation. Qualitative evaluation of generated graphs by 2 knowledge engineers.

benchmarks.name: Balanced Conceptual Metaphor Testing Dataset (BCMTD)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark introduced to test metaphor detection and understanding, with a specific focus on domain-specific (scientific) metaphors, which requires specialized creative reasoning.

tasks.name: Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: Classify sentences from a balanced set of general metaphors, scientific metaphors, and literal sentences as metaphorical or not.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model generates a structured knowledge graph to perform a final classification task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Llama 3.1 70B-Instruct were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 Score

tasks.name: Conceptual Metaphor Understanding
tasks.description: Identify the correct source and target domains for general and scientific conceptual metaphors within the dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Llama 3.1 70B-Instruct were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Manual evaluation of source/target correctness by 3 annotators (majority vote, Fleiss' Kappa), BLEURT score, point-biserial correlation, Spearman correlation. Qualitative evaluation of generated graphs by 2 knowledge engineers.

benchmarks.name: Visual Metaphors Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates the ability to understand visual metaphors, a key aspect of multimodal creativity that requires interpreting non-literal visual communication.

tasks.name: Visual Metaphor Understanding
tasks.description: Given an image containing a visual metaphor, the task is to identify the abstract property that links the two conceptual domains being blended.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses Claude 3.5 Sonnet, which accepts image inputs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Manual evaluation of the connecting property by 3 annotators (Accuracy), comparison with human participant performance, and qualitative evaluation of generated graphs by 2 knowledge engineers.

title: Summary of the Visually Grounded Story Generation Challenge

benchmarks.name: Visually Grounded Story Generation (VGSG)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new shared task designed to evaluate the ability of vision-and-language models to generate creative, coherent, and visually grounded stories from image sequences. It is an open-ended generation task with empirical results from multiple AI systems.

tasks.name: Visually Grounded Story Generation
tasks.description: Given a sequence of images, the system must generate a coherent short story where characters and events are grounded in the provided images. The shared task was structured into two tracks: a 'Closed track' with a fixed visual encoder and an 'Open track' allowing any model. The evaluation used several datasets, including Visual Writing Prompts (VWP), VIST-Character, Travel blogs (TB), and Movie Synopses Associations (MSA).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates various Vision-Language Models (VLMs) including GPT-4o, LLaVA, and custom Transformer-based models like EntityGrid.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics: BLEU-1/2/3/4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, character-matching (CM), various diversity metrics (e.g., unique verbs, predicate ratios), and coherence (generative Entity Grid model). Human evaluation: Ratings for Coherence, Diversity, Grammaticality, Visual Grounding, and Overall quality.

title: EmoArt: A Multidimensional Dataset for Emotion-Aware Artistic Generation

benchmarks.name: EmoArt
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new large-scale dataset and benchmark for evaluating the ability of text-to-image models to generate emotionally expressive and stylistically coherent artistic images, a core aspect of computational creativity.

tasks.name: Emotion-Aware Artistic Image Generation
tasks.description: Text-to-image diffusion models are evaluated on their ability to generate artistic images based on prompts combining style, arousal, valence, and a content description from the EmoArt dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests FLUX.1-dev, FLUX.1-schnell, SDXL, SD3.5, PixArt-sigma, Playground, and Openjourney.
tasks.scoring_detail: Standard image quality metrics (FID, SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS) and a custom 'Attributes Alignment' score. The alignment score uses a fine-tuned VLM (MiniCPM-V-2.6) to compute CLIP embedding similarity for 5 artistic attributes: brushwork, color, composition, light, and line.

title: Outline to Story: Fine-grained Controllable Story Generation from Cascaded Events

benchmarks.name: Outline to Story (O2S)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Proposes a new task, datasets, and evaluation for fine-grained controllable creative story generation, a core aspect of AI creativity.

tasks.name: Controllable Story Generation (WritingPrompts)
tasks.description: Generate a multi-paragraph story from a prompt and a sequence of keyword-based events for each paragraph. The dataset is created by applying keyword extraction to stories from the WritingPrompts corpus.
tasks.scoring_detail: Perplexity (word-level and BPE), BLEU-4, ROUGE-1 (F1, P, R), ROUGE-2 (F1, P, R), ROUGE-L (F1, P, R)

tasks.name: Controllable Story Generation (WikiPlots)
tasks.description: Generate a multi-paragraph story from a title and a sequence of keyword-based events for each paragraph. The dataset is created by segmenting and applying keyword extraction to plots from the WikiPlots corpus.
tasks.scoring_detail: Perplexity (word-level and BPE), BLEU-4, ROUGE-1 (F1, P, R), ROUGE-2 (F1, P, R), ROUGE-L (F1, P, R)

tasks.name: Event Generation and Analysis
tasks.description: Evaluate the model's ability to generate its own subsequent outline events under different decoding scenarios (e.g., free generation after the first event). The quality of both the generated events and the resulting story is measured.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4 (for events), BLEU-4 (for story), ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L

title: ***YesBut***: A High-Quality Annotated Multimodal Dataset for evaluating Satire Comprehension capability of Vision-Language Models

benchmarks.name: YesBut
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new multimodal dataset and set of tasks designed specifically to evaluate the satire and humor comprehension capabilities of Vision-Language Models, which is a form of creative understanding.

tasks.name: Satirical Image Detection
tasks.description: A binary classification task where a model must predict whether a given image is satirical or not.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on Gemini, GPT4, LLaVA, MiniGPT4, Kosmos-2.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1-Score

tasks.name: Satirical Image Understanding
tasks.description: Given a satirical image, the model generates a textual description explaining why the image is satirical or funny.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on Gemini, GPT4, LLaVA, MiniGPT4, Kosmos-2.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, BERTScore, Polos) and human evaluation (Correctness, Appropriate Length, Visual Completeness, Faithfulness).

tasks.name: Satirical Image Completion
tasks.description: Given one sub-image, the model must choose the correct second sub-image from two options to form a meaningful and satirical complete image.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on Gemini, GPT4, LLaVA, MiniGPT4, Kosmos-2.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: Real Satirical Photographs Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of 119 real photographs used to evaluate satire detection and understanding in a non-synthetic context, which is a form of creative comprehension.

tasks.name: Satirical Image Detection
tasks.description: A detection task where models must classify real photographs as satirical. Since all images in the set are satirical, this measures the model's ability to correctly identify them as such.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on Gemini, GPT4, LLaVA, MiniGPT4, Kosmos-2.
tasks.scoring_detail: Detection accuracy

tasks.name: Satirical Image Understanding
tasks.description: Given a real satirical photograph, the model generates text explaining the satire, which is then evaluated by humans.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested on Gemini, GPT4, LLaVA, MiniGPT4, Kosmos-2.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human judgment on whether the generated text correctly describes the satire, reported as accuracy.

title: Diverse, not Short: A Length-Controlled Data Selection Strategy for Improving Response Diversity of Language Models

benchmarks.name: Divergent Associations Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard psychological test for divergent thinking, adapted to evaluate the creativity and ideological diversity of language models by measuring semantic dissimilarity in generated words.

tasks.name: Divergent Word Generation
tasks.description: Generate a list of 10 words that are as dissimilar from each other as possible.
tasks.scoring_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) score, Number of unique words

benchmarks.name: Persona Generation Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Assesses diversity in structured generation by requiring the model to produce varied persona descriptions in a specific format (JSON), testing its ability to avoid repetition.

tasks.name: JSON Persona Generation
tasks.description: Generate a JSON object with three fields: first name, city of birth, and current occupation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Proportion of unique values for each JSON key (first name, city, occupation)

benchmarks.name: Alternate Uses Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A classic psychological test of divergent thinking that measures the ability to generate creative and unconventional uses for common objects.

tasks.name: Alternate Uses Generation
tasks.description: Generate creative and unconventional uses for common objects (e.g., broom, brick, candle).
tasks.scoring_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) score (semantic distance between object and uses)

benchmarks.name: Creative Writing Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A validated psychological assessment of creativity that tasks the model with generating a short story under constraints, evaluating both diversity and quality of the output.

tasks.name: Constrained Story Generation
tasks.description: Generate a creative short story that includes a given set of three words.
tasks.scoring_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) score, ArmoRM reward model score, 4-gram diversity, human pairwise preference (diversity), LLM-as-a-Judge pairwise preference (diversity), ∆Diversity Decile (∆DD)

title: ALF at SemEval-2024 Task 9: Exploring Lateral Thinking Capabilities of LMs through Multi-task Fine-tuning

benchmarks.name: BrainTeaser
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark is explicitly designed to evaluate lateral thinking and creative reasoning abilities in NLP models through puzzles that defy common sense.

tasks.name: Sentence Puzzle
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question answering task where models must solve puzzles that require lateral thinking. This paper's system was developed for this specific subtask as part of SemEval 2024 Task 9.
tasks.origin_paper: Jiang et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2023
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is multiple-choice question answering. T5-based models are fine-tuned to generate the correct choice text, while BERT-based models perform classification.
tasks.model_type_notes: BERT-based (ALBERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTa) and T5-based (Flan T5, Unified-QA) models were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Instance-based accuracy (overall, original, semantic, context), Group-based accuracy (ori-sem, ori-sem-con), 5-fold cross-validation accuracy.

benchmarks.name: RiddleSense
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This benchmark focuses on computational creativity through riddle questions. It was used in this paper as a key auxiliary dataset for multi-task fine-tuning to improve performance on the primary creative task (BrainTeaser).

tasks.name: Riddle Question Answering
tasks.description: The RiddleSense dataset was used for multi-task fine-tuning alongside the BrainTeaser dataset to enhance model performance. The paper's final models were all fine-tuned on a combination of BrainTeaser and RiddleSense.
tasks.task_type_notes: The dataset was used for fine-tuning models for a multiple-choice question answering task.
tasks.model_type_notes: A Flan-T5-base model was used for initial comparison, and then all models (BERT-based and T5-based) were fine-tuned using this dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Performance was measured by the resulting 5-fold cross-validation accuracy on the BrainTeaser task, not on RiddleSense itself.

benchmarks.name: Auxiliary Commonsense Datasets
benchmarks.relevance_reason: These are standard commonsense reasoning benchmarks, not creativity benchmarks. They were used in an experiment to see if multi-task fine-tuning on them could improve performance on the creative BrainTeaser task.

tasks.name: CommonSenseQA (CSQA)
tasks.description: Used as an auxiliary dataset in a comparative experiment (Table 2) to evaluate its impact on the BrainTeaser task performance when used for multi-task fine-tuning.
tasks.task_type_notes: The dataset was used for fine-tuning a model for a multiple-choice question answering task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Flan-T5-base
tasks.scoring_detail: Performance was measured by the resulting 5-fold cross-validation accuracy on the BrainTeaser task.

tasks.name: Physical IQA (PIQA)
tasks.description: Used as an auxiliary dataset in a comparative experiment (Table 2) to evaluate its impact on the BrainTeaser task performance when used for multi-task fine-tuning.
tasks.task_type_notes: The dataset was used for fine-tuning a model for a multiple-choice question answering task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Flan-T5-base
tasks.scoring_detail: Performance was measured by the resulting 5-fold cross-validation accuracy on the BrainTeaser task.

tasks.name: Social IQA (SIQA)
tasks.description: Used as an auxiliary dataset in a comparative experiment (Table 2) to evaluate its impact on the BrainTeaser task performance. Its format was transformed into MCQA for this study.
tasks.task_type_notes: The dataset was used for fine-tuning a model for a multiple-choice question answering task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Flan-T5-base
tasks.scoring_detail: Performance was measured by the resulting 5-fold cross-validation accuracy on the BrainTeaser task.

tasks.name: HellaSWAG
tasks.description: Used as an auxiliary dataset in a comparative experiment (Table 2) to evaluate its impact on the BrainTeaser task performance. Its format was transformed into MCQA for this study.
tasks.task_type_notes: The dataset was used for fine-tuning a model for a multiple-choice question answering task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Flan-T5-base
tasks.scoring_detail: Performance was measured by the resulting 5-fold cross-validation accuracy on the BrainTeaser task.

tasks.name: SWAG
tasks.description: Used as an auxiliary dataset in a comparative experiment (Table 2) to evaluate its impact on the BrainTeaser task performance. Its format was transformed into MCQA for this study.
tasks.task_type_notes: The dataset was used for fine-tuning a model for a multiple-choice question answering task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Flan-T5-base
tasks.scoring_detail: Performance was measured by the resulting 5-fold cross-validation accuracy on the BrainTeaser task.

title: MELFuSION: Synthesizing Music from Image and Language Cues Using Diffusion Models

benchmarks.name: MeLBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of image, text, and music triplets designed for the creative task of multimodal music generation.

tasks.name: Multimodal Music Generation
tasks.description: Generating a 10-second music clip conditioned on a reference image and an associated text prompt.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests its audio diffusion model (MELFUSION) against various other text-to-music models (e.g., MusicLM, MusicGen, TANGO++).
tasks.scoring_detail: Objective metrics: FAD, KL Divergence, FD, IMSM. Subjective human evaluation: Overall Audio Quality (OVL), Relevance (REL).

benchmarks.name: Extended MusicCaps
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An existing text-music dataset extended with images to support the creative task of multimodal music generation.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Agostinelli et al., Musiclm: Generating music from text, 2023

tasks.name: Multimodal Music Generation
tasks.description: Generating a 10-second music clip conditioned on a reference image and an associated text prompt using the extended dataset.
tasks.origin_paper: Agostinelli et al., Musiclm: Generating music from text, 2023
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests its audio diffusion model (MELFUSION) against various other text-to-music models (e.g., MusicLM, MusicGen, TANGO++).
tasks.scoring_detail: Objective metrics: FAD, KL Divergence, FD, IMSM. Subjective human evaluation: Overall Audio Quality (OVL), Relevance (REL).

benchmarks.name: IMSM (Image Music Similarity Metric) Validation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new metric proposed and validated to quantitatively measure the perceptual similarity and creative alignment between an image and a music clip.

tasks.name: Metric Validation User Study
