tasks.description: A user study conducted to validate the proposed IMSM metric by comparing its automatically generated scores against human judgments of image-music similarity.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task evaluates the correlation of a new automatic metric (IMSM) with human perception.
tasks.model_type_notes: The task evaluates a metric, not a generative model. It involves human participants and pre-trained models (CLIP, CLAP) that constitute the metric.
tasks.scoring_detail: Correlation between the automatic IMSM score and average human similarity ratings on a scale of [0,1].

title: Learning to Generate Research Idea with Dynamic Control

benchmarks.name: Learn2Gen
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and framework for generating and evaluating novel research ideas from scientific papers, which is a core creative task focusing on novelty, feasibility, and effectiveness.

tasks.name: Research Idea Generation
tasks.description: Given an input research paper, an LLM generates a follow-up research idea consisting of a method and an experiment plan. The quality of the idea is the subject of evaluation.
tasks.model_type_notes: T5 and LLaMA2 models were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic evaluation via GPT-4 (as a reviewing agent) and manual evaluation by 15 domain experts. Both methods score Novelty, Feasibility, and Effectiveness on a 1-10 scale. An Overall score is also reported.

title: Hypothesis Generation with Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: SHOE SALES
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A synthetic task created by the authors to test an LLM's ability to generate a single, correct, hidden hypothesis from data, which is a form of inductive reasoning and pattern discovery.

tasks.name: Hypothesis-driven Shoe Color Prediction
tasks.description: LLMs first generate hypotheses to explain the relationship between a customer's appearance and the color of shoes they buy. Then, these hypotheses are used to predict the shoe color for new customers in a 6-class classification setup.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude-2.1, Mixtral, GPT-3.5-turbo were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy; Verification of recovering the single known valid hypothesis.

benchmarks.name: DECEPTIVE REVIEWS
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A real-world task requiring LLMs to generate hypotheses about linguistic patterns that distinguish truthful from deceptive reviews, a creative social science problem.

tasks.name: Hypothesis-driven Deception Detection
tasks.description: LLMs generate hypotheses about linguistic cues for deception in hotel reviews. These hypotheses are then used to classify new reviews as truthful or deceptive.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude-2.1, Mixtral, GPT-3.5-turbo were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy; Qualitative analysis comparing generated hypotheses to findings in existing literature.

benchmarks.name: HEADLINE POPULARITY
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A real-world task where LLMs generate hypotheses about what linguistic features make a headline more engaging (popular), which involves creative reasoning about language and psychology.

tasks.name: Hypothesis-driven Popularity Prediction
tasks.description: LLMs generate hypotheses to explain why one headline is more popular (gets more clicks) than another. These hypotheses are then used to predict the more popular headline in new pairs.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude-2.1, Mixtral, GPT-3.5-turbo were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy; Qualitative analysis comparing generated hypotheses to findings in existing literature.

benchmarks.name: TWEET POPULARITY
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A real-world task where LLMs generate hypotheses about linguistic features that increase a tweet's propagation (retweets), a creative social science problem.
benchmarks.origin_name: The effect of wording on message propagation dataset

tasks.name: Hypothesis-driven Popularity Prediction
tasks.description: LLMs generate hypotheses to explain why one tweet gets more retweets than another. These hypotheses are then used to predict the more popular tweet in new pairs.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude-2.1, Mixtral, GPT-3.5-turbo were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy; Qualitative analysis comparing generated hypotheses to findings in existing literature.

benchmarks.name: Deceptive Reviews (OOD)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Tests the generalization of generated hypotheses for deception detection on an out-of-distribution dataset, assessing the robustness of the creative reasoning.
benchmarks.origin_name: Manipulated offerings on review portals dataset

tasks.name: Out-of-Distribution Hypothesis-driven Deception Detection
tasks.description: Uses hypotheses generated on the DECEPTIVE REVIEWS dataset to classify reviews from a different dataset (different cities, websites) as truthful or deceptive, testing for generalization.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task uses pre-generated hypotheses to generate predictions on a new dataset to test generalization.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude-2.1, Mixtral, GPT-3.5-turbo were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy

title: The Fabrication of Reality and Fantasy: Scene Generation with LLM-Assisted Prompt Interpretation

benchmarks.name: Realistic-Fantasy Benchmark (RFBench)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark introduced by the paper specifically to evaluate text-to-image models on prompts requiring creativity, imagination, and complex reasoning, which are open-ended generation tasks.

tasks.name: Creative and Complex Scene Generation
tasks.description: Generating images from a curated set of 229 text prompts divided into two main categories: 'Realistic & Analytical' (testing factual, scientific, and cultural understanding) and 'Creativity & Imagination' (testing imaginative, counterfactual, and anthropomorphic scenarios).
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include Stable Diffusion, MultiDiffusion, Attend and Excite, LMD, BoxDiff, SDXL, and the proposed RFNet.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT4-CLIP (text-text cosine similarity), GPT4Score (GPT-4 rating 0-100), Human preference (visual quality and text fidelity ratings 1-5)

benchmarks.name: DrawBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An existing benchmark for text-to-image models that includes prompts requiring creativity and imagination. It is used here to test the generalization of the proposed method on open-ended generation tasks.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Saharia et al., 2022 (Photorealistic text-to-image diffusion models with deep language understanding)

tasks.name: Creative and Imaginative Scene Generation (DrawBench subset)
tasks.description: Generating images from a subset of prompts from the DrawBench benchmark that focus on creativity and imagination (e.g., 'A horse riding an astronaut') to compare the proposed model with Imagen.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper's method (RFNet) is compared against Imagen.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT4Score

title: CERD: A Comprehensive Chinese Rhetoric Dataset for Rhetorical Understanding and Generation in Essays

benchmarks.name: Chinese Essay Rhetoric Dataset (CERD)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new dataset and benchmark for understanding and generating rhetorical devices (metaphor, personification, etc.), which are key aspects of creative language. It includes open-ended generation tasks and classification/extraction tasks focused on these creative elements, and reports empirical results for several LLMs.

tasks.name: Rhetoric Classification (RC)
tasks.description: A multi-label classification task where a model predicts the coarse-grained rhetorical devices (metaphor, personification, hyperbole, parallelism, or literal) used in a given sentence.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates RoBERTa, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Qwen1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact Match, Precision, Recall, F1 score (micro and macro)

tasks.name: Form Classification (FC)
tasks.description: A multi-label classification task where a model predicts fine-grained form-level rhetorical categories (e.g., simile, metonymy, verb-based personification) from 13 possible categories.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates RoBERTa, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Qwen1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact Match, Precision, Recall, F1 score (micro and macro)

tasks.name: Content Classification (CC)
tasks.description: A multi-label classification task where a model predicts fine-grained content-level rhetorical categories (e.g., concrete metaphor, amplification hyperbole) from 12 possible categories.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates RoBERTa, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Qwen1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact Match, Precision, Recall, F1 score (micro and macro)

tasks.name: Component Extraction (CE)
tasks.description: A named entity recognition task where a model extracts rhetorical components (connectors, objects, contents) from a given sentence.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates RoBERTa, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Qwen1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 score (micro and macro)

tasks.name: Rhetoric Generation (RG)
tasks.description: A controllable text generation task where a model generates a rhetorical sentence based on preceding context, a specified rhetorical device, and specific rhetorical objects (e.g., tenor for a metaphor).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Qwen1.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic (BLEU, ROUGE-L, PPL, BERTScore), LLM-based (Single-answer Rating, Pairwise Ranking), Human (Single-answer Rating, Pairwise Ranking)

title: Predicting Empirical AI Research Outcomes with Language Models

benchmarks.name: Research Outcome Prediction Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark evaluates an AI's ability to predict the success of novel research ideas. This is a forecasting task related to the creative process of research, but not a direct measure of an AI's creative output (like generation or divergent thinking).

tasks.name: Research Outcome Prediction
tasks.description: Given a pair of research ideas and a research goal, predict which idea will perform better across a set of empirical benchmarks. The dataset consists of 6,000 training pairs and 1,585 test pairs scraped from published AI papers.
tasks.scoring_detail: Prediction accuracy

tasks.name: Human Expert Comparison
tasks.description: Comparing the prediction accuracy of the AI system against 25 human NLP experts on a subset of 45 NLP-focused idea pairs from the main test set.
tasks.scoring_detail: Prediction accuracy (model vs. human experts)

tasks.name: Robustness Stress Tests
tasks.description: Analyzing the system's prediction accuracy on subsets of the test data to check for sensitivity to superficial features like idea recency, description length, author affiliation (famous labs), and other LM-proposed features.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy on supported vs. unsupported data subsets

benchmarks.name: Unpublished Idea Outcome Prediction
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a generalization test for the main task on a new dataset. It evaluates the potential of novel, unpublished research ideas, which is related to creativity and innovation, but is primarily a forecasting task.
benchmarks.origin_name: Dataset of 35 ideas from an AI ideation study

tasks.name: Generalization Test on Unpublished Ideas
tasks.description: Predicting the empirical outcome of 33 pairs of unpublished research ideas (novel idea vs. baseline) to test the system's generalization capabilities.
tasks.scoring_detail: Prediction accuracy

title: The Budget AI Researcher and the Power of RAG Chains

benchmarks.name: Research Ideation Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new framework for evaluating AI-generated research ideas (in the form of abstracts) based on creativity-focused metrics like novelty and interestingness, using both LLM and human judges.

tasks.name: LLM-based Abstract Evaluation (Quality Ratings)
tasks.description: LLMs generate research abstracts which are then evaluated by a judge LLM (ChatGPT-4o) on three criteria: interestingness, novelty, and feasibility. This was used for the main quantitative evaluation and the ablation study.
tasks.scoring_detail: ChatGPT-4o ratings for Interestingness, Novelty, and Feasibility.

tasks.name: LLM-based Abstract Evaluation (Future Similarity)
tasks.description: Generated research abstracts are evaluated for their similarity to papers from future academic conferences (unpublished at the time of system development). Higher similarity is interpreted as a measure of novelty and feasibility.
tasks.scoring_detail: Similarity score (0-1) rated by an augmented Llama 3.1 8B model against 1000 future conference papers.

tasks.name: Human Evaluation of Abstracts
tasks.description: Human evaluators (master's and Ph.D. students) rate generated research abstracts from the proposed system and a baseline system on three criteria.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings (1-5 scale) for Interestingness, Feasibility, and Novelty.

tasks.name: LLM-based Abstract Evaluation (Detailed Rubric)
tasks.description: A judge LLM (ChatGPT-4o) evaluates a generated abstract using a detailed rubric, including ratings for originality, practicality, soundness, presentation, contribution, and an overall accept/reject decision.
tasks.model_type_notes: ChatGPT-4o was used as the evaluator.
tasks.scoring_detail: ChatGPT-4o ratings for Originality (1-10), Practicality (1-10), Soundness (1-5), Presentation (1-5), Contribution (1-5), Overall (1-5), Confidence (1-5), and a binary Accept/Reject decision.

title: Characterising the Creative Process in Humans and Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Alternate Uses Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A classic divergent thinking task used to evaluate the creativity of both humans and LLMs by generating novel uses for common objects. The paper analyzes the process of idea generation.
benchmarks.origin_paper: A classic psychological test, e.g., by J.P. Guilford, though no specific origin paper is cited.

tasks.name: Alternate Uses for a Brick
tasks.description: Generate a sequence of creative, alternative uses for a brick.
tasks.scoring_detail: Response originality scored by Open Creativity Scoring (ocsai-chatgpt). Response sequence flexibility/persistence analyzed via a 'jump profile' derived from sentence embeddings and clustering.

tasks.name: Alternate Uses for a Paperclip
tasks.description: Generate a sequence of creative, alternative uses for a paperclip.
tasks.scoring_detail: Response originality scored by Open Creativity Scoring (ocsai-chatgpt). Response sequence flexibility/persistence analyzed via a 'jump profile' derived from sentence embeddings and clustering.

benchmarks.name: Verbal Fluency Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard cognitive task used not to measure creativity directly, but as a comparative baseline to analyze the semantic search process (flexibility vs. persistence) against a creative task (AUT).
benchmarks.origin_paper: A standard neuropsychological test, no specific origin cited in the paper.

tasks.name: Animal Naming Fluency
tasks.description: Generate a sequence of as many animal names as possible.
tasks.scoring_detail: Response sequence flexibility/persistence analyzed via a 'jump profile' derived from sentence embeddings and clustering.

title: STORIUM: A Dataset and Evaluation Platform for Machine-in-the-Loop Story Generation

benchmarks.name: STORIUM Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale dataset of long-form collaborative stories with rich structural annotations, designed for training and evaluating creative story generation models.

tasks.name: Scene Entry Generation
tasks.description: Generating a story continuation ('scene entry') conditioned on rich context including previous entries, character descriptions, challenges, and other narrative elements from the STORIUM platform.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper fine-tunes GPT-2 medium.
tasks.scoring_detail: The generated text is evaluated using the STORIUM Evaluation Platform, which includes expert human ratings (relevance, fluency, coherence, likability), crowdsourced ratings, and the automatic USER, ROUGE-L, and ROUGE-W metrics. Perplexity is also used for model selection.

benchmarks.name: STORIUM Evaluation Platform
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new machine-in-the-loop platform where real authors interact with and evaluate AI-generated story continuations, providing expert feedback and enabling novel metrics.

tasks.name: Expert Human Evaluation
tasks.description: Expert authors on the live STORIUM platform rate AI-generated story continuations on a 5-point Likert scale after editing them for their own stories.
tasks.scoring_detail: 5-point Likert scale ratings for relevance, fluency, coherence, and likability.

tasks.name: USER (User Story Edit Ratings)
tasks.description: An automatic metric that quantifies the usefulness of generated text by measuring the proportion of it that is preserved by a human author in their final, edited version. It is based on matching contiguous substrings.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a metric for evaluating generated text.
tasks.scoring_detail: USER score (a precision-like score based on longest common contiguous substrings).

tasks.name: Crowdsourced Human Evaluation
tasks.description: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers rate AI-generated story continuations on Likert scales. This was used as a comparison to expert evaluation, and the paper found it to be unreliable for this task.
tasks.scoring_detail: Likert scale ratings for relevance, fluency, coherence, likability; Fleiss' kappa for inter-annotator agreement.

title: Understanding Large Language Models' Ability on Interdisciplinary Research

benchmarks.name: IDRBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for evaluating LLMs on scientific creativity, specifically their ability to identify, integrate, and recommend interdisciplinary research ideas.

tasks.name: IDR Paper Identification (IPI)
tasks.description: LLM classifies if a given scientific paper (title and abstract) is interdisciplinary research (IDR). If yes, it also identifies the disciplines involved.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score, Macro-F1 score

tasks.name: IDR Idea Integration (I3)
tasks.description: Given two papers from distinct disciplines, the LLM predicts if their integration is a promising IDR idea. If yes, it generates a new abstract and the reasoning for the integration.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1 score (for classification), SciBERT Similarity, BLEU, ROUGE-1 (for generated text)

tasks.name: IDR Idea Recommendation (I2R)
tasks.description: Given a seed paper and a list of candidate papers, the LLM re-ranks the list to find the best candidate for forming a promising IDR idea with the seed paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), NDCG@10, Kendall's τ

title: Automatic Generation of Fashion Images using Prompting in Generative Machine Learning Models

benchmarks.name: Human Evaluation of Fashion Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new human evaluation framework that explicitly measures creativity, aesthetic appeal, and coherence of AI-generated fashion designs, which are open-ended tasks.

tasks.name: Image Evaluation
tasks.description: Human participants evaluate generated fashion images on a 1-5 Likert scale for style alignment, occasion suitability, wearer suitability, creativity, aesthetic appeal, and cohesion.
tasks.model_type_notes: The evaluated images are the output of a pipeline involving an LLM (Mistral-7B or Falcon-7B) and a Diffusion model (Stable Diffusion).
tasks.scoring_detail: 1-5 Likert scale ratings for style alignment, occasion suitability, wearer suitability, creativity, aesthetic appeal, cohesion; Yes/No for abnormalities and inspiration potential.

tasks.name: Description Evaluation
tasks.description: Human participants evaluate generated fashion text descriptions on a 1-5 Likert scale for comprehensibility, coherence, and suitability of the outfit, colors, and textures for the given occasion, style, and wearer type.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluates text output from Mistral-7B and Falcon-7B.
tasks.scoring_detail: 1-5 Likert scale ratings for comprehensibility, coherence, and suitability (outfit, colors, textures) for occasion, style, and wearer.

tasks.name: Comparative Ranking of Generated Images
tasks.description: Human participants are shown images generated from five different methods (ZS, FS, CoT, RAG-PDFs, RAG-BLOGs) and asked to rank them from 1st to 5th based on preference.
tasks.model_type_notes: The evaluated images are the output of a pipeline involving an LLM and a Diffusion model.
tasks.scoring_detail: Comparative ranking (1st to 5th place) based on user preference.

benchmarks.name: CLIPscore
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a standard automated metric for text-image alignment (cosine similarity) and does not directly measure creativity, novelty, or other divergent thinking aspects.

tasks.name: Text-Image Alignment Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluates text-image alignment by computing the cosine similarity between CLIP embeddings of the generated image and the text description.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluates the output of a pipeline involving an LLM and a Diffusion model.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine similarity between text and image embeddings

title: Mining Contextualized Visual Associations from Images for Creativity Understanding

benchmarks.name: MSCOCO with Abstract Visual Associations and Creative Captions
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of creative captions for MSCOCO images, generated at increasing levels of abstraction. The paper includes human evaluation of these captions, focusing on creativity-related aspects like abstraction and visual grounding.

tasks.name: Visual Grounding Evaluation
tasks.description: Human annotators rated generated creative captions on a 4-point Likert scale to determine if they were visually grounded (i.e., free of hallucinations and relevant to the image).
tasks.task_type_notes: Humans evaluate AI-generated content.
tasks.model_type_notes: The captions were generated by a pipeline using a VLM (Molmo-7B-D-0924) and an LLM (GPT-4o-mini).
tasks.scoring_detail: 4-point Likert scale rating for visual grounding; Fleiss' kappa for inter-annotator agreement.

tasks.name: Abstraction Ranking
tasks.description: Human annotators were shown an image's original caption and five generated creative captions (one for each abstraction level) in random order and asked to rank them by increasing abstraction.
tasks.task_type_notes: Humans evaluate AI-generated content.
tasks.model_type_notes: The captions were generated by a pipeline using a VLM (Molmo-7B-D-0924) and an LLM (GPT-4o-mini).
tasks.scoring_detail: Average rank (out of 6) for each caption type; Fleiss' kappa for inter-annotator agreement.

benchmarks.name: Multi-Modal Poem (MultiM-Poem)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This benchmark evaluates a model's ability to connect images with poetry, a creative and abstract form of language. It is used to test if fine-tuning on the paper's new dataset improves performance in a creative domain.

tasks.name: Poetry-to-Image Retrieval
tasks.description: Given a short poem, the task is to retrieve its corresponding image from a large set of candidates.
tasks.task_type_notes: Cross-modal retrieval task.
tasks.model_type_notes: OpenCLIP-ViT-B/32, both baseline and fine-tuned.
tasks.scoring_detail: Recall@k (k=1, 5, 10, 20), Average Rank

benchmarks.name: HAIVMet
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This benchmark evaluates a model's understanding of visual and linguistic metaphors, a key component of creative and abstract thought. It is used to test the fine-tuned model's capabilities in another creative domain.

tasks.name: Visual Metaphor-to-Linguistic Metaphor Retrieval
tasks.description: Given a visual metaphor (an image), the task is to retrieve the corresponding linguistic metaphor (text) from a set of candidates.
tasks.task_type_notes: Cross-modal retrieval task.
tasks.model_type_notes: OpenCLIP-ViT-B/32, both baseline and fine-tuned.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average Rank

tasks.name: Linguistic Metaphor-to-Visualization Matching
tasks.description: Given a linguistic metaphor, the model must choose the correct, metaphorical visualization over an incorrect, overly literal visualization.
tasks.task_type_notes: A binary choice matching task.
tasks.model_type_notes: OpenCLIP-ViT-B/32, both baseline and fine-tuned.
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage preference for the correct visualization

benchmarks.name: FOIL
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Focuses on factual correctness/hallucination, not creativity. It is used here as a baseline to demonstrate that standard models confuse creative abstraction with factual errors, which is relevant to the paper's argument, but the benchmark itself is not for creativity.

tasks.name: Literal vs. Abstract/Hallucinatory Caption Scoring
tasks.description: The FOIL dataset, which contains captions with factual errors (hallucinations), is used to analyze how a VLM (OpenCLIP) scores them compared to the paper's generated abstract captions and the original literal captions.
tasks.origin_name: The original task is to identify the mismatch between image and caption.
tasks.task_type_notes: A VLM is used to score different caption types for analysis.
tasks.model_type_notes: OpenCLIP-ViT-B/32
tasks.scoring_detail: Image-text similarity scores; percentage of times one caption type scores higher than another.

title: Generation of Punning Riddles in Portuguese with Prompt Chaining

benchmarks.name: Puntuguese
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new, manually curated dataset for punning humor recognition in Portuguese, created with a micro-editing methodology to be a challenging benchmark for computational creativity.

tasks.name: Humor Recognition
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine if a given text is a pun (humorous) or a non-humorous micro-edited version. The dataset contains 4,903 puns and their non-humorous counterparts.
tasks.origin_paper: The task is standard in the field and is directly compared to prior work on a different Portuguese corpus by Gonçalo Oliveira et al. (2020) and Inácio et al. (2023).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates traditional ML models (Random Forest) and transformer-based LLMs (BERTimbau, Albertina PT-*).
tasks.scoring_detail: F1-Score

title: CrowdCounter: A benchmark type-specific multi-target counterspeech dataset

benchmarks.name: CROWDCOUNTER
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark dataset for generating type-specific, nuanced, and creative counterspeech responses to hate speech, an open-ended text generation task.

tasks.name: Vanilla Counterspeech Generation
tasks.description: Generate a counterspeech response to a given hate speech post using a vanilla prompt.
tasks.scoring_detail: gleu, meteor, bleurt, mover-score, novelty, semantic diversity (div), dist-2, ent-2, GRUEN, argument quality, counter-argument quality, counterspeech quality, toxicity

tasks.name: Type-Specific Counterspeech Generation
tasks.description: Generate a counterspeech response of a specific type (e.g., humor, shaming) to a given hate speech post using a type-controlled prompt.
tasks.scoring_detail: bleurt, GRUEN, argument quality, counter-argument quality, counterspeech quality, toxicity, semantic diversity (div), dist-2, ent-2, precision (Flan-T5 judge), recall (GPT-4 judge), human rating (1-5)

tasks.name: Dataset Analysis
tasks.description: Statistical comparison of the dataset's quality against other datasets on metrics like readability, diversity, and argumentativeness.
tasks.task_type_notes: Dataset characterization
tasks.model_type_notes: Classifier models used for scoring dataset properties
tasks.scoring_detail: Fleisch Kincaid, Dale Chall, semantic diversity (div), argument quality, counter-argument quality, counterspeech quality, toxicity

benchmarks.name: Gab and Reddit Counterspeech Datasets
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Reused benchmark for the open-ended task of generating counterspeech, used as a baseline to evaluate the new dataset and models.
benchmarks.origin_name: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning to Intervene in Online Hate Speech

tasks.name: Vanilla Counterspeech Generation
tasks.description: Generate a counterspeech response to a given hate speech post using a vanilla prompt, for comparison against CROWDCOUNTER.
tasks.scoring_detail: gleu, meteor, bleurt, mover-score, novelty, semantic diversity (div), dist-2, ent-2, GRUEN, argument quality, counter-argument quality, counterspeech quality, toxicity

tasks.name: Dataset Analysis
tasks.description: Statistical comparison of the dataset's quality against CROWDCOUNTER on metrics like readability, diversity, and argumentativeness.
tasks.task_type_notes: Dataset characterization
tasks.model_type_notes: Classifier models used for scoring dataset properties
tasks.scoring_detail: Fleisch Kincaid, Dale Chall, semantic diversity (div), argument quality, counter-argument quality, counterspeech quality, toxicity

benchmarks.name: Counterspeech Type Classification Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset, extended from prior work, for classifying strategic and creative language types (e.g., humor, shaming) in counterspeech. Used to build models for evaluating generation tasks.
benchmarks.origin_name: Datasets from Mathew et al. (2020) and Chung et al. (2021a)
benchmarks.origin_paper: Mathew et al. (2020) and Chung et al. (2021a)

tasks.name: Counterspeech Type Classification
tasks.description: Classify a given counterspeech into one or more of six types (e.g., humor, shaming, empathy).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Hamming loss

title: DuanzAI: Slang-Enhanced LLM with Prompt for Humor Understanding

benchmarks.name: Chinese Homophonic Puns and Slang Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and evaluation framework for assessing humor understanding in LLMs, specifically focusing on Chinese homophonic puns and slang, which is a form of linguistic creativity.

tasks.name: Punchline Entity Recognition
tasks.description: Identifying and extracting the specific words or phrases that constitute the punchlines within Chinese slang expressions from the provided dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the model's ability to identify a specific component (the punchline), which is a form of named entity recognition applied to humor.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tested ChatGLM-6B, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4, and compared them against a custom BERT-LSTM-CRF system.
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact Match Accuracy (EMA), Similar Match Accuracy (SMA), Precision, Recall, F1-score

tasks.name: Comprehensive Humor Understanding
tasks.description: Evaluating an LLM's ability to understand the humor in Chinese slang expressions, tested in 0-shot, 5-shot, and clue-provided settings where punchline information is given.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model generates an output demonstrating its understanding, which is then evaluated by humans.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tested ChatGPT 3.5.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human-assigned score from 0-100 based on perceived humor understanding.

title: Creative Agents: Empowering Agents with Imagination for Creative Tasks

benchmarks.name: Minecraft Building Creation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark with 20 open-ended creative tasks (building from text prompts) in Minecraft, specifically designed to evaluate agent creativity, novelty, and diversity. Reports empirical results for several AI agents.

tasks.name: Building Creation from Text Instructions
tasks.description: An embodied agent in Minecraft receives one of 20 free-form language instructions and must generate a corresponding building by placing blocks in the game's survival mode.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests several agent architectures: LLM-only (Vanilla GPT-4, CoT+GPT-4), VLM-based (Diffusion+GPT-4V), and a behavior-cloning policy (Diffusion+BC).
tasks.scoring_detail: The generated buildings are evaluated by both a VLM (GPT-4V) and human judges on multiple criteria.

tasks.name: VLM Pairwise Comparison
tasks.description: A Vision-Language Model (GPT-4V) is prompted to evaluate two buildings generated by different agents for the same text instruction and determine which one is better overall. Results are used to calculate Elo ratings for the agents.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4V is used as the evaluator.
tasks.scoring_detail: Binary preference (left or right is better), used to compute Elo ratings.

tasks.name: VLM Direct Scoring
tasks.description: A Vision-Language Model (GPT-4V) is prompted to score a single generated building on a scale out of 10 across four aspects: Correctness, Complexity, Quality, and Functionality.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4V is used as the evaluator.
tasks.scoring_detail: Scores (out of 10) for Correctness, Complexity, Quality, Functionality, and a total score.

tasks.name: Human Evaluation
tasks.description: To validate the reliability of the VLM-based metrics, 49 human evaluators perform the same tasks as the VLM evaluator: pairwise comparison and direct scoring of the generated buildings.
tasks.model_type_notes: Human evaluation is used to score the outputs of the various creative agents tested in the paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise preference (1v1 comparison) and direct scores (0-10) on Correctness, Complexity, Aesthetics (Quality), and Functionality.

title: ModelingAgent: Bridging LLMs and Mathematical Modeling for Real-World Challenges

benchmarks.name: ModelingBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark of open-ended mathematical modeling problems from real-world competitions, designed to evaluate creativity, interdisciplinary reasoning, and practical problem-solving in LLMs.

tasks.name: Mathematical Modeling Task
tasks.description: LLMs are required to solve open-ended, real-world problems from math modeling competitions. This involves translating natural language problems into formal mathematical models, using tools to gather data, implementing the model, and producing a structured, defensible report.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates models including GPT-4o, Deepseek-Chat, Gemini, Llama3.1, Qwen2.5, and QwQ-32B.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-based evaluation via the 'ModelingJudge' framework, scoring on Structural Coherency, Solution Completeness, Groundedness (of Modeling, Data, Analysis), and Innovativeness. Also includes arena-style human ranking of solution quality and a Turing Test.

title: AGENT-DRIVEN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS FOR MANDARIN LYRIC GENERATION

benchmarks.name: Mpop600 Lyric-Melody Alignment Analysis
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a statistical analysis of an existing dataset of human-created songs to validate a premise (the importance of lyric-melody alignment). It does not evaluate the creative output of an AI system.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Chu et al., Mpop600: A mandarin popular song database with aligned audio, lyrics, and musical scores for singing voice synthesis, 2020

tasks.name: Statistical Analysis of Lyric-Melody Alignment
tasks.description: A statistical analysis was conducted on 10,427 phrases from the Mpop600 dataset to measure the match rate between Mandarin character tones and melodic contours, both with and without considering word segmentation.
tasks.task_type_notes: Dataset statistical analysis
tasks.model_type_notes: No AI model was evaluated; this is an analysis of a human-created dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Non-Segment Match Rate (NSMR), Segment Match Rate (SMR)

benchmarks.name: Character Count Control Test
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This task evaluates a technical capability (generating text of a specific length), which is a constraint for lyric generation, but does not measure the creative quality of the output itself.

tasks.name: Character Count Control
tasks.description: Different LLMs were prompted to generate Mandarin text with a specific character count (5, 10, and 20) using various methods (unrestricted, prompting, formatting, fill-in-the-blank) to test their accuracy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact character count accuracy rate

benchmarks.name: Listening Test for Agent-based Lyric Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a direct evaluation of a creative generation task (melody-to-lyric generation). It uses human judgment (ranking via a listening test) to assess the quality of the AI-generated lyrics, which is an open-ended task.

tasks.name: Listening Test
tasks.description: Four different agent groups (with varying numbers of agents) generated lyrics for three popular Chinese songs. The lyrics were rendered by a singing voice synthesizer, and 22 human participants ranked the four versions for each song.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper describes an agent-based system built on LLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average rank

title: Culturally-Nuanced Story Generation for Reasoning in Low-Resource Languages: The Case of Javanese and Sundanese

benchmarks.name: Javanese and Sundanese Story Cloze
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset for commonsense reasoning via story comprehension and generation in low-resource languages. This evaluates narrative coherence and plausibility, which are components of creative text generation.

tasks.name: Story Cloze Classification
tasks.description: Given a four-sentence story premise, the model must classify which of two provided endings is the correct and plausible continuation.
tasks.model_type_notes: Specifically, BiLSTM and XLM-R models were fine-tuned.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification accuracy

tasks.name: Story Generation
tasks.description: Given a four-sentence story premise, the model must generate a plausible fifth sentence to continue the story.
tasks.model_type_notes: Specifically, the Sahabat.AI model was fine-tuned.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, METEOR, BERTScore) and human evaluation (pairwise preference).

title: Concept Drift Guided LayerNorm Tuning for Efficient Multimodal Metaphor Identification

benchmarks.name: MET-Meme
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark consists of a dataset of internet memes and includes a core task of identifying multimodal metaphors, which is a key aspect of creative and figurative language understanding.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Xu et al., 2022. Met-meme: A multimodal meme dataset rich in metaphors.

tasks.name: Metaphor Identification (MI)
tasks.description: A multimodal classification task to determine whether a given meme contains a metaphor.
tasks.origin_paper: Xu et al., 2022. Met-meme: A multimodal meme dataset rich in metaphors.
tasks.model_type_notes: The model uses CLIP (vision-language encoder) and GPT-2 (language model) to classify memes.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (Acc), Weighted F1-score (W-F1)

tasks.name: Sentiment Analysis (SA)
tasks.description: A multimodal classification task to determine the sentiment of a given meme.

tasks.scoring_detail: Flesch-Kincaid grade level, text length, vocabulary size, number of difficult words, grammatical errors, SBERT embedding similarity.

tasks.name: Human Preference Simulation with GPT-4
tasks.description: GPT-4 is used in a few-shot setting to rate Showerthoughts on the same criteria as human evaluators, to test its ability to simulate human preferences.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4 is used as the evaluator.
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4 provides ratings from 1-6 for general score, validity, creativity, funniness, cleverness, and perceived authorship. Performance is measured by Pearson correlation with human ratings.

title: APT: Architectural Planning and Text-to-Blueprint Construction Using Large Language Models for Open-World Agents

benchmarks.name: APT Minecraft Construction Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents on creative, open-ended construction tasks in Minecraft, focusing on spatial reasoning, creativity, and instruction following. It reports empirical results for LLM-based agents.

tasks.name: Simple Wooden House Construction
tasks.description: Agent must build a basic 8x8 wooden house with specific interior furnishings (door, window, bed, crafting table) based on textual instructions.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, and GPT-o1 were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Primary scoring via VLM (GPT-4o) on Correctness, Complexity, Creativity, and Functionality (1-10 scale). VLM scores validated against assessments from 22 human judges.

tasks.name: Snow Pyramid Construction
tasks.description: Agent must build a pyramid structure using unconventional materials (snow and ice blocks) to test creativity.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, and GPT-o1 were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Primary scoring via VLM (GPT-4o) on Correctness, Complexity, Creativity, and Functionality (1-10 scale). VLM scores validated against assessments from 22 human judges.

tasks.name: Village House Construction (from Reference Image)
tasks.description: Agent must replicate a structurally complex village house from a provided reference image, testing visual interpretation.
tasks.model_type_notes: Only multimodal models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini) were tested on this task.
tasks.scoring_detail: Primary scoring via VLM (GPT-4o) on Correctness, Complexity, Creativity, and Functionality (1-10 scale). VLM scores validated against assessments from 22 human judges.

tasks.name: Watchtower with Redstone Lighting System Construction
tasks.description: Agent must build a tall watchtower with a functional Redstone-powered lighting system that activates automatically at night.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, and GPT-o1 were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Primary scoring via VLM (GPT-4o) on Correctness, Complexity, Creativity, and Functionality (1-10 scale). VLM scores validated against assessments from 22 human judges.

tasks.name: Two-Floor Mansion Construction
tasks.description: Agent must build a complex two-story mansion with detailed interior layouts, a flower garden, and a chimney, testing long-horizon planning.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, and GPT-o1 were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Primary scoring via VLM (GPT-4o) on Correctness, Complexity, Creativity, and Functionality (1-10 scale). VLM scores validated against assessments from 22 human judges.

title: Deceptive Humor: A Synthetic Multilingual Benchmark Dataset for Bridging Fabricated Claims with Humorous Content

benchmarks.name: Deceptive Humor Dataset (DHD)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new multilingual dataset and classification tasks for detecting deceptive humor, a form of creative and nuanced language use. It includes empirical results from various language models.

tasks.name: Satire Level Classification
tasks.description: A 3-class classification task to identify the level of satire (Low, Moderate, High) in a humorous comment related to a fabricated claim.
tasks.model_type_notes: Paper evaluates Encoder-Only (BERT, mBERT, etc.), Encoder-Decoder (BART, T5), and Decoder-Only (Gemma, Llama) models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1-Score, Precision, Recall, Pearson Correlation

tasks.name: Humor Attribute Prediction
tasks.description: A 5-class classification task to identify the type of humor (Irony, Absurdity, Social Commentary, Dark Humor, Wordplay) in a comment.
tasks.model_type_notes: Paper evaluates Encoder-Only (BERT, mBERT, etc.), Encoder-Decoder (BART, T5), and Decoder-Only (Gemma, Llama) models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1-Score, Precision, Recall

title: Assessing the Creativity of LLMs in Proposing Novel Solutions to Mathematical Problems

benchmarks.name: CREATIVEMATH
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark designed specifically to assess the creativity of LLMs in mathematical reasoning by tasking them with generating novel solutions to problems where some solutions are already known. It is an open-ended generation task with empirical results.

tasks.name: Novel Mathematical Solution Generation
tasks.description: Given a mathematical problem from the CREATIVEMATH dataset and a set of 'k' known reference solutions, an LLM is prompted to generate a new, correct, and novel solution that is distinct from the provided ones.
tasks.task_type_notes: The primary task is for the model under test to generate a solution. This generated solution is then evaluated for correctness and novelty by a separate panel of LLMs as the scoring mechanism.
tasks.scoring_detail: A panel of 3 LLM evaluators (GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro) judges correctness (unanimous vote) and novelty (majority vote). Reported metrics include Correctness Ratio (C), Novelty Ratio (N), Novel-Unknown Ratio (Nu), Novelty-to-Correctness Ratio (N/C), and Novel-Unknown-to-Novelty Ratio (Nu/N).

title: Improving Scientific Hypothesis Generation with Knowledge Grounded Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Scientific Hypothesis Generation Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new dataset and task for scientific hypothesis generation, which is a form of creative reasoning to produce novel, plausible scientific ideas. It evaluates LLMs on this open-ended reasoning task.

tasks.name: Scientific Hypothesis Generation
tasks.description: Given two biochemical entities, the task is to hypothesize the relationship between them ('stimulate', 'inhibit', or 'no relation') by generating a step-by-step reasoning chain (a chain of ideas). The dataset was constructed by removing known relations from the PubTator3 knowledge graph.
tasks.model_type_notes: Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.1-70B, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, F1 score, and a 'Confidence' score based on the proportion of reasoning steps verified by a KG and an LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini).

benchmarks.name: Claim Verification Annotation Set
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a fact-checking/verification task used to validate the LLM-based judge (LLM-V) in the main experiment's scoring pipeline. The task itself is not creative, but it is an evaluation performed in the paper to support the main creativity benchmark.

tasks.name: Claim Verification
tasks.description: Given a reasoning step (a claim) from a model's output and a relation triple from a knowledge graph, determine if the triple supports the claim. This was used to evaluate different LLMs as verifiers against human annotations.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates LLMs on their ability to act as judges for claim verification.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact match ratio with two human annotators.

title: DataNarrative: Automated Data-Driven Storytelling with Visualizations and Texts

benchmarks.name: DataNarrative
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark and open-ended task for generating multimodal (text + visualization specifications) data-driven stories, a form of creative synthesis and narrative construction.

tasks.name: Data Story Generation
tasks.description: Given one or more data tables, titles, and user intent, the task is to generate a coherent data story consisting of multiple textual paragraphs and corresponding visualization specifications.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise comparison (agentic vs. direct prompting) via LLM-judge (Gemini-1.5-pro) and human evaluation on Informativeness, Clarity and Coherence, Visualization Quality, Narrative Quality, and Factual Correctness.

title: Mathemyths: Leveraging Large Language Models to Teach Mathematical Language through Child-AI Co-Creative Storytelling

benchmarks.name: LLM Story Co-Creator Model Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Presents a new evaluation framework with human raters to assess the quality of LLM-generated creative content (questions and story continuations) for a child-AI co-creative storytelling context.

tasks.name: Question Generation Evaluation
tasks.description: Human evaluators rated questions generated by a prompt-engineered GPT-4, a fine-tuned GPT-3.5, and humans on a 5-point Likert scale across four dimensions to assess their quality for prompting children in a storytelling context.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares prompt-engineered GPT-4, fine-tuned GPT-3.5, and a human baseline.
tasks.scoring_detail: 5-point Likert scale ratings on readability, inspiration, story relevancy, and math language relevancy.

tasks.name: Story Continuation Evaluation
tasks.description: Human evaluators compared pairs of story continuations, one generated by GPT-4 and one by a human, to assess their quality and creativity.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares prompt-engineered GPT-4 with a human baseline.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise comparison on preference, perceived creativity, mathematics relevancy, and readability.

benchmarks.name: Child-AI Co-Creative Storytelling User Study
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A user study where children engage in an open-ended, co-creative storytelling task with an LLM-based agent (Mathemyths) to evaluate creativity, engagement, and learning.

tasks.name: Co-Creative Storytelling
tasks.description: Children aged 4-8 were randomly assigned to co-create two short stories with either the Mathemyths AI agent or a human partner. The interaction and resulting stories were evaluated on multiple dimensions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The Mathemyths system is powered by GPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human coding of engagement (response rate, length, nature of response) and story creation performance (number of ideas, elaborations). Human survey for enjoyment. Automatic metrics for system speech recognition accuracy.

benchmarks.name: Mathematical Language Assessment
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a pre/post test to measure knowledge of math vocabulary, not creativity. It is used to evaluate the educational effectiveness of the creative storytelling task.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Common Core State Standards [3, 45] and Purpura et al. [74]

tasks.name: Math Vocabulary Test
tasks.description: A 24-item questionnaire assessing children's knowledge of six math terms across four dimensions: definition, recall, transfer, and practice. Used as a pre-test and post-test in the user study.
tasks.origin_paper: Common Core State Standards [3, 45] and Purpura et al. [74]
tasks.task_type_notes: Knowledge assessment of human participants (children) to measure learning outcomes from interacting with the AI system.
tasks.model_type_notes: The LLM-based system (Mathemyths) is the intervention being evaluated; the test is administered to human participants.
tasks.scoring_detail: Binary scoring (0/1) for open-ended items (definition, practice). Scaled scoring (0/1/2) for recall/transfer items based on free recall vs. multiple choice. Total score range 0-36.

title: What Shapes a Creative Machine Mind? Comprehensively Benchmarking Creativity in Foundation Models

benchmarks.name: C2-Eval
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces C2-Eval as a new, comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the creativity of foundation models across both convergent (constrained) and divergent (open-ended) tasks, grounded in social science theories of creativity (Usefulness, Originality, Surprise).

tasks.name: Question Answering
tasks.description: A convergent creativity task where models answer open-domain questions. Creativity is measured by the accuracy (Usefulness), diversity of correct answers (Originality), and non-obviousness of correct answers (Surprise).
tasks.scoring_detail: Usefulness (accuracy), Originality (number of distinct clusters of correct solutions via cosine similarity), Surprise (1 - model's self-reported confidence on correct answers).

tasks.name: Code Generation
tasks.description: A convergent creativity task where models generate code to solve programming problems. Creativity is evaluated based on correctness (Usefulness), diversity of correct solutions (Originality), and the model's confidence (Surprise).
tasks.scoring_detail: Usefulness (passrate), Originality (number of distinct clusters of correct solutions), Surprise (1 - model's self-reported confidence on correct answers).

tasks.name: Visual Question Answering
tasks.description: A convergent creativity task where models answer questions about an image, requiring external knowledge. Creativity is assessed via correctness (Usefulness), diversity of correct answers (Originality), and non-obviousness (Surprise).
tasks.scoring_detail: Usefulness (accuracy), Originality (number of distinct clusters of correct solutions), Surprise (1 - model's self-reported confidence on correct answers).

tasks.name: Story Telling
tasks.description: A divergent creativity task where models generate short stories from prompts. An LLM-as-a-Judge evaluates the stories on coherence (Usefulness), novelty (Originality), and unexpectedness (Surprise).
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judge scores Usefulness, Originality, and Surprise on a 0-5 scale based on detailed rubrics.

tasks.name: Idea Generation
tasks.description: A divergent creativity task where models devise solutions to constrained, real-world problems. An LLM-as-a-Judge evaluates the solutions for Usefulness, Originality, and Surprise.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judge scores Usefulness, Originality, and Surprise.

tasks.name: Visual Story Telling
tasks.description: A divergent creativity task where models continue a story based on an image and background text. A Multimodal LLM (MLLM) judge evaluates the story on coherence (Usefulness), novelty (Originality), and unexpectedness (Surprise).
tasks.scoring_detail: MLLM judge scores Usefulness, Originality, and Surprise on a 0-5 scale based on detailed rubrics.

title: Past Meets Present: Creating Historical Analogy with Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Historical Analogy Acquisition
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new task, dataset, and evaluation framework for generating historical analogies, a form of creative and divergent thinking. The evaluation explicitly measures innovation by penalizing high literal similarity.

tasks.name: Popular Analogy Generation
tasks.description: Given a contemporary event, generate a well-known, analogous historical event. The dataset consists of 20 samples with standard, recognized answers.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pass@1 against standard answers; human ranking of analogy quality.

tasks.name: General Analogy Generation
tasks.description: Given a historical event from one of four themes (War, Politics, Culture/Society, Economy), generate an analogous historical event. This dataset has no standard answers and is used to test generalization.
tasks.scoring_detail: Multi-dimensional similarity (MDS) score (a mix of LLM-judged abstract similarity and Jaccard-based literal similarity); human ranking of analogy quality.

title: The Creative Psychometric Item Generator: a Framework for Item Generation and Validation Using Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Creative Problem-Solving (CPS) Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper builds a new framework (CPIG) to automatically generate and validate test items for this classic, open-ended creativity task, using LLMs for generation and evaluation.

tasks.name: CPS Item Generation
tasks.description: LLMs are used to generate new problem scenarios for the CPS task. The generation process is iterative, using high-quality examples from previous rounds to improve subsequent generations.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include Llama-2 (7b, 13b, 70b), Vicuna-1.5 (7b, 13b), and Claude-3-haiku.
tasks.scoring_detail: Iterative selection based on automated originality scores of responses; Final validation via human ratings of complexity and difficulty (1-5 scale).

tasks.name: CPS Response Generation (as human simulacra)
tasks.description: LLMs generate solutions to the newly created CPS items, simulating human test-takers. Different prompting styles (baseline, demographic, psychometric) are used to induce response variability.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models used include Llama-2, Vicuna-1.5, and Llama-7b.
tasks.scoring_detail: Originality scores predicted by a fine-tuned roberta-base model.

tasks.name: Originality Scoring of CPS Responses
tasks.description: A pre-trained model is used to automatically score the originality of LLM-generated solutions to CPS items on a five-point Likert scale.
tasks.model_type_notes: roberta-base model
tasks.scoring_detail: Predicted mean originality scores on a five-point Likert scale.

tasks.name: Human Quality Rating of CPS Items
tasks.description: Five human annotators with expertise in creativity rated the LLM-generated CPS items on their complexity and difficulty.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task evaluates the output of the generative models.
tasks.model_type_notes: The items being evaluated were generated by various LLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Complexity and difficulty ratings on a 5-point Likert scale.

title: MoPS: Modular Story Premise Synthesis for Open-Ended Automatic Story Generation

benchmarks.name: MoPS Premise Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new framework with novel automated and LLM-based metrics to evaluate the diversity and quality of AI-generated story premises, a core aspect of creative narrative generation.

tasks.name: Premise Diversity and Quality Assessment
tasks.description: Evaluating sets of story premises on semantic diversity (Breadth and Density scores) and quality (Fascination, Completeness, Originality). The paper evaluates its own MoPS method against LLM-based baselines (Vanilla, Complex) and public datasets (DOC, WritingPrompts, Storium).
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is the evaluation itself, applied to content generated by various methods.
tasks.model_type_notes: The systems being evaluated are LLM-based premise generators: MoPS (using gpt-3.5-turbo), gpt-3.5-turbo, and llama2-13b-chat (for the DOC dataset).
tasks.scoring_detail: Breadth Score (embedding polygon area), Density Score (embedding histogram std dev), Fascination/Completeness/Originality ratings (0-100 by GPT-4-Turbo/Claude-3-Opus, 1-5 by humans).

tasks.name: Premise Module Ablation Study
tasks.description: An ablation study to verify the effectiveness of different components (e.g., Twist, Ending, Event) and module dependencies within the MoPS premise generation process by masking them and re-evaluating premise quality.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the impact of ablating parts of the generation process.
tasks.model_type_notes: The MoPS system, which uses gpt-3.5-turbo, is evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fascination, Completeness, and Originality ratings by GPT-4-Turbo.

benchmarks.name: Premise-based Story Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces new tasks to measure the downstream impact of premise quality on the quality of generated long-form and short-form stories, a key aspect of controllable creative writing.

tasks.name: Long Story Quality Evaluation
tasks.description: Generating long stories (novels and scripts) from different premises using RecurrentGPT and Dramatron, and evaluating the output story quality.
tasks.model_type_notes: RecurrentGPT and Dramatron with gpt-3.5-turbo backend.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fascination, Completeness, and Originality ratings (0-100) by GPT-4-Turbo and Claude-3-Opus.

tasks.name: Short Story Quality Comparison
tasks.description: Generating short stories from MoPS premises and comparing their quality against human-written reference stories from ROC Stories and WritingPrompts datasets.
tasks.model_type_notes: gpt-3.5-turbo was used to generate the short stories.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fascination, Completeness, and Originality ratings (0-100) by GPT-4-Turbo.

title: Interesting Scientific Idea Generation using Knowledge Graphs and LLMs: Evaluations with 100 Research Group Leaders

benchmarks.name: SciMuse Scientific Idea Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new, large-scale benchmark for evaluating AI-generated scientific research ideas, a specialized form of creative ideation. It uses human expert ratings as a gold standard and tests AI systems for both generation and evaluation of these ideas.

tasks.name: Human Evaluation of AI-Generated Scientific Ideas
tasks.description: The SciMuse system (using GPT-4) generates personalized research ideas for collaboration between two scientists. These ideas (over 4,400) are then evaluated for 'interest' on a 1-5 scale by 110 expert research group leaders.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper's SciMuse system uses GPT-4 for generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Interest rating on a 1-5 scale.

tasks.name: Supervised Interest Prediction
tasks.description: A supervised model (neural network or decision tree) predicts whether a research idea will be rated as highly interesting (4 or 5) by human experts, using only knowledge graph features as input, not the generated text.
tasks.model_type_notes: Neural Network, Decision Tree
tasks.scoring_detail: AUC of ROC curve and top-N precision against human ratings.

tasks.name: Zero-Shot LLM-based Interest Ranking
tasks.description: An LLM acts as a zero-shot judge to rank generated research ideas. It performs pairwise comparisons of ideas based on predicted interest for the target researcher, and an ELO system produces a final ranking.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, and GPT-4o-mini were tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: AUC of ROC curve and top-N precision against human ratings.

title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models for Novelty Assessment in Scholarly Publications

benchmarks.name: SchNovel
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the ability of LLMs to assess novelty in scholarly publications, which is a specialized form of creativity evaluation.

tasks.name: Scholarly Novelty Assessment
tasks.description: Given a pair of scholarly papers (title, abstract, and sometimes other metadata like author or affiliation) from the same field but with different publication dates, an LLM must determine which paper is more novel. The ground truth assumes the more recently published paper is the more novel one.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs

benchmarks.name: GPQA Main Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a graduate-level Q&A benchmark focused on factual reasoning and knowledge in science domains. While it tests coherence, the task is closed-ended (multiple-choice) and does not evaluate creativity.

tasks.name: Graduate-Level Reasoning (5-shot)
tasks.description: Answering challenging, graduate-level multiple-choice questions in biology, physics, and chemistry using a 5-shot prompting strategy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

benchmarks.name: GSM8K Chain-of-Thought (GSM8K CoT)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a math word problem benchmark. Although the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) method involves generating reasoning steps, the primary goal is solving a problem with a single correct answer, not open-ended creative generation.

tasks.name: Grade School Math (8-shot CoT)
tasks.description: Solving grade school math word problems by generating intermediate reasoning steps (Chain-of-Thought) using an 8-shot prompting strategy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

tasks.name: Accuracy vs. Diversity Trade-off on GSM8K CoT-SC
tasks.description: Evaluating the trade-off between accuracy and diversity on GSM8K using chain-of-thought reasoning with self-consistency decoding (majority voting across multiple reasoning paths).
tasks.origin_paper: Cobbe et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2022
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%), Avg. Entropy of Correct Predictions

benchmarks.name: AlpacaEval Creative Writing
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is an LLM-as-a-judge benchmark specifically designed to assess an LLM's ability to generate creative and engaging text, which is an open-ended creativity task.

tasks.name: Creative Writing Generation
tasks.description: Generating creative and engaging text in response to prompts, with outputs evaluated by GPT-4 Turbo as a judge.
tasks.scoring_detail: Win Rate (%), Length-Controlled Win Rate (LC-Win Rate) (%)

benchmarks.name: Human Evaluation of Creative Writing
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a new human evaluation framework introduced by the paper to directly assess the perceived quality and diversity of creative stories generated by LLMs, an open-ended creativity task.

tasks.name: Human Rating of Story Quality and Diversity
tasks.description: Human participants recruited via Prolific rated sets of 3 generated stories on a 1-10 scale for both overall quality (coherence, relevance) and diversity (creativity, distinctness).
tasks.task_type_notes: Models generate stories which are then evaluated by humans.
tasks.scoring_detail: Quality rating 1-10, Diversity rating 1-10

benchmarks.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation for Creative Writing
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a new, structured evaluation framework introduced by the paper in the appendix to assess creative writing on multiple dimensions using an LLM judge.

tasks.name: Structured Creative Writing Evaluation
tasks.description: Models generate stories based on specific prompts within a constrained JSON schema. A GPT-4o judge then scores the outputs on creativity, originality, narrative flow, emotional impact, and imagery, and declares an overall winner.
tasks.task_type_notes: Models generate stories which are then evaluated by an LLM.
tasks.scoring_detail: Creativity score 0-10, Originality score 0-10, Narrative Flow score 0-10, Emotional Impact score 0-10, Imagery score 0-10, Overall winner

title: ANALOGYKB: Unlocking Analogical Reasoning of Language Models with A Million-scale Knowledge Base

benchmarks.name: ANALOGYKB
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new large-scale knowledge base for analogical reasoning, a core component of creative cognition. The paper evaluates its quality and its utility for training models on analogy tasks.

tasks.name: Quality Evaluation of ANALOGYKB
tasks.description: Human annotators evaluate the accuracy of randomly sampled analogies (A:B::C:D) from the newly constructed knowledge base.
tasks.task_type_notes: Humans evaluate the quality of the knowledge base content, which was partially generated by LLMs.
tasks.model_type_notes: The knowledge base itself is evaluated. Its construction involved LLMs (InstructGPT003).
tasks.scoring_detail: Analogy Accuracy (%), Fleiss's kappa

tasks.name: Filtering Pipeline Ablation
tasks.description: Evaluating the effectiveness of the automatic filtering rules (symmetry, meta-relation summarization) and manual correction for identifying analogous relation pairs.
tasks.task_type_notes: Humans evaluate the correctness of relation pairs identified by LLMs and filtering rules.
tasks.scoring_detail: # Correct analogous relation pairs, Fleiss's kappa

benchmarks.name: E-KAR
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for rationalizing natural language analogical reasoning, which is a key aspect of creativity and complex problem-solving.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question-answering task to recognize the most analogous candidate to a query pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Analogy Generation
tasks.description: Given A, B, and C, the model must generate D to complete the analogy 'A is to B as C is to D'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (judged by annotators), Fleiss's kappa

tasks.name: Analogy Explanation
tasks.description: The model must provide a reasonable explanation for a given analogy from the E-KAR dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Explanation Accuracy (%), Fleiss's kappa

benchmarks.name: BATS
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard test set for word analogies, testing for relational understanding which is a component of creative reasoning.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question-answering task to recognize the most analogous candidate to a query pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: UNIT 2
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark of word analogy problems from an educational resource, testing relational reasoning.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question-answering task to recognize the most analogous candidate to a query pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: UNIT 4
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark of word analogy problems from an educational resource, testing relational reasoning.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question-answering task to recognize the most analogous candidate to a query pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Analogy Generation
tasks.description: Given A, B, and C, the model must generate D to complete the analogy 'A is to B as C is to D'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (judged by annotators), Fleiss's kappa

benchmarks.name: Google Analogy Test Set
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A classic benchmark for intrinsic evaluation of word embeddings on semantic and morphological relations, a foundational aspect of analogical reasoning.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question-answering task to recognize the most analogous candidate to a query pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: SAT Analogy Questions
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark constructed from SAT exams, testing complex word analogies which require sophisticated relational reasoning.

tasks.name: Analogy Recognition
tasks.description: A multiple-choice question-answering task to recognize the most analogous candidate to a query pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Analogy Generation
tasks.description: Given A, B, and C, the model must generate D to complete the analogy 'A is to B as C is to D'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (judged by annotators), Fleiss's kappa

benchmarks.name: SCAN
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset specifically focused on metaphorical and scientific analogies, which are considered highly creative and abstract forms of reasoning.

tasks.name: Out-of-domain Analogy Generation
tasks.description: Models are tested on their ability to generate the final term of metaphorical and scientific analogies to evaluate generalization.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, MRR, Rec@5

title: Making New Connections: LLMs as Puzzle Generators for The New York Times' Connections Word Game

benchmarks.name: Connections Puzzle Generation & Human Preference Study
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new task and evaluation framework for generating creative word puzzles (NYT Connections) using LLMs. The evaluation is a direct comparison against human-expert puzzles via a user study measuring creativity, difficulty, and enjoyment.

tasks.name: Connections Puzzle Generation
tasks.description: An LLM generates a complete Connections puzzle, which consists of a 4x4 grid of 16 words that can be sorted into four unique groups of four words, each with a common theme. The paper evaluates several generation pipelines: a baseline 'one-step' prompt, an 'intentional overlap' method, and a 'false connection' method (both LLM-seeded and human-seeded).
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4 is used as the puzzle creator and editor.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human preference ratings (creativity, difficulty, enjoyment) in a head-to-head comparison with real NYT puzzles. Gameplay metrics like solve rate and number of mistakes are also collected.

tasks.name: Word Group Difficulty Estimation
tasks.description: To validate a proxy for puzzle difficulty, the paper analyzes 150 published NYT Connections puzzles. It calculates the average pairwise cosine similarity between word embeddings (using MPNET) for each official word group and correlates this score with the puzzle's stated difficulty color (Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple).
tasks.task_type_notes: This is an analysis task to validate an automatic metric (cosine similarity) as a proxy for human-judged difficulty. No AI generation is involved in this specific sub-task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses an embedding model (MPNET from Sentence-Transformers), not a generative LLM.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average pairwise cosine similarity of word embeddings, correlated with NYT difficulty colors.

tasks.scoring_detail: Concept Accuracy, System Accuracy

tasks.name: Embedding-based Concept Mapping
tasks.description: Using concept embeddings and various algorithms (Max-Similarity, Greedy, Kuhn-Munkres), find the optimal one-to-one mappings between concepts of two systems based on cosine similarity.
tasks.task_type_notes: Algorithmic mapping based on pre-computed embeddings, not generative text output from an LLM.

tasks.scoring_detail: System Accuracy

tasks.name: Open Analogical Structure Abduction

title: Can AI Examine Novelty of Patents?: Novelty Evaluation Based on the Correspondence between Patent Claim and Prior Art

tasks.name: Novelty Classification (Claim-Cited Texts input)
tasks.description: A binary classification task where models determine if a patent claim is 'Novel' or 'Non-Novel' by comparing its text against cited texts from prior art documents. Models are tested using both classification heads and generative prompting (including explanation generation).
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is framed as binary classification but is tested with both traditional classification heads and generative models that produce a label and an optional explanation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 score, Qualitative analysis of generated explanations

tasks.name: Novelty Classification (Only Claim input)
tasks.description: A baseline binary classification task where models determine if a patent claim is 'Novel' or 'Non-Novel' based only on the claim's text, without access to prior art.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is framed as binary classification but is tested with both traditional classification heads and generative models that produce a label.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Human Testing
tasks.description: A human baseline evaluation where one of the authors classified 20 examples for both the 'Only Claim' and 'Claim-Cited Texts' input conditions to establish a performance benchmark and gauge task difficulty.
tasks.task_type_notes: Human performing the classification task to set a performance baseline.
tasks.model_type_notes: Human expert (one of the authors)
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: Beyond Memorization: Mapping the Originality-Quality Frontier of Language Models

tasks.name: Story Completion
tasks.description: Models are given the first line of a story from the TinyStories dataset and must generate a coherent and creative completion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Novelty score: Harmonic mean of (1) n-gram originality (fraction of unseen 4,5,6-grams vs. training data) and (2) LLM-judged quality (0-5 scale, normalized).

tasks.name: Poetry Writing
tasks.description: Based on the CoPoet dataset, models must generate a single line of poetry that follows a given instruction about content and literary devices.
tasks.scoring_detail: Novelty score: Harmonic mean of (1) n-gram originality (fraction of unseen 4,5,6-grams vs. training data) and (2) LLM-judged quality (0-5 scale, normalized).

tasks.name: Creative Tool Use
tasks.description: Using the MacGyver dataset, models are given a reasoning problem and must generate a solution that requires creative and feasible use of common objects.
tasks.scoring_detail: Novelty score: Harmonic mean of (1) n-gram originality (fraction of unseen 4,5,6-grams vs. training data) and (2) LLM-judged quality (0-5 scale, normalized).
