title: Harnessing Large Language Models for Scientific Novelty Detection

benchmarks.name: Scientific Novelty Detection Datasets (Marketing & NLP)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces new datasets and tasks specifically for evaluating scientific novelty detection in LLMs, a key aspect of creativity in a research context.

tasks.name: Research Idea Retrieval
tasks.description: Given a synthesized (non-novel) research idea, the task is to retrieve its original 'anchor' paper/idea from a large corpus of novel ideas.
tasks.task_type_notes: Information retrieval task to find conceptually similar ideas, used as a preliminary step for the novelty detection task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Various text embedding models (GTE, E5, SimCSE, SBERT, BGE) are tested.

tasks.name: Novelty Detection (ND)
tasks.description: Classify a given research idea as either 'Novel' or 'Non-Novel' with respect to a corpus of existing ideas using a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach.
tasks.model_type_notes: A RAG system using a retriever (e.g., BGE) and an LLM judge (e.g., deepseek-reasoner).
tasks.scoring_detail: An LLM assigns novelty scores (0.0-1.0) based on a rubric; a decision tree classifier makes the final binary prediction. Performance is measured by Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score.

title: Learning Personalized Alignment for Evaluating Open-ended Text Generation

benchmarks.name: Per-MPST
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset for evaluating LLMs on their ability to align with personalized, subjective preferences for creative text (movie plots), which is a key aspect of creativity evaluation.

tasks.name: Personalized Scalar Rating and Review Generation
tasks.description: Given a reviewer's profile of past movie reviews, the model predicts a scalar score (1-10) for a new movie plot and generates a textual review from the reviewer's perspective.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model both evaluates (predicts a score) and generates (writes a review).
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson, Spearman, Kendall correlation (for scores); BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, BARTScore (for generated reviews)

benchmarks.name: Per-DOC
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset for evaluating LLMs on making fine-grained, personalized preference judgments between two generated story plots across creative aspects like interestingness, surprise, and character development.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Zhu et al. (2023) / Yang et al. (2023)

tasks.name: Personalized Pairwise Rating on Creative Aspects
tasks.description: Given a reviewer's profile and two story plots, the model chooses the preferred plot across five subjective aspects: Interestingness, Adaptability, Surprise, Character Development, and Ending.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: Amazon book review dataset (personalized)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used to test the zero-shot generalization of a personalized evaluation model on a new domain of creative content (books), assessing its ability to align with user preferences without domain-specific fine-tuning.

tasks.name: Zero-shot Personalized Scalar Rating
tasks.description: A model trained on personalized movie reviews (Per-MPST) is evaluated on its ability to predict a user's rating for a book in a zero-shot setting, based on the user's profile.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson, Spearman, Kendall correlation

title: AI Idea Bench 2025: AI Research Idea Generation Benchmark

benchmarks.name: AI Idea Bench 2025
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the creative task of AI research idea generation by LLMs. It includes a new dataset and a suite of evaluation tasks focused on alignment, novelty, and feasibility, and reports empirical results for several LLM-based systems.

tasks.name: Idea Multiple-Choice Evaluation (IMCQ)
tasks.description: An LLM judge selects which of four candidate ideas (one ground-truth, three distractors) is the closest match to an idea generated by a model. The metric is the success rate of the generated idea leading the judge to select the ground-truth option.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is an evaluation protocol applied to the output of a generation model. An LLM judge performs the evaluation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Success rate of an LLM judge (Deepseek V3) selecting the ground-truth paper idea as the best match for the generated idea.

tasks.name: Idea-to-Idea Matching (I2I)
tasks.description: An LLM judge directly compares a generated idea (motivation and experimental plan) with the ground-truth idea from the target paper and assigns a similarity score.
tasks.scoring_detail: Similarity score [0-5] from an LLM judge (Deepseek V3).

tasks.name: Idea-to-Topic Matching (I2T)
tasks.description: An LLM judge assesses the alignment between a generated idea and the specified topic of the target paper, assigning a similarity score.
tasks.scoring_detail: Similarity score [0-5] from an LLM judge (Deepseek V3).

tasks.name: Ideas Competition (IC)
tasks.description: An LLM judge conducts pairwise comparisons of ideas generated by different baseline models across six aspects (e.g., innovativeness, feasibility) to determine a winner for each pair.
tasks.scoring_detail: Total score based on pairwise wins as determined by an LLM judge (Deepseek V3).

tasks.name: Novelty Assessment (NA)
tasks.description: Quantifies the novelty of a generated idea by calculating a score based on its similarity to historical and contemporary literature (retrieved via Semantic Scholar API) and the citation counts of contemporary papers.
tasks.origin_name: Holistic evaluation schema (HD, CD, CI, ON)
tasks.origin_paper: Su et al., 2024 (Two heads are better than one...)
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall Novelty (SN) score calculated from historical difference, contemporary difference, and contemporary citation count.

tasks.name: Feasibility Assessment (FA)
tasks.description: Assesses an idea's feasibility by decomposing it into conceptual steps, retrieving relevant literature for each step, and calculating a score based on the normalized citation influence of the retrieved papers.
tasks.scoring_detail: Feasibility (SF) score calculated as the average normalized influence of reference papers. Also reports Feasibility Per Step (FPS).

title: TPPoet: Transformer-Based Persian Poem Generation using Minimal Data and Advanced Decoding Techniques

benchmarks.name: Persian Poem Generation

tasks.name: Automatic Quality and Diversity Evaluation
tasks.description: Generated Persian poem couplets are evaluated for quality using BLEU score against a validation set and for diversity using Self-BLEU score, which measures the similarity of generated texts to each other.
tasks.origin_paper: BLEU is from Papineni et al., 2002 (cited as [39]); Self-BLEU is from Zhu et al., 2018 (cited as [41]).
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU2, BLEU3, BLEU4, Self-BLEU2 (S-BLEU2), Self-BLEU3 (S-BLEU3), Self-BLEU4 (S-BLEU4)

tasks.name: Human Evaluation of Generated Poetry
tasks.description: Human participants rated poems from the proposed model (TPPoet), a baseline model (GPT2-Persian), and human poets on a 1-5 scale across five criteria. They also identified whether they believed the poem was written by a human or AI.
tasks.origin_paper: H. M. Manurung, 'An evolutionary algorithm approach to poetry generation' (cited as [3])
tasks.scoring_detail: 1-5 ratings for fluency, coherence, meaningfulness, poeticness, and overall quality; Percentage identified as human-written

title: Can Language Models Laugh at YouTube Short-form Videos?

benchmarks.name: ExFunTube
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale dataset of short-form videos with human-annotated timestamps and explanations of funny moments, designed to evaluate multimodal humor understanding and explanation generation in AI models.

tasks.name: Video Humor Explanation
tasks.description: Models generate a textual explanation for why a given short-form video from the ExFunTube dataset is humorous.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tests include text-only LLMs (T5, BART, GPT-3.5), an end-to-end multimodal model (MAF), and multimodal prompting frameworks (VideoChat-Text, and the paper's own method).
tasks.scoring_detail: SentBERT score, ROSCOE (RA) score, Rationale quality score (via moment localization), Human rating (0-1 scale), Human comparison (preference).

tasks.name: Moment Localization for Rationale Quality
tasks.description: A video moment retrieval model (QD-DETR) predicts the start and end timestamps of a funny moment in a video, given a textual explanation. This task is used to evaluate the quality of the generated explanations from the main task.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a video moment retrieval task used as a proxy to evaluate the quality of generated humor explanations.
tasks.model_type_notes: Video moment retrieval model (QD-DETR)
tasks.scoring_detail: Sum of IoU differences between predictions from gold vs. model-generated explanations. Lower score is better.

tasks.name: Humor Taxonomy Classification
tasks.description: Videos are classified into one of 20 humor categories based on their annotated explanation. This is done to analyze the performance of humor explanation models across different types of humor.
tasks.model_type_notes: ChatGPT was used for classification.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification into 20 humor categories via one-shot prompting of ChatGPT. Used for performance analysis of other models.

title: Curiosity-Driven LLM-as-a-judge for Personalized Creative Judgment

benchmarks.name: Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the creative writing capabilities of LLMs, based on the established Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking. The tasks involve judging creativity along multiple dimensions, which is a core aspect of creativity evaluation.

tasks.name: Personalized Creative Judgment Prediction (In-Distribution)
tasks.description: An LLM-as-a-judge predicts the binary creativity verdicts (yes/no) of individual human experts for stories, based on specific creative dimensions. The model is trained and tested using 5-fold cross-validation on the same set of 5 creative dimensions (Originality in Thought, Form, Theme; Structural Flexibility; Perspective/Voice Flexibility).
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson correlation, Cohen’s κ, F1-score, Precision, Recall

tasks.name: Personalized Creative Judgment Prediction (Out-of-Distribution)
tasks.description: An LLM-as-a-judge is trained on 4 creative dimensions from the TTCW dataset and tested on its ability to predict expert verdicts for a held-out 5th dimension ('Originality in Thought') to measure generalization.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pearson correlation, Cohen’s κ, F1-score, Precision, Recall

title: Sparks of Science: Hypothesis Generation Using Structured Paper Data

tasks.scoring_detail: Perplexity, IAScore, Idea Distinctiveness Index, pairwise comparison by LLM judges (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, o3-mini) on novelty/feasibility/overall quality, and human evaluation on novelty/feasibility/overall preference.

title: Richer Output for Richer Countries: Uncovering Geographical Disparities in Generated Stories and Travel Recommendations

benchmarks.name: HumorBench Hard
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A challenging subset of a creativity benchmark (HumorBench) used to test the limits of LLM reasoning on difficult humor comprehension tasks.

tasks.name: Joke Explanation on Hard Subset

benchmarks.name: Autograder Validation Benchmark

tasks.name: Judging Humor Explanations

benchmarks.name: GPQA-Diamond

benchmarks.name: ARC-AGI

tasks.name: Correlation Analysis
tasks.description: The performance scores of various LLMs on ARC-AGI were used to calculate the correlation with their performance on HumorBench.
tasks.task_type_notes: Comparative analysis; uses existing benchmark scores to validate a new benchmark.
tasks.scoring_detail: Spearman's rank correlation (ρ) and p-value.

benchmarks.name: LM Arena ELO
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A general chatbot evaluation benchmark based on human preference, not specifically focused on creativity. It was used in this paper only for correlational analysis.

tasks.name: Correlation Analysis
tasks.description: The ELO ratings of various LLMs from LM Arena were used to calculate the correlation with their performance on HumorBench.
tasks.task_type_notes: Comparative analysis; uses existing benchmark scores to validate a new benchmark.
tasks.scoring_detail: Spearman's rank correlation (ρ) and p-value.

title: Can Large Language Models Unlock Novel Scientific Research Ideas?

benchmarks.name: Future Research Idea Generation Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new dataset, tasks, and metrics (both automated and human) to evaluate the creative capacity of LLMs for generating novel scientific research ideas, a key aspect of scientific innovation.

tasks.name: Future Research Idea (FRI) Generation
tasks.description: LLMs are prompted to generate potential future research ideas based on the full text of a scientific paper from which the authors' original future work section has been removed. The evaluation is performed on papers from five domains: Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, and Medicine.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-based Idea Alignment Score (IAScore), embedding-based Idea Distinctness Index, and human ratings for Novelty, Relevance, and Feasibility.

tasks.name: FRI Generation with Background Knowledge
tasks.description: An extension of the FRI generation task where LLMs are provided with additional background knowledge retrieved from related papers (using a RAG-like pipeline) to improve idea generation. This was tested on the Computer Science domain.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation ratings for Novelty, Relevance, and Feasibility.

tasks.name: Idea Matching
tasks.description: A task to determine if a single generated research idea is semantically contained within a collection of author-proposed ideas. This was used to select the best model for the 'IdeaMatcher' component of the IAScore metric.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tested a RoBERTa MNLI model, BERTScore, and a prompted GPT-3.5 model.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy on a manually annotated corpus of matching and non-matching idea pairs.

title: Visually Grounded Story Generation Challenge

benchmarks.name: Visually Grounded Story Generation (VGSG) Challenge
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new shared task (benchmark) for generating coherent and visually grounded stories from image sequences, a creative, open-ended task for vision-language models. It defines the datasets, evaluation metrics, and experimental setup.

tasks.name: Strict Track
tasks.description: Generate a story from an image sequence using only provided visual features and training data to explore language-vision mapping and generation models in a controlled setting.
tasks.model_type_notes: The challenge is designed for Vision-and-Language Models. Baselines mentioned include Seq2Seq, TAPM, VL-T5, BLIP, and MiniGPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BERTScore, character-matching (CM), event diversity metrics, entity grid coherence. Human: narrativity, character grounding, coherence.

tasks.name: Open Track
tasks.description: Generate a story from an image sequence using any resources (e.g., pre-trained models, additional text/vision data) except other vision-and-language datasets, aiming to test state-of-the-art performance.
tasks.model_type_notes: The challenge is designed for Vision-and-Language Models. Baselines mentioned include Seq2Seq, TAPM, VL-T5, BLIP, and MiniGPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BERTScore, character-matching (CM), event diversity metrics, entity grid coherence. Human: narrativity, character grounding, coherence.

tasks.name: Grounding Track
tasks.description: Generate a story from an image sequence and also provide a mapping of all generated text entities to the provided characters in the images. This track is specifically evaluated on the VIST-Character dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: The challenge is designed for Vision-and-Language Models. Baselines mentioned include Seq2Seq, TAPM, VL-T5, BLIP, and MiniGPT-4.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BERTScore, character-matching (CM), event diversity metrics, entity grid coherence. Human: narrativity, character grounding, coherence.

title: TwistList: Resources and Baselines for Tongue Twister Generation

benchmarks.name: TwistList
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset and task for a creative language generation problem (tongue twisters), and provides baseline results for several LLMs using both automatic and human evaluation.

tasks.name: Tongue Twister Generation
tasks.description: Given a set of keywords, generate a tongue twister that is semantically related to the keywords, exhibits high phonetic overlap across tokens, and is grammatically valid.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: Perplexity (PPL), BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, Phonetic Overlap (PO), Initial Phonetic Overlap (Init-PO). Human: 5-point Likert scale ratings for Relevance, Fluency, Difficulty of Articulation, Cohesion, and Entertainment Value.

title: Amuse: Human-AI Collaborative Songwriting with Multimodal Inspirations

benchmarks.name: Technical Evaluation of Chord Progression Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Presents a set of new automatic and human evaluation tasks to assess the diversity, coherence, and relevance of AI-generated musical chord progressions, which are core aspects of musical creativity.

tasks.name: Diversity Evaluation of Prompting Technique
tasks.description: An automatic evaluation comparing the diversity of chord progressions generated by the paper's batch prompting technique against a conventional method of querying an LLM multiple times.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o was used for generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Self-BLEU score

tasks.name: Automatic Coherence Evaluation
tasks.description: An automatic evaluation to assess the musical coherence of generated chord progressions by computing the Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) between their distribution and the distribution of chords in a real music dataset (HookTheory).
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares GPT-4o, an LSTM model, and the paper's rejection-sampling method.
tasks.scoring_detail: Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) on unigram and bigram chord distributions

tasks.name: Human Listening Study
tasks.description: Human listeners were presented with pairs of chord progression audio clips and asked to choose which one was more musically coherent ('pleasant and natural') and which better reflected given keywords.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares GPT-4o, an LSTM model, and the paper's rejection-sampling method.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise preference on musical coherence and keyword relevance

benchmarks.name: Songwriting User Study
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A user study designed to evaluate a human-AI co-creative system (Amuse) in an open-ended songwriting task. It measures user experience, perceived creativity, agency, and other HCI aspects of creativity support.

tasks.name: 8-bar Chorus Composition Task
tasks.description: A within-subjects study where 10 songwriters were tasked to write an 8-bar chorus based on a given prompt. They completed the task under two conditions: using a baseline AI tool (Aria) alone, and using both the baseline tool and the paper's new system (Amuse).
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates an AI system's ability to support a human's creative generation process.
tasks.model_type_notes: The Amuse system uses GPT-4o.
tasks.scoring_detail: Seven-point Likert scale ratings (including Creativity Support Index), semi-structured interviews, interaction logs

title: The Next Chapter: A Study of Large Language Models in Storytelling

benchmarks.name: Conditional Story Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The core of the paper is an empirical evaluation of open-ended story generation from prompts, a classic AI creativity task. It compares multiple LLMs on three different datasets.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Mostafazadeh et al., 2016; Fan et al., 2018; Hermann et al., 2015

tasks.name: ROCStories Generation
tasks.description: Generate the last 4 sentences of a 5-sentence commonsense story, given the first sentence as context.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: CBL (Corpus BLEU), MSJ (MS-Jaccard), BES (BERTScore), BRT (BLEURT), BBL (Backward BLEU), SBL (Self-BLEU), D-3 (Distinct-3), LR-n (Lexical Repetition), BAS (BARTScore), LEN (Length). Human: 1-5 Likert scale ratings for fluency, coherence, relatedness, logicality, interestingness.

tasks.name: WritingPrompts Generation
tasks.description: Generate a 10-sentence fictional story from a short paragraph prompt.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: CBL (Corpus BLEU), MSJ (MS-Jaccard), BES (BERTScore), BRT (BLEURT), BBL (Backward BLEU), SBL (Self-BLEU), D-3 (Distinct-3), LR-n (Lexical Repetition), BAS (BARTScore), LEN (Length). Human: 1-5 Likert scale ratings for fluency, coherence, relatedness, logicality, interestingness.

tasks.name: CNN News Generation
tasks.description: Generate a long news story (around 20 sentences) conditioned on the news title.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: CBL (Corpus BLEU), MSJ (MS-Jaccard), BES (BERTScore), BRT (BLEURT), BBL (Backward BLEU), SBL (Self-BLEU), D-3 (Distinct-3), LR-n (Lexical Repetition), BAS (BARTScore), LEN (Length). Human: 1-5 Likert scale ratings for fluency, coherence, relatedness, logicality, interestingness.

benchmarks.name: Story Plagiarism Investigation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Assesses the originality of generated stories by checking for direct and indirect copying, which is a critical aspect of evaluating generation creativity.

tasks.name: iThenticate Plagiarism Check
tasks.description: Use iThenticate software to assess the percentage of lexical overlap between GPT-3 generated stories and online articles.
tasks.origin_paper: Commercial software, not from a paper.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper only reports results for GPT-3.
tasks.scoring_detail: Similarity score (%)

tasks.name: Manual Plagiarism Check
tasks.description: Human annotators manually check for 'soft plagiarism' by searching for keywords, named entities, and long phrases from generated stories on the web to find matching real-world articles.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper only reports results for GPT-3.
tasks.scoring_detail: Identification of instances based on real stories (e.g., count of plagiarized stories out of a sample).

title: BottleHumor: Self-Informed Humor Explanation using the Information Bottleneck Principle

benchmarks.name: MemeCap
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for generating explanations of humor in memes, which is an open-ended, creative language task. The paper uses it to evaluate VLM performance.

tasks.name: Humor Explanation Generation
tasks.description: Given a meme image and its associated title, the task is to generate a brief explanation interpreting the visual metaphors and their relation to the text.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-based precision, recall, and macro-F1 scores, where an LLM (Gemini-Flash-1.5) verifies the presence of atomic facts from a reference explanation in the generated explanation, and vice-versa.

benchmarks.name: New Yorker Cartoon
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for explaining humor in cartoons, requiring commonsense and world knowledge. It is an open-ended generation task used to evaluate VLMs.

tasks.name: Humor Explanation Generation
tasks.description: Given a New Yorker cartoon and its caption, the task is to generate an explanation for why the caption is funny in the context of the cartoon.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-based precision, recall, and macro-F1 scores, where an LLM (Gemini-Flash-1.5) verifies the presence of atomic facts from a reference explanation in the generated explanation, and vice-versa.

benchmarks.name: YesBut
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A benchmark for explaining humor or satire in images that present a contrast. It is an open-ended generation task used to evaluate VLMs.

tasks.name: Humor/Satire Explanation
tasks.description: Given an image with two parts captioned 'yes' and 'but', the task is to explain why the image is funny or satirical.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-based precision, recall, and macro-F1 scores, where an LLM (Gemini-Flash-1.5) verifies the presence of atomic facts from a reference explanation in the generated explanation, and vice-versa.

title: I Spy a Metaphor: Large Language Models and Diffusion Models Co-Create Visual Metaphors

benchmarks.name: HAIVMet (Human-AI Visual Metaphor)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and set of evaluation tasks for generating visual metaphors from linguistic metaphors, a core creative capability combining linguistic and visual modalities.

tasks.name: Visual Metaphor Generation
tasks.description: Generating a visual metaphor image from a linguistic metaphor. The experiment compares five systems: generating directly from the metaphor using DALL·E 2 or Stable Diffusion (SD), versus using an LLM-generated "visual elaboration" as a prompt for DALL·E 2, SD, or a structured version of SD.
tasks.model_type_notes: The systems tested were combinations of an LLM (Instruct GPT-3) and Diffusion models (DALL·E 2, Stable Diffusion v2.1).
tasks.scoring_detail: Average rank, percentage of 'Lost Cause' images, average number of suggested edits. All ratings by professional illustrators.

tasks.name: HAIVMet vs. LLM-DALL·E 2 Quality Comparison
tasks.description: Professional artists perform a blind pairwise comparison between images from the final curated HAIVMet dataset (which includes human filtering and editing) and raw outputs from the best-performing automated system (LLM-DALL·E 2) to evaluate the benefit of human-AI collaboration.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the quality of generated content from two different pipelines.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares images generated by LLM-DALL·E 2 with and without a final human curation step.
tasks.scoring_detail: Preference percentage, % Lost Cause, % Perfect.

tasks.name: Prompting Strategy Comparison (CoT vs. Completion)
tasks.description: Human annotators compare images generated from visual elaborations created with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting versus standard Completion prompting to determine which prompting strategy yields better visual metaphors.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the quality of generated content resulting from different prompting methods.
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses Instruct GPT-3 for prompt generation and DALL·E 2 for image generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Majority vote preference count between images from CoT vs. Completion prompts.

benchmarks.name: Visual Entailment on Metaphoric Images
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The task is a closed-ended classification (entailment/contradiction/neutral), not a creative generation task. However, it is used to evaluate the utility of a new creative dataset (HAIVMet) by testing a model's understanding of the generated visual metaphors.

tasks.name: Visual Entailment Classification
tasks.description: Given a visual metaphor image from the HAIVMet dataset and a textual hypothesis, a Vision-Language Model predicts whether the image entails, contradicts, or is neutral to the hypothesis. This is used as a downstream task to evaluate the quality and utility of the HAIVMet dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is a 3-way classification problem to assess a model's understanding of the image-text relationship.
tasks.model_type_notes: The OFA model was fine-tuned and tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: FunQA: Towards Surprising Video Comprehension

benchmarks.name: FunQA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale video question answering (VideoQA) dataset designed to evaluate AI systems' understanding of counter-intuitive and surprising content, including humor, creativity, and magic. The tasks are open-ended and focus on reasoning, description, and localization of these creative elements.

tasks.name: Humor Timestamp Localization (H1)
tasks.description: Identify the specific time period within a humorous video when the most amusing event takes place.
tasks.task_type_notes: Localization task to output a start and end timestamp.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on various VLMs and TimeChat.
tasks.scoring_detail: Intersection of Unions (IOU) based on time span

tasks.name: Humor Detailed Description (H2)
tasks.description: Generate a free-text, objective description of the events within the identified humorous segment of a video.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Humor Reasoning (H3)
tasks.description: Generate a free-text explanation for why a video is humorous, requiring reasoning about the entire video and common sense.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Humor Title Generation (H4)
tasks.description: Generate a concise, vivid, and appropriate title summarizing the humorous video's content.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Creative Timestamp Localization (C1)
tasks.description: Identify the specific time period within a creative video when the most creative segment takes place.
tasks.task_type_notes: Localization task to output a start and end timestamp.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on various VLMs and TimeChat.
tasks.scoring_detail: Intersection of Unions (IOU) based on time span

tasks.name: Creative Detailed Description (C2)
tasks.description: Generate a free-text, objective description of the events within the identified creative segment of a video.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Creative Reasoning (C3)
tasks.description: Generate a free-text explanation for why a video is creative.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Creative Title Generation (C4)
tasks.description: Generate a concise title summarizing the creative video's content.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Creative Scoring (C5)
tasks.description: Rate the creativity of a video on a scale of 1 to 20.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (based on CreativeScoreMetric)

tasks.name: Magic Timestamp Localization (M1)
tasks.description: Identify the specific time period within a magic video when the magic trick takes place.
tasks.task_type_notes: Localization task to output a start and end timestamp.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on various VLMs and TimeChat.
tasks.scoring_detail: Intersection of Unions (IOU) based on time span

tasks.name: Magic Detailed Description (M2)
tasks.description: Generate a free-text, objective description of the events within the identified magical segment of a video.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Magic Reasoning (M3)
tasks.description: Generate a free-text explanation for why a video is counter-intuitive or magical.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on models like mPLUG, GIT, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Otter, etc.
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Multiple-Choice Question Answering (FunQA-MC & FunQA-MC-R)
tasks.description: Answer multiple-choice questions about the video's content or the reason for its counter-intuitiveness. FunQA-MC-R specifically focuses on reasoning questions.
tasks.task_type_notes: Classification/selection task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on Otter (VLM), GPT-4 (LLM), and GPT-4V (VLM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: NExT-QA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Used as a comparative benchmark for general video reasoning. Its focus is on explaining temporal actions in daily life videos, which is related to but not explicitly centered on creativity. The paper uses it to show that existing reasoning benchmarks are less challenging for modern VLMs compared to FunQA.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Xiao, J., Shang, X., Yao, A., Chua, T.S.: Next-qa:next phase of question-answering to explaining temporal actions (2021)

tasks.name: Open-Ended Question Answering (NExT-OE)
tasks.description: Answer open-ended questions requiring temporal and causal reasoning about events in daily life videos.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on Otter (VLM) and GPT-4 (LLM).
tasks.scoring_detail: WUPS, GPT-4 score

tasks.name: Multiple-Choice Question Answering
tasks.description: Answer multiple-choice questions requiring temporal and causal reasoning about events in daily life videos.
tasks.task_type_notes: Classification/selection task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Evaluated on Otter (VLM), GPT-4 (LLM), and GPT-4V (VLM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

title: Harmonizing Pixels and Melodies: Maestro-Guided Film Score Generation and Composition Style Transfer

benchmarks.name: FilmScoreDB
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale dataset of 32,520 film clip-music pairs specifically curated for the creative task of generating film scores.

tasks.name: Film Score Generation
tasks.description: Generating a 10-second music score from a given film clip, aiming to align with the video's semantic, emotional, and aesthetic content.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent diffusion model with a ControlNet architecture (HPM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Rhythm Correspondence (BCS, BHS, F1 scores), Music Quality (IS, KL, FAD), Generation Stability (CSD, HSD), and subjective human evaluation (MOS).

tasks.name: Composition Style Transfer
tasks.description: Generating a music score for a film clip while transferring the style from a target music piece, using melody and dynamics as control signals.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent diffusion model with a ControlNet architecture (HPM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Melody accuracy, Dynamics correlation (micro and macro), Music Quality (IS, KL, FAD).

benchmarks.name: EmoMV
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An existing dataset for video-to-music generation, used here for comparative evaluation of the proposed model against baselines on a standard benchmark.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Thao, H.T.P., Roig, G., Herremans, D.: Emomv: Affective music-video correspondence learning datasets for classification and retrieval. Information Fusion 91, 64–79 (2023)

tasks.name: Video-to-Music Generation
tasks.description: Generating a music score from a music video clip, evaluated for rhythm correspondence and music quality.
tasks.origin_paper: Thao, H.T.P., Roig, G., Herremans, D.: Emomv: Affective music-video correspondence learning datasets for classification and retrieval. Information Fusion 91, 64–79 (2023)
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent diffusion model with a ControlNet architecture (HPM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Rhythm Correspondence (BCS, BHS, F1 scores), Music Quality (IS, KL, FAD), Generation Stability (CSD, HSD), and subjective human evaluation (MOS).

tasks.name: Composition Style Transfer
tasks.description: Generating a music score for a music video clip while transferring style based on melody and dynamics, where each emotion category in the dataset is treated as a distinct style.
tasks.origin_paper: The task of style transfer using specific melody/dynamic controls on this dataset is an extension by the current paper.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses a latent diffusion model with a ControlNet architecture (HPM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Melody accuracy, Dynamics correlation (micro and macro), Music Quality (IS, KL, FAD).

benchmarks.name: Originality vs. Recognizability Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A novel evaluation framework for generated music that measures two key aspects of creativity: originality (novelty) and recognizability (stylistic adherence).
benchmarks.origin_paper: Boutin, V., Singhal, L., Thomas, X., Serre, T.: Diversity vs. recognizability: Human-like generalization in one-shot generative models. (2022)

tasks.name: Originality vs. Recognizability Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating generated film scores on two dimensions: originality, measured by feature variance, and recognizability, measured by the accuracy of a one-shot musical style classifier.
tasks.origin_paper: The framework is adapted from prior work and applied as a new evaluation metric for film score generation.
tasks.model_type_notes: This framework is used to evaluate the audio output of diffusion-based music generation models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Originality score (based on variance of features from a pre-trained model) and Recognizability score (one-shot classification accuracy).

title: Generating similes like a Pro: A Style Transfer Approach for Simile Generation

benchmarks.name: Simile Generation from Literal Sentences
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new open-ended generation task focused on a creative linguistic device (similes), with a novel dataset and human evaluation criteria for creativity, relevance, and quality.

tasks.name: Simile Generation
tasks.description: Given a literal sentence, the task is to generate a corresponding simile by replacing a descriptive property (e.g., an adjective or adverb) with a comparative phrase ('like a [vehicle]').
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: BLEU-1, BLEU-2, BERTScore, Novelty. Human: 1-5 ratings for Creativity, Overall Quality, Relevance1 (vehicle-property), Relevance2 (vehicle-topic), and pairwise win rate.

benchmarks.name: Simile for Story Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A task-based evaluation measuring the creative impact (evocativeness) of generated similes when integrated into a downstream story generation task.

tasks.name: Story Enhancement Evaluation
tasks.description: A literal sentence in a machine-generated story is replaced with a generated simile, and humans evaluate the resulting story's creativity and evocativeness.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves generating stories, then generating similes to insert into them, followed by human evaluation of the final story.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-2 was used for story generation and BART-based models for simile generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings (1-5 scale) for story creativity and evocativeness; pairwise win percentage reported.

title: MOOSE-Chem2: Exploring LLM Limits in Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery via Hierarchical Search

benchmarks.name: Fine-grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating the generation of detailed, actionable scientific hypotheses in chemistry, a key aspect of scientific creativity. It uses an open-ended generation task and reports empirical results with LLMs.

tasks.name: Fine-grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery
tasks.description: Given a research background, a survey of methods, and a coarse-grained hypothesis direction, the task is to generate a detailed, experimentally actionable fine-grained hypothesis.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM-based pairwise comparison (effectiveness, novelty, detailedness, feasibility), human expert ranking, and LLM-based Soft Recall and Hard Recall against ground-truth hypotheses.

title: Benchmarking Cognitive Domains for LLMS: Insights from Taiwanese Hakka Culture

benchmarks.name: Hakka Cultural Knowledge Cognitive Domain Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset to evaluate LLMs on higher-order cognitive skills, including a 'Creating' domain based on Bloom's Taxonomy, which directly assesses creative synthesis and ideation in a specific cultural context.

tasks.name: Remembering
tasks.description: LLMs are tested on their ability to recall facts about Hakka culture through multiple-choice questions. Example: 'What are Miaoli County’s main Hakka settlements?'
tasks.origin_paper: Bloom, B. (1956). Handbook I: Cognitive domain.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Understanding
tasks.description: LLMs are tested on their comprehension of concepts related to Hakka culture through multiple-choice questions. Example: 'What distinguishes Hakka culinary practices?'
tasks.origin_paper: Bloom, B. (1956). Handbook I: Cognitive domain.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Applying
tasks.description: LLMs are tested on their ability to apply knowledge of Hakka culture to new situations through multiple-choice questions. Example: 'How can Hakka clothing styles be used in modern fashion?'
tasks.origin_paper: Bloom, B. (1956). Handbook I: Cognitive domain.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Analyzing
tasks.description: LLMs are tested on their ability to examine and compare elements of Hakka culture through multiple-choice questions. Example: 'Compare Hakka opera with other Han Chinese theater forms.'
tasks.origin_paper: Bloom, B. (1956). Handbook I: Cognitive domain.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Evaluating
tasks.description: LLMs are tested on their ability to make critical assessments about Hakka culture through multiple-choice questions. Example: 'Evaluate the historical evolution of Hakka social status in Taiwan.'
tasks.origin_paper: Bloom, B. (1956). Handbook I: Cognitive domain.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Creating
tasks.description: LLMs are tested on their ability to generate innovative ideas based on Hakka culture through multiple-choice questions. Example: 'Design an art exhibition showcasing Hakka heritage.'
tasks.origin_paper: Bloom, B. (1956). Handbook I: Cognitive domain.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

title: GAVEL: Generating Games Via Evolution and Language Models

benchmarks.name: GAVEL Game Generation and Evaluation Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new framework for generating and evaluating novel board games using a combination of automated metrics and human expert review.

tasks.name: Automated Game Evaluation
tasks.description: Generated games, represented in Ludii Game Description Language (L-GDL), are evaluated using a hierarchical set of automated metrics. These include compilability, playability, and metrics derived from self-play between AI agents (MCTS and random), such as balance, agency, and strategic depth.
tasks.scoring_detail: Harmonic mean of: Balance, Decisiveness, Completion, Agency, Coverage (from MCTS self-play), and Strategic Depth (MCTS vs. random agent). Also includes binary checks for compilability and playability.

tasks.name: Qualitative Human Evaluation
tasks.description: Expert evaluators playtest high-fitness games generated by the system to assess their novelty, engagement, and potential for sophisticated strategy.
tasks.scoring_detail: Expert qualitative assessment of novelty, engagement, and strategic potential.

title: Collective Critics for Creative Story Generation

benchmarks.name: Creative Story Plan Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper proposes and uses a new evaluation setup for assessing the creativity of AI-generated story plans. It involves open-ended generation, human and LLM-based evaluation on creativity-focused metrics, and reports empirical results for LLMs.

tasks.name: CRPLAN Evaluation
tasks.description: Generating a creative and coherent story plan from a given premise. The evaluation is a pairwise comparison between plans generated by the proposed CRPLAN framework and a baseline (DOC pipeline).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) and also reports results with GPT-4 and the Re3 baseline in the appendix.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human pairwise comparison on Interesting, Coherence, Creative, Relevant. GPT-4 based automatic pairwise comparison on the same metrics for ablation studies.

benchmarks.name: Creative Story Text Refinement Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces and uses a new evaluation for assessing an AI's ability to creatively refine sentences within a story. It is an open-ended generation task evaluated by humans and LLMs on creativity and style metrics.

tasks.name: CRTEXT Evaluation
tasks.description: Refining individual sentences within a long-form story to enhance expressiveness and creativity. The evaluation is a pairwise comparison between stories refined by the CRTEXT framework and a baseline.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is a text refinement/editing task.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) and also reports results with GPT-4 and the Re3 baseline in the appendix.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human pairwise comparison on Coherence, Writing Style Consistency, Interesting, Creative. GPT-4 based automatic pairwise comparison on the same metrics for ablation studies.

benchmarks.name: Human-Machine Interactive Writing Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper conducts a user study to evaluate the effectiveness of its proposed interactive system for creative writing, which is a direct test of AI-assisted creativity.

tasks.name: User Experience Experiment
tasks.description: A user experience experiment where a human acts as the 'leader' module to evaluate the effectiveness of the CRITICS interactive writing system in refining stories based on user-provided critiques.
tasks.task_type_notes: The system generates refinements based on human input/selection, and humans evaluate the output.
tasks.model_type_notes: The underlying CRITICS framework uses LLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pass/Fail rates for 'Edited' (whether the story changed due to critique) and 'Accepted' (whether the change aligned with user critique). Inter-annotator agreement (Kappa) is also reported.

title: ViPE: Visualise Pretty-much Everything

benchmarks.name: Fig-QA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Tests AI's ability to interpret figurative language, a key aspect of creative language understanding, using a Winograd-style question answering format.

tasks.name: Figurative Language Interpretation
tasks.description: Models are evaluated on their ability to choose the correct interpretation of a figurative sentence from two options in a Winograd-style format.
tasks.task_type_notes: The model's understanding is evaluated by its ability to select the correct textual interpretation.
tasks.model_type_notes: ViPE-S, GPT2
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: HAIVMet
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset of linguistic metaphors and expert-written visual elaborations, specifically designed for evaluating the visualization of figurative language.

tasks.name: Image-Text Retrieval on Metaphors
tasks.description: Evaluating the alignment between metaphors, their generated visual elaborations, and images synthesized from those elaborations using image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval.
tasks.task_type_notes: Involves generating visual elaborations (ViPE, GPT-3.5), generating images from them (Stable Diffusion), and then evaluating the alignment using a retrieval model (BLIP).
tasks.model_type_notes: LLMs (ViPE, GPT-3.5), Diffusion (Stable Diffusion), Vision-Language Model (BLIP)
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean recall across top-1, top-5, and top-10 retrieval scores

tasks.name: Human Evaluation of Metaphor Visualization
tasks.description: Human participants were shown a metaphor and three images generated from prompts by different sources (human expert, ChatGPT, ViPE) and asked to choose the image that best represented the metaphor's meaning.
tasks.task_type_notes: Involves generating prompts and images, followed by human evaluation.
tasks.model_type_notes: LLMs (ViPE, ChatGPT) and Diffusion model (Stable Diffusion)
tasks.scoring_detail: Percentage of times participants chose an image from a specific source

benchmarks.name: Emotion Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The original dataset is for standard emotion classification. This paper uses it in a creative context: to evaluate if a generated visual elaboration (a creative transformation) of a tweet preserves the original emotion.

tasks.name: Emotion Preservation in Visual Elaboration
tasks.description: Generating visual elaborations for emotionally charged tweets and evaluating if the elaborations preserve the original emotion (Semantic Proximity) and are visually perceptible (Visual Perceptibility).
tasks.task_type_notes: Involves generating visual elaborations (ViPE, GPT-3.5), generating images (Stable Diffusion), and then evaluating using classification (BERT) and embedding similarity (CLIP).
tasks.model_type_notes: LLMs (ViPE-M, GPT-3.5), BERT, CLIP, Stable Diffusion
tasks.scoring_detail: Semantic Proximity (classification accuracy), Visual Perceptibility (cosine similarity of CLIP embeddings)

benchmarks.name: LyricCanvas
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale dataset created by the authors for training and evaluating models on the creative task of generating visual elaborations from figurative text (lyrics).

tasks.name: Internal Validation on LyricCanvas
tasks.description: The validation set of the newly created LyricCanvas dataset is used to measure the quality of generated visual elaborations during model training.
tasks.model_type_notes: ViPE-S, ViPE-M
tasks.scoring_detail: CiDEr score

tasks.name: Safety and Appropriateness Evaluation
tasks.description: Measuring the profanity score of visual elaborations generated from lyrics in the LyricCanvas validation set to assess the model's ability to generate safe content.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT2-M, ViPE-M, GPT3.5
tasks.scoring_detail: Profanity score from Alt-profanity-check framework

title: Few-shot multi-token DreamBooth with LoRa for style-consistent character generation

benchmarks.name: Style-Consistent Character Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new evaluation framework for generating novel, style-consistent characters from few-shot examples, a core creative AI task. It uses open-ended generation and evaluates results with both novel quantitative metrics and human studies.

tasks.name: Style-Consistent Character Generation
tasks.description: Given a small set of 10-30 reference character images from a specific artistic style, the task is for a diffusion model to generate novel characters that preserve the artistic style and shared visual traits of the reference set. The generated images are then evaluated using other tasks in this benchmark.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper tests fine-tuned versions of Stable Diffusion v1-5, including Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, and the proposed multi-token DreamBooth with LoRA.
tasks.scoring_detail: The output of this task is evaluated by the Fidelity, Diversity, and Human Evaluation tasks within this benchmark.

tasks.name: Fidelity
tasks.description: A quantitative metric to assess how closely generated characters match the style of a reference dataset, using a style-specific image encoder.
tasks.model_type_notes: This task evaluates images generated by diffusion models using a separate, style-specific image encoder.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average max cosine similarity between generated and reference image embeddings.

tasks.name: Diversity
tasks.description: A quantitative metric to assess the diversity of generated characters based on their image embeddings.
tasks.model_type_notes: This task evaluates images generated by diffusion models using a CLIP image encoder.
tasks.scoring_detail: Geometric mean of the standard deviation of each embedding component across all generated images.

tasks.name: Human Evaluation (Pairwise Comparison)
tasks.description: General participants are shown pairs of generated images and asked to select which one better fits the reference style, or indicate a tie.
tasks.origin_paper: Bradley and Terry, 1952 (cited for the BT model)
tasks.scoring_detail: Bradley-Terry (BT) model aggregates comparisons into a global ranking score.

tasks.name: Human Evaluation (Absolute Rating)
tasks.description: Professional artists rate single generated images on a 1-5 scale based on how well each image fits the reference set.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average rating on a 1-5 scale.

title: Puzzled by Puzzles: When Vision-Language Models Can't Take a Hint

benchmarks.name: Rebus Puzzle Probe Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset of 432 hand-annotated rebus puzzles to test VLM capabilities in abstract reasoning, lateral thinking, and understanding visual metaphors, which are key aspects of creative problem-solving.

tasks.name: Rebus Puzzle Solving
tasks.description: VLMs are prompted to solve a rebus puzzle image and generate the correct answer phrase along with reasoning.
tasks.scoring_detail: Naive Matching (exact string match with ground truth) and LLM-Judged (GPT-4o and Qwen3-8B judge semantic equivalence).

tasks.name: In-Context Learning Puzzle Solving
tasks.description: VLMs solve rebus puzzles with a prompt that includes one complete example (image, answer, reasoning) to test if performance improves with an in-context demonstration.
tasks.scoring_detail: Naive Matching and LLM-Judged accuracy.

tasks.name: Skill-Guided Prompting Puzzle Solving
tasks.description: VLMs solve rebus puzzles with prompts that explicitly state the cognitive skills (e.g., Phonetics, Spatial Reasoning) required for the specific puzzle.
tasks.scoring_detail: Naive Matching and LLM-Judged accuracy.

tasks.name: Iterative Refinement Puzzle Solving
tasks.description: VLMs are prompted to re-attempt solving a puzzle if their initial answer is incorrect, for up to five retries, to measure self-correction capabilities.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cumulative accuracy based on Naive Matching over 5 attempts.

tasks.name: Caption-Only Puzzle Solving
tasks.description: Models solve rebus puzzles based only on a detailed text caption of the image, without direct visual input, to isolate textual reasoning ability.
tasks.model_type_notes: VLMs are used, but conditioned on text-only input.
tasks.scoring_detail: Naive Matching and LLM-Judged accuracy.

tasks.name: Image-to-Text Retrieval
tasks.description: Contrastive vision-language models are evaluated on their ability to retrieve the correct text answer for a given puzzle image from the set of all possible answers in the dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: Retrieval task: model ranks text answers for a given image.
tasks.model_type_notes: Specifically contrastive models like CLIP, SigLIP, Tulip.
tasks.scoring_detail: Recall@K (K=1, 5), Precision@1, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG).

title: Multimodal Prediction of Spontaneous Humour: A Novel Dataset and First Results

benchmarks.name: Passau-Spontaneous Football Coach Humor (Passau-SFCH)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new multimodal dataset and evaluation framework for the creative task of humor recognition, including its sentiment and direction.

tasks.name: Humor Recognition
tasks.description: A binary classification task to predict the presence of humor in 2-second segments of speech from football coaches' press conferences.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tests unimodal GRUs and various multimodal Transformer architectures (LMF, MulT, MISA, and the newly proposed VFMM). Features are extracted using models like BERT, ELECTRA, Wav2Vec2, and FaRL.
tasks.scoring_detail: Area Under the Curve (AUC)

tasks.name: Humor Direction Prediction
tasks.description: A binary classification task to predict the direction (self-directed vs. others-directed) of segments previously identified as humorous.
tasks.model_type_notes: Support Vector Machines (SVMs) on unimodal features, with late fusion for multimodal evaluation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Area Under the Curve (AUC)

tasks.name: Humor Sentiment Prediction
tasks.description: A binary classification task to predict the sentiment (negative vs. positive) of segments previously identified as humorous.
tasks.model_type_notes: Support Vector Machines (SVMs) on unimodal features, with late fusion for multimodal evaluation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Area Under the Curve (AUC)

title: KiVA: Kid-inspired Visual Analogies for Testing Large Multimodal Models

benchmarks.name: KiVA (Kid-inspired Visual Analogies)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark for visual analogical reasoning, a key component of creative intelligence, using transformations of real-world objects. It is designed to be solvable by young children and is used to test LMMs.

tasks.name: Verbal Classification
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task where the model must identify the general domain of a visual transformation from five categories (e.g., color, size, number, rotation, reflection).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Verbal Specification
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task, conditional on correct classification, where the model must specify the exact transformation rule (e.g., 'objects become bigger', 'rotate 90 degrees clockwise').
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Visual Extrapolation
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task where the model must apply the inferred transformation rule to a new object and select the correct outcome from three options.
tasks.model_type_notes: The primary evaluation was on Vision-Language Models (GPT-o1, GPT-4V, LLaVA-1.5, MANTIS). An additional experiment in the appendix tested a Large Vision Model (Bai et al., 2024).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

benchmarks.name: KiVA-adults
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A more challenging version of the KiVA benchmark for visual analogical reasoning, designed to be solvable by human adults but not young children. It tests more complex transformations.

tasks.name: Verbal Classification
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task where the model must identify the general domain of a more complex visual transformation (e.g., color, size, number, rotation, reflection).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Verbal Specification
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task, conditional on correct classification, where the model must specify the exact complex transformation rule (e.g., 'stretching', 'multiplication', '45-degree rotation').
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

tasks.name: Visual Extrapolation
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task where the model must apply the inferred complex transformation rule to a new object and select the correct outcome from three options.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (multiple-choice)

title: A Novel Mathematical Framework for Objective Characterization of Ideas

benchmarks.name: Mathematical Framework for Objective Characterization of Ideas
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new computational framework and a set of metrics (Idea Sparsity, Cluster Sparsity, etc.) to objectively evaluate the diversity and distribution of AI-generated ideas, which is a core aspect of creativity evaluation.

tasks.name: Idea Generation for Product Design Problems
tasks.description: Generating 100 ideas for each of six product design problem statements using a custom Conversational AI (CAI) tool. The resulting dataset of 600 ideas, structured with an Action-Object-Context (AOC) model, serves as the basis for all subsequent evaluations.
tasks.model_type_notes: A custom-built CAI tool was used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Dataset of 600 ideas was created for subsequent evaluation.

tasks.name: Semantic Validity of Idea Embeddings
tasks.description: Expert designers (N=30) evaluated the semantic similarity of idea triplets (from the same cluster, a neighboring cluster, and a distant cluster) relative to a reference idea to validate if the embedding-based clusters align with human judgment.
tasks.model_type_notes: The task evaluates the representation of LLM-generated ideas.
tasks.scoring_detail: Categorical similarity rating (Very Similar, Somewhat Similar, Very Different)

tasks.name: Usefulness of Clustered Idea Representation
tasks.description: Novice designers (N=40) selected 10 ideas from a 2D visual plot of 100 clustered ideas to assess if the visual representation aids in selecting a diverse set of ideas efficiently.
tasks.task_type_notes: Human-in-the-loop selection task to measure the utility of visual clustering for ensuring diversity.
tasks.model_type_notes: The task evaluates the utility of a visual representation of LLM-generated ideas.
tasks.scoring_detail: Selection Index (SI), Sampling Score (SS)

tasks.name: Objective Characterization of Idea Space
tasks.description: Applying the proposed mathematical framework to quantify the distribution and dispersion of the 600 generated ideas using UMAP, DBSCAN, and PCA.
tasks.model_type_notes: The framework is used to evaluate the output of an LLM-based idea generator.
tasks.scoring_detail: Idea Sparsity (IS), Cluster Sparsity (CS), Distribution Score (DS), PCA eigenvalues

benchmarks.name: Comparative Evaluation with AI-based Methods
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper uses several existing AI-based creativity evaluation methods (OCSAI, SemDis, etc.) to score its newly generated dataset, providing a comparative analysis against its proposed framework. This directly involves the application of creativity benchmarks.
benchmarks.origin_name: GPT-based evaluation, OCSAI, AIDE, CLAUS, SemDis
benchmarks.origin_paper: Various, including Organisciak et al. 2023 (OCSAI), Beaty & Johnson 2021 (SemDis)

tasks.name: Automated Novelty Scoring
tasks.description: The 600 generated product design ideas were evaluated for novelty or originality using five existing automated methods (GPT-based, OCSAI, AIDE, CLAUS, and SemDis) to compare their outputs and utility against the proposed framework.
tasks.origin_name: GPT-based evaluation, OCSAI, AIDE, CLAUS, SemDis
tasks.origin_paper: Various, including Organisciak et al. 2023 (OCSAI), Beaty & Johnson 2021 (SemDis)
tasks.model_type_notes: The ideas being evaluated were generated by an LLM. The evaluators are also AI/LLM-based systems.
tasks.scoring_detail: Novelty/originality rating (1-5 scale)

title: Pun Intended: Multi-Agent Translation of Wordplay with Contrastive Learning and Phonetic-Semantic Embeddings

benchmarks.name: CLEF JOKER 2025 Task 2: Wordplay Translation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A shared task focused on the creative challenge of translating wordplay (puns) from English to French, evaluated by both automated metrics and human judges.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Ermakova et al., Overview of the CLEF 2025 JOKER lab: Humour in machine, 2025

tasks.name: Wordplay Translation
tasks.description: Translate English pun sentences into French, with the primary objective of preserving the wordplay and humor rather than achieving literal translation.
tasks.origin_paper: Ermakova et al., Overview of the CLEF 2025 JOKER lab: Humour in machine, 2025
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation (Count, Location, Percent), BLEU score, BERTScore (Precision, Recall, F1-Score)

benchmarks.name: Internal Pipeline Evaluation Suite
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A collection of intermediate tasks created by the authors to evaluate specific components of their pun translation pipeline, focusing on understanding, translating, and evaluating creative language.

tasks.name: Pun Location and Type Identification
tasks.description: Identify the pun word and classify its type (homographic or homophonic) within an English sentence. This was evaluated against a newly created manually annotated dataset.
tasks.origin_name: CLEF JOKER 2023 Task 2 Pun Location and Interpretation
tasks.origin_paper: Ermakova, et al., Overview of joker–clef-2023 track on automatic wordplay analysis, 2023
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score

tasks.name: Pun Word and Meanings Translation Quality
tasks.description: Translate the identified English pun word and its associated synonym lists into French, and evaluate the quality of the translation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean cosine similarity using bilingual embeddings, variance, top quartile, percentage of untranslated words

tasks.name: Contrastive Pun Discrimination
tasks.description: A binary classification task where a discriminator model identifies whether a generated French sentence contains a pun or not, using a newly created contrastive dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Multi-Agent Pun Translation Evaluation
tasks.description: A panel of four LLM agents evaluates generated French puns based on four criteria: Equivalence, Mistranslation, Emotion, and Authenticity.
tasks.scoring_detail: Ratings for Equivalence (0-2), Mistranslation (0-2), Emotion (0-1), Authenticity (0-4), and averaged scores.

title: PoemTale Diffusion: Minimising Information Loss in Poem to Image Generation with Multi-Stage Prompt Refinement

benchmarks.name: P4I (PoemForImage) Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of 1111 poems with metadata (theme, protagonist, mood), created specifically to support and evaluate the creative task of poem-to-image generation.

tasks.name: Dataset Creation
tasks.description: Collection of 1111 poems from various online and offline sources, followed by annotation with metadata such as theme, protagonist, and emotion. The paper reports its statistics and creation process.
tasks.task_type_notes: Dataset creation and annotation. No models are evaluated in this task; the dataset is used for evaluation in other tasks.
tasks.model_type_notes: Human annotators were used for data collection and annotation.
tasks.scoring_detail: The paper reports dataset statistics and Cohen's Kappa for inter-annotator agreement, but no models are evaluated.

benchmarks.name: Poem-to-Image Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: An evaluation of generating images from poetry, comparing different prompting strategies on the new P4I dataset. It's a creative, open-ended task with both human and automatic evaluation.

tasks.name: Image Generation via Direct Poems (Approach 1)
tasks.description: A baseline task where the entire text of a poem from the P4I dataset is used as a single prompt to generate one corresponding image.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested with Playground V3, Stable Diffusion XL, and Janus.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation (Semantic Alignment, Emotional Resonance on 1-5 scale); Automatic metrics (BLIP score, Long-CLIP score, Emotion CLIP score).

tasks.name: Image Generation per Poem Stanzas (Approach 2)
tasks.description: A baseline task where poems from the P4I dataset are segmented by emotional shifts, and each segment is used as a prompt to generate a corresponding image.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested with Playground V3, Stable Diffusion XL, and Janus.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation (Semantic Alignment, Emotional Resonance on 1-5 scale); Automatic metrics (BLIP score, Long-CLIP score, Emotion CLIP score, Character Consistency CLIP score).

tasks.name: PoemTale Diffusion Approach
tasks.description: The proposed method for generating a sequence of images from a poem, involving poem segmentation, a multi-stage prompt refinement loop (MSPR) with an LLM, and consistent self-attention for image generation.
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses GPT-4o-mini for prompt refinement and Diffusion models (Playground V3, Stable Diffusion XL, Janus) for image generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human evaluation (Semantic Alignment, Emotional Resonance, Consistency on 1-5 scale); Automatic metrics (BLIP score, Long-CLIP score, Emotion CLIP score, Character Consistency CLIP score).

title: Diffusion Models as Artists: Are we Closing the Gap between Humans and Machines?

benchmarks.name: Diversity vs. Recognizability Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A quantitative framework for evaluating one-shot generative models on their ability to produce drawings that are both diverse (creative) and recognizable, directly addressing a core aspect of creative AI.

tasks.name: One-shot Drawing Generation
tasks.description: Generative models are conditioned on a single exemplar image from a class (from either Omniglot or the new QuickDraw-FS dataset) and must generate new, diverse drawings of that class. The outputs are then evaluated using the framework's metrics.
tasks.origin_paper: Established task in few-shot learning literature (e.g., Lake et al., 2015)
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested VAEs (VAE-NS, VAE-STN), GANs (DA-GAN-RN, DA-GAN-UN), and Diffusion models (DDPM, CFGDM, FSDM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Outputs are scored using Diversity and Recognizability metrics.

benchmarks.name: Generalization Curves
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a novel method to evaluate the trade-off between originality (creativity) and recognizability in generated content, providing a finer-grained analysis than aggregate diversity scores.

tasks.name: Originality Scoring
tasks.description: Quantifies the distance between an individual generated sample and its corresponding exemplar using an L2-norm in the feature space of a SimCLR network. This is applied to generations on the QuickDraw-FS dataset.
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses a SimCLR network as a critic.
tasks.scoring_detail: l2 distance to the exemplar in SimCLR latent space.

tasks.name: Generalization Curve Plotting
tasks.description: Plots the recognizability of generated samples (y-axis) as a function of their originality (x-axis) to evaluate how well models maintain recognizability as they generate more original content.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares DDPM, CFGDM, and FSDM against human performance.
tasks.scoring_detail: Plot of Recognizability score vs. Originality score.

benchmarks.name: Feature Importance Map Comparison
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Probes the internal visual strategies of generative models and compares them to human perceptual strategies for a creative task, offering insights into the alignment of machine vs. human creative processes.

tasks.name: Model Feature Importance Map Generation
tasks.description: Derives feature importance maps from a trained CFGDM model by calculating the misalignment between its conditional and unconditional score functions.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task evaluates the internal representations of the generative model.
tasks.model_type_notes: Specifically applied to the CFGDM model.
tasks.scoring_detail: Misalignment metric ϕ(x, y) based on model's internal scores.

tasks.name: ClickMe-QuickDraw
tasks.description: An online experiment where human participants paint over regions of a drawing they deem important for categorization, generating human-centric importance maps for comparison with model maps.
tasks.origin_paper: Linsley et al., 2018 (The protocol is inspired by this work, but applied to a new domain and dataset).
tasks.task_type_notes: Human data collection via an interactive game.
tasks.model_type_notes: Human participants, not an AI model being tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Aggregated click/paint maps from human participants.

benchmarks.name: QuickDraw-FewShot (QuickDraw-FS)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset of human drawings specifically curated for one-shot creative generation tasks, enabling more complex and meaningful human-machine comparisons than previous datasets like Omniglot.

tasks.name: One-shot Drawing Generation
tasks.description: Generate diverse drawings of a visual concept given a single exemplar from the QuickDraw-FS dataset. This dataset is used as input for the paper's evaluation frameworks.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested VAEs, GANs, and Diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Outputs are evaluated using the Diversity vs. Recognizability framework and Generalization Curves.

benchmarks.name: Omniglot
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard dataset for one-shot concept learning and generation, used here as a baseline to compare model performance against prior work and on a less complex drawing task.

tasks.name: One-shot Drawing Generation
tasks.description: Generate diverse drawings of a handwritten character given a single exemplar from the Omniglot dataset. This dataset is used as input for the Diversity vs. Recognizability framework.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested VAEs, GANs, and Diffusion models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Outputs are evaluated using the Diversity vs. Recognizability framework.

title: Eye of Judgement: Dissecting the Evaluation of Russian-speaking LLMs with POLLUX

benchmarks.name: POLLUX
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale benchmark for evaluating the generative capabilities of Russian LLMs, including creative writing, brainstorming, and other open-ended tasks. It uses expert human evaluation based on a detailed criteria taxonomy.

tasks.name: AI as a character (formal setting)
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM adopts a persona in a formal setting, acting as a companion to chat, work, or disagree with, based on a given prompt.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: AI as a character (informal setting)
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM adopts a persona in an informal setting, acting as a companion to chat, work, flirt, or disagree with, based on a given prompt.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Applied brainstorming
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM is prompted to brainstorm ideas for applied, practical problems.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Creative brainstorming
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM is prompted to brainstorm creative ideas to stimulate imagination.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: General-purpose brainstorming
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM is prompted to brainstorm general ideas.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Word tasks (editorial brainstorming)
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM is prompted to brainstorm ideas related to words and editorial concepts.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Advice
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM acts as a guide to provide advice for day-to-day challenges.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Recommendations
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM acts as a guide to provide recommendations.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Plans
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM acts as a guide to create plans for the user.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Journalistic text generation
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM creates a unique journalistic text from a given idea or concept.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Literary text generation
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM creates a unique literary text from a given idea or concept.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

tasks.name: Official text generation
tasks.description: A generative task where the LLM creates a unique official or business text from a given idea or concept.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean expert scores on a 0/1/2 scale across a set of fine-grained criteria.

title: GraphicBench: A Planning Benchmark for Graphic Design with Language Agents

tasks.name: Workflow Plan Generation

tasks.scoring_detail: Execution Success Rate, Fidelity (template matching), Content Similarity (CLIPSCORE), VQA Pass Rate (LLaVA-1.5), and Creativity (GPT-o1 rating for Originality & Elaboration).

title: PlotMachines: Outline-Conditioned Generation with Dynamic Plot State Tracking
