tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative visual assessment

title: Trade-offs in Image Generation: How Do Different Dimensions Interact?

benchmarks.name: TRIG-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale benchmark for evaluating text-to-image and image-to-image models on their ability to handle trade-offs between 10 different dimensions, including creative aspects like Originality, Aesthetics, and Ambiguity. It uses open-ended generation tasks and reports empirical results for 14 models.

tasks.name: Text-to-Image Generation
tasks.description: Generating images from 13,200 text prompts designed to test trade-offs between pairs of 10 dimensions (e.g., Realism, Originality, Style, Knowledge, Ambiguity).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates a range of T2I models, primarily based on diffusion and transformer architectures (e.g., FLUX, DALL-E 3, SD3.5).
tasks.scoring_detail: TRIGScore (VLM-as-judge rating on 10 dimensions: Realism, Originality, Aesthetics, Content, Relation, Style, Knowledge, Ambiguity, Toxicity, Bias)

tasks.name: Image Editing
tasks.description: Modifying a source image based on one of 13,500 text prompts, with prompts designed to test trade-offs between pairs of 10 different dimensions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates a range of I2I models (e.g., InstructP2P, HQEdit, OmniGen).
tasks.scoring_detail: TRIGScore (VLM-as-judge rating on 10 dimensions)

tasks.name: Subject-driven Generation
tasks.description: Generating an image featuring a specific subject from a source image, guided by one of 13,500 text prompts designed to test trade-offs between pairs of 10 dimensions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates a range of subject-driven models (e.g., Blip-diffusion, SSR-Encoder, FLUX-IP-Adapter).
tasks.scoring_detail: TRIGScore (VLM-as-judge rating on 10 dimensions)

tasks.name: Human Evaluation for Metric Validation
tasks.description: Human participants rated 300 generated images (100 from each task type) on a continuous scale to validate the consistency of the TRIGScore metric with human judgment.
tasks.model_type_notes: Outputs from FLUX, HQEdit, and Omnigen were evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human rating on a [0,1] scale

benchmarks.name: HEIM
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A holistic benchmark for text-to-image models that evaluates multiple dimensions, including creative ones like Aesthetics and Originality. It was used in this paper for an ablation study.

tasks.name: Text-to-Image Generation (Ablation Study)
tasks.description: An ablation study was conducted on the HEIM benchmark's test set to evaluate the effectiveness of fine-tuning a model using the paper's proposed Dimension Trade-off Map (DTM).
tasks.model_type_notes: The SD v3.5 model was tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIPScore, FID, LAION score (for Aesthetics & Originality), Simple Rate of NSFW (for Toxicity), Simple Gender Proportion (for Bias)

title: Zero-shot Image Editing with Reference Imitation

benchmarks.name: Imitative Editing Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for a novel image editing task (imitative editing) which involves creative composition and texture transfer. It uses open-ended generation tasks and evaluates models with both automatic metrics and human studies.

tasks.name: Part Composition
tasks.description: The model composites a local part from a reference image onto a masked region of a source image, requiring semantic correspondence discovery. The benchmark includes an 'inner-ID' track (same object instance) and an 'inter-ID' track (different instances/categories).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper's model, MimicBrush, and competitors like AnyDoor and Paint-by-Example are diffusion-based image editing models.
tasks.scoring_detail: SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS (for inner-ID track with ground truth); DINO image similarity, CLIP image similarity, CLIP text similarity (for inter-ID track); Human ranking of fidelity, harmony, and quality.

tasks.name: Texture Transfer
tasks.description: The model transfers a texture or pattern from a reference image onto a masked object in the source image, while preserving the source object's shape. The benchmark includes an 'inner-ID' track and an 'inter-ID' track.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper's model, MimicBrush, is a diffusion-based image editing model.
tasks.scoring_detail: SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS (for inner-ID track with ground truth); DINO image similarity, CLIP image similarity, CLIP text similarity (for inter-ID track).

title: Stylebreeder: Exploring and Democratizing Artistic Styles through Text-to-Image Models

benchmarks.name: STYLEBREEDER
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a large-scale dataset of AI-generated art and a suite of tasks for discovering, personalizing, and recommending artistic styles, directly addressing creative AI capabilities.

tasks.name: Discovering Diverse Artistic Styles
tasks.description: Clustering images from the dataset based on stylistic similarity using CSD feature embeddings and K-Means++ to identify and categorize unique, user-generated artistic styles.
tasks.task_type_notes: Data analysis/clustering to identify styles, which serves as a basis for other tasks.
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses a Vision Transformer (ViT) based feature extractor (CSD) for style embedding.
tasks.scoring_detail: Silhouette score

tasks.name: Personalized Image Generation Based on Style
tasks.description: Benchmarking state-of-the-art personalization methods (Textual Inversion, LoRA w/DreamBooth, Custom Diffusion, EDLoRA) to generate new images that adhere to a specific artistic style identified from the dataset's clusters.
tasks.scoring_detail: CLIP-T (image-text similarity), CLIP-I (image-image similarity), DINO (image-image similarity)

tasks.name: Style-based Recommendation
tasks.description: A matrix-factorization-based system that recommends artistic styles (clusters) to users based on the styles of images they have previously generated.
tasks.task_type_notes: Recommendation task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) algorithm.
tasks.scoring_detail: MAE, RMSE

title: ArtInsight: Enabling AI-Powered Artwork Engagement for Mixed Visual-Ability Families

benchmarks.name: ArtInsight Artwork Description Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new evaluation framework, including a dataset, a formal rubric, and tasks, for assessing the quality and creativity of AI-generated text descriptions of children's artwork, an open-ended generation task.

tasks.name: AI Model Comparison for Artwork Description
tasks.description: Four state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Flash) generate descriptions for a dataset of 30 children's artworks. The quality of the descriptions is evaluated to select the best model for the ArtInsight system.
tasks.model_type_notes: Tested Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o, and Gemini 1.5 Flash.
tasks.scoring_detail: Score out of 16 based on a 4-category rubric (presumptive, reductive, simplicity, completeness), applied by a custom GPT-4o based 'LLM Scorer' and human spot-checkers.

tasks.name: System Comparison of Artwork Descriptions
tasks.description: In a user study, participants compared artwork descriptions generated by the ArtInsight system against those from the Be My AI application for artwork they provided.
tasks.model_type_notes: Compares ArtInsight (GPT-4o backend) with Be My AI.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings on a 5-point Likert scale for Usefulness and Perceived Accuracy. Also scored using the paper's custom rubric by an LLM Scorer and three human scorers.

tasks.name: Creative Description Generation
tasks.description: The ArtInsight system generates a more vivid, interpretive, and 'creative' description of a child's artwork, which users evaluated qualitatively.
tasks.model_type_notes: ArtInsight's GPT-4o backend was used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative feedback and preference ranking from user study participants.

tasks.name: Discussion Question Generation
tasks.description: The ArtInsight system generates a set of questions to facilitate discussion between a family member and a child about their artwork.
tasks.model_type_notes: ArtInsight's GPT-4o backend was used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative feedback and preference ranking from user study participants.

title: DiCTI: Diffusion-based Clothing Designer via Text-guided Input

benchmarks.name: Text-guided Clothing Generation on VITON-HD
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates a creative task (fashion design) using an open-ended image generation task. The evaluation includes both automated metrics and a human user study to assess quality, realism, and adherence to creative prompts.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Choi, S., Park, S., Lee, M., & Choo, J. (2021). VITON-HD: High-resolution virtual try-on via misalignment-aware normalization. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF conference on computer vision and pattern recognition (CVPR).

tasks.name: State-of-the-Art Comparison
tasks.description: Generating images of people wearing clothing described by text prompts on the VITON-HD test set to compare the proposed DiCTI model against the FICE model.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper's model (DiCTI) is diffusion-based. It is compared to a GAN-based model (FICE).
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic metrics: Kernel Inception Distance (KID), CLIP-S, CLIP-IQA. Human study: preference ratings on perceived realism, prompt adherence, identity preservation, and pose preservation.

tasks.name: Ablation Study on Mask Dilation
tasks.description: Evaluating the impact of the mask dilation kernel size on the quality of generated clothing using the VITON-HD dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Kernel Inception Distance (KID), CLIP-S, CLIP-IQA

benchmarks.name: Text-guided Clothing Generation on Fashionpedia
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates a creative fashion design task on a challenging 'in-the-wild' dataset to test the robustness and versatility of the generation model.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Jia, M., Shi, M., Sirotenko, M., Cui, Y., Cardie, C., Hariharan, B., Adam, H., & Belongie, S. (2020). Fashionpedia: Ontology, segmentation, and an attribute localization dataset. In European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV).

tasks.name: Qualitative Analysis
tasks.description: Visually analyzing the quality and diversity of generated clothing on challenging 'in-the-wild' images from the Fashionpedia dataset, testing different fabrics, shapes, and patterns.
tasks.scoring_detail: Visual inspection by authors of generated images for fabric types, garment shapes, patterns, and robustness to background clutter.

tasks.name: Ablation Study on Mask Dilation
tasks.description: Evaluating the impact of the mask dilation kernel size on the quality of generated clothing using the Fashionpedia dataset.
tasks.scoring_detail: Kernel Inception Distance (KID), CLIP-S, CLIP-IQA

title: Thinking with Generated Images

benchmarks.name: GenEval
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates text-to-image generation, an open-ended creative task focusing on compositional accuracy and alignment with complex prompts involving multiple objects, attributes, and spatial relationships.

tasks.name: Object-Focused Text-to-Image Alignment
tasks.description: Models generate images from prompts designed to test compositional understanding. The outputs are evaluated on their ability to correctly render multiple objects, counts, colors, positions, and attributes.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses Anole-7b, a unified autoregressive Large Multimodal Model (LMM) for interleaved image-text generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Scores for categories: Single Object, Two Objects, Counting, Colors, Position, and Color Attribute alignment.

benchmarks.name: DPGBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates text-to-image generation, an open-ended creative task focusing on semantic alignment with detailed prompts that specify entities, attributes, and relations.

tasks.name: Semantic Text-to-Image Alignment
tasks.description: Models generate images from prompts, which are then evaluated for semantic alignment across global scene properties, specific entities, attributes, and relations.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses Anole-7b, a unified autoregressive Large Multimodal Model (LMM) for interleaved image-text generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Scores for categories: Global, Entity, Attribute, Relation, and Other.

title: InfoChartQA: A Benchmark for Multimodal Question Answering on Infographic Charts

benchmarks.name: InfoChartQA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark evaluates MLLMs on understanding infographic charts, which use creative pictorial elements, symbolic visuals, and metaphors to convey information. This goes beyond simple data extraction and assesses the model's ability to interpret creative and communicative intent in visual data representation.

tasks.name: Text-based Question Answering
tasks.description: Answering questions about infographic charts and their plain chart counterparts. Questions are based on eleven types of data facts (e.g., value, rank, trend, difference) and require reasoning over the chart's data.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Model). 20 models were tested, including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and various open-source models.
tasks.scoring_detail: ANLS score for textual answers, relaxed accuracy for numeric answers, exact match for option answers.

tasks.name: Visual-element-based Question Answering (Basic)
tasks.description: Answering questions that require referencing specific visual elements (e.g., icons, pictograms) within an infographic. Tasks include identifying the data value corresponding to an icon or determining the function of a visual element.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Model). 20 models were tested, including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and various open-source models.
tasks.scoring_detail: ANLS score for textual answers, relaxed accuracy for numeric answers, exact match for multiple-choice answers.

tasks.name: Visual-element-based Question Answering (Metaphor)
tasks.description: Answering multiple-choice questions about the metaphorical meaning conveyed by visual elements in an infographic chart. This requires interpreting abstract concepts, narratives, or emotional tones conveyed through imagery.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Model). 20 models were tested, including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and various open-source models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact match for multiple-choice answers.

title: JAM: A Tiny Flow-based Song Generator with Fine-grained Controllability and Aesthetic Alignment

benchmarks.name: JAME
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, public, genre-diverse dataset specifically designed for the objective evaluation of full-song generation models, focusing on creative audio output. It includes empirical results for multiple models.

tasks.name: Full-Song Generation Objective Evaluation
tasks.description: Models generate full-length songs from lyrics and style prompts. The outputs are evaluated using a suite of objective and model-based metrics for intelligibility, style adherence, and aesthetic quality.
tasks.model_type_notes: Song generation models (Flow Matching, Autoregressive, Diffusion).
tasks.scoring_detail: Word Error Rate (WER), Phoneme Error Rate (PER), MuQ-MuLan similarity, Genre Accuracy (Qwen-2.5-Omni), Audiobox-aesthetic (CE, CU, PC, PQ), SongEval (CO, MU, ME, CL, NA), Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD).

tasks.name: Evaluation of Duration Predictors
tasks.description: Compares song generation quality on the JAME dataset when using different word-level timing strategies: ground-truth continuous timestamps (Oracle), GPT-4o predicted timestamps (GPT-Dur), and beat-aligned quantized timestamps (Direct-Quant).
tasks.model_type_notes: Uses an LLM (GPT-4o) to generate timing inputs for an audio generation model (JAM).
tasks.scoring_detail: Word Error Rate (WER), Phoneme Error Rate (PER), MuQ-MuLan similarity, Genre Accuracy, Audiobox-aesthetic (CE, CU, PC, PQ), SongEval (CO, MU, ME, CL, NA), Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD).

benchmarks.name: Subjective Evaluation of Song Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A human evaluation framework to assess the creative and perceptual qualities of AI-generated songs, such as enjoyment, musicality, and naturalness. It reports empirical results from human experts.

tasks.name: Human Evaluation of Song Quality
tasks.description: Eight human annotators with a music background rated generated songs on a 1-5 Likert scale across five perceptual dimensions: Quality, Enjoyment, Musicality, Voice Naturalness, and Song Structure Clarity.
tasks.task_type_notes: Models generate content which is then evaluated by humans.
tasks.model_type_notes: Song generation models (Flow Matching, Autoregressive, Diffusion).
tasks.scoring_detail: 1-5 Likert scale ratings for Quality, Enjoyment, Musicality, Voice Naturalness, and Song Structure Clarity (SSC).

benchmarks.name: Ablation Studies
benchmarks.relevance_reason: These studies use quantitative metrics to evaluate specific components of a creative generation system (a song generator), which is relevant to understanding how to build and improve such systems.

tasks.name: Impact of Token-level Duration Modeling
tasks.description: An ablation study to evaluate the effectiveness of token-level duration control by measuring the audio amplitude generated after the target song duration.
tasks.model_type_notes: Song generation model (JAM variants).
tasks.scoring_detail: Root Mean Square (RMS) amplitude ratio.

tasks.name: Phoneme Assignment Methods
tasks.description: An ablation study comparing two phoneme assignment strategies ('Average Sparse' vs 'Pad Right') using objective and model-based metrics.
tasks.model_type_notes: Song generation model (JAM variants).
tasks.scoring_detail: MuQ, PER, FAD, Average Audio-Aesthetic scores (AES), Average SongEval scores.

title: Subtle Biases Need Subtler Measures: Dual Metrics for Evaluating Representative and Affinity Bias in Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Creativity-Oriented Generation Suite (CoGS)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark suite of 12 diverse, open-ended creative generation tasks (e.g., short story writing, poetry, dance choreography, game invention) designed to evaluate LLMs. While the paper's focus is on bias, the tasks themselves are explicitly creativity-oriented.

tasks.name: Representative Bias Measurement
tasks.description: LLMs generate content for 12 creative tasks from the CoGS suite, both with a default prompt and with identity-specific prompts (race, gender, sexual orientation). The semantic similarity between default and identity-prompted outputs is measured to calculate the Representative Bias Score (RBS).
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4, LLaMA-2, and Mixtral were used for generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine similarity between vector embeddings of default and identity-prompted outputs; Representative Bias Score (RBS).

tasks.name: Affinity Bias Measurement
tasks.description: An evaluator LLM or human is presented with multiple outputs generated for a CoGS task (each with a different identity prompt) and selects the 'best' one based on a provided rubric. This measures evaluative preference via the Affinity Bias Score (ABS).
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4, LLaMA-2, and Mixtral were used as evaluators.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM preference selection; Human preference selection (for a subset of 50 instances); Affinity Bias Score (ABS); Fleiss Kappa for human inter-rater agreement.

title: Learning to Reason for Long-Form Story Generation

benchmarks.name: Next-Chapter Prediction (NCP)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new, open-ended task for long-form creative story generation, requiring models to predict a subsequent book chapter based on rich context. Evaluation is focused on creative writing quality.

tasks.name: Pairwise Human Evaluation of Generated Chapters
tasks.description: Human judges with creative writing backgrounds perform pairwise comparisons of generated next-chapters. They provide preference judgments on six dimensions: Plot, Creativity, Development, Language Use, Characters, and Overall Preference.
tasks.task_type_notes: Humans evaluate AI-generated text.
tasks.model_type_notes: Qwen-2.5 7B and 3B models were used to generate the content being evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise preference judgments on Plot, Creativity, Development, Language Use, Characters, and Overall Preference; analyzed with a Bradley-Terry model for relative strengths and preference probabilities.

tasks.name: Automated Analysis of Generated Chapters
tasks.description: Calculating automated metrics to analyze surface-level properties of the generated chapters, such as length, lexical diversity, and n-gram overlap with the source material and gold reference.
tasks.origin_name: Standard NLP metrics (Word Count, Diversity, ROUGE)
tasks.task_type_notes: Automated metrics are used to evaluate AI-generated text.
tasks.model_type_notes: Qwen-2.5 7B and 3B models were used to generate the content being evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average number of words, % unique words, % unseen trigrams, ROUGE-L F1, ROUGE-L Precision.

tasks.name: Perplexity Improvement as a Proxy for Quality
tasks.description: Evaluating the utility of the paper's proposed VR-CLI reward metric (based on perplexity improvement) as a proxy for human judgments by calculating its correlation with human preference scores.
tasks.task_type_notes: An automatic metric is evaluated against human judgments.
tasks.model_type_notes: The metric is calculated based on LLM outputs and compared to human ratings of those outputs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Spearman's rank correlation between per-token perplexity improvement and human preference judgments.

title: Evaluating Creative Short Story Generation in Humans and Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: Cue-word-based Creative Story Generation and Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces a new experimental setup that combines a creative story generation task with a comprehensive evaluation by automated metrics, human judges (expert and non-expert), and LLM judges to systematically compare human and AI creativity.

tasks.name: Creative Short Story Generation
tasks.description: Generate a creative short story of approximately five sentences based on three given cue words, while avoiding a typical or uncreative storyline.
tasks.origin_paper: Prabhakaran, Green, and Gray 2014; Johnson et al. 2023; Orwig et al. 2024
tasks.model_type_notes: 60 different LLMs were tested, including models from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Anthropic, and others.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automated metrics (n-gram diversity, inverse homogenization, novelty, surprise, lexical/syntactic complexity), human ratings (expert & non-expert), and LLM-as-judge ratings (creativity, originality, surprise, effectiveness).

tasks.name: LLM-as-Judge Creativity Evaluation
tasks.description: Three LLMs were prompted to rate human- and AI-generated stories on creativity, originality, surprise, and effectiveness, and to classify the author as human or AI (Turing Test).
tasks.origin_paper: The paper notes this is an increasingly common method, citing works like Bavaresco et al. 2024.
tasks.model_type_notes: Claude, Gemini, and GPT-4 were used as judges.
tasks.scoring_detail: LLM judges' ratings were compared against human expert ratings. Inter-rater reliability (ICC) was calculated among the LLM judges.

tasks.name: Automated Creativity Evaluation
tasks.description: A suite of automated metrics was used to evaluate generated stories across dimensions of diversity, novelty, surprise, and complexity.
tasks.origin_name: Various NLP and semantic distance metrics
tasks.origin_paper: Metrics for novelty and surprise are from Karampiperis et al. (2014); diversity metric is similar to Padmakumar and He (2023); complexity metrics are standard NLP measures.
tasks.task_type_notes: This is not a task performed by the models being tested, but an automated scoring protocol applied to their output.
tasks.model_type_notes: This protocol was applied to the output of 60 LLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Diversity (n-gram diversity, inverse homogenization), Novelty (semantic distance of dominant terms), Surprise (semantic distance of consecutive sentences), Complexity (Flesch score, word/sentence length, POS ratios, dependency path length, constituency tree depth).

title: Can Language Models Make Fun? A Case Study in Chinese Comical Crosstalk

benchmarks.name: Chinese Comical Crosstalk (C3) Generation Benchmark
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark and dataset (C3) for evaluating the ability of LLMs to generate humorous and culturally-specific dialogue (Chinese crosstalk), a form of creative text generation.

tasks.name: Crosstalk Generation
tasks.description: Given the first ten utterances of a Chinese crosstalk script, the model's task is to generate the next ten utterances in a coherent and humorous manner.
tasks.model_type_notes: Models tested include LSTM Seq2seq, UniLM, T5, GPT, CPM, Pangu-α, Zhouwenwang, and GPT-3.
tasks.scoring_detail: Automatic: BLEU-1/2/4, ROUGE-1/2/L, GLEU, Distinct-1/2. Human: 5-point ratings for General quality and Humor; binary scores for Coherence and Ethically-risky flag.

title: Plot Writing From Pre-Trained Language Models

benchmarks.name: Story Ending Ranking Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new human evaluation task designed to compare different methods (NSP, PPL, Random) for ranking generated story endings based on coherence and quality.

tasks.name: Pairwise Comparison of Story Endings
tasks.description: Human annotators are presented with two stories, each with a different ending selected by a different ranking method, and are asked to choose which story has a better ending.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT2-XL generates stories and endings. BERT (NSP) and GPT-2 (PPL) are used for ranking.
tasks.scoring_detail: Win/Loss count from pairwise comparison based on majority vote from three annotators.

benchmarks.name: Story Cloze Test
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A standard benchmark for commonsense story understanding, used here to quantitatively evaluate the proposed story ending ranking methods (NSP and PPL).

tasks.name: Story Ending Prediction
tasks.description: Given a four-sentence story, the task is to predict the correct ending from two options: a 'right ending' and a 'wrong ending'.
tasks.task_type_notes: The models (BERT for NSP, GPT-2 for PPL) are used to score and select the most plausible ending, not generate it.
tasks.model_type_notes: bert-base-uncased for NSP, gpt2 (base) for PPL.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

benchmarks.name: SCRATCHPLOT Story Generation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new evaluation setup to assess the quality of stories generated by the proposed SCRATCHPLOT model against several baselines using both human and automatic metrics.

tasks.name: Story Generation Quality Assessment
tasks.description: Models generate stories based on a content plan. The stories are then evaluated by human crowdworkers for naturalness, interestingness, and cohesiveness, and by automatic metrics for diversity (self-BLEU) and repetition (distinct-n).
tasks.model_type_notes: SCRATCHPLOT (GPT2-XL) is compared against baselines: Fusion, Plan-and-write, ProGen, and GPT2-XL without content planning.
tasks.scoring_detail: Human ratings (1-5) for naturalness, interestingness, cohesiveness; Automatic metrics: self-BLEU, distinct-n.

benchmarks.name: Content Plan Quality Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new expert evaluation to assess the quality of the intermediate content plans (plot elements) generated by the proposed method.

tasks.name: Expert Rating of Plot Elements
tasks.description: An expert annotator rates the quality of generated plot elements: location, cast, and genre are rated with a binary score (acceptable/unacceptable), while the theme is rated on a 1-5 scale.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT2-XL is used to generate the plot elements.
tasks.scoring_detail: Binary rating (acceptable/unacceptable) for location, cast, genre; 1-5 scale rating for theme. Scores are normalized to a 0-1 range.

title: Manipulating Embeddings of Stable Diffusion Prompts

benchmarks.name: Prompt Embedding Manipulation Evaluation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces and evaluates three new methods for fine-grained, user-driven control over creative image generation, which is a core aspect of AI creativity.

tasks.name: Metric-Based Optimization
tasks.description: A prompt's embedding is automatically optimized via gradient ascent/descent to improve a specific, differentiable image quality metric (e.g., aesthetics, sharpness).
tasks.model_type_notes: Stable Diffusion was used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Blurriness (variance of Laplacian), Sharpness (negative blurriness), LAION aesthetic predictor score

tasks.name: Iterative Human Feedback User Study
tasks.description: A user study where participants iteratively create an image fitting a description by selecting from system-generated options, which modify the prompt embedding.
tasks.model_type_notes: Stable Diffusion was used.
tasks.scoring_detail: User preference ranking of the final image compared to one generated via traditional prompt engineering; qualitative user feedback on the process (e.g., 'less tedious').

tasks.name: Seed-Invariant Prompt Embedding
tasks.description: A method to modify a prompt's embedding to reproduce the key features of an image generated with a specific 'target' seed, even when using different random seeds for generation.
tasks.model_type_notes: Stable Diffusion was used.
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative visual inspection of generated images against the target image; L2 norm (pixel-wise distance) used as loss function during optimization.

title: S-DAT: A Multilingual, GenAI-Driven Framework for Automated Divergent Thinking Assessment

benchmarks.name: S-DAT (Synthetic-Divergent Association Task)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces this new framework as a scalable, multilingual, automated assessment for divergent thinking, a core component of creativity.

tasks.name: Divergent Word Generation
tasks.description: Participants generate a set of semantically unrelated words. The S-DAT framework then scores these responses based on semantic distance calculated using a multilingual transformer-based embedding model.
tasks.model_type_notes: The scoring framework uses multilingual transformer-based embedding models, specifically selecting 'granite-embedding-278m-multilingual'.
tasks.scoring_detail: Semantic distance calculated as 1 - cosine similarity between word embeddings.

benchmarks.name: Divergent Association Task (DAT)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The original DAT is used as the primary benchmark for calibration and comparison. The paper re-scores original DAT responses with the new S-DAT framework and compares the results.

tasks.name: Divergent Word Generation
tasks.description: Participants generate 10 semantically unrelated words. The paper uses the original data and scores from this task for comparison with its new S-DAT scores.
tasks.model_type_notes: The original scoring used GloVe, a static embedding model. This paper uses the original data to test its new LLM-based scoring system.
tasks.scoring_detail: Average semantic distance based on GloVe embeddings (original scoring).

benchmarks.name: Alternate Uses Test (AUT)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A classic divergent thinking task reused for convergent validity. The paper correlates existing human-rated AUT scores with the new automated S-DAT scores.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Christensen et al. (1960), with data from Olson et al. (2021)

tasks.name: Creative Uses Generation
tasks.description: Participants list creative uses for common household objects. The paper uses existing human-rated scores from this task to validate the S-DAT framework.
tasks.model_type_notes: The task itself involves human generation, but the data is used to validate the S-DAT, which is an LLM-based scoring system.
tasks.scoring_detail: Fluency (total number of uses), Originality (rarity within sample), Flexibility (number of distinct categories).

benchmarks.name: Bridge-the-Associative-Gap Task
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A convergent thinking task reused for discriminant validity to demonstrate that the S-DAT measure of divergent thinking is distinct from convergent thinking.

tasks.name: Associative Linking
tasks.description: Participants generate a third word that semantically links two given words. The paper uses existing human-rated scores from this task for discriminant validity of S-DAT.
tasks.model_type_notes: The task itself involves human generation, but the data is used to validate the S-DAT, which is an LLM-based scoring system.
tasks.scoring_detail: Appropriateness rating on a 1-5 scale by two judges.

title: CSD-VAR: Content-Style Decomposition in Visual Autoregressive Models

benchmarks.name: CSD-100
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new dataset and evaluation protocol specifically designed for the creative task of content-style decomposition in image generation models. It involves open-ended generation and reports empirical results.

tasks.name: Content-Style Decomposition (Quantitative Evaluation)
tasks.description: Models disentangle content and style from a single image from the CSD-100 dataset. Evaluation involves generating new images by recontextualizing the content with new prompts and applying the style to new subjects, measured by automatic metrics.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates its Visual Autoregressive (VAR) model and compares it against diffusion-based models (DreamBooth, B-LoRA, Inspiration Tree).
tasks.scoring_detail: CSD-C, CLIP-I for content alignment; CSD-S, DINO for style alignment; CLIP-T for text alignment.

tasks.name: Content-Style Decomposition (User Study)
tasks.description: Human participants compared generated images from different models based on an input image from the CSD-100 dataset and a prompt, evaluating them on several criteria in a preference study.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates its Visual Autoregressive (VAR) model and compares it against diffusion-based models (DreamBooth, B-LoRA, Inspiration Tree).
tasks.scoring_detail: User preference ratings for Image Quality, Prompt Adherence, Content Alignment, Style Alignment, and Overall Quality.

benchmarks.name: Validation Set (Content-Style Decomposition)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A custom-curated dataset of 35 images used for empirical evaluation (ablation studies) of a creative image generation task (content-style decomposition).
benchmarks.origin_paper: Sohn et al., 2023; Frenkel et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2024; Ruiz et al., 2023

tasks.name: Content-Style Decomposition (Ablation Study)
tasks.description: Different configurations of the proposed CSD-VAR model are tested on their ability to disentangle content and style from a curated set of 35 images for ablation purposes.
tasks.model_type_notes: Visual Autoregressive (VAR) models.
tasks.scoring_detail: CSD-C, CLIP-I for content alignment; CSD-S, DINO for style alignment; CLIP-T for text alignment.

title: Probing and Generalization of Metaphorical Knowledge in Pre-Trained Language Models Anonymous ACL-IJCNLP submission

benchmarks.name: LCC Metaphor Datasets
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates an AI's ability to identify metaphorical language, a form of figurative and creative language use. The task is a classification/judgment task focused on a non-literal aspect of language.

tasks.name: Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: Classifying a word in a sentence as either metaphorical or literal. This paper uses the dataset for probing experiments (in English) and for cross-lingual generalization experiments (English, Spanish, Russian, Farsi).
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is a binary classification (literal vs. metaphor) used to probe the internal knowledge of language models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, MDL compression

tasks.name: Domain Prediction
tasks.description: Probing PLM representations to predict the source and target conceptual domains of a metaphorical expression, using existing annotations from the LCC dataset.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is a classification task used to probe the model's understanding of the conceptual structure of metaphors.
tasks.scoring_detail: MDL compression

benchmarks.name: TroFi Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates an AI's ability to distinguish between literal and non-literal (metaphorical) usages of verbs, which is a judgment task related to creative language.

tasks.name: Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: Classifying verb usages in sentences from the Wall Street Journal as either literal or nonliteral (metaphorical). This paper uses the dataset for probing and cross-dataset generalization experiments.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is a binary classification (literal vs. nonliteral) used to probe the internal knowledge of language models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, MDL compression

benchmarks.name: VUA Corpus
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Evaluates an AI's ability to identify metaphorical word usage across different parts of speech, a judgment task related to understanding creative and figurative language.

tasks.name: Metaphor Detection
tasks.description: Classifying words in sentences as either metaphorical or literal. The paper uses two subsets: VUA Verbs (only verbs) and VUA POS (all parts of speech). These are used for probing and cross-dataset generalization experiments.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is a binary classification (literal vs. metaphor) used to probe the internal knowledge of language models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, MDL compression

title: YINYANG-ALIGN: Benchmarking Contradictory Objectives and Proposing Multi-Objective Optimization based DPO for Text-to-Image Alignment

benchmarks.name: YinYangAlign
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new benchmark framework introduced in this paper for evaluating text-to-image models on six contradictory objectives, many of which are core to creativity, such as artistic freedom, originality, and emotional impact. It involves generating images and evaluating them on these axes.

tasks.name: Faithfulness to Prompt vs. Artistic Freedom
tasks.description: Evaluating the trade-off in text-to-image models between adhering closely to user instructions and introducing creative or artistic elements that deviate from the prompt.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates DPO and their proposed CAO method, which are alignment techniques for diffusion models like Stable Diffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Lfaith (Sinkhorn-VAE Wasserstein Distance) and Lartistic (Style Difference via VGG Gram features, Content Abstraction/Difference via CLIP embeddings).

tasks.name: Emotional Impact vs. Neutrality
tasks.description: Evaluating the balance in generated images between evoking specific emotions as implied by a prompt and maintaining an unbiased, objective representation.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates DPO and their proposed CAO method, which are alignment techniques for diffusion models like Stable Diffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Lemotion (Emotional Impact Score using emotion detection models like DeepEmotion) and Neutrality Score.

tasks.name: Visual Realism vs. Artistic Freedom
tasks.description: Evaluating the trade-off between creating photorealistic images that mimic the real world and incorporating artistic styles when requested.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates DPO and their proposed CAO method, which are alignment techniques for diffusion models like Stable Diffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Lartistic (Style Difference via VGG Gram features, Content Abstraction/Difference via CLIP embeddings) and an implicit realism metric.

tasks.name: Originality vs. Referentiality
tasks.description: Evaluating the balance between maintaining stylistic originality and avoiding over-reliance on established artistic styles, which could risk plagiarism.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates DPO and their proposed CAO method, which are alignment techniques for diffusion models like Stable Diffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Loriginality and Lreferentiality, calculated as the average cosine dissimilarity/similarity of CLIP embeddings against top-K reference images retrieved from databases like WikiArt and BAM.

tasks.name: Verifiability vs. Artistic Freedom
tasks.description: Evaluating the balance between factual accuracy in generated images and creative freedom, with the goal of minimizing misinformation.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates DPO and their proposed CAO method, which are alignment techniques for diffusion models like Stable Diffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Lverifiability, calculated as 1 minus the average cosine similarity of DINO ViT embeddings between the generated image and top-K images retrieved from Google Image Search.

tasks.name: Cultural Sensitivity vs. Artistic Freedom
tasks.description: Evaluating the trade-off between respecting cultural representations and ensuring creative liberties do not lead to insensitivity or misrepresentation.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates DPO and their proposed CAO method, which are alignment techniques for diffusion models like Stable Diffusion.
tasks.scoring_detail: Lcultural, calculated using a proposed metric called Simulated Cultural Context Matching (SCCM), which uses LLMs to generate cultural sub-prompts and measures alignment with CLIP similarity.

benchmarks.name: Weighted Alpha
benchmarks.relevance_reason: This is a metric for analyzing a model's internal properties (generalization and overfitting) by examining the eigenvalue distribution of its weight matrices. It does not evaluate the creative output of the model.

tasks.name: Generalization and Overfitting Analysis
tasks.description: Assessing model generalization and overfitting tendencies by analyzing the eigenvalue distribution of the model's weight matrices without requiring training or test data.
tasks.task_type_notes: Model analysis task, not a generation or evaluation task.
tasks.model_type_notes: Applied to Stable Diffusion 3.5, DPO, and DPO-CAO models.
tasks.scoring_detail: Weighted Alpha score (ˆα) computed from the power-law exponent of the weight matrices' Empirical Spectral Density (ESD).

title: Building-Block Aware Generative Modeling for 3D Crystals of Metal Organic Frameworks

benchmarks.name: MOF Crystal Structure Generation
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Presents a new framework for evaluating the generative capabilities of an AI model for creating novel, valid, and synthesizable 3D crystal structures (MOFs), a key task in creative materials discovery.

tasks.name: De Novo MOF Generation
tasks.description: Unconditional generation of novel Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) by sampling building blocks (nodes, edges, nets) and assembling them into 3D crystal structures.
tasks.model_type_notes: SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model (BBA MOF Diffusion)
tasks.scoring_detail: Validity rate (based on chemical/geometric rules), Novelty rate (comparison to training set), Uniqueness rate, Distributional similarity (using revised autocorrelation features), Property distribution similarity (edge angle, node RMSD).

tasks.name: Conditional MOF Generation
tasks.description: Generation of a specific building block (an organic edge) given a fixed inorganic node, a fixed topological net, and a target chemical composition.
tasks.model_type_notes: SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model (BBA MOF Diffusion)
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative assessment of the chemical and structural plausibility of the generated building blocks.

tasks.name: Experimental Validation of Generated MOF
tasks.description: A high-scoring generated MOF, [Zn(1, 4 −TDC)(EtOH)2], was selected for laboratory synthesis and characterization to verify the model's ability to produce physically realizable structures.
tasks.model_type_notes: SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model (BBA MOF Diffusion)
tasks.scoring_detail: Physical synthesis and characterization using Powder X-ray Diffraction (PXRD), Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA), and N2 sorption analysis to confirm structural fidelity.

title: ConvBench: A Multi-Turn Conversation Evaluation Benchmark with Hierarchical Capability for Large Vision-Language Models

benchmarks.name: ConvBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) with a hierarchical structure that explicitly evaluates creativity as its highest level, alongside perception and reasoning, in a multi-turn conversational setting.

tasks.name: Perception Tasks
tasks.description: The first level of the benchmark's hierarchy, where models are evaluated on their ability to perform basic perceptual comprehension of an image in the first turn of a conversation. The benchmark includes 71 distinct perception task types.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates 19 Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise win rate vs human reference; Direct grading score (0-10). Evaluation is performed by an LLM judge (ChatGPT-3.5) using the ConvEval pipeline.

tasks.name: Reasoning Tasks
tasks.description: The second level of the benchmark's hierarchy, where models must perform logical reasoning based on the image and the context from the first (perception) turn. The benchmark includes 65 distinct reasoning task types.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates 19 Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise win rate vs human reference; Direct grading score (0-10). Also evaluated in an ablative setting where the model is given a perfect perception response to isolate reasoning capability.

tasks.name: Creation Tasks
tasks.description: The third and highest level of the benchmark's hierarchy, requiring models to generate creative content (e.g., poems, plans, dialogues) based on the preceding perception and reasoning turns. The benchmark includes 79 distinct creation task types.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates 19 Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise win rate vs human reference; Direct grading score (0-10). Also evaluated in ablative settings with perfect perception and/or reasoning responses to isolate creative capability. Evaluation is guided by annotated 'Focus Points'.

tasks.name: Multi-turn Conversation Evaluation
tasks.description: An overall evaluation of the entire three-turn conversation, assessing the model's ability to maintain context, follow progressive instructions, and produce a coherent and high-quality dialogue across the perception, reasoning, and creation turns.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates 19 Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall conversation score (Pairwise win rate vs human); Overall conversation score (Direct grading 0-10). Also evaluated in ablative settings.

title: AnaScore: Understanding Semantic Parallelism in Proportional Analogies

benchmarks.name: Curated Sentence Analogy Datasets
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper curates, preprocesses, and annotates multiple existing sentence analogy datasets. Analogical reasoning is a core cognitive skill related to creative problem-solving and identifying novel relationships.
benchmarks.origin_paper: Lepage (2019), Afantenos et al. (2021), Wang and Lepage (2023), Blain-Montesano and Langlais (2024)

tasks.name: Analogy Quality Annotation
tasks.description: Analogies from four datasets (Semantico, MixGoogle, MulNLIs, SATS) are classified into three categories ('formal', 'semantic', 'no criterion') based on formal criteria and the paper's proposed AnaScore metric. This is done to analyze the properties and quality of the datasets.
tasks.task_type_notes: This task uses the new AnaScore metric to evaluate and classify the analogies within existing datasets, rather than evaluating an AI model's performance.
tasks.model_type_notes: The system being applied is the AnaScore metric algorithm itself, not a generative AI model.
tasks.scoring_detail: Classification into 'formal', 'semantic', or 'no criterion' based on formal rules and the AnaScore value.

tasks.name: Sentence Analogy Solving
tasks.description: LLMs are prompted to generate the fourth sentence (D) in a proportional analogy (A : B :: C : D). The test set consists of 1,000 analogies sampled from the four curated datasets.
tasks.model_type_notes: Llama3.2, Gemma2, DeepSeek-V2
tasks.scoring_detail: BLEU score, Accuracy of generating non-overlapping components

title: PunchBench: Benchmarking MLLMs in Multimodal Punchline Comprehension

benchmarks.name: PunchBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on their ability to comprehend humor and sarcasm (punchlines) in image-caption pairs, a creative and nuanced understanding task.

tasks.name: Punchline Perception - Yes/No QA
tasks.description: Given an image-caption pair, the model must answer 'Yes' or 'No' to whether it contains a punchline.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Punchline Perception - Matching QA
tasks.description: Given an image and two captions, the model must select the caption that conveys a punchline.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Punchline Perception - Multi-option QA
tasks.description: Given an image-caption pair, the model must select the correct description from four options.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Punchline Reasoning - Yes/No QA
tasks.description: Given an image-caption pair and a reasoning sentence, the model must identify if the reasoning sentence correctly explains the punchline.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Punchline Reasoning - Matching QA
tasks.description: Given an image-caption pair and two reasoning sentences, the model must select the one that correctly explains the punchline.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Punchline Reasoning - Generation QA
tasks.description: Given an image-caption pair, the model must generate a reasoning sentence to explain the punchline.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
tasks.scoring_detail: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 binary judgment (Yes/No) of semantic match to reference

title: Rhetorical Text-to-Image Generation via Two-layer Diffusion Policy Optimization

benchmarks.name: FLUTE (filtered)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A dataset of rhetorical language (metaphors, similes) used for the open-ended, creative task of text-to-image generation, which requires interpreting figurative meaning rather than literal descriptions.

tasks.name: Rhetorical Text-to-Image Generation
tasks.description: Generating images from rhetorical text prompts, specifically metaphors and similes, with the goal of capturing the intended figurative meaning rather than a literal interpretation.
tasks.model_type_notes: The primary model, Rhet2Pix, is a fine-tuned diffusion model. It is compared against other diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, DDPO, MMaDA, Imagen) and multimodal large language models (GPT-4o, Grok-3).
tasks.scoring_detail: Qualitative visual inspection; Quantitative 'Semantic-alignment' and 'Elemental-alignment' scores based on custom CLIP cosine similarity metrics.

title: How do Language Models Generate Slang: A Systematic Comparison between Human and Machine-Generated Slang Usages

benchmarks.name: Slang Generation Evaluative Framework
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new multi-faceted framework for evaluating the creativity, characteristics, and informativeness of AI-generated slang, which is an open-ended, creative language task.

tasks.name: Slang Generation for Dataset Creation
tasks.description: LLMs are prompted to generate novel slang usages (term, definition, context) under various controlled (given definition) and uncontrolled settings, with constraints on word choice (coinage, reuse, free-form). This creates the dataset for subsequent analysis.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o and Llama-3 were used for generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: This task is for data collection; no model evaluation is performed at this stage.

tasks.name: Usage Characteristics Analysis
tasks.description: Comparing aggregate characteristics of generated slang against human slang from the Online Slang Dictionary (OSD), including the proportion of coinage vs. reuse, word formation patterns, and topical preferences.
tasks.task_type_notes: Analysis of generated text properties, not a direct generation/evaluation task for the model being tested.
tasks.scoring_detail: Reuse-Coinage proportion, Distribution of word formation processes (compounding, blending) via Morfessor and Wiktionary, LDA topic modeling.

tasks.name: Creativity in Coinage Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating the morphological creativity of coined slang terms based on their complexity and semantic coherence.
tasks.scoring_detail: Morphological Complexity (average number of Morfessor segments), Morphological Coherence (average Euclidean distance of SBERT embeddings).

tasks.name: Creativity in Reuse Evaluation
tasks.description: Evaluating the creativity of reused slang terms based on the semantic novelty of the sense extension and the contextual surprisal.
tasks.scoring_detail: Novelty (semantic distance between SBERT embeddings), Surprisal (average negative log-likelihood from Gemma-2-9b-Instruct).

tasks.name: Task 1 - Generation (Cloze + Definition -> Word)
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task where a model infers a slang term given a masked usage sentence and its definition. Used to evaluate models fine-tuned on human vs. machine-generated slang, tested on data from the Online Slang Dictionary (OSD) and OpenSub-Slang.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is multiple-choice selection.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o and fine-tuned Llama-3-8B models were evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Task 2 - Interpretation (Word + Usage -> Definition)
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task where a model selects the correct definition for a slang word given its usage context. Used to evaluate models fine-tuned on human vs. machine-generated slang, tested on data from the Online Slang Dictionary (OSD) and OpenSub-Slang.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is multiple-choice selection.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o and fine-tuned Llama-3-8B models were evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Task 3 - Free-form interpretation (Word + Usage -> Definition (Generation))
tasks.description: An open-ended task where a model generates a definition for a slang word given its usage context. Used to evaluate models fine-tuned on human vs. machine-generated slang, tested on data from the Online Slang Dictionary (OSD) and OpenSub-Slang.
tasks.model_type_notes: GPT-4o and fine-tuned Llama-3-8B models were evaluated.
tasks.scoring_detail: SBERT semantic similarity

title: ANALOGICAL - A Novel Benchmark for Long Text Analogy Evaluation in Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: ANALOGICAL
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark to evaluate LLMs on their ability to identify analogies of increasing complexity, from word-level to metaphorical. Analogy-making is a core component of creative cognition and reasoning.

tasks.name: BATS
tasks.description: Word-level analogies from four categories: Morphology-inflections, Morphology-derivation, Semantics-encyclopedia, and Semantics-lexicography.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: MSR Dataset
tasks.description: A dataset containing analogies between two words.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Google Dataset
tasks.description: Proportional analogies between word pairs (e.g., a:b :: c:d) covering syntactic and semantic relations.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: SAT Dataset
tasks.description: Word pair analogy problems from SAT exams and other educational resources.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Crossword Dataset
tasks.description: Analogies between a crossword clue (sentence/phrase) and its corresponding answer (word).
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: WordNet Dataset
tasks.description: Analogies between a WordNet word and its sentential definition (sense).
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Random Deletion Dataset
tasks.description: Syntactic analogies between an original sentence and a version with 20% of its words randomly deleted.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Random Masking Dataset
tasks.description: Syntactic analogies between an original sentence and a version with 20% of its tokens randomly replaced with [MASK].
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Random Reorder Dataset
tasks.description: Syntactic analogies between an original sentence and a version with 20% of its words randomly reordered.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Negation Dataset
tasks.description: Non-analogous pairs consisting of a sentence and its negation. A good model should produce distant embeddings for these pairs.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of non-analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Entailment Dataset
tasks.description: Analogies between a sentence and another sentence that it entails.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: ePiC Dataset
tasks.description: Metaphorical analogies between a proverb (sentence) and its corresponding explanatory narrative (paragraph).
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

tasks.name: Quotes Dataset
tasks.description: Metaphorical analogies between a quote and its elaborated meaning.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task evaluates the semantic vector space of LLMs by measuring the distance between embeddings of analogical pairs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Cosine distance, Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance between embeddings

title: Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings: Exploring Creative Problem Solving and Einstellung Effect using the Only Connect Wall Dataset

benchmarks.name: Only Connect Wall (OCW) Dataset
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A novel dataset designed to evaluate creative problem-solving in LLMs, framed as an analog to the Remote Associates Test (RAT). It involves finding heterogeneous connections among clues and is designed with 'red herrings' to test for cognitive fixation.

tasks.name: Grouping
tasks.description: Given 16 jumbled word clues, the task is to sort them into four distinct groups, each containing four connected words.
tasks.model_type_notes: Various text models were tested, including static word embeddings (GloVe, FastText), Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs like BERT, RoBERTa, ELMo), Sentence Transformers (MPNet, E5), and Large Language Models (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4).
tasks.scoring_detail: # Solved Walls, # Correct Groups, Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI), Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Fowlkes Mallows Score (FMS), Wasserstein Distance (WD)

tasks.name: Connections
tasks.description: Given four correctly formed groups of four clues, the task is to identify and name the correct connection or relationship for each group.
tasks.scoring_detail: Exact match, ROUGE-1 F1, BERTScore F1

benchmarks.name: OCW-Randomized
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A synthetically generated dataset derived from OCW to perform an ablation study on the effect of 'red herrings'. It dilutes the presence of distractors by creating walls from randomly selected groups from different original walls, directly testing an aspect of creative problem-solving.

tasks.name: Grouping
tasks.description: Grouping 16 clues into four groups of four on a dataset where the presence of deliberate 'red herrings' has been reduced by randomizing the groups within each wall.
tasks.model_type_notes: Various text models were tested, including static word embeddings, Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs), and Large Language Models (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4).
tasks.scoring_detail: # Solved Walls, # Correct Groups, Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI), Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Fowlkes Mallows Score (FMS), Wasserstein Distance (WD)

benchmarks.name: OCW-WordNet
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A synthetically generated dataset derived from OCW and WordNet to create a simplified version of the task with red herrings removed. It uses synonym and hyponym relationships to create unambiguous groups, serving as a control condition for creative problem-solving evaluation.

tasks.name: Grouping
tasks.description: Grouping 16 clues into four groups of four on a simplified dataset where groups are formed by synonyms or clear hyponym-hypernym relationships from WordNet, effectively removing red herrings.
tasks.model_type_notes: Various text models were tested, including static word embeddings, Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs), and Large Language Models (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4).
tasks.scoring_detail: # Solved Walls, # Correct Groups, Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI), Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Fowlkes Mallows Score (FMS), Wasserstein Distance (WD)

title: WritingBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Generative Writing

benchmarks.name: WritingBench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The paper introduces this new comprehensive benchmark for evaluating generative writing capabilities of LLMs across 6 domains and 100 subdomains, focusing on open-ended text generation with various constraints.

tasks.name: Generative Writing Evaluation
tasks.description: LLMs generate text based on 1,000 queries across 6 domains (Academic & Engineering, Finance & Business, Politics & Law, Literature & Art, Education, Advertising & Marketing) with specific constraints on style, format, and length.
tasks.scoring_detail: Scoring on a 1-10 scale by a fine-tuned critic model based on 5 dynamically generated, instance-specific criteria.

benchmarks.name: Human Consistency Evaluation Set
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new evaluation task designed to validate the paper's automated evaluation framework against human judgment for generative writing tasks.

tasks.name: Pairwise Comparison of Generated Text
tasks.description: Human annotators perform pairwise comparisons of responses generated by different LLMs for 300 writing queries to validate the alignment of automated evaluation methods (the critic model, GPT-4o, Claude-3.7).
tasks.task_type_notes: The primary goal is to evaluate the performance of different AI judges against a human ground truth.
tasks.model_type_notes: Both the text generators and the judges being evaluated are LLMs.
tasks.scoring_detail: Pairwise preference (A/B/Tie) by human annotators, used to calculate alignment percentage with LLM judges.

benchmarks.name: LongBench-Write
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A reused benchmark for general-purpose writing, used to evaluate the performance of the paper's writing-enhanced models.

tasks.name: Long Text Generation Quality Evaluation
tasks.description: Writing-enhanced models were evaluated on this general-purpose writing benchmark, following the quality evaluation settings of the original paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall quality score (as per original benchmark protocol).

benchmarks.name: EQ-Bench
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A reused benchmark for creative writing, used to test the hypothesis that Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves performance on creative tasks.

tasks.name: Creative Writing Evaluation
tasks.description: A CoT-enhanced model was evaluated on this specialized benchmark for creative writing to validate the efficacy of CoT in creative content generation.
tasks.scoring_detail: Overall score (as per original benchmark protocol).

title: Weak-eval-Strong: Evaluating and Eliciting Lateral Thinking of LLMs with Situation Puzzles

benchmarks.name: SPLAT
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new benchmark of situation puzzles to evaluate and elicit lateral thinking, a form of creative problem-solving, in LLMs via an open-ended scenario deduction task.

tasks.name: Scenario Deduction
tasks.description: An LLM (player) interacts with another LLM (judge) by asking yes/no questions about an incomplete story to deduce the full, hidden scenario. The evaluation is conducted within a multi-turn player-judge framework.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (semantic alignment with reference answer judged by an LLM), Average Round, Overall (O/A) score

benchmarks.name: RiddleSense
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A reused benchmark of riddle-style questions that test linguistic creativity and commonsense reasoning in LLMs, which are facets of creative thinking. The paper uses it to show that its proposed methods can elicit and improve performance on other lateral thinking tasks.

tasks.name: Riddle Question Answering
tasks.description: LLMs are presented with multiple-choice riddles from the RiddleSense dev set and must select the correct answer in a zero-shot setting. This task is used to evaluate if auxiliary reasoning prompts from the SPLAT benchmark can elicit better performance.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is multiple-choice question answering, where the model generates the token for the correct choice.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy (%)

benchmarks.name: BrainTeaser
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A reused benchmark of lateral thinking puzzles designed to evaluate creative problem-solving and non-conventional thinking in LLMs. The paper uses it to show that its proposed methods can elicit and improve performance on other lateral thinking tasks.

tasks.name: Sentence Puzzles
tasks.description: LLMs solve sentence-based lateral thinking puzzles, which are presented as multiple-choice questions. The evaluation includes original, semantic, and contextual variations of the puzzles.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is multiple-choice question answering, where the model generates the token for the correct choice.
tasks.scoring_detail: Instance-based Accuracy (Original, Semantic, Context), Group-based Accuracy

tasks.name: Word Puzzles
tasks.description: LLMs solve word-based lateral thinking puzzles, which are presented as multiple-choice questions. The evaluation includes original, semantic, and contextual variations of the puzzles.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task is multiple-choice question answering, where the model generates the token for the correct choice.
tasks.scoring_detail: Instance-based Accuracy (Original, Semantic, Context), Group-based Accuracy

title: Metaphor Understanding Challenge Dataset for LLMs

benchmarks.name: Metaphor Understanding Challenge Dataset (MUNCH)
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset and tasks to evaluate LLMs on metaphor understanding, a key aspect of figurative and creative language comprehension involving non-literal interpretation and analogical reasoning.

tasks.name: Paraphrase Judgement
tasks.description: A multiple-choice task where a model must select the correct paraphrase(s) for a given sentence containing a metaphorical word. The choices include an apt paraphrase, an inapt paraphrase (related to the literal meaning), both, or neither.
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy

tasks.name: Paraphrase Generation
tasks.description: A fill-in-the-blank task where a model is prompted to generate a single word to replace a highlighted metaphorical word in a sentence, creating a literal and semantically equivalent paraphrase.
tasks.scoring_detail: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Recall@5, Recall@10

title: D-HUMOR: Dark Humor Understanding via Multimodal Open-ended Reasoning

benchmarks.name: D-HUMOR
benchmarks.relevance_reason: Introduces a new dataset and set of tasks for evaluating AI's ability to understand a nuanced and creative form of communication: dark humor in multimodal memes. The tasks require judging subjective and implicit content.

tasks.name: Dark Humor Detection
tasks.description: A binary classification task to determine whether a multimodal meme contains dark humor (yes/no).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-only models (BERT, Llama), image-only models (CLIP, ViT), and multimodal models (Qwen, LLaVA, TCRNet).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Macro-F1, Weighted-F1

tasks.name: Target Identification
tasks.description: A multi-class classification task to identify the target group or topic of the dark humor (e.g., gender, mental health, race, disability, violence, other).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-only models (BERT, Llama), image-only models (CLIP, ViT), and multimodal models (Qwen, LLaVA, TCRNet).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Macro-F1, Weighted-F1

tasks.name: Intensity Prediction
tasks.description: An ordinal classification task to rate the intensity of the dark humor on a three-level scale (mild, moderate, severe).
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates text-only models (BERT, Llama), image-only models (CLIP, ViT), and multimodal models (Qwen, LLaVA, TCRNet).
tasks.scoring_detail: Accuracy, Macro-F1, Weighted-F1, Pearson correlation

title: VOILA: Evaluation of MLLMs For Perceptual Understanding and Analogical Reasoning

benchmarks.name: VOILA
benchmarks.relevance_reason: A new, large-scale, open-ended benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on visual analogical reasoning, a core cognitive skill related to creativity and problem-solving. It requires generating novel image and text outputs based on inferred abstract rules. The paper introduces and tests on two splits: VOILA-WD (with distractions) and VOILA-ND (without distractions).

tasks.name: Describing Images
tasks.description: In the first step of a multi-step reasoning process, MLLMs are prompted to describe the content of three input images, focusing on the number of subjects, subject types, and actions.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Models).
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4o scores the correctness of the generated description for each property (number, subject, action) against ground truth text.

tasks.name: Identifying Relations
tasks.description: In the second step, MLLMs identify the changed and unchanged properties (number of subjects, subject type, action) between the first and second images of the visual analogy.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Models).
tasks.scoring_detail: GPT-4o scores the correctness of the identified relationship for each property against ground truth.

tasks.name: Applying Relationship
tasks.description: In the third step, MLLMs apply the relationship identified in the previous step to the third image to predict the properties of the missing fourth image, generating a text description of the result.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Models).
tasks.scoring_detail: MLLM text outputs are scored for property correctness (number, subject, action) by GPT-4o against ground truth. Human baseline performance is also measured by comparing participant text answers from Amazon Mechanical Turk to the ground truth.

tasks.name: Generating Image
tasks.description: In the final step, MLLMs generate the fourth image based on the properties derived in the 'Applying Relationship' step.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper uses the term MLLM (Multimodal Large Language Models), specifically those with image generation capabilities like GPT-4o and Seed-LLaMa.
tasks.scoring_detail: A VQA-style evaluation where GPT-4o answers questions about the generated image's properties (number, subject, action) to check alignment with the ground truth.

title: AAAR-1.0: Assessing AI's Potential to Assist Research

benchmarks.name: AAAR-1.0
benchmarks.relevance_reason: The benchmark as a whole is relevant because it includes open-ended generation tasks like EXPERIMENTDESIGN and PAPERWEAKNESS, which require ideation, critical thinking, and divergent problem-finding, all core aspects of creativity in a research context.

tasks.name: EQUATIONINFERENCE
tasks.description: A binary inference task where a model must determine if a given equation is correct based on the surrounding context from a research paper.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1, Precision, Recall

tasks.name: EXPERIMENTDESIGN
tasks.description: Given the pre-experiment context of a research paper (including text and figures), the model generates a list of experiments and explains the motivation behind each one.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both text-only LLMs and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) like GPT-4o and InternVL2.
tasks.scoring_detail: En-Precision/En-Recall (GPT-4o judge), S-Match (SentenceBERT cosine similarity), ROUGE, Human evaluation (necessity rating, acceptability ratio)

tasks.name: PAPERWEAKNESS
tasks.description: Given a full research paper draft (including text, figures, and tables), the model identifies and generates a list of its weaknesses.
tasks.model_type_notes: The paper evaluates both text-only LLMs and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) like GPT-4o and InternVL2.
tasks.scoring_detail: S-Precision, S-Recall (SentenceBERT cosine similarity), ITF-IDF (diversity metric)

tasks.name: REVIEWCRITIQUE
tasks.description: Given a paper submission and a human-written review, the model identifies which segments of the review are deficient or unreliable and provides an explanation.
tasks.task_type_notes: The task involves both classifying review segments (deficient/not) and generating explanations for the deficient ones.
tasks.scoring_detail: F1, Precision, Recall (for classification); ROUGE, BERTScore (for explanation)
